body.text: (GBr_0.0.0a) oṃ namo 'tharvavedāya namaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Oṃ! Salutation to the <s>Atharvaveda</s>! Salutation!

children.text: (GBr_1,1.1m) tasmāt suvedo 'bhavat
children.translated_text: Therefore he became <s>Suveda</s> (the well-discovered one).

children.text: (GBr_1,1.1n) taṃ vā etaṃ suvedaṃ santaṃ sveda ity ācakṣate parokṣeṇa
children.translated_text: Him, though being <s>Suveda</s>, they call <s>Sveda</s> (sweat) by an indirect name.

children.text: (GBr_1,1.1o) parokṣapriyā iva hi devā bhavanti pratyakṣadviṣaḥ || 1 ||
children.translated_text: For the gods are fond of the indirect (<s>parokṣa</s>) and averse to the direct. ||1||

body.translated_text:
Oṃ! In the beginning, <s>Brahman</s> alone existed here, self-born, one only.
It willed:
"What a great being (<s>yakṣa</s>) that I alone am!
Let me create from myself alone a second deity, equal to my thought."
It strove, it heated, it intensely heated.
Of that striving, heated, intensely heated one, from the forehead arose moisture, something wet.
By that it rejoiced.
It said:
"What a great being — well-discovered (<s>suveda</s>), I have found myself!"
Because it said:
"What a great being — well-discovered, I have found myself!"

children.text: (GBr_1,1.2v) tasmād āpo 'bhavan_
children.translated_text: Therefore the waters (<s>āpaḥ</s>) came into being.

children.text: (GBr_1,1.2w) tad apām aptvam
children.translated_text: That is the water-nature (<s>aptva</s>) of the waters.

children.text: (GBr_1,1.2x) āpnoti vai sa sarvān kāmān yān kāmayate || 2 ||
children.translated_text: He who knows this obtains all desires that he desires. ||2||

body.translated_text:
He again strove, again heated, again intensely heated himself.
Of that striving, heated, intensely heated one, from all the hair-pores separate streams of sweat flowed forth.
By them he rejoiced.
He said:
"With these I shall sustain everything whatsoever that exists;
with these I shall beget everything whatsoever that exists;
with these I shall obtain everything whatsoever that exists."
Because he said:
"With these I shall sustain (<s>dhārayiṣyāmi</s>) everything whatsoever that exists,"
therefore they became streams (<s>dhārāḥ</s>).
That is the stream-nature of streams, and what is sustained in them.
Because he said:
"With these I shall beget (<s>janayiṣyāmi</s>) everything whatsoever that exists,"
therefore they became wives (<s>jāyāḥ</s>).
That is the wife-nature of wives — that in them a man is born, and that a son is born.
<s>Pun</s> is the name of a hell with many hundreds of layers;
from that he saves (<s>trāti</s>), therefore he is called a son (<s>putra</s>).
That is the son-nature of a son.
Because he said:
"With these I shall obtain (<s>āpsyāmi</s>) everything whatsoever that exists,"

(GBr_1,1.3b) tāsu svāṃ chāyām apaśyat
(GBr_1,1.3b) tām asyekṣamāṇasya svayaṃ reto 'skandat

children.text: (GBr_1,1.3m) tasmād bhṛguḥ samabhavat
children.translated_text: Therefore <s>Bhṛgu</s> came into being.

children.text: (GBr_1,1.3n) tad bhṛgor bhṛgutvam_
children.translated_text: That is the <s>Bhṛgu</s>-nature of <s>Bhṛgu</s>.

children.text: (GBr_1,1.3o) bhṛgur iva vai sa sarveṣu lokeṣu bhāti ya evaṃ veda || 3 ||
children.translated_text: He who knows this shines like <s>Bhṛgu</s> in all worlds. ||3||

body.translated_text:
Having created those waters, he looked into them.
In them he saw his own shadow.
As he was gazing, his seed fell of its own accord.
It settled in the waters.
He strove, heated, and intensely heated those very waters.
Those waters, exhausted, heated, intensely heated, together with the seed, split in two.
One half of them was extremely salty, undrinkable, and tasteless.
They stood unsettled, surrounding the ocean of seed.
But the other waters were drinkable, sweet, and calm.
He strove, heated, and intensely heated those very waters.

children.text: (GBr_1,1.4x) tat prajāpateḥ prajāpatitvam
children.translated_text: That is the <s>Prajāpati</s>-nature of <s>Prajāpati</s>.

children.text: (GBr_1,1.4y) atharvā vai prajāpatiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Atharvā</s> indeed is <s>Prajāpati</s>.

children.text: (GBr_1,1.4z) prajāpatir iva vai sa sarveṣu lokeṣu bhāti ya evaṃ veda || 4 ||
children.translated_text: He who knows this shines like <s>Prajāpati</s> in all worlds. ||4||

body.translated_text:
Having created <s>Bhṛgu</s>, he disappeared.
<s>Bhṛgu</s>, once created, moved eastward.
Speech (<s>Vāc</s>) followed him, calling: "<s>Vāyu</s>! <s>Vāyu</s>!"
He turned back and moved to the southern direction.
Speech followed him, calling: "<s>Mātariśvan</s>! <s>Mātariśvan</s>!"
He turned back and moved to the western direction.
Speech followed him, calling: "<s>Pavamāna</s>! <s>Pavamāna</s>!"
He turned back and moved to the northern direction.
Speech followed him, calling: "<s>Vāta</s>! <s>Vāta</s>!"

body.text:
(GBr_1,1.5a) tam atharvāṇam ṛṣim abhyaśrāmyad abhyatapat samatapat
(GBr_1,1.5b) tasmāc chrāntāt taptāt saṃtaptād daśatayān atharvaṇa ṛṣīn niramimataikarcān dvyṛcāṃs tṛcāṃs caturṛcān pañcarcānt ṣaḍarcānt saptarcān aṣṭarcān navarcān daśarcān iti [ed.: ṣaḍarcāṃt]
(GBr_1,1.5b) tān atharvaṇa ṛṣīn abhyaśrāmyad abhyatapat samatapat
(GBr_1,1.5d) tebhyaḥ śrāntebhyas taptebhyaḥ saṃtaptebhyo daśatayān ātharvaṇān ārṣeyān niramimataikādaśān dvādaśāṃs trayodaśāṃś caturdaśān pañcadaśān ṣoḍaśānt saptadaśān aṣṭādaśān navadaśān viṃśān iti [ed.: ṣoḍaśāṃt, note also pañcarcānt above]
(GBr_1,1.5f) tān atharvaṇa ṛṣīn ātharvaṇāṃś cārṣeyān abhyaśrāmyad abhyatapat samatapat
(GBr_1,1.5g) tebhyaḥ śrāntebhyas taptebhyaḥ saṃtaptebhyo yān mantrān apaśyat sa ātharvaṇo vedo 'bhavat
(GBr_1,1.5h) tam ātharvaṇaṃ vedam abhyaśrāmyad abhyatapat samatapat

children.text: (GBr_1,1.5i) tasmāc chrāntāt taptāt saṃtaptād om iti mana evordhvam akṣaram udakrāmat
children.translated_text: From him, exhausted, heated, and intensely heated, the syllable <s>Om</s> arose upward as the mind itself, an imperishable syllable.

children.text: (GBr_1,1.5j) sa ya icchet sarvair etair atharvabhiś cātharvaṇaiś ca kurvīyety etayaiva tan mahāvyāhṛtyā kurvīta
children.translated_text: He who wishes, 'May I perform with all these <s>Atharvans</s> and <s>Ātharvaṇas</s>,' should perform with this <s>mahāvyāhṛti</s> (great utterance) alone.

children.text: (GBr_1,1.5k) sarvair ha vā asyaitair atharvabhiś cātharvaṇaiś ca kṛtaṃ bhavati ya evaṃ veda yaś caivaṃvidvān evam etayā mahāvyāhṛtyā kurute || 5 ||
children.translated_text: For one who knows this, it is as if performed with all these <s>Atharvans</s> and <s>Ātharvaṇas</s>; and so too for the knower who thus performs with this <s>mahāvyāhṛti</s>. ||5||

body.translated_text:
He strove, heated, and intensely heated that seer <s>Atharvā</s>.
From him, exhausted, heated, and intensely heated, he created ten groups of <s>Atharvan</s> seers — those of one <s>ṛc</s> (verse), of two verses, of three, of four, of five, of six, of seven, of eight, of nine, and of ten verses.
He strove, heated, and intensely heated those <s>Atharvan</s> seers.
From them, exhausted, heated, and intensely heated, he created ten groups of <s>Ātharvaṇa</s> descendants — those of eleven, twelve, thirteen, fourteen, fifteen, sixteen, seventeen, eighteen,

(GBr_1,1.6a) sa bhūyo 'śrāmyad bhūyo 'tapyad bhūya ātmānaṃ samatapat
(GBr_1,1.6b) sa ātamata eva trīṃl lokān niramimīta pṛthivīm antarikṣaṃ divam iti

(GBr_1,1.6k) tebhyaḥ śrāntebhyas taptebhyaḥ saṃtaptebhyas trīn vedān niramimīta ṛgvedaṃ yajurvedaṃ sāmavedam iti_

children.translated_text: <s>Bhūḥ</s> from the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, <s>Bhuvaḥ</s> from the <s>Yajurveda</s>, <s>Svaḥ</s> from the <s>Sāmaveda</s>.

children.text: (GBr_1,1.6p) sa ya icchet sarvair etais tribhir vedaiḥ kurvīyety etābhir eva tan mahāvyāhṛtibhiḥ kurvīta
children.translated_text: He who wishes, 'May I perform with all these three <s>Vedas</s>,' should perform with these <s>mahāvyāhṛtis</s> (great utterances) alone.

children.text: (GBr_1,1.6q) sarvair ha vā asyaitais tribhir vedaiḥ kṛtaṃ bhavati ya evaṃ veda yaś caivaṃvidvān evam etābhir mahāvyāhṛtibhiḥ kurute || 6 ||
children.translated_text: For one who knows this, it is as if performed with all these three <s>Vedas</s>; and so too for the knower who thus performs with these <s>mahāvyāhṛtis</s>. ||6||

body.translated_text:
He again strove, again heated, again intensely heated himself.
From himself he created the three worlds — <s>Pṛthivī</s> (earth), <s>Antarikṣa</s> (atmosphere), and <s>Div</s> (heaven).
Indeed, from his feet he fashioned the earth,
from his belly the atmosphere, and from his head heaven.
He strove, heated, and intensely heated those three worlds.
From them, exhausted, heated, and intensely heated, he created three gods —
<s>Agni</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, and <s>Āditya</s>.
Indeed, from the earth he fashioned <s>Agni</s>, from the atmosphere <s>Vāyu</s>,

(GBr_1,1.7i) sa samudrād amucyata
(GBr_1,1.7j) sa mucyur abhavat

children.text: (GBr_1,1.7o) so 'ṅgaraso 'bhavat
children.translated_text: He became <s>Aṅgarasa</s> (coal-essence).

children.text: (GBr_1,1.7p) taṃ vā etaṃ aṅgarasaṃ santam aṅgirā ity ācakṣate parokṣeṇa
children.translated_text: Him, though being <s>Aṅgarasa</s>, they call <s>Aṅgirā</s> by the indirect name.

children.text: (GBr_1,1.7q) parokṣapriyā iva hi devā bhavanti pratyakṣadviṣaḥ || 7 ||
children.translated_text: For the gods are fond of the indirect and averse to the direct. ||7||

body.translated_text:
Those waters that stood surrounding the ocean of seed — they ran together from east, south, west, and north.
Because they ran together (<s>samavadravanta</s>), therefore it is called the ocean (<s>samudra</s>).
Being afraid, they said:
"Let us choose this blessed one as our king."
Because they stood encircling (<s>vṛtvā</s>), he became <s>Varaṇa</s>.
Him, though being <s>Varaṇa</s>, they call <s>Varuṇa</s> by the indirect name.
For the gods are fond of the indirect and averse to the direct.
He was freed from the ocean.
He became <s>Mucyu</s>,

(GBr_1,1.8b) tasmāc chrāntāt taptāt saṃtaptād viṃśino 'ṅgirasa ṛṣīn niramimīta
(GBr_1,1.8b) tān viṃśino 'ṅgirasa ṛṣīn abhyaśrāmyad abhyatapat samatapat
(GBr_1,1.8d) tebhyaḥ śrāntebhyas taptebhyaḥ saṃtaptebhyo daśatayān āṅgirasān ārṣeyān niramimīta ṣoḍaśino 'ṣṭādaśino dvādaśina ekarcān dvyṛcāṃs tṛcāṃś caturṛcān pañcarcān ṣaḍarcān saptarcān iti
(GBr_1,1.8f) tān aṅgirasa ṛṣīn āṅgirasāṃś cārṣeyān abhyaśrāmyad abhyatapat samatapat

(GBr_1,1.8h) tām āṅgirasaṃ vedam abhyaśrāmyad abhyatapat samatapat

children.text: (GBr_1,1.8i) tasmāc chrāntāt taptāt saṃtaptāj janad iti dvaitam akṣaraṃ vyabhavat
children.translated_text: From him, exhausted, heated, and intensely heated, the dual syllable <s>janat</s> came forth.

children.text: (GBr_1,1.8j) sa ya icchet sarvair etair aṅgirobhiś cāṅgirasaiś ca kurvīyety etayaiva tan mahāvyāhṛtyā kurvīta
children.translated_text: He who wishes, 'May I perform with all these <s>Aṅgiras</s> and <s>Āṅgirasas</s>,' should perform with this <s>mahāvyāhṛti</s> (great utterance) alone.

children.text: (GBr_1,1.8k) sarvair ha vā asyaitair aṅgirobhiś cāṅgirasaiś ca kṛtaṃ bhavati ya evaṃ veda yaś caivaṃvidvān evam etayā mahāvyāhṛtyā kurute || 8 ||
children.translated_text: For one who knows this, it is as if performed with all these <s>Aṅgiras</s> and <s>Āṅgirasas</s>; and so too for the knower who thus performs with this <s>mahāvyāhṛti</s>. ||8||

body.translated_text:
He strove, heated, and intensely heated that seer <s>Aṅgiras</s>.
From him, exhausted, heated, and intensely heated, he created twenty <s>Aṅgiras</s> seers.
He strove, heated, and intensely heated those twenty <s>Aṅgiras</s> seers.
From them, exhausted, heated, and intensely heated, he created ten groups of <s>Āṅgirasa</s> descendants — those of sixteen, of eighteen, of twelve verses, of one verse, of two, of three, of four, of five, of six, and of seven verses.
He strove, heated, and intensely heated the <s>Aṅgiras</s> seers and the <s>Āṅgirasa</s> descendants.

children.translated_text: "That which was created as the straight being, this which was projected — a dwelling free from debt, far from here."

children.translated_text: These are indeed the sisters of the <s>Aṅgirasas</s>, namely the <s>Menā</s> maidens.

children.translated_text: He who knows this achieves prowess through the <s>Menīs</s>. ||9||

body.translated_text:
He stood upright.
He propped apart these worlds.
Therefore, one who recites the <s>Aṅgirasas</s> stands upright.
That is the observance (<s>vrata</s>). He should meditate with his mind: 'Whatever I shall meditate upon with my mind, so shall it indeed be.'
And so it indeed came to be.
And regarding this, it is said in a <s>ṛc</s> (verse):
"The best <s>Veda</s>, born of <s>tapas</s> (austerity), came into being for the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>."

children.text: (GBr_1,1.10s) sa ya icchet sarvair etaiḥ pañcabhir vedaiḥ kurvīyety etābhir eva tan mahāvyāhṛtibhiḥ kurvīta
children.translated_text: (GBr 1,1.10s) He who would desire 'May I accomplish [ritual acts] with all these five <s>Vedas</s>' — he should accomplish them with these very <s>mahāvyāhṛtis</s> (great utterances).

children.text: (GBr_1,1.10t) sarvair ha vā asyaitaiḥ pañcabhir vedaiḥ kṛtaṃ bhavati ya evaṃ veda yaś caivaṃvidvān evam etābhir mahāvyāhṛtibhiḥ kurute || 10 ||
children.translated_text: (GBr 1,1.10t) Indeed, for him it is as though accomplished with all these five <s>Vedas</s> — he who knows thus, and he who, knowing thus, performs with these <s>mahāvyāhṛtis</s>. [10]

body.translated_text: (GBr 1,1.10a) He looked upon the directions — the eastern, the southern, the western, the northern, the fixed (nadir), and the upward (zenith). (GBr 1,1.10b) He labored over them, he heated them with <s>tapas</s> (austerity), he thoroughly heated them. (GBr 1,1.10b) From those [directions], labored over, heated, and thoroughly heated, he created five <s>Vedas</s>: (GBr 1,1.10d) the <s>Sarpa-veda</s> (Veda of serpents), the <s>Piśāca-veda</s> (Veda of demons), the <s>Asura-veda</s> (Veda of anti-gods), the <s>Itihāsa-veda</s> (Veda of legends), and the <s>Purāṇa-veda</s> (Veda of ancient lore). (GBr 1,1.10f) Indeed, from the eastern direction he created the <s>Sarpa-veda</s>. (GBr 1,1.10g) From the southern, the <s>Piśāca-veda</s>. (GBr 1,1.10h) From the western, the <s>Asura-veda</s>. (GBr 1,1.10i) From the northern, the <s>Itihāsa-veda</s>. (GBr 1,1.10j) And from the fixed and the upward [directions], the <s>Purāṇa-veda</s>. (GBr 1,1.10k) He labored over those five <s>Vedas</s>, he heated them, he thoroughly heated them. (GBr 1,1.10l) From those, labored over, heated, and thoroughly heated, he created five great utterances (<s>mahāvyāhṛtis</s>): (GBr 1,1.10m) <s>vṛdhat</s>, <s>karat</s>, <s>ruhat</s>, <s>mahat</s>, <s>tat</s>. (GBr 1,1.10n) <s>Vṛdhat</s> from the <s>Sarpa-veda</s>. (GBr 1,1.10o) <s>Karat</s> from the <s>Piśāca-veda</s>. (GBr 1,1.10p) <s>Ruhat</s> from the <s>Asura-veda</s>. (GBr 1,1.10q) <s>Mahat</s> from the <s>Itihāsa-veda</s>.

body.translated_text: (GBr 1,1.13a) He performed that [sacrifice]. (GBr 1,1.13b) He sacrificed with it. (GBr 1,1.13b) <s>Agni</s> was its <s>Hotṛ</s> (invoking priest). (GBr 1,1.13d) <s>Vāyu</s> was the <s>Adhvaryu</s> (officiating priest). (GBr 1,1.13f) <s>Sūrya</s> was the <s>Udgātṛ</s> (chanting priest). (GBr 1,1.13g) <s>Candramā</s> (the moon) was the <s>Brahmā</s> (supervising priest). (GBr 1,1.13h) <s>Parjanya</s> was the <s>Sadasya</s> (assembly-member). (GBr 1,1.13i) The herbs and trees were the <s>Camasādhvaryus</s> (cup-bearing priests). (GBr 1,1.13j) The <s>Viśvedevas</s> (all the gods) were the <s>Hotrakas</s> (assistant invoking priests). (GBr 1,1.13k) The <s>Atharvāṅgirasas</s> were the protectors. (GBr 1,1.13l) Indeed, former <s>Śrotriyas</s> (learned ones) who knew thus used to approach this sacrifice when it was spread, saying for the purpose of concluding it: (GBr 1,1.13m) 'May this heated [offering] that has been raised up not burn our immortal progeny while we are inattentive.' (GBr 1,1.13n) They call those very ones — the protectors who move about the assembly — '<s>sadaḥprasarpakas</s>,' endowed with <s>dakṣiṇās</s> (ritual fees). (GBr 1,1.13o) And then <s>Prajāpati</s> said: (GBr 1,1.13p) 'When the <s>ṛtvijs</s> (priests) at a sacrifice are unskilled, have not practiced <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate studentship), or are not devoted — (GBr 1,1.13q) that they call the <s>viriṣṭa</s> (defect/injury) of the sacrifice. (GBr 1,1.13r) Following the defect of the sacrifice, the <s>yajamāna</s> (sacrificer) is injured. (GBr 1,1.13s) Following the defect of the <s>yajamāna</s>, the <s>ṛtvijs</s> are injured. (GBr 1,1.13t) Following the defect of the <s>ṛtvijs</s>, the <s>dakṣiṇās</s> (fees) are injured.

children.translated_text: (GBr 1,1.14l) Following the repair of the <s>dakṣiṇās</s>, the <s>yajamāna</s> is repaired in his sons and cattle.

children.text: (GBr_1,1.14m) putrapaśūnāṃ saṃdhitim anu yajamānaḥ svargeṇa lokena saṃdhīyate
children.translated_text: (GBr 1,1.14m) Following the repair of sons and cattle, the <s>yajamāna</s> is repaired in his heavenly world.

children.text: (GBr_1,1.14n) svargasya lokasya saṃdhitim anu tasyārdhasya yogakṣemaḥ saṃdhīyate yasminn ardhe yajanta iti brāhmaṇam || 14 ||
children.translated_text: (GBr 1,1.14n) Following the repair of the heavenly world, the welfare (<s>yogakṣema</s>) of that half in which they sacrifice is repaired — thus is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [teaching]. [14]

body.translated_text: (GBr 1,1.14a) They used to approach such a knowing <s>Brahmā</s> priest — those who had experienced sacrifice-defects or those who wished to know about sacrifice-defects — [saying:] (GBr 1,1.14b) 'Salutation to you, Blessed One. (GBr 1,1.14c) Repair the defect of our sacrifice.' (GBr 1,1.14d) Then, wherever the defect might be, having built up the fires there, having made the pacificatory water, he sprinkles the fires three times with [the mantra] 'To the earth, for hearing,' and circumambulates them three times with sprinkling. (GBr 1,1.14e) Three times he makes [the sacrificer] sip water and sprinkles him. (GBr 1,1.14f) He sprinkles the sacrificial ground. (GBr 1,1.14g) And moreover, by the essence of the <s>Vedas</s>, the defect of the sacrifice is repaired. (GBr 1,1.14h) Just as one would join gold with salt, silver with gold, copper with silver, lead with copper, tin with lead — even so the defect of this sacrifice is repaired. (GBr 1,1.14i) Following the repair of the sacrifice, the <s>yajamāna</s> is repaired. (GBr 1,1.14j) Following the repair of the <s>yajamāna</s>, the <s>ṛtvijs</s> are repaired. (GBr 1,1.14k) Following the repair of the <s>ṛtvijs</s>, the <s>dakṣiṇās</s> are repaired.

body.text: (GBr_1,1.15a) tad u ha smāhātharvā devo vijānan yajñaviriṣṭānandānīty upaśamayeran yajñe prāyaścittiḥ kriyate 'pi ca yad u bahv iva yajñe vilomaṃ kriyate na caivāsya kā canārtir bhavati na ca yajñaviṣkandham upayāty apahanti punarmṛtyum apātyeti punārājātiṃ kāmacāro 'sya sarveṣu lokeṣu bhāti ya evaṃ veda yaś caivaṃvidvān brahmā bhavati yasya caivaṃvidvān brahmā dakṣiṇataḥ sado 'dhyāste yasya caivaṃvidvān brahmā dakṣiṇata udaṅmukha āsīno yajña ājyāhutīr juhotīti brāhmaṇam || 15 ||
body.translated_text: (GBr 1,1.15a) And then <s>Atharvā</s>, the divine one, knowing [this], said: 'They should pacify the occasions of sacrifice-defect or the defect of sacrifice.' In the sacrifice, an expiatory rite (<s>prāyaścitta</s>) is performed; and even if much is done wrongly in the sacrifice, no affliction whatsoever befalls him, nor does he incur the obstruction of sacrifice. He wards off repeated death, avoids rebirth, and he moves freely in all worlds. He who knows thus shines; and he whose <s>Brahmā</s> priest knows thus; and he for whom such a knowing <s>Brahmā</s> priest sits to the south of the assembly; and he for whom such a knowing <s>Brahmā</s> priest, sitting facing north to the south, offers <s>ājya</s>-oblations (<s>ājyāhutis</s>) in the sacrifice — thus is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [teaching]. [15]

children.text: (GBr_1,1.16g) tayā sarvāṃś ca kāmānt sarvāṃś ca lokānt sarvāṃś ca devānt sarvāṃś ca vedānt sarvāṃś ca yajñānt sarvāṃś ca śabdānt sarvāś ca vyuṣṭīḥ sarvāṇi ca bhūtāni sthāvarajaṅgamāny anvabhavat
children.translated_text: (GBr 1,1.16g) Through that [syllable], he experienced all desires, all worlds, all gods, all <s>Vedas</s>, all sacrifices, all sounds, all dawns, and all beings — both stationary and moving.

children.text: (GBr_1,1.16h) tasya prathamena varṇenāpaḥ snehaṃ cānvabhavat
children.translated_text: (GBr 1,1.16h) Through its first phoneme, he experienced the waters and moisture.

children.text: (GBr_1,1.16i) tasya dvitīyena varṇena tejo jyotīṃṣy anvabhavat || 16 ||
children.translated_text: (GBr 1,1.16i) Through its second phoneme, he experienced radiance and luminaries. [16]

body.translated_text: (GBr 1,1.16a) <s>Brahman</s> (the Absolute) indeed created <s>Brahmā</s> (the Creator) in the lotus. (GBr 1,1.16b) He, <s>Brahmā</s>, having been created, fell into contemplation: (GBr 1,1.16c) 'By what single syllable might I experience all desires, all worlds, all gods, all <s>Vedas</s>, all sacrifices, all sounds, all dawns, and all beings — both stationary and moving?' (GBr 1,1.16d) He practiced <s>brahmacarya</s> (austere studentship). (GBr 1,1.16f) He beheld this syllable <s>Om</s> — having two phonemes, four <s>mātrās</s> (measures), all-pervading, all-encompassing, not stale (<s>ayātayāma</s>), not [mere] <s>brahman</s> — the <s>Brāhmī</s> utterance (<s>vyāhṛti</s>), having <s>Brahman</s> as its deity.

body.text: (GBr_1,1.17a) tasya prathamayā svaramātrayā pṛthivīm agnim oṣadhivanaspatīn ṛgvedaṃ bhūr iti vyāhṛtiṃ gāyatraṃ chandas trivṛtaṃ stomaṃ prācīṃ diśaṃ vasantam ṛtuṃ vācam adhyātmaṃ jihvāṃ rasam itīndriyāṇy anvabhavat || 17 ||
body.translated_text: (GBr 1,1.17a) Through its first vowel-measure, he experienced the earth, <s>Agni</s> (fire), herbs and trees, the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, the utterance <s>Bhūḥ</s>, the <s>Gāyatrī</s> meter, the <s>Trivṛt</s> <s>Stoma</s> (hymn-form), the eastern direction, the spring season, speech as the inner self, the tongue, and taste — [these] sense faculties. [17]

body.text: (GBr_1,1.18a) tasya dvitīyayā svaramātrayāntarikṣaṃ vāyuṃ yajurvedaṃ bhuva iti vyāhṛtiṃ traiṣṭubhaṃ chandaḥ pañcadaśaṃ stomaṃ pratīcīṃ diśaṃ grīṣmam ṛtuṃ prāṇam adhyātmaṃ nāsike gandhaghrāṇam itīndriyāṇy anvabhavat || 18 ||
body.translated_text: (GBr 1,1.18a) Through its second vowel-measure, he experienced the atmosphere, <s>Vāyu</s> (wind), the <s>Yajurveda</s>, the utterance <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>, the <s>Traiṣṭubha</s> meter, the <s>Pañcadaśa</s> <s>Stoma</s>, the western direction, the summer season, breath (<s>prāṇa</s>) as the inner self, the nostrils, and smell — [these] sense faculties. [18]

body.text: (GBr_1,1.19a) tasya tṛtīyayā svaramātrayā divam ādityaṃ sāmavedaṃ svar iti vyāhṛtiṃ jāgataṃ chandaḥ saptadaśaṃ stomam udīcīṃ diśaṃ varṣā ṛtuṃ jyotir adhyātmaṃ cakṣuṣī darśanam itīndriyāny anvabhavat || 19 ||
body.translated_text: (GBr 1,1.19a) Through its third vowel-measure, he experienced heaven, <s>Āditya</s> (the sun), the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, the utterance <s>Svaḥ</s>, the <s>Jāgata</s> meter, the <s>Saptadaśa</s> <s>Stoma</s>, the northern direction, the rainy season, light (<s>jyotis</s>) as the inner self, the two eyes, and sight — [these] sense faculties. [19]

body.text: (GBr_1,1.20a) tasya vakāramātrayāpaś candramasam atharvavedaṃ nakṣatrāṇy om iti svam ātmānaṃ janad ity aṅgirasām ānuṣṭubhaṃ chanda ekaviṃśaṃ stomaṃ dakṣiṇāṃ diśaṃ śaradam ṛtuṃ mano 'dhyātmaṃ jñānaṃ jñeyam itīndriyāṇy anvabhavat || 20 ||
body.translated_text: (GBr 1,1.20a) Through its <s>va</s>-phoneme measure, he experienced the waters, the moon, the <s>Atharvaveda</s>, the <s>nakṣatras</s> (stars), <s>Om</s> as his own self, <s>janat</s> as [the utterance] of the <s>Aṅgirasas</s>, the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> meter, the <s>Ekaviṃśa</s> <s>Stoma</s>, the southern direction, the autumn season, mind (<s>manas</s>) as the inner self, knowledge, and the knowable — [these] sense faculties. [20]

body.text: (GBr_1,1.21b) tasya makāraśrutyetihāsapurāṇaṃ vākovākyaṃ gāthā nārāśaṃsīr upaniṣado 'nuśāsanānīti vṛdhat karad ruhan mahat tac cham om iti vyāhṛtīḥ svaraśamyanānātantrīḥ svaranṛtyagītavāditrāṇy anvabhavac caitrarathaṃ daivataṃ vaidyutaṃ jyotir bārhataṃ chandas triṇavatrayastriṃśau stomau dhruvām ūrdhvāṃ diśaṃ hemantaśiśirāv ṛtū śrotram adhyātmaṃ śabdaśravaṇam itīndriyāṇy anvabhavat || 21 ||
body.translated_text: (GBr 1,1.21b) Through its <s>ma</s>-phoneme sound, he experienced the <s>Itihāsa-Purāṇa</s>, dialogue (<s>vākovākya</s>), songs (<s>gāthā</s>), <s>nārāśaṃsīs</s>, <s>Upaniṣads</s>, and instructions (<s>anuśāsanas</s>); the utterances <s>vṛdhat</s>, <s>karat</s>, <s>ruhat</s>, <s>mahat</s>, <s>tat</s>, <s>śam</s>, and <s>Om</s>; the string-instruments of melodies and pacification, the musical instruments of melody, dance, song, and instrumental music; the <s>Caitraratha</s> divinity, the lightning luminosity, the <s>Bārhata</s> meter, the <s>Triṇava</s> and <s>Trayastriṃśa</s> <s>Stomas</s>, the fixed and upward directions, the winter and cool seasons, the ear as the inner self, and hearing of sounds — [these] sense faculties. [21]

children.translated_text: (GBr 1,1.22m) His goals are accomplished, and all his ritual actions [succeed] — thus is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [teaching]. [22]

body.translated_text: (GBr 1,1.22a) This very single syllable of <s>Brahman</s> appeared first, before <s>tapas</s> (austerity) — the radiant seed (<s>śukra</s>) of the <s>Atharvanic Brahmaveda</s>. (GBr 1,1.22b) From it, the <s>mantras</s> came forth. (GBr 1,1.22c) And indeed, whatever is deficient, defective, or stale that one creates through <s>mantras</s> without <s>tapas</s>, without devoted service, without study and teaching — that one should restore by the power of the <s>Atharvaṇas</s>. (GBr 1,1.22d) 'And may the <s>mantras</s> turn toward me, like embryos toward their mother, desiring to rush forth.' (GBr 1,1.22e) One employs <s>Oṃkāra</s> at the beginning. (GBr 1,1.22f) By this very <s>ṛc</s> (verse) one should restore [the defect]. (GBr 1,1.22g) This very [syllable] is employed at the beginning of the sacrifice. (GBr 1,1.22h) This [is employed] at the end. (GBr 1,1.22i) The sacrifice is extended by it on all sides. (GBr 1,1.22j) This too is stated in a <s>ṛc</s> (verse):

body.translated_text: The city of <s>Indra</s> belongs to the streams of <s>Vasu</s>. The <s>Asuras</s> besieged it. The <s>Devas</s> were afraid. 'Who will strike down these <s>Asuras</s>?' They saw <s>Oṃkāra</s>, the eldest son of <s>Brahman</s>. They said to him: 'With you at the fore, let us conquer these <s>Asuras</s>.' He said: 'What shall be my reward?' 'Choose a boon.' 'I choose,' he said. He chose this boon: 'Let the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> not utter <s>Brahman</s> (sacred speech) without first uttering me; if they do, that shall be non-<s>Brahman</s> (devoid of sacred power).' 'So be it.' The <s>Devas</s>, arrayed against the <s>Asuras</s> on the northern half of the sacrificial ground, defeated the <s>Asuras</s> with <s>Oṃkāra</s> from the <s>Āgnīdhrīya</s> fire. Because they defeated [them], therefore <s>Oṃkāra</s> is uttered first. He who does not know this <s>Oṃkāra</s> would be powerless; but he who knows thus would have mastery over <s>Brahman</s>. Therefore <s>Oṃkāra</s> is <s>Ṛc</s> in the <s>Ṛc</s>, <s>Yajus</s> in the <s>Yajus</s>, <s>Sāman</s> in the <s>Sāman</s>, <s>Sūtra</s> in the <s>Sūtra</s>,

children.translated_text: Of the prior and latter, there are three groups of twelve each.

children.text: (GBr_1,1.24ff) etair oṃkāraṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ || 24 ||
children.translated_text: By these we shall explain <s>Oṃkāra</s>.

body.translated_text: We inquire about <s>Oṃkāra</s>: What is the root (<s>dhātu</s>)? What is the nominal stem (<s>prātipadika</s>)? Is it a noun or a verb (<s>nāmākhyāta</s>)? What is the gender (<s>liṅga</s>)? What is the number (<s>vacana</s>)? What is the case (<s>vibhakti</s>)? What is the suffix (<s>pratyaya</s>)? What is the accent (<s>svara</s>), prefix (<s>upasarga</s>), or indeclinable particle (<s>nipāta</s>)? What is the grammatical analysis (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>)? What is the modification (<s>vikāra</s>)? What is the thing modified (<s>vikārin</s>)? How many <s>mātrās</s> (morae)? How many letters (<s>varṇa</s>)? How many syllables (<s>akṣara</s>)? How many words (<s>pada</s>)? What is the conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>)? What are the place of articulation, effort, and instrument? What do the phoneticians pronounce? What is the meter (<s>chandas</s>)? What is the letter (<s>varṇa</s>)? — These are the prior questions. Now the latter: <s>Mantra</s>, <s>Kalpa</s>, <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Ṛc</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, <s>Sāman</s>. Why do speakers of <s>Brahman</s> place <s>Oṃkāra</s> at the beginning? What is the deity? What is the astronomical significance? What is the etymology (<s>nirukta</s>)? What is the place (<s>sthāna</s>)? What is the original form (<s>prakṛti</s>)? What is the <s>adhyātma</s> (spiritual) [significance]?

body.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> asked <s>Prajāpati</s>: 'Blessed One, having praised [you], I ask.' 'Ask, dear child,' he said. 'What is this <s>Oṃkāra</s>? Whose son is it? What is its meter? What is its letter? What is this <s>Brahman</s> by which one attains <s>Brahman</s>?' Therefore he first took hold of that auspicious <s>Oṃkāra</s>. In the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, <s>Oṃkāra</s> is a single-syllable [sound] with <s>svarita-udātta</s> accent. In the <s>Yajurveda</s>, <s>Oṃkāra</s> is a single-syllable [sound] with <s>traisvarya-udātta</s> accent. In the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, <s>Oṃkāra</s> is a single-syllable [sound] with long protracted <s>udātta</s> accent. In the <s>Atharvaveda</s>, <s>Oṃkāra</s> is a single-syllable [sound] with short <s>udātta</s> accent. [It has] two feet — <s>a</s> and <s>u</s> — with <s>udātta-udātta</s> [accent]; they say it has three and a half <s>mātrās</s>, and the <s>makāra</s> is a consonant. The first <s>mātrā</s> has <s>Brahmā</s> as its deity and is red in color; he who meditates on it constantly attains the abode of <s>Brahmā</s>. The second <s>mātrā</s> has <s>Viṣṇu</s> as its deity and is dark in color; he who meditates on it constantly attains the abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. The third <s>mātrā</s> has <s>Īśāna</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) as its deity and is tawny in color; he who meditates on it constantly attains the abode of <s>Īśāna</s>. The three-and-a-half <s>mātrā</s> has all deities as its deity; having become manifest, it wanders through space, resembling pure crystal in color; he who meditates on it constantly attains the nameless abode. And the origin of <s>Oṃkāra</s> [is thus]. A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who does not know this should undergo the <s>upanayana</s> (initiation) again. Therefore the statement of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should be heeded, for <s>Oṃkāra</s> is the son of <s>Brahman</s>, of the <s>Lātavya</s> lineage. <s>Gāyatrī</s> is its meter. White is its color.

children.text: (GBr_1,1.26o) eva dvivarṇa ekākṣara om ity oṃkāro nirvṛttaḥ || 26 ||
children.translated_text: Thus <s>Oṃkāra</s>, having two letters and one syllable — <s>Om</s> — is accomplished.

body.translated_text: 'What is the root?' The root is <s>āp</s> (to obtain). Some say <s>av</s> (to protect). From similarity of form follows similarity of meaning, which is closer. Therefore from <s>āp</s>, <s>Oṃkāra</s> 'obtains everything' — this is the meaning; it is a <s>kṛdanta</s> (primary derivative) and meaningful. The nominal stem (<s>prātipadika</s>) is not visible [directly]. By means of the suffix, [its] name is accomplished; and the grammarians enumerate it as <s>udātta</s> among the indeclinables — that is <s>avyayībhūta</s> (an indeclinable compound). A word whose meaning is self-evident does not perish at any time. That which is the same in all three genders, in all case-endings, and in all numbers, and which does not perish — that is <s>avyaya</s> (indeclinable). What is modified? It undergoes change. It is the extension. Of <s>āpnoti</s> (the verb 'to obtain'), the <s>ā-kāra</s> and <s>pa-kāra</s> are the modifiable elements.

children.translated_text: This is the grammatical analysis — the statement of roots and meanings, phonetics (<s>śikṣā</s>), and the statement of meters. Now the latter two groups of twelve have been explained as the secret doctrine of the <s>Vedas</s>.

children.text: (GBr_1,1.27z) mantraḥ kalpo brāhamaṇam ṛg yajuḥ sāmātharvāṇi_
children.translated_text: <s>Mantra</s>, <s>Kalpa</s>, <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Ṛc</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, <s>Sāman</s>, and <s>Atharvan</s>.

children.text: (GBr_1,1.27aa) eṣā vyāhṛtiś caturṇāṃ vedānām ānupūrveṇoṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svar iti vyāhṛtayaḥ || 27 ||
children.translated_text: This is the <s>vyāhṛti</s> (sacred utterance) of the four <s>Vedas</s> in order: <s>Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svar</s> — these are the <s>vyāhṛtis</s>.

body.translated_text: 'How many <s>mātrās</s>?' From the beginning, three <s>mātrās</s>; for in prolonged utterance it is protracted. The <s>ma-kāra</s> [constitutes] the fourth. 'What is the place [of articulation]?' Both lips are the place. Voiced sound and effort — these are the two places of articulation. It is a combined syllable (<s>saṃdhyakṣara</s>), with a trace of <s>a-varṇa</s>, guttural, with the remainder as stated. The first [element] is in the open articulation position, and the second is in the closed contact position. There is no conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>). The earlier teachers were students of the [phonetic] configuration — verb, prefix, <s>anudātta</s>, <s>svarita</s>, gender, case, and number. They understood simply from hearing and did not inquire into the cause. But among those of the later school, the poet <s>Pañcālacaṇḍa</s> became an inquirer, [saying]: 'Let the learned ones state the faults of the <s>Udgītha</s> separately.' One should examine that speech by its letters, syllables, words, and markers. They praise the speech 'employed in the <s>vibhakti</s> (case) frequented by the <s>Ṛṣis</s>.' Therefore we state the cause — 'of the letters, this one will become that.' Those who know the six auxiliary sciences (<s>ṣaḍaṅga</s>), we study it thus. 'What is the meter?' <s>Gāyatrī</s> indeed is the meter. <s>Gāyatrī</s> of the <s>Devas</s> has been explained as single-syllabled and of white color. [These constitute] two groups of twelve [questions each].

children.translated_text: 'So be it, so be it, Blessed One' — they agreed and became nourished.

children.text: (GBr_1,1.28v) tasmād brahmavādina oṃkāram āditaḥ kurvanti || 28 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore speakers of <s>Brahman</s> place <s>Oṃkāra</s> at the beginning.

body.translated_text: Statements uttered without due consideration are heard. At the beginning of the <s>Dvāpara</s> age, some among the <s>Ṛṣis</s>, a lord of faults, conceived this worry here: '<s>Soma</s> is to be drunk with [only] three [Vedas]; it seems as if it is complete [without the Atharvaveda].' Therefore the <s>Ṛc</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, and <s>Sāman</s> had their splendor diminished. Then the great <s>Ṛṣis</s> lamented: 'We have come to a great fear of grief. And this was not spoken by all of us. Let us approach the Blessed One (<s>Bhagavat</s>). May the Blessed One be the refuge of all.' Having said 'so be it,' they stood in silence. 'Not to those who have not approached [with humility].' 'We approach humbly' — they became humble. He, having initiated them, spoke: 'Place my own <s>vyāhṛti</s> at the very beginning, from the start.' 'Thus my [verses] are to be recited. Not without those versed in [the traditions of] <s>Bhṛgu</s> and <s>Aṅgiras</s> should <s>Soma</s> be drunk. [Otherwise] the priests are defeated, the sacrificer is overwhelmed by <s>rajas</s> (passion), and the revealed text stands diminished.' 'Thus, from each successive stage of practice, rule generation after generation.' 'In this way, the power will not be defeated.'

children.text: (GBr_1,1.29z) bhṛgvaṅgirovidā saṃskṛto 'nyān vedān adhīyīta
children.translated_text: One who has been initiated through [the traditions of] <s>Bhṛgu</s> and <s>Aṅgiras</s> may study the other <s>Vedas</s>,

children.text: (GBr_1,1.29aa) nānyatra saṃskṛto bhṛgṅgiraso 'dhīyīta
children.translated_text: but one initiated elsewhere should not study [the traditions of] <s>Bhṛgu</s> and <s>Aṅgiras</s>.

children.text: (GBr_1,1.29bb) sāmavede 'tha khilaśrutir brahmacaryeṇa caitasmād atharvāṅgiraso ha yo veda sa veda sarvam iti brāhmaṇam || 29 ||
children.translated_text: In the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, there is also a supplementary revelation (<s>khilaśruti</s>) [that says]: through <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate studentship), 'he who knows the <s>Atharvāṅgirasa</s> from this [tradition] knows everything' — thus [says] the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.

body.translated_text: 'What is the deity?' The deity of the <s>Ṛcs</s> is <s>Agni</s>. That itself is the light. <s>Gāyatrī</s> is the meter. The earth (<s>pṛthivī</s>) is the place. Beginning with '<s>Agnim īḷe purohitam</s>' (I praise <s>Agni</s>, the foremost, the divine priest of the sacrifice, the invoker, the best bestower of treasures), the <s>Ṛgveda</s> is recited. The deity of the <s>Yajus</s> is <s>Vāyu</s>. That itself is the light. <s>Triṣṭubh</s> is the meter. The atmosphere (<s>antarikṣa</s>) is the place. Beginning with '<s>Iṣe tvā ūrje tvā</s>' (For nourishment [I take] you, for strength [I take] you; O <s>Vāyu</s>, you are [here]; may the divine <s>Savitṛ</s> impel you to the most excellent ritual action), the <s>Yajurveda</s> is recited. The deity of the <s>Sāmans</s> is <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun). That itself is the light. <s>Jagatī</s> is the meter. Heaven (<s>dyaus</s>) is the place. Beginning with '<s>Agna ā yāhi vītaye</s>' (O <s>Agni</s>, come for the feast, being praised, for the giving of oblations; sit, O invoker, on the sacred grass), the <s>Sāmaveda</s> is recited. The deity of the <s>Atharvans</s> is the Moon (<s>Candramā</s>). That itself is the light. All meters [are its meters]. The waters (<s>āpas</s>) are the place. Beginning with '<s>Śaṃ no devīr abhiṣṭaye</s>' (May the divine [waters] be auspicious for our protection), the <s>Atharvaveda</s> is recited. From the waters, the entire host of beings, both stationary and mobile, comes into existence. Therefore every being consists of water, everything consists of <s>Bhṛgu</s> and <s>Aṅgiras</s>. The three [other] <s>Vedas</s> are within these, [being] dependent on <s>Bhṛgu</s> and <s>Aṅgiras</s>. Water is the original nature (<s>prakṛti</s>) of the waters, and [so is] <s>Oṃkāra</s>. Therefore <s>Vyāsa</s> declared:

body.text: (GBr_1,1.30a) adhyātmam ātmabhaiṣajyam ātmakaivalyam oṃkāraḥ_

children.text: (GBr_1,1.30b) ātmānaṃ nirudhya saṅgamamātrīṃ bhūtārthacintāṃ cintayet_
children.translated_text: Having restrained the self, one should contemplate the thought of the reality of beings, which is the point of convergence (<s>saṅgamamātrī</s>).

children.text: (GBr_1,1.30c) atikramya vedebhyaḥ sarvaparam adhyātmaphalaṃ prāpnotītyarthaḥ
children.translated_text: Having transcended the <s>Vedas</s>, one attains the supreme fruit of the spiritual (<s>adhyātma</s>) [realization] — this is the meaning.

children.text: (GBr_1,1.30d) savitarkaṃ jñānamayam ity etaiḥ praśnaiḥ prativacanaiś ca yathārthaṃ padam anuvicintya prakaraṇajño hi prabalo viṣayī syāt sarvasmin vākovākya iti brāhmaṇam || 30 ||
children.translated_text: Knowledge endowed with deliberation (<s>savitarka</s>) — with these questions and answers, having reflected upon the matter as it truly is, one who knows the topic (<s>prakaraṇajña</s>) would indeed be powerful in debate (<s>vākovākya</s>) regarding every subject. Thus is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. [30]

body.translated_text: In the spiritual (<s>adhyātma</s>) sense, <s>Oṃkāra</s> is self-medicine (<s>ātmabhaiṣajya</s>), self-liberation (<s>ātmakaivalya</s>).

Then you should say: "It is you, sir, who called <s>Maudgalya</s> poorly learned.',

children.text: (GBr_1,1.31y) purā saṃvatsarād ārtim āriṣyasīti || 31 ||
children.translated_text: 'Before the year [is out], you will fall into distress." [31]'

body.translated_text: Now, knowing this, <s>Glāva Maitreya</s> approached <s>Maudgalya</s> of the eleven syllables. While he was observing <s>brahmacarya</s> (studentship) under him, [<s>Glāva</s>] said upon learning [about him]: 'What could this young man be studying under <s>Maudgalya</s>, that he is observing <s>brahmacarya</s> under him?' A pupil of <s>Maudgalya</s> heard this. He went to his teacher and reported: 'The one who is your guest today has called you poorly learned (<s>duradhīyāna</s>)!' [<s>Maudgalya</s> asked:] 'What does he know, dear one?' [The pupil replied:] 'He says he knows the three <s>Vedas</s>, sir.' [<s>Maudgalya</s> said:] 'Dear one, his bright and eager pupil — summon him to me.' He summoned him. He addressed him thus — 'Sir!' — 'Yes!' — 'Dear one, what does your teacher study?' — 'He knows the three <s>Vedas</s>.' — 'Indeed!' — 'Then, dear one, since all the <s>Vedas</s> have been received by us orally, how does your teacher speak thus? How would the learned speak thus to the learned? Whatever question I ask him, he will not be able to answer it; for he does not truly know it.' Then <s>Maudgalya</s> said to his own pupil: 'Go, dear one, approach <s>Glāva Maitreya</s>. [Say:] "Teach, sir, the <s>Sāvitrī Gāyatrī</s> of twenty-four sources (<s>yoni</s>) and twelve pairs (<s>mithuna</s>), whose eye is the <s>Bhṛgu-Aṅgirases</s>, in which all this is founded — let the venerable one expound it!"'

children.translated_text: Having embraced him, he asked: 'Teach, sir! Who is <s>Savitṛ</s>? What is <s>Sāvitrī</s>?' [32]

body.translated_text: He went to where the other was. He questioned him. And he did not know the answer. Then he said to him: 'It is you, sir, who called <s>Maudgalya</s> poorly learned. He asked you a question and you did not answer it. Before the year [is out], you will fall into distress.' Then <s>Maitreya</s> said to his own pupils: 'Let you all be dismissed, each as he sees fit, each to his home, each to his heart's desire. For I called <s>Maudgalya</s> poorly learned. He asked me a question and I did not answer it. I shall go to him. I shall make amends.' Then <s>Maitreya</s>, in the morning, fuel-stick in hand, approached <s>Maudgalya</s> [saying]: 'I am <s>Maitreya</s>, sir.' — 'For what purpose?' — 'I called you, sir, poorly learned. You asked me a question and I did not answer it. I shall come to you [as a pupil]. I shall make amends.' [<s>Maudgalya</s>] said: 'Here, both the coming and all [the study] has been accomplished. They say you have been going about in an evil vehicle. Now, this good chariot of mine — I give it to you. Go with it!' [<s>Maitreya</s>] replied: 'This very thing here is the cause of enmity and of cruelty, as you say, sir. Nevertheless, I shall indeed come to you [as a pupil].' He approached him. Having approached, he asked: 'What do the poets say is the "choicest splendor" (<s>vareṇyaṃ bhargaḥ</s>) of <s>Savitṛ</s> the god? What do they say are the "thoughts" (<s>dhiyaḥ</s>)? Explain, if you know them. By which ones does <s>Savitṛ</s> impel?' [<s>Maudgalya</s>] expounded this to him: 'The <s>Vedas</s> and the metres (<s>chandas</s>) are the "choicest" of <s>Savitṛ</s>;

children.translated_text: Then rising up, he departed [saying]: 'This indeed I know — [I am] not [born] in these sources, nor from these pairs. Let a <s>brahmacārin</s> born from me not depart before [the completion of] my full lifespan.' [33]

body.translated_text: Mind (<s>manas</s>) indeed is <s>Savitṛ</s>; speech (<s>vāc</s>) is <s>Sāvitrī</s>. For wherever there is mind, there is speech; wherever there is speech, there is mind. These two are the sources, one pair. <s>Agni</s> (fire) indeed is <s>Savitṛ</s>; the earth (<s>pṛthivī</s>) is <s>Sāvitrī</s>. For wherever there is fire, there is earth; wherever there is earth, there is fire. These two are the sources, one pair. <s>Vāyu</s> (wind) indeed is <s>Savitṛ</s>; the atmosphere (<s>antarikṣa</s>) is <s>Sāvitrī</s>. For wherever there is wind, there is the atmosphere; wherever there is the atmosphere, there is wind. These two are the sources, one pair. <s>Āditya</s> (the sun) indeed is <s>Savitṛ</s>; heaven (<s>dyaus</s>) is <s>Sāvitrī</s>. For wherever there is the sun, there is heaven; wherever there is heaven, there is the sun. These two are the sources, one pair. The moon (<s>Candramā</s>) indeed is <s>Savitṛ</s>; the constellations (<s>nakṣatras</s>) are <s>Sāvitrī</s>. For wherever there is the moon, there are the constellations; wherever there are the constellations, there is the moon. These two are the sources, one pair. Day (<s>ahar</s>) indeed is <s>Savitṛ</s>; night (<s>rātri</s>) is <s>Sāvitrī</s>. For wherever there is day, there is night; wherever there is night, there is day. These two are the sources, one pair. Heat (<s>uṣṇa</s>) indeed is <s>Savitṛ</s>; cold (<s>śīta</s>) is <s>Sāvitrī</s>. For wherever there is heat, there is cold; wherever there is cold, there is heat. These two are the sources, one pair. Cloud (<s>abhra</s>) indeed is <s>Savitṛ</s>; rain (<s>varṣa</s>) is <s>Sāvitrī</s>. For wherever there is cloud, there is rain; wherever there is rain, there is cloud. These two are the sources, one pair. Lightning (<s>vidyut</s>) indeed is <s>Savitṛ</s>; thunder (<s>stanayitnu</s>) is <s>Sāvitrī</s>. For wherever there is lightning, there is thunder; wherever there is thunder, there is lightning. These two are the sources, one pair. <s>Prāṇa</s> (breath) indeed is <s>Savitṛ</s>; food (<s>anna</s>) is <s>Sāvitrī</s>. For wherever there is breath, there is food; wherever there is food, there is breath. These two are the sources, one pair. The <s>Vedas</s> indeed are <s>Savitṛ</s>; the metres (<s>chandas</s>) are <s>Sāvitrī</s>. For wherever there are the <s>Vedas</s>, there are the metres; wherever there are the metres, there are the <s>Vedas</s>. These two are the sources, one pair. The sacrifice (<s>yajña</s>) indeed is <s>Savitṛ</s>; the <s>dakṣiṇās</s> (ritual fees) are <s>Sāvitrī</s>. For wherever there is the sacrifice, there are the <s>dakṣiṇās</s>; wherever there are the <s>dakṣiṇās</s>, there is the sacrifice.

body.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s> (the Absolute) indeed beheld this — prosperity (<s>śrī</s>), foundation (<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>), and abode (<s>āyatana</s>). [It resolved:] 'Perform <s>tapas</s>!' If that were maintained in the vow (<s>vrata</s>), it would be established in truth (<s>satya</s>). That <s>Savitṛ</s>, having created the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> through <s>Sāvitrī</s>, placed the <s>Sāvitrī</s> over it. 'That choicest of <s>Savitṛ</s>' — this is the first foot (<s>pāda</s>) of the <s>Sāvitrī</s>. Upon the earth he placed the <s>Ṛc</s> (verse); upon the <s>Ṛc</s>, <s>Agni</s> (fire); upon <s>Agni</s>, prosperity; upon prosperity, woman; upon woman, the pair (<s>mithuna</s>); upon the pair, offspring (<s>prajā</s>); upon offspring, ritual action (<s>karman</s>); upon action, <s>tapas</s> (austerity); upon <s>tapas</s>, truth (<s>satya</s>); upon truth, <s>Brahman</s>;

(GBr_1,1.37k) vācā vedā abhipannā grasitāḥ parāmṛṣṭāḥ_

children.text: (GBr_1,1.37l) vedair yajño 'bhipanno grasitaḥ parāmṛṣṭas [ed. parimṛṣṭas]
children.translated_text: By the <s>Vedas</s>, the sacrifice (<s>yajña</s>) is encompassed, seized, and grasped.

children.text: (GBr_1,1.37m) tāni ha vā etāni dvādaśamahābhūtāny evaṃvidi pratiṣṭhitāni
children.translated_text: These indeed are the twelve great elements (<s>mahābhūtas</s>), established in one who knows thus.

children.text: (GBr_1,1.37n) teṣāṃ yajña eva parārdhyaḥ || 37 ||
children.translated_text: Among them, the sacrifice indeed is the highest. [37]

body.translated_text: By such a knowing <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> indeed — <s>Brahman</s> is encompassed, seized, and grasped. By <s>Brahman</s>, space (<s>ākāśa</s>) is encompassed, seized, and grasped. By space, <s>Vāyu</s> (wind) is encompassed, seized, and grasped. By wind, light (<s>jyotis</s>) is encompassed, seized, and grasped. By light, the waters (<s>āpas</s>) are encompassed, seized, and grasped. By the waters, the earth (<s>bhūmi</s>) is encompassed, seized, and grasped. By earth, food (<s>anna</s>) is encompassed, seized, and grasped. By food, <s>prāṇa</s> (breath) is encompassed, seized, and grasped. By breath, mind (<s>manas</s>) is encompassed, seized, and grasped. By mind, speech (<s>vāc</s>) is encompassed, seized, and grasped. By speech, the <s>Vedas</s> are encompassed, seized, and grasped.

(GBr_1,1.38n) yo ha vā evaṃvit sa brahmavit

children.text: (GBr_1,1.38o) puṇyāṃ ca kīrtiṃ labhate surabhīṃś ca gandhān_
children.translated_text: (GBr 1,1.38o) He obtains meritorious fame and fragrant scents.

children.text: (GBr_1,1.38p) so 'pahatapāpmā_
children.translated_text: (GBr 1,1.38p) He becomes freed from evil.

children.text: (GBr_1,1.38q) anantāṃ śriyam aśnute ya evaṃ veda yaś caivaṃvidvān evam etāṃ vedānāṃ mātaraṃ sāvitrīṃ saṃpadam upaniṣadam upāsta iti brāhmaṇam || 38 ||
children.translated_text: (GBr 1,1.38q) He attains infinite prosperity — whoever knows thus, and whoever, knowing thus, meditates upon this <s>Sāvitrī</s> as the fulfillment, the <s>Upaniṣad</s> (secret teaching), the mother of the <s>Vedas</s> — thus is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [teaching]. [38]

body.translated_text:
(GBr 1,1.38a) Those who do not truly know think of this: 'We know it' — [but they speak] untruly, being ignorant.
(GBr 1,1.38b) This sacrifice is established in the <s>Vedas</s>.
(GBr 1,1.38c) The <s>Vedas</s> are established in speech.
(GBr 1,1.38d) Speech is established in the mind.
(GBr 1,1.38e) The mind is established in <s>prāṇa</s> (breath).
(GBr 1,1.38f) <s>Prāṇa</s> is established in food.
(GBr 1,1.38g) Food is established in the earth.
(GBr 1,1.38h) The earth is established in the waters.
(GBr 1,1.38i) The waters are established in light.
(GBr 1,1.38j) Light is established in wind.
(GBr 1,1.38k) Wind is established in space.
(GBr 1,1.38l) Space is established in <s>Brahman</s>.
(GBr 1,1.38m) <s>Brahman</s> is established in the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, the knower of <s>Brahman</s>.
(GBr 1,1.38n) He who knows thus — he is the knower of <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: (GBr_1,1.39cc) sa yat sarvāṇi khāni sarvaṃ deham āpyāyayati yac cānyadātāraṃ mantrakāryaṃ yajñe skandati sarvaṃ tenāsminnavarunddhe
children.translated_text: (GBr 1,1.39cc) When he nourishes all openings and the entire body, and whatever other <s>mantra</s>-duty for the giver falls short in the sacrifice, all that he secures therein.

children.text: (GBr_1,1.39dd) sa yad oṃpūrvān mantrān prayuṅkta ā sarvamedhād ete kratava eta evāsya sarveṣu lokeṣu sarveṣu deveṣu sarveṣu vedeṣu sarveṣu bhūteṣu sarveṣu sattveṣu kāmacāraḥ kāmavimocanaṃ bhavaty ardhe ca na pramīyate ya evaṃ veda
children.translated_text: (GBr 1,1.39dd) When he employs <s>mantras</s> preceded by <s>Oṃ</s>, up to the <s>Sarvamedha</s> (all-sacrifice) — these are the rites; this indeed is his free movement in all worlds, among all gods, in all <s>Vedas</s>, among all beings, among all creatures; it becomes the release of desires, and he does not perish midway — whoever knows thus.

children.text: (GBr_1,1.39ee) tad apy etad ṛcoktam āpo bhṛgvaṅgiro rūpam āpo bhṛgvaṅgiromayaṃ sarvam āpomayaṃ bhūtaṃ sarvaṃ bhṛgvaṅgiromayam antaraite trayo vedā bhṛgūn aṅgiraso 'nugāḥ ||
children.translated_text: (GBr 1,1.39ee) And this too is declared by the <s>Ṛk</s> verse: 'Waters are the form of <s>Bhṛgu-Aṅgiras</s>, everything made of waters is made of <s>Bhṛgu-Aṅgiras</s>; within these three <s>Vedas</s>, the <s>Bhṛgus</s> are followed by the <s>Aṅgirases</s>.'

body.translated_text:
(GBr 1,1.39a) 'The waters generating the embryo' [PS 4.1.8] — thus [the verse begins].
(GBr 1,1.39b) The embryo of the waters is the <s>puruṣa</s> (person).
(GBr 1,1.39c) He is the sacrifice.
(GBr 1,1.39d) The sacrifice, being led forth by the waters, extends eastward.
(GBr 1,1.39e) Therefore one brings the sipping water (<s>ācamanīya</s>) first.
(GBr 1,1.39f) When he sips, he sips three times.
(GBr 1,1.39g) He purifies himself twice.
(GBr 1,1.39h) Having descended upon life, he drives away evil.
(GBr 1,1.39i) Having approached, having extracted with the <s>Yajus</s>, having employed the <s>mantras</s>, having concluded, having joined the eastern branches, in the thumbless palms [he says]: 'You are <s>amṛta</s> (immortality), you are the spreading of <s>amṛta</s>, for immortality I spread you' — [thus] in the palms.

body.text:
(GBr_1,1.39ff) apāṃ puṣpaṃ mūrtir ākāśaṃ pavitram uttamam iti_
(GBr_1,1.39gg) ācamyābhyukṣyātmānam anumantrayata <indra jīva [PS 20.43.1, ŚS 19.70.1]>_iti brāhmaṇaṃ || 39 ||
body.translated_text:
(GBr 1,1.39ff) 'The flower of the waters is the visible form, space is the supreme purifier' — thus.
(GBr 1,1.39gg) Having sipped and having sprinkled himself, he invokes upon himself: '<s>Indra</s>, live!' [PS 20.43.1, ŚS 19.70.1] — thus is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [teaching]. [39]

body.text: (GBr_1,1.39col) ity atharvavede gopathabrāhmaṇapūrvabhāge prathamaḥ prapāṭhakaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus in the <s>Atharvaveda</s>, in the <s>Gopatha Brāhmaṇa</s>, the first section (<s>prapāṭhaka</s>) of the former part (<s>pūrvabhāga</s>) [ends].

children.translated_text: (GBr 1,2.1e) This is the consecrated one, this is the one with a long beard; standing in the place of the teacher, he is praised as 'the teacher.'

children.text: (GBr_1,2.1f) vaidyutasthāne tiṣṭhan vāyur iti stūyate dyausthāne tiṣṭhann āditya iti stūyate
children.translated_text: (GBr 1,2.1f) Standing in the place of lightning, he is praised as '<s>Vāyu</s>'; standing in the place of heaven, he is praised as '<s>Āditya</s>.'

children.text: (GBr_1,2.1g) tad apy etad ṛcoktaṃ <brahmacārīṣṇan [ŚS 11.3.1, PS 16.153.1]>_iti brāhmaṇam || 1 ||
children.translated_text: (GBr 1,2.1g) This too is declared by the <s>Ṛk</s> verse: 'The <s>brahmacārin</s> moves...' [ŚS 11.3.1, PS 16.153.1] — thus is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [teaching]. [1]

body.translated_text:
(GBr 1,2.1a) <s>Oṃ</s> — 'The <s>brahmacārin</s> (Vedic student) moves through both worlds' [ŚS 11.3.1a, PS 16.153.1a] — this refers to the teacher.
(GBr 1,2.1b) 'In him the gods become of one mind' [ŚS 11.3.1, PS 16.153.1b] — this refers to <s>Vāyu</s>.
(GBr 1,2.1c) 'He goes at once from the former to the further ocean' [ŚS 11.3.6, PS 16.153.6] — this refers to <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun).
(GBr 1,2.1d) The consecrated one (<s>dīkṣita</s>) has a long beard.

children.text: (GBr_1,2.2z) athaitad brahmacāriṇaḥ puṇyo gandho ya oṣadhivanaspatīnāṃ tāsāṃ puṇyaṃ gandhaṃ pracchidya nopajighret
children.translated_text: (GBr 1,2.2z) Now this fragrant scent of the <s>brahmacārin</s> which is in the plants and trees — having cut their fragrant scent, one should not smell [them].

children.text: (GBr_1,2.2aa) tena taṃ puṇyaṃ gandham avarunddhe yo 'syauṣadhivanasvapatiṣu bhavati
children.translated_text: (GBr 1,2.2aa) Thereby he secures that fragrant scent of his which resides in the plants and trees.

children.text: (GBr_1,2.2bb) sa ha snātaḥ puṇyagandhir bhavati || 2 ||
children.translated_text: (GBr 1,2.2bb) He, when bathed [at the completion of studentship], becomes one of fragrant scent. [2]

body.translated_text:
(GBr 1,2.2a) A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, when born, is born with seven faculties: <s>brahmavarcasa</s> (Vedic splendor), fame, sleep, anger, boasting, beauty, and fragrant scent as the seventh.
(GBr 1,2.2b) These indeed depart from him when he enters upon <s>brahmacarya</s> (Vedic studentship).
(GBr 1,2.2c) His <s>brahmavarcasa</s> goes to the deer.
(GBr 1,2.2d) His fame [goes] to the teacher.
(GBr 1,2.2e) His sleep [goes] to the python.
(GBr 1,2.2f) His anger [goes] to the boar.
(GBr 1,2.2g) His boasting [goes] to the waters.
(GBr 1,2.2h) His beauty [goes] to the maiden.
(GBr 1,2.2i) His fragrant scent [goes] to the plants and trees.
(GBr 1,2.2j) When he wears deer skins, thereby

body.text:
(GBr_1,2.3a) sa vā eṣa upayaṃś caturdhopaity agniṃ pādenācāryaṃ pādena grāmaṃ pādena mṛtyuṃ pādena
(GBr_1,2.3b) sa yad aharahaḥ samidha āhṛtya sāyaṃprātar agniṃ paricaret tena taṃ pādam avarunddhe yo 'syāgnau bhavati

children.text: (GBr_1,2.3c) sa yad aharahar ācāryāya karma karoti tena taṃ pādam avarunddhe yo 'syācārye bhavati
children.translated_text: (GBr 1,2.3c) When day after day he performs work for the teacher, thereby he secures that quarter of his which resides in the teacher.

children.text: (GBr_1,2.3d) sa yad aharahar grāmaṃ praviśya bhikṣām eva parīpsati na maithunaṃ tena taṃ pādam avarunddhe yo 'sya grāme bhavati
children.translated_text: (GBr 1,2.3d) When day after day, entering the village, he seeks only alms and not sexual intercourse, thereby he secures that quarter of his which resides in the village.

children.text: (GBr_1,2.3e) sa yat kruddho vācā na kaṃ cana hinasti puruṣātpuruṣāt pāpīyān iva manyamānas tena taṃ pādam avarunddhe yo 'sya mṛtyau bhavati || 3 ||
children.translated_text: (GBr 1,2.3e) When, though angry, he does not hurt anyone by speech, considering himself worse than every other person, thereby he secures that quarter of his which resides in death. [3]

body.translated_text:
(GBr 1,2.3a) This one indeed, when approaching [the teacher], approaches in four parts: with one quarter to the fire, with one quarter to the teacher, with one quarter to the village, and with one quarter to death.
(GBr 1,2.3b) When day after day, having brought fuel, he tends the fire morning and evening, thereby he secures that quarter of his which resides in the fire.

body.text:

body.translated_text:
(GBr 1,2.4a) Five fires are indeed placed in this <s>brahmacārin</s>.
(GBr 1,2.4b) Two separately in his hands, one in his mouth, one in his heart, and the fifth in his generative organ.
(GBr 1,2.4c) When with the right hand he does not touch a woman, thereby day after day he secures the world of those who maintain sacrificial fires (<s>yājins</s>).
(GBr 1,2.4d) With the left hand — the world of wandering ascetics (<s>pravrājins</s>).
(GBr 1,2.4e) With the mouth — the world of those who tend the sacred fire (<s>agnipraṣkandins</s>).
(GBr 1,2.4f) With the heart — the world of heroes.
(GBr 1,2.4g) With the generative organ — the world of householders (<s>gṛhamedhin</s>s).
(GBr 1,2.4h) If with these he approaches a woman, he becomes as one without fire.
(GBr 1,2.4i) When day after day for the teacher in the household he

children.translated_text: To him [<s>Dantāvala</s>], he [<s>Janamejaya</s>] gave two bulls and a thousand [cows] as fee.

children.text: (GBr_1,2.5z) apy apakīrtitam ācāryo brahmacārīty eka āhur ākāśam adhidaivatam
children.translated_text: It has also been declared: some say that 'the teacher is the <s>brahmacārin</s> (celibate student)' — [with] space as the presiding deity.

children.text: (GBr_1,2.5aa) athādhyātmaṃ brāhmaṇo vratavāṃś caraṇavān brahmacārī || 5 ||
children.translated_text: And in the spiritual (<s>adhyātma</s>) sense, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who observes vows and has [proper] conduct is a <s>brahmacārin</s>.

body.translated_text: <s>Janamejaya</s>, son of <s>Parīkṣit</s>, while about to go hunting, sat down near two swans to study. The two said to him; <s>Janamejaya</s>, son of <s>Parīkṣit</s>, came [to them]. He said: 'Salutation to you, Blessed Ones. Who are the Blessed Ones?' The two said: 'We are the <s>Dakṣiṇāgni</s> (southern fire) and the <s>Āhavanīya</s> (offertorial fire).' He said: 'Salutation to you, Blessed Ones. Let that be told.' 'Let us rest here.' 'But do the <s>Devas</s> not delight [in rest]? Indeed, the <s>Devas</s> do delight. And from a single resting place, the <s>Devas</s> proceed to [their] pleasure garden.' He said: 'Salutation to you, Blessed Ones. What is meritorious (<s>puṇya</s>)?' '<s>Brahmacarya</s> (celibate studentship).' 'What is worldly (<s>laukya</s>)?' '<s>Brahmacarya</s> indeed.' 'Who knows that?' '<s>Dantāvala Dhaumra</s>.' Then <s>Dantāvala Dhaumra</s>, in due time, came to <s>Janamejaya</s> the son of <s>Parīkṣit</s>. [Janamejaya] rose and himself placed a seat for him. Having clasped [his feet], he asked: 'Teach me, sir. What is meritorious?' '<s>Brahmacarya</s>.' 'What is worldly?' '<s>Brahmacarya</s> indeed.' He taught him this: forty-eight years is the complete <s>brahmacarya</s> for all <s>Vedas</s>. Distributing that fourfold among the <s>Vedas</s>, twelve years of <s>brahmacarya</s> [for each], and twelve years is the minimum. Even after the ritual bath (<s>snāna</s>, completing studentship), one should continue to practice as much as one is able thereafter.

children.translated_text: Therefore the housewife should give alms to the <s>brahmacārin</s> daily, [thinking:] 'Let me not lose the wealth of meritorious deeds, <s>iṣṭāpūrta</s>, and good fortune.'

children.text: (GBr_1,2.6n) saptamīṃ nātinayet saptamīm atinayan na brahmacārī bhavati
children.translated_text: He should not let the seventh day pass [without begging]; one who lets the seventh day pass is not a <s>brahmacārin</s>.

children.text: (GBr_1,2.6o) samidbhaikṣe saptarātram acaritavān brahmacārī punarupaneyo bhavati || 6 ||
children.translated_text: A <s>brahmacārin</s> who has not performed the fuel-gathering and alms-begging for seven nights must undergo initiation (<s>upanayana</s>) again.

body.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s> (the Absolute) indeed gave over creatures to Death (<s>Mṛtyu</s>). Only the <s>brahmacārin</s> he did not give over. He [Death] said: 'Let me have a share in this one.' 'What [share]?' 'Whatever night he passes without having brought fuel (<s>samidh</s>) — let that [night] be withheld from his lifespan.' Therefore the <s>brahmacārin</s> should bring fuel daily and tend the fire morning and evening. He should not place [fuel] on top [carelessly]; rather he should place it properly. If he were to place [fuel] on top, <s>Parjanya</s> (the rain-god) would become a rain-cloud on that day. The <s>Devas</s> said: 'This <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> will indeed practice <s>brahmacarya</s>. Tell the householder to give him alms (<s>bhikṣā</s>). Tell him, he is a frequent visitor; [tell] the housewife.' 'What would she lose by not giving?' 'She would lose the wealth of meritorious deeds, <s>iṣṭāpūrta</s> (merit from sacrifices and charitable works), and good fortune.'

children.translated_text: If he spits, he spits right in the middle of himself.

children.text: (GBr_1,2.7g) sa cen niṣṭhīved <divo nu mām [ŚS 6.124.1, PS 19.40.4, VaitS 12.7]> <yad atrāpi madhor ahaṃ [PS 20.38.6, VaitS 12.8]> <yad atrāpi rasasya me [PS 20.27.8, VaitS 12.9]>_ity ātmānam anumantrayate
children.translated_text: If he must spit, he should recite to himself [the mantras]: '<s>Divo nu mām</s>' (From heaven, me...), '<s>Yad atrāpi madhor aham</s>' (Whatever sweetness of mine here too...), '<s>Yad atrāpi rasasya me</s>' (Whatever essence of mine here too...).

children.text: (GBr_1,2.7h) <yad atrāpi madhor ahaṃ niraṣṭhaviṣam asmṛtam agniś ca tat savitā ca punar me jaṭhare dhattāṃ [PS 20.38.6, VaitS 12.8]> || <yad atrāpi rasasya me parāpapātāsmṛtaṃ tad ihopahvayāmahe tan ma āpyāyatāṃ punaḥ [PS 20.27.8]>_iti
children.translated_text: '<s>Yad atrāpi madhor ahaṃ niraṣṭhaviṣam asmṛtam agniś ca tat savitā ca punar me jaṭhare dhattām</s>' (Whatever sweetness of mine that has been spat out and forgotten here — may <s>Agni</s> and <s>Savitṛ</s> place that back in my belly). '<s>Yad atrāpi rasasya me parāpapātāsmṛtaṃ tad ihopahvayāmahe tan ma āpyāyatāṃ punaḥ</s>' (Whatever essence of mine has fallen away here unremembered — that we call back hither; may it nourish me again).

(GBr_1,2.7i) na śmaśānam ātiṣṭhet
(GBr_1,2.7j) sa ced abhitiṣṭhed udakaṃ haste kṛtvā <yadīd amṛtukāmyety [PS 20.54.9]> abhimantrya japant samprokṣya parikrāmet
(GBr_1,2.7k) samayāyoparivrajed

children.translated_text: He should not stand upon a cremation ground. But if he must stand there, having taken water in hand, having consecrated it with [the mantra] '<s>Yadīd amṛtukāmya</s>' (If desiring deathlessness) and reciting [it], he should sprinkle [himself] and circumambulate. He should walk over [the cremation ground] by the appointed [path]. '<s>Yadīd amṛtukāmyāghaṃ ripram upeyima; andhaḥ śloṇa iva hīyatāṃ mā no 'nvāgād aghaṃ yataḥ</s>' (If, desiring deathlessness, we should approach evil and filth — let it be left behind like a blind and lame [man]; let not evil follow us from that place). Now, the <s>brahmacārin</s> is indeed the distilled essence (<s>pariṣūta</s>) of the <s>Devas</s>. This too is stated in the <s>Ṛc</s>: 'This is the distilled essence of the <s>Devas</s>, unascended, it moves shining; in it are all animals, there the sacrifices, in it the food together with the deities' — thus is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [teaching].

body.translated_text: He should not sleep on a raised bed; he should not sing; he should not dance; he should not run; he should not spit. If he sleeps on a raised bed, fires break out frequently. If he sings, cries of lamentation ring out frequently. If he dances, corpses are frequently carried out. If he runs, the subjects [of the realm] fall asleep [i.e., die] frequently.

children.text: (GBr_1,2.8q) brāhmāṇyaṣṭācatvāriṃśad varṣasahasrāṇi salilasya pṛṣṭhe śivo 'bhyatapat
children.translated_text: For <s>Brāhmic</s> forty-eight thousand years, <s>Śiva</s> practiced austerity on the surface of the waters.

children.text: (GBr_1,2.8r) tasmāt taptāt tapaso bhūya evābhyatapat
children.translated_text: From that austerity performed, he performed yet further austerity.

children.text: (GBr_1,2.8s) tad apy etā ṛco 'bhivadanti prāṇāpānau janayann iti brāhmaṇam || 8 ||
children.translated_text: This too the <s>Ṛc</s> verses declare: 'Generating <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>' — thus is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [teaching].

body.translated_text: 'Generating <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>' — in the mouth of the conch, the son of the great sage <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> created this speech: 'May cold and heat become manifest here.' Thus that continues perpetually. Now, in the middle of the <s>Vipāś</s> [river], the rock called <s>Vasiṣṭha-śilā</s> is the first hermitage. The second is <s>Kṛṣṇa-śilā</s>. There <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> practiced austerity (<s>tapas</s>). <s>Viśvāmitra</s> and <s>Jamadagni</s> practice austerity at <s>Jāmadagneya</s>. <s>Gautama</s> and <s>Bharadvāja</s> practice austerity at <s>Siṃhau Prabhave</s>. <s>Guṅgu</s> practices austerity at <s>Guṅguvāsa</s>. A <s>Ṛṣi</s> practiced austerity at <s>Ṛṣidroṇa</s>. <s>Agastya</s> practices austerity at <s>Agastyatīrtha</s>. <s>Atri</s> indeed practices austerity in heaven. The self-born <s>Kaśyapa</s> practiced austerity at <s>Kaśyapatuṅga</s>. [There are] bears, boars, <s>Cilvaṭi</s>, <s>Babruka</s> [snakes], serpents with fangs, having jaws — from the sight of <s>Kaśyapatuṅga</s>, from the path of approach, accomplishment (<s>siddhi</s>) comes. For a <s>Brāhmic</s> thousand years, the <s>brahmacārin</s> stood on one foot in the forest of the <s>Ṛṣis</s>. For a second thousand years, he held a stream of immortal nectar (<s>amṛta</s>) upon his head.

children.text: (GBr_1,2.9vv) vāyur āpaś candramā ity ete bhṛgavaḥ_
children.translated_text: <s>Vāyu</s>, the waters, and the Moon — these are the <s>Bhṛgus</s>.

children.text: (GBr_1,2.9ww) eta idaṃ sarvaṃ samāpyāyayanti_
children.translated_text: These nourish this entire [universe].

children.text: (GBr_1,2.9xx) ekam eva saṃsthaṃ bhavatīti brāhmaṇam || 9 ||
children.translated_text: There is but one foundation — thus is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [teaching].

body.translated_text: 'One-footed, two-footed': <s>Vāyu</s> (Wind) is one-footed; space (<s>ākāśa</s>) is his foot. The Moon (<s>Candramā</s>) is two-footed; the bright and dark fortnights are his two feet. <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun) is three-footed; these worlds are his feet. <s>Agni</s> (Fire) is six-footed; earth, atmosphere, heaven, waters, herbs, and trees — these beings are his feet. Of all of them, the <s>Vedas</s> are the path, the self (<s>ātman</s>), and the foundation — the four branches of <s>Brahman</s>. Moreover, they say six [branches], [including] form (<s>mūrti</s>) and space. The <s>Ṛc</s> is the form. The <s>Yajus</s> is the path. The <s>Sāman</s> is the luminous power. The <s>Bhṛgvaṅgirasa</s> (Atharvaveda) is the creative power (<s>māyā</s>). This <s>Brahman</s> itself is the sacrifice, four-footed, established in two. Of it, the <s>Bhṛgvaṅgirasa</s> constitutes the two foundations. Moreover, they say it is established in one. When the <s>Hotṛ</s> priest performs with the <s>Ṛc</s> maṇḍalas, he nourishes the earth. For <s>Agni</s> moves upon the earth. This too is stated in the <s>Ṛc</s>: 'The earth is fire-clad, with dark knees.' When the <s>Adhvaryu</s> priest performs with the <s>Yajus</s>, he nourishes the atmosphere. In it <s>Vāyu</s> does not rest, nor any particular day. This too is stated in the <s>Ṛc</s>: 'Carried along the paths in the atmosphere, he does not settle on any particular day; the womb of the waters, the first-born of cosmic order — where was he born, whence did he come?' When the <s>Udgātṛ</s> priest performs with the <s>Sāman</s>, he nourishes heaven. For there <s>Āditya</s> moves, shining. This too is stated in the <s>Ṛc</s>: 'The tawny eagle flying high.' When the <s>Brahmā</s> priest performs with the <s>Ṛc</s> divisions, he nourishes the waters. For the Moon moves in the waters. This too is stated in the <s>Ṛc</s>: 'The Moon [moves] within the waters.' The herbs and trees are the divisions of those [waters]. From roots, stems, leaves, flowers, fruits, sprouts, sap, and fragrance, the sacrifice operates. By means of waters, the ritual actions proceed. By means of waters, <s>Soma</s> is pressed. When the <s>Brahmā</s> priest invokes the ritual actions of the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, he thereby gives permission to the waters. For this is his share. Just as one about to eat should first sip water and [sip] water again at the end — just so the sacrifice operates by means of waters.

children.text: (GBr_1,2.10j) tāsāṃ samudram abhipadyamānānāṃ chidyate nāmadheyaṃ samudra ity ācakṣate
children.translated_text: When they reach the ocean, their names are cut off; they are called simply 'the ocean.'

children.text: (GBr_1,2.10k) evam ime sarve vedā nirmitāḥ sakalpāḥ sarahasyāḥ sabrāhmaṇāḥ sopaniṣatkāḥ setihāsāḥ sānvākhyānāḥ sapurāṇāḥ sasvarāḥ sasaṃskārāḥ saniruktāḥ sānuśāsanāḥ sānumārjanāḥ savākovākyās
children.translated_text: Just so, all these <s>Vedas</s> — created together with their <s>Kalpas</s>, with their esoteric doctrines, with their <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, with their <s>Upaniṣads</s>, with their <s>Itihāsas</s>, with their narrative supplements, with their <s>Purāṇas</s>, with their accents, with their ritual preparations, with their etymologies (<s>Nirukta</s>), with their instructions, with their purifications, with their dialogues —

children.text: (GBr_1,2.10l) teṣāṃ yajñam abhipadyamānānāṃ chidyate nāmadheyaṃ yajña ity evācakṣate || 10 ||
children.translated_text: when they reach the sacrifice, their names are cut off; they are called simply 'the sacrifice.'

body.translated_text: <s>Vicārī</s>, the son of <s>Kabandha</s> the <s>Ātharvaṇa</s>, was indeed intelligent, a <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s> (investigator), and learned. He, by his own excessive pride, did not accept human livelihood. His mother said to him: 'These [others] I told about this food — they eat food in these [lands of] <s>Kuru-Pañcāla</s>, <s>Aṅga-Magadha</s>, <s>Kāśi-Kośala</s>, <s>Śālva-Matsya</s>, <s>Savaśa-Uśīnara</s>, and the Northerners. But we, by your very pride, are unfed. O child, seek a conveyance [i.e., patronage].' He came to the <s>Soma</s> sacrifice of King <s>Māndhātṛ Yauvanāśva</s>, the sovereign ruler. Having entered the assembly, he addressed the priests and the sacrificer. 'Now, the rivers that flow eastward, those that flow southward, those that flow westward, and those that flow northward — all these are called by separate names.'

children.text: (GBr_1,2.11o) manasaiva brahmā brahmatvaṃ karoti
children.translated_text: By the mind (<s>manas</s>) alone does the <s>Brahmā</s> priest perform the office of <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: (GBr_1,2.11p) manasā hi tiryak ca diśa ūrdhvaṃ yac ca kiṃ ca manasaiva karoti tad brahma
children.translated_text: For whatever the mind does — sideways, in [all] directions, upward, or whatever — that is <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: (GBr_1,2.11q) te brūmo mana eva brahmā mano brahma mano deva iti || 11 ||
children.translated_text: We say: the mind alone is the <s>Brahmā</s> priest; the mind is <s>Brahman</s>; the mind is the deity. ||11||

body.translated_text:
That which is cut off from the earth is indeed the divine sacrifice-ground (<s>devayajana</s>) — that which does not slope toward the east, that which does not slope toward the north, that which is artificial, that which is uneven.
But this indeed is the divine sacrifice-ground: that which is level, has natural soil, is not scorched, is established, slopes toward the east and north, is even, and appears as if spread out — where one would know the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-hood of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, [saying] 'the <s>Brahmā</s> priest performs the office of <s>Brahman</s>.'
The meters said: 'We do not find [a meter] by which we may go to the higher [world].'
He asked them: 'Knowing what does the <s>Hotṛ</s> (invoking priest) perform the <s>Hautra</s> (invoking function)? Knowing what does the <s>Adhvaryu</s> (offertory priest) perform the <s>Ādhvaryava</s> (offertory function)? Knowing what does the <s>Udgātṛ</s> (chanting priest) perform the <s>Audgātra</s> (chanting function)? Knowing what does the <s>Brahmā</s> (superintending priest) perform the office of <s>Brahman</s>?'
The meters said: 'We do not find [a meter] by which we may go to the higher [world].'
We say: speech (<s>vāc</s>) alone is the <s>Hotṛ</s> that performs the <s>Hautra</s> function.
For the <s>stomas</s> (praise-forms) and the <s>vaṣaṭkāras</s> (sacrificial exclamations) originate from speech.
We say: speech alone is the <s>Hotṛ</s>; speech is <s>Brahman</s>; speech is the deity.
By the in-breath (<s>prāṇa</s>) and the out-breath (<s>apāna</s>) alone does the <s>Adhvaryu</s> perform the <s>Ādhvaryava</s> function.
For beings are led by <s>prāṇa</s>; the sacred waters (<s>praṇītās</s>) are led by <s>prāṇa</s>.
We say: the in-breath and out-breath alone are the <s>Adhvaryu</s>; the in-breath and out-breath are <s>Brahman</s>; the in-breath and out-breath are the deity.
By the eye (<s>cakṣus</s>) alone does the <s>Udgātṛ</s> perform the <s>Audgātra</s> function.
For by the eye these beings see.
Thus the eye alone is the <s>Udgātṛ</s>; the eye is <s>Brahman</s>; the eye is the deity.

children.text: (GBr_1,2.12a) tad yathā ha vā idaṃ yajamānaś ca yājayitāraś ca divaṃ brūyuḥ pṛthivīti pṛthivīṃ vā dyaur iti brūyus tad anyo nānujānāty etām evaṃ nānujānāti yad etad brūyāt_
children.translated_text: Just as if the sacrificer and the officiants were to call heaven 'earth' or the earth 'heaven' — another would not approve of that; even so, one does not approve when this [mis-designation] is spoken.

children.text: (GBr_1,2.12b) atha nu katham iti
children.translated_text: 'Then how [should one speak]?'

children.text: (GBr_1,2.12c) hotety eva hotāraṃ brūyād vāg iti vācaṃ brahmeti brahma deva iti devam adhvaryur ity evādhvaryuṃ brūyāt prāṇāpānāv iti prāṇāpānau brahmeti brahma deva iti devam udgātety evodgātāraṃ brūyāc cakṣur iti cakṣur brahmeti brahma deva iti devaṃ brahmety eva brahmāṇaṃ brūyān mana iti mano brahmeti brahma deva iti devam || 12 ||
children.translated_text: One should address the <s>Hotṛ</s> as '<s>Hotṛ</s>,' speech as 'speech,' <s>Brahman</s> as '<s>Brahman</s>,' the deity as 'deity'; one should address the <s>Adhvaryu</s> as '<s>Adhvaryu</s>,' the in-breath and out-breath as '<s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>,' <s>Brahman</s> as '<s>Brahman</s>,' the deity as 'deity'; one should address the <s>Udgātṛ</s> as '<s>Udgātṛ</s>,' the eye as 'eye,' <s>Brahman</s> as '<s>Brahman</s>,' the deity as 'deity'; one should address the <s>Brahmā</s> as '<s>Brahmā</s>,' the mind as 'mind,' <s>Brahman</s> as '<s>Brahman</s>,' the deity as 'deity.' ||12||

body.translated_text:
Verily, these beings have various teachings.
Those who officiate for one who has not drunk <s>Soma</s>, those who officiate for a liquor-drinker, and those who officiate for a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who has been cut off from the <s>Soma</s>-sacrificers — they approached him in the morning with fuel-sticks in hand [saying]: 'We approach you, sir.'
'For what purpose?'
'Those same questions which you asked us yesterday — please explain those same [questions] to us.'
'So be it.'

children.text: (GBr_1,2.14u) nottarato 'gneḥ paryupasīderann iti brāhmaṇam || 14 ||
children.translated_text: One should not sit to the north of the fire — thus is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [teaching]. ||14||

body.translated_text:
Now, regarding the divine sacrifice-grounds (<s>devayajana</s>).
The self (<s>ātman</s>) is a divine sacrifice-ground.
Faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) is a divine sacrifice-ground.
The priests (<s>ṛtvij</s>) are a divine sacrifice-ground.
The earthly [ground] is a divine sacrifice-ground.
That indeed is the self as divine sacrifice-ground: that while exerting or not exerting, one inhabits the body.
This is the sacrifice.
This is the one who sacrifices.
These are the ones offering to this.
This is the divine sacrifice-ground.
Now this is faith as the divine sacrifice-ground:
Whenever one would establish [the sacred fires],
faith should not abandon him.
That is the divine sacrifice-ground.
Now this is the priests as the divine sacrifice-ground:
Wherever a learned <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> performs [a rite] with a <s>mantra</s> — that is the divine sacrifice-ground.
Now this is the earthly divine sacrifice-ground:
Where waters stand, where they flow, where they carry forth and carry up — that is the divine sacrifice-ground.
