children.text: (GBr_1,2.15cc) uccheṣaṇabhājā vā ādityāḥ_
children.translated_text: The <s>Ādityas</s> are indeed the recipients of remnants (<s>ucchiṣṭa</s>).

children.text: (GBr_1,2.15dd) [yad ucchiṣṭam]_
children.translated_text: [That which is remnant] —

children.text: (GBr_1,2.15ee) yad ucchiṣṭena samidho 'nakti tebhya eva prāvocat tebhya eva procya svargaṃ lokaṃ yāti || 15 ||
children.translated_text: When one anoints the kindling-sticks with the remnant, one has thereby spoken to them; having spoken to them, one goes to the heavenly world. ||15||

body.translated_text:
<s>Aditi</s> indeed, desiring offspring, cooked rice (<s>odana</s>).
From that she ate the remnant.
She conceived.
From that the <s>Ādityas</s> were born.
This rice that is cooked — that indeed is the beginning, that is the undertaking.
The kindling-sticks are a span in length,
for the self (<s>ātman</s>) is measured as equal to <s>Prajāpati</s> by that much.
The sacrificial form of <s>Agni</s> (fire) that is in the <s>Aśvattha</s> (sacred fig tree) — with that it was united.
This is his ghee-form — namely, ghee.
When one anoints the kindling-sticks with ghee, one thereby unites him with both those forms.
When one places [the fire] on an unswept [ground], it is by means of concealment that the deed of valor is performed.
When one places [the fire] on an unswept [ground] — it is by concealment alone.
The year is indeed procreation.
Fire (<s>Agni</s>) is procreation.
This is procreation.
When in the [course of the] year one places a kindling-stick on the fire with a <s>ṛc</s> verse, from procreation itself the procreator causes him to be born.
A person indeed has no [fixed] season of birth.
For he does not know in which season he is born.
Whatever <s>nakṣatra</s> (lunar mansion) is [current] — that he attains.
This rice that is cooked — this is the womb that is being made.
When the kindling-sticks are placed — that is the seed being deposited.
Seed deposited in the year gives birth.
He who, when the year has passed, establishes the [sacred] fire — he establishes one that is [already] born.
[The fires] should be established within twelve nights before [the completion of] the year.
For those [twelve nights] are the image of the year.
Or also within three [nights]; or also within two; or also on the day before — those [rules apply] to one establishing the fire.
The <s>Ādityas</s> indeed went from here to the highest world.
They are the path-guardians. They push back one who desires to sacrifice.

(GBr_1,2.16a) prajāpatir atharvā devaḥ sa tapas taptvaitaṃ cātuḥprāśyaṃ brahmaudanaṃ niramimīta caturlokaṃ caturdevaṃ caturvedaṃ caturhautram iti

(GBr_1,2.16r) yo ha vā etam amantravantaṃ brahmaudanam upeyād apaśirasā ha vā asya yajñam upeto bhavati
(GBr_1,2.16s) tasmān mantravantam eva brahmaudanam upeyān nāmantravantam iti brāhmaṇam || 16 || [ed. brāhmanam]
body.translated_text:
<s>Prajāpati Atharvan</s>, the divine one, having performed austerity, fashioned this <s>brahmaudana</s> (the <s>Brahman</s>-rice offering) to be shared in four portions — comprising the four worlds, four deities, four <s>Vedas</s>, and four priestly functions.
These four are the worlds: earth, atmosphere, heaven, and the waters.
These four are the deities: <s>Agni</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Āditya</s>, and <s>Candramā</s> (the Moon).
These four are the <s>Vedas</s>: the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, the <s>Yajurveda</s>, the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, and the <s>Brahmaveda</s> (<s>Atharvaveda</s>).
These four are the priestly functions: the <s>Hautra</s> (of the <s>Hotṛ</s>), the <s>Ādhvaryava</s> (of the <s>Adhvaryu</s>), the <s>Audgātra</s> (of the <s>Udgātṛ</s>), and the office of <s>Brahman</s>.
And this too is stated in the <s>Ṛc</s> verse: 'Four are his horns, three are his feet, two are his heads, seven are his hands; bound threefold, the bull roars aloud — the great god has entered mortals' [<s>Paippalāda Saṃhitā</s> 8.13.3].
'Four are his horns' — the <s>Vedas</s> are meant by this.
'Three are his feet' — the pressings (<s>savanas</s>) indeed.
'Two are his heads' — the <s>brahmaudana</s> and the <s>Pravargya</s> (hot-milk ritual) indeed.
'Seven are his hands' — the meters (<s>chandas</s>) indeed.
'Bound threefold' — the <s>mantra</s>, the ritual procedure (<s>kalpa</s>), and the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [exegesis].
'The bull roars aloud' — he indeed is the bull; he roars when at sacrifices he recites the <s>śastras</s> (litanies) with <s>ṛc</s> verses, <s>yajus</s> formulas, <s>sāman</s> chants, and <s>brahman</s> spells.
'The great god has entered mortals' — the great god indeed is the sacrifice.
He has entered mortals.
'He who would know the seven slopes' — he refers to the <s>prāṇas</s> (in-breaths).
'He who would know the seven far distances' — he refers to the <s>apānas</s> (out-breaths).
'He who would know the head of the sacrifice' — this indeed is the head of the sacrifice: the <s>brahmaudana</s> that is accompanied by <s>mantras</s>.
He who would approach this <s>brahmaudana</s> without <s>mantras</s> — his sacrifice would be approached headless.
Therefore one should approach the <s>brahmaudana</s> only when accompanied by <s>mantras</s>, not without <s>mantras</s> — thus is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [teaching]. ||16||

children.translated_text: He [<s>Āditya</s>] said to him: 'Choose a boon.'

children.text: (GBr_1,2.17h) sa hovāca dakṣiṇīyā me prajā syād iti
children.translated_text: He [<s>Atri</s>] said: 'Let my progeny be worthy of receiving the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee).'

children.text: (GBr_1,2.17i) tasmād ātreyāya prathamaṃ dakṣiṇā yajñe dīyanta iti brāhmaṇam || 17 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> at a sacrifice is given first to an <s>Ātreya</s> — thus is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [teaching]. ||17||

body.translated_text:
'By what knowledge does one become an <s>Ātreya</s> (descendant of <s>Atri</s>)?'
Darkness indeed seized <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun).
<s>Atri</s> dispelled it.
<s>Atri</s> perceived it.
And this too is stated in the <s>Ṛc</s> verse: '[The Sun] whom <s>Atri</s> led up to heaven from the hearing' [<s>Śaunaka Saṃhitā</s> 13.2.4c, <s>Paippalāda Saṃhitā</s> 18.20.8c].
'<s>Atri</s> established you in heaven — for the <s>Moon</s> to create' [<s>Śaunaka Saṃhitā</s> 13.2.12ab, <s>Paippalāda Saṃhitā</s> 18.21.6ab].

children.translated_text: (GBr 1,2.18jj) When the horse is being led to the fire, the <s>Brahmā</s> priest has the <s>yajamāna</s> (sacrificer) recite, with his hand touching [the horse], five [verses beginning with] '<s>yad akrandaḥ prathamaṃ jāyamānaḥ</s>' [ṚV 1.163.1].

children.translated_text: (GBr 1,2.18kk) The <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> lead him on; the <s>Brahmā</s> priest prepares him.

children.translated_text: (GBr 1,2.18ll) He indeed is the wise, all-knowing <s>Brahmā</s> priest who knows [the lore of] <s>Bhṛṅgi</s> — thus is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [teaching]. [18]

body.translated_text: (GBr 1,2.18a) <s>Prajāpati</s> said to the <s>Vedas</s>: 'Set up the fires.' (GBr 1,2.18b) <s>Vāc</s> (Speech) replied to them: 'The horse indeed is [one] of the materials [for the sacrifice].' (GBr 1,2.18c) They brought him up from the terrible, cruel waters of the lake. (GBr 1,2.18d) <s>Vāc</s> replied to them: 'The horse should be pacified.' (GBr 1,2.18e) 'So be it.' (GBr 1,2.18f) The <s>Ṛgveda</s> came and said: 'I shall pacify the horse.' (GBr 1,2.18g) When it approached [the horse], great fear was produced for it. (GBr 1,2.18h) [The horse] took to this eastern quarter. (GBr 1,2.18i) [The <s>Ṛgveda</s>] said: 'This horse is indeed not pacified.' (GBr 1,2.18j) The <s>Yajurveda</s> came and said: 'I shall pacify the horse.' (GBr 1,2.18k) When it approached [the horse], great fear was produced for it. (GBr 1,2.18l) [The horse] took to this western quarter. (GBr 1,2.18m) [The <s>Yajurveda</s>] said: 'This horse is indeed not pacified.' (GBr 1,2.18n) The <s>Sāmaveda</s> came and said: 'I shall pacify the horse.' (GBr 1,2.18o) 'By what means will you pacify [it]?' (GBr 1,2.18p) 'I have a <s>Sāman</s> called <s>Rathantara</s>, which is not terrible and not cruel.' (GBr 1,2.18q) 'Let the horse be praised with that.' (GBr 1,2.18r) When it too approached, that same great fear was produced. (GBr 1,2.18s) [The horse] took to this northern quarter. (GBr 1,2.18t) [The <s>Sāmaveda</s>] said: 'This horse is indeed not pacified.' (GBr 1,2.18u) <s>Vāc</s> said to them: 'Go to <s>Śaṃyu</s> the <s>Ātharvaṇa</s>.' (GBr 1,2.18v) They approached <s>Śaṃyu</s> the <s>Ātharvaṇa</s> while he was seated and said: 'Salutation to you, Blessed One. May the horse be pacified.' (GBr 1,2.18w) 'So be it.' (GBr 1,2.18x) He indeed addressed the son of <s>Kabandha</s> the <s>Ātharvaṇa</s>, [saying] 'O Wanderer (<s>Vicārin</s>).' (GBr 1,2.18y) An echo answered him: '<s>Bhago</s> (Fortune)!' (GBr 1,2.18z) 'May the horse be pacified.' (GBr 1,2.18aa) 'So be it.' (GBr 1,2.18bb) He indeed prepared pacificatory water, and pacifies with <s>Ātharvaṇī</s> and <s>Āṅgirasī</s> [hymns], with dispelling chants, with mother-name [hymns], and with <s>Vāstoṣpati</s> [hymns]. (GBr 1,2.18cc) From all the pores of that bathed and sprinkled horse, burning coals fell away. (GBr 1,2.18dd) The horse, being pleased, made obeisance. (GBr 1,2.18ee) 'Salutation to <s>Śaṃyu</s> the <s>Ātharvaṇa</s>, who made me fit for the sacrifice.' (GBr 1,2.18ff) 'In the future, there will be other <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> of the lightest [sacrificial] materials. (GBr 1,2.18gg) They shall set up [fires] at the place of <s>Āditya</s> — [using] an ox, a calf, a goat, a <s>Śravaṇa</s>-animal, or a <s>brahmacārin</s>. (GBr 1,2.18hh) This indeed is the place of <s>Āditya</s>, namely the earth. (GBr 1,2.18ii) [The fire] will be set up at that very place.'

body.translated_text: (GBr 1,2.19a) The <s>Devas</s> and the <s>Asuras</s> were in rivalry. (GBr 1,2.19b) The <s>Devas</s> said to <s>Indra</s>: 'Guard this sacrifice of ours while we fight the <s>Asuras</s>.' (GBr 1,2.19c) 'Guard us in such a form by which you cover us most and by which you can protect [us].' (GBr 1,2.19d) He, having become the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, went around and stood before [them] in the east. (GBr 1,2.19e) The <s>Devas</s> said to him: 'Take another form; you do not cover us most in this form, you cannot protect [us] in this.' (GBr 1,2.19f) He, having become the <s>Yajurveda</s>, went around and stood behind [them] in the west. (GBr 1,2.19g) The <s>Devas</s> said to him: 'Take another form; you do not cover us most in this form, you cannot protect [us] in this.' (GBr 1,2.19h) He, having become the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, went around and stood to the north. (GBr 1,2.19i) The <s>Devas</s> said to him: 'Take yet another form; you do not cover us most in this form, you cannot protect [us] in this.' (GBr 1,2.19j) <s>Indra</s>, wearing the turban (<s>uṣṇ��ṣin</s>), having become the <s>Brahmaveda</s> (Atharvaveda), went around and stood to the south. (GBr 1,2.19k) The <s>Devas</s> said to him: 'Take this very form; in this form you cover us most, in this you can protect [us].' (GBr 1,2.19l) Because <s>Indra</s>, wearing the turban, having become the <s>Brahmaveda</s>, went around and stood to the south — that became the <s>Brahmā</s> [priest's office]. (GBr 1,2.19m) That is the <s>Brahmā</s>-hood of the <s>Brahmā</s> priest. (GBr 1,2.19n) This indeed is the form of the <s>Atharvan</s> — that the <s>Brahmā</s> priest wears a turban. (GBr 1,2.19o) The <s>Viśvedevas</s> (All-gods) sat by him on the south. (GBr 1,2.19p) Because the <s>Viśvedevas</s> sat by him on the south, that became the <s>Sadasya</s> (assessor). (GBr 1,2.19q) That is the <s>Sadasya</s>-hood of the <s>Sadasya</s>. (GBr 1,2.19r) Indeed, the power of <s>Bali</s> (offering) is produced by the <s>Sadasya</s>. (GBr 1,2.19s) From the herd of the ailing one, they find a more abundant herd. (GBr 1,2.19t) Terrible indeed is this southern quarter; the others are pacified. (GBr 1,2.19u) That which is praised — the <s>Brahmā</s> priest approves mentally — the <s>Sadasya</s> murmurs the utterance '<s>janat</s>.' (GBr 1,2.19v) He generates himself; having generated, he establishes himself in concealment. (GBr 1,2.19w) The <s>Devas</s> said to him: 'Choose a boon.' (GBr 1,2.19x) 'I choose,' he said. (GBr 1,2.19y) He chose a boon: (GBr 1,2.19z) 'In this very priestly office, purifying me as one who has become <s>Indra</s>, let them stand praising and reciting.' (GBr 1,2.19aa) In that very priestly office, purifying him as one who had become <s>Indra</s>, they stood praising and reciting. (GBr 1,2.19bb) Because in that very priestly office, purifying him as one who had become <s>Indra</s>, they stood praising and reciting — that became the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> (reciter for the <s>Brahmā</s> priest). (GBr 1,2.19cc) That is the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>-hood of the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>. (GBr 1,2.19dd) This indeed is the priestly office of <s>Indra</s>, which is the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsī</s>. (GBr 1,2.19ee) 'Choose a second boon.' (GBr 1,2.19ff) 'I choose,' he said. (GBr 1,2.19gg) He chose a boon: (GBr 1,2.19hh) 'In this very priestly office, purifying me as one who has become <s>Vāyu</s>, let them stand praising and reciting.' (GBr 1,2.19ii) In that very priestly office, purifying him as one who had become <s>Vāyu</s>, they stood praising and reciting. (GBr 1,2.19jj) Because in that very priestly office, purifying him as one who had become <s>Vāyu</s>, they stood praising and reciting — that became the <s>Potṛ</s> (purifier-priest). (GBr 1,2.19kk) That is the <s>Potṛ</s>-hood of the <s>Potṛ</s>. (GBr 1,2.19ll) This indeed is the priestly office of <s>Vāyu</s>, which is the <s>Potrī</s>. (GBr 1,2.19mm) 'Choose a third boon.' (GBr 1,2.19nn) 'I choose,' he said. (GBr 1,2.19oo) He chose a boon: (GBr 1,2.19pp) 'In this very priestly office, kindling me as one who has become <s>Agni</s>, purifying, praising, and reciting — let them stand.' (GBr 1,2.19qq) In that very priestly office, kindling him as one who had become <s>Agni</s>, purifying, praising, and reciting — they stood.

body.translated_text: (GBr 1,2.20a) A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> indeed bore this fire, <s>Agni Vaiśvānara</s>. (GBr 1,2.20b) This <s>Agni Vaiśvānara</s>, while being borne by the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, generates these worlds. (GBr 1,2.20c) Then this <s>Agni Jātavedas</s> considered: 'Accompanied by a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, this <s>Agni Vaiśvānara</s> blazes. (GBr 1,2.20d) Come, let me display the radiance, the power, and the vigor that are in me; perhaps then he would bear me [instead].' (GBr 1,2.20e) He nourished himself and milked forth this milk. (GBr 1,2.20f) Having shown this to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, he offered it into himself. (GBr 1,2.20g) A second time he nourished himself and milked forth this ghee. (GBr 1,2.20h) Having shown this to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, he offered it into himself. (GBr 1,2.20i) A third time he nourished himself and milked forth this entire manifold food. (GBr 1,2.20j) Having shown this to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, he offered it into himself. (GBr 1,2.20k) A fourth time he nourished himself and through this beheld <s>Virāj</s>, the wife of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. (GBr 1,2.20l) He presented her to him. (GBr 1,2.20m) She became his own self and his concealment. (GBr 1,2.20n) Then they cast away this <s>Agni Vaiśvānara</s>; the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> established <s>Agni Jātavedas</s> [in his place]. (GBr 1,2.20o) He said: 'O <s>Agni Jātavedas</s>, set me ablaze and kindle me!' (GBr 1,2.20p) He gave him a twofold name — one not terrible and one not cruel. (GBr 1,2.20q) He became a horse. (GBr 1,2.20r) Therefore a horse carries a chariot by its harness, not a rider on its back. (GBr 1,2.20s) He came to the <s>Devas</s>. (GBr 1,2.20t) He stood before the <s>Devas</s>.

children.translated_text: Therefore a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should neither sing nor dance, nor should he be one seized by <s>āglā</s> (calamity).

children.text: (GBr_1,2.21yy) tasmād brāhmyaṃ pūrvaṃ havir aparaṃ prājāpatyaṃ

body.translated_text: "They call you <s>Agni</s> <s>Vaiśvānara</s> (the fire belonging to all men); burning your dwellings you departed. Tell us on behalf of the gods, may we not be harmed, O yours" — thus [PS 1.95.3]. He consecrates him (the horse) with these five <s>ṛc</s> verses: "When you neighed at first being born" [ṚV 1.163.1] — thus. He (the horse) did not become pacified. Therefore the horse is the most voracious among animals, for he is <s>Vaiśvānara</s> (all-consuming fire). Therefore one gives a horse marked with fire to the <s>Brahman</s> priest, for it was given to the <s>Brahman</s> priest. He pressed out its essence (<s>rasa</s>). That became the essence. This indeed is the essence. That which is the essence, they call it "chariot" (<s>ratha</s>) by an indirect name, for the gods are fond of the indirect and averse to the direct. It (the chariot) went to the gods. It stood over the gods. Therefore the gods were afraid. They gave it to the <s>Brahman</s> priest. He offered into it with this verse and a ghee oblation (<s>ājyāhuti</s>). Having offered into the chariot with "The strength of <s>Indra</s>, the vanguard of the <s>Maruts</s>" [ŚS 6.125.3], he mounted it with this verse: "O lord of the forest, may you be firm-limbed" [ŚS 6.125.1]. Therefore one gives the chariot of the <s>āgnyādheya</s> (fire-establishment rite) to the <s>Brahman</s> priest, for it was given to the <s>Brahman</s> priest. The carpenters fashioned its foremost body as the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (ritual gift). He perceived it in five forms: in the <s>ṛc</s> (verse), <s>yajus</s> (formula), <s>sāman</s> (chant), the peaceful, and the terrible. Of these he gave two to the <s>Brahman</s> priest: speech (<s>vāc</s>) and light (<s>jyotis</s>). Speech indeed is the cow; light is gold. Therefore one gives to the <s>Brahman</s> priest a <s>cātuḥprāśya</s> (four-meal-yielding) cow of the <s>āgnyādheya</s>, for it was given to the <s>Brahman</s> priest. When the animals are being pacified, they lose their sight. That sight he places in himself. That which is sight is gold (<s>hiraṇya</s>). Therefore one gives the gold of the <s>āgnyādheya</s> to the <s>Brahman</s> priest, for it was given to the <s>Brahman</s> priest. He placed it in himself. With that he blazed forth. What he did not place (in himself), that became <s>āglā</s> (firebrand/calamity). Having become <s>āglā</s>, it entered the ocean. It burned the ocean. Therefore the ocean is difficult to swallow, for it was burned by <s>Vaiśvānara</s>. It rose up over the earth. It burned through the earth. It went to the gods. It harassed the gods. The gods ran to the <s>Brahman</s> priest. He neither sang nor danced. This is that <s>āglā</s>. This is called <s>kāruvidā</s> by name. That which is struck by <s>āglā</s>, they call it <s>āglāgṛdha</s> (seized by calamity) by an indirect name, for the gods are fond of the indirect and averse to the direct. A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who sings or dances, him they call <s>āglāgṛdha</s>.

children.translated_text: Thus this <s>Sāṃtapana</s> fire, the foremost, being satisfied, satisfies all that are satisfied — thus ends the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> passage. [22]

body.translated_text: Now the <s>Atharvans</s> and the <s>Aṅgirases</s>, having the vision of <s>Bhṛgu</s>, perceived that <s>Brahman</s>. They knew: "We indeed are all this, namely the <s>Bhṛgvaṅgirases</s>." Those gods offered the oblation belonging to <s>Brahman</s> into the <s>Sāṃtapana</s> (scorching) fire. That indeed is the oblation belonging to <s>Brahman</s> which is offered into the <s>Sāṃtapana</s> fire. This <s>Sāṃtapana</s> fire is indeed the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. The gods shared in its nourishing power (<s>ūrja</s>); the <s>Pitṛs</s> (ancestors), being well-disposed, shared in the <s>svadhā</s> (oblation to ancestors); the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> attained the heavenly world through faith (<s>śraddhā</s>). By that, the <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages) press the <s>Soma</s>; women perform it internally; those who are outside perform it in both ways. If at the sacrifice the oblation belonging to <s>Brahman</s> were not offered, humans born from the offering to <s>Prajāpati</s> would be crooked. "Hear, O those worlds" — for he (the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>) is the father of the <s>Āhavanīya</s>, <s>Gārhapatya</s>, and <s>Dakṣiṇāgni</s> fires — he who offers the <s>Agnihotra</s>. The gods rejoice in their dear abode. Among them this <s>Sāṃtapana</s> fire is the foremost. When the speech of this one is satisfied, <s>Agni</s> is satisfied. When the breath (<s>prāṇa</s>) is satisfied, <s>Vāyu</s> is satisfied. When the eye is satisfied, <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun) is satisfied. When the mind is satisfied, <s>Candramās</s> (the Moon) is satisfied. When the ear is satisfied, the directions and intermediate directions are satisfied. When the fluids are satisfied, the waters are satisfied.

(GBr_1,2.23d) tad yathā kumbhe loṣṭaḥ prakṣipto naiva śaucārthāya kalpate naiva śasyaṃ nirvartayaty evam evāyaṃ brāhmaṇo 'nagnikas tasya brāhmaṇasyānagnikasya naiva daivaṃ dadyān na pitryaṃ na cāsya svādhyāyāśiṣo na yajñāśiṣaḥ svargaṃgamā bhavanti
(GBr_1,2.23e) tad apy etad ṛcoktam <agniṃ dūtaṃ vṛṇīmahe hotāraṃ viśvavedasam | asya yajñasya sukratum [ŚS 20.101.1, ṚV 1.12.1]> iti brāhmaṇam || 23 ||
body.translated_text: "O <s>Sāṃtapana</s>, this is the oblation" — thus. This indeed is the <s>Sāṃtapana</s> fire, namely the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> for whom the rites of <s>garbhādhāna</s> (conception), <s>puṃsavana</s> (male-producing rite), <s>sīmantonnayana</s> (parting of the hair), <s>jātakarma</s> (birth rite), <s>nāmakaraṇa</s> (naming ceremony), <s>niṣkramaṇa</s> (first outing), <s>annaprāśana</s> (first feeding), <s>godāna</s> (cow-gift/shaving), <s>cūḍākaraṇa</s> (tonsure), <s>upanayana</s> (initiation), <s>aplavana</s> (ritual bath), <s>agnihotra</s> (fire oblation), <s>vratacaryā</s> (observance of vows), and so forth have been performed — he is the <s>Sāṃtapana</s>. Now he who is without fire (<s>anagnika</s>), he is a lump of clay in a pot. Just as a lump of clay thrown into a pot is useful neither for cleansing nor for producing grain, even so is this <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who is without fire; to such a fireless <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> one should give neither divine offerings nor ancestral offerings, nor do his <s>svādhyāya</s> (self-study) blessings or sacrifice blessings lead to heaven. Moreover, this is declared by the <s>ṛc</s> verse: "We choose <s>Agni</s> as our messenger, the <s>Hotṛ</s> priest, the all-knowing, the wise one of this sacrifice" [ŚS 20.101.1, ṚV 1.12.1] — thus ends the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> passage. [23]

body.translated_text: Then <s>Prajāpati</s>, about to perform the <s>Soma</s> sacrifice, said to the <s>Vedas</s>: "Whom shall I choose as your <s>Hotṛ</s> (invoking priest)? Whom as <s>Adhvaryu</s> (officiating priest)? Whom as <s>Udgātṛ</s> (chanting priest)? Whom as <s>Brahman</s> (supervising priest)?" They replied: "Choose one who knows the <s>Ṛgveda</s> as <s>Hotṛ</s>, one who knows the <s>Yajurveda</s> as <s>Adhvaryu</s>, one who knows the <s>Sāmaveda</s> as <s>Udgātṛ</s>, and one who knows the <s>Atharvāṅgirasa</s> as <s>Brahman</s>." Thus his sacrifice, established in the four worlds, in the four gods, in the four <s>Vedas</s>, in the four priestly offices (<s>hotrā</s>), stands firm as a four-footed sacrifice. He becomes established with progeny and cattle, he who knows thus. Therefore choose one who knows the <s>Ṛgveda</s> as <s>Hotṛ</s>, for he knows the <s>hautra</s> (art of invoking). <s>Agni</s> indeed is the <s>Hotṛ</s>. The earth is the abode of the <s>ṛc</s> verses. <s>Agni</s> is the deity, <s>Gāyatra</s> is the meter, <s>Bhūḥ</s> is the luminous call. Therefore choose him as <s>Hotṛ</s> — for the conquest of this world, for the complete conquest of this world, for the thorough conquest of this world, for the securing of this world, for the increase of this world, for the prosperity of this world, for the elevation of this world, for the pervading of this world, for the attainment of this world, for the completion of this world. But if one does not choose a <s>Hotṛ</s> who knows thus, then their sacrifice is diminished from the east. Choose one who knows the <s>Yajurveda</s> as <s>Adhvaryu</s>, for he knows the <s>ādhvaryava</s> (art of officiating). <s>Vāyu</s> indeed is the <s>Adhvaryu</s>. The atmosphere (<s>antarikṣa</s>) is the abode of the <s>yajus</s> formulas. <s>Vāyu</s> is the deity, <s>Traiṣṭubha</s> is the meter, <s>Bhuvaḥ</s> is the luminous call. Therefore choose him as <s>Adhvaryu</s> — for this world, and so on. But if one does not choose an <s>Adhvaryu</s> who knows thus, then their sacrifice is diminished from the west. Choose one who knows the <s>Sāmaveda</s> as <s>Udgātṛ</s>, for he knows the <s>audgātra</s> (art of chanting). <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun) indeed is the <s>Udgātṛ</s>. Heaven (<s>Dyaus</s>) is the abode of the <s>sāman</s> chants. <s>Āditya</s> is the deity, <s>Jāgata</s> is the meter, <s>Svaḥ</s> is the luminous call. Therefore choose him as <s>Udgātṛ</s> — for this world, and so on. But if one does not choose an <s>Udgātṛ</s> who knows thus, then their sacrifice is diminished from the north. Choose one who knows the <s>Atharvāṅgirasa</s> as <s>Brahman</s> priest, for he knows the office of <s>Brahman</s> (<s>brahmatva</s>). <s>Candramās</s> (the Moon) indeed is the <s>Brahman</s> priest. The waters are the abode of the <s>Bhṛgvaṅgirases</s>. <s>Candramās</s> is the deity; <s>Vaidyuta</s> (relating to lightning) and <s>Uṣṇik</s> and <s>Kakubh</s> are the meters; <s>Om</s> is the luminous call of the <s>Atharvans</s>, <s>Janat</s> is that of the <s>Aṅgirases</s>. Therefore choose him as <s>Brahman</s> priest — for the conquest of this world, for the complete conquest of this world, for the thorough conquest of this world, for the securing of this world, for the increase of this world, for the prosperity of this world, for the elevation of this world, for the pervading of this world,

children.text: (GBr_1,3.1p) pratitiṣṭhati prajayā paśubhir ya evaṃ veda yaś caivam ṛtvijām ārtvijyaṃ veda yaś ca yajñe yajanīyaṃ vedeti brāhmaṇam || 1 ||
children.translated_text: He becomes firmly established with offspring and cattle — he who knows thus, and he who knows the priestly office (<s>ārtvijya</s>) of the priests, and he who knows what is worthy of sacrifice in the sacrifice — thus is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. [1]

body.translated_text: <s>Om</s>. The earth slopes toward the south; the waters flow southward. Therefore the sacrificial ground is somewhat elevated compared to the land where the <s>Bhṛgvaṅgirases</s> are stationed. Just as the waters carry along these worlds, so too the <s>Bhṛgvaṅgirases</s> carry along all the gods. Likewise, this <s>vyāhṛti</s> (sacred utterance) carries along all the <s>Vedas</s>: <s>Om</s> for the <s>ṛc</s> verses, <s>Om</s> for the <s>yajus</s> formulas, <s>Om</s> for the <s>sāman</s> chants, <s>Om</s> is the greeting of all. The learned ones place this (the <s>Brahman</s> priest) in the superior position at the sacrifice. "O gods, let the <s>Brahman</s> priests come, come!" — these gods who are <s>Brahman</s> priests are indeed the <s>Bhṛgvaṅgirases</s>. By praising them, by choosing them, they consider that they are invoking them. No one who does not know the <s>Bhṛgvaṅgirasa</s> tradition, when chosen, should come to the sacrifice. By the splendor of the sacrifice one attains splendor, by nourishing power one attains nourishing power, by glory one attains glory. No one who does not know the <s>Bhṛgvaṅgirasa</s> tradition, when chosen, should come to the sacrifice, lest he rob the sacrifice. Just as a calf, having first learned (to suckle), should then suck the cow, so should a <s>Brahman</s> priest who knows the <s>Bhṛgvaṅgirasa</s> tradition, when chosen, come to the sacrifice, lest he rob the sacrifice. Just as if a cow, or a horse, or a mule were one-footed, two-footed, or three-footed — what could it carry? What could it achieve?

children.translated_text: Following the ruin of the heavenly world, the welfare and security (<s>yogakṣema</s>) of that half goes to ruin — the half in which they sacrifice — thus is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. [2]

body.translated_text: <s>Prajāpati</s> extended the sacrifice. He made the <s>hautram</s> (office of the Hotṛ) by means of the <s>Ṛc</s>, the <s>ādhvaryavam</s> (office of the Adhvaryu) by means of the <s>Yajus</s>, the <s>audgātram</s> (office of the Udgātṛ) by means of the <s>Sāman</s>, and the <s>brahmatva</s> (office of the Brahman priest) by means of the <s>Atharvāṅgirasas</s>. He makes this great declaration (<s>mahāvādya</s>): that he made the <s>hautram</s> by means of the <s>Ṛc</s>, the <s>ādhvaryavam</s> by means of the <s>Yajus</s>, the <s>audgātram</s> by means of the <s>Sāman</s>, and the <s>brahmatva</s> by means of the <s>Atharvāṅgirasas</s>. One side of the sacrifice is prepared by the three <s>Vedas</s>; the <s>Brahman</s> priest prepares the other side of the sacrifice by mind alone. That which purifies here — that is the sacrifice. Mind and speech are its two tracks (<s>vartanī</s>), for the sacrifice proceeds by means of mind and by means of speech. That [yonder world] indeed is mind; this [world] indeed is speech. If one should know that speech is absent, [one should know that] half of this sacrifice has gone away. Just as a one-footed man walking, or a one-wheeled chariot moving, goes to ruin (<s>bhreṣa</s>), so does his sacrifice go to ruin. Following the ruin of the sacrifice, the sacrificer goes to ruin. Following the ruin of the sacrificer, the priests go to ruin. Following the ruin of the priests, the <s>dakṣiṇās</s> (ritual fees) go to ruin.

body.text:
(GBr_1,3.3a) tad u ha smāha śvetaketur āruṇeyo brahmāṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhāṣamāṇam ardhaṃ me 'sya yajñasyāntaragād iti
(GBr_1,3.3b) tasmād brahmā stute bahiḥpavamāne vācoyamyam upāṃśv antaryāmābhyām
(GBr_1,3.3c) atha ye pavamānā odṛcas teṣu_
(GBr_1,3.3d) atha yāni stotrāṇi saśastrāṇy ā vaṣaṭkārāt teṣu
(GBr_1,3.3e) sa yad ṛkto bhreṣaṃ nyṛcched oṃ bhūr janad iti gārhapatye juhuyāt_
(GBr_1,3.3f) yadi yajuṣṭa oṃ bhuvo janad iti dakṣiṇāgnau juduyāt_
(GBr_1,3.3g) yadi sāmata oṃ svar janad ity āhavanīye juhuyāt_
(GBr_1,3.3h) yady anājñātād brahmato voṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svar janad om ity āhavanīya eva juhuyāt
(GBr_1,3.3i) tad vākovākyasyarcāṃ yajuṣāṃ sāmnām atharvāṅgirasām
(GBr_1,3.3j) athāpi vedānāṃ rasana yajñasya viriṣṭaṃ saṃdhīyate
(GBr_1,3.3k) tad yathā lavaṇenety uktam_
(GBr_1,3.3l) tad yathobhayapāt puruṣo yann ubhayacakro vā ratho vartamāno 'bhreṣaṃ nyeti evam evāsya yajño 'bhreṣaṃ nyeti
(GBr_1,3.3m) yajñasyābhreṣam anu yajamāno 'bhreṣaṃ nyeti
(GBr_1,3.3n) yajamānasyābhreṣam anv ṛtvijo 'bhreṣaṃ niyanti_
(GBr_1,3.3o) ṛtvijām abhreṣam anu dakṣiṇā abhreṣaṃ niyanti

children.text: (GBr_1,3.3p) dakṣiṇānām abhreṣam anu yajamānaḥ putrapaśubhir abhreṣaṃ nyeti
children.translated_text: Following the freedom from ruin of the <s>dakṣiṇās</s>, the sacrificer goes without ruin with respect to sons and cattle.

children.text: (GBr_1,3.3q) putrapaśūnām abhreṣam anu yajamānaḥ svargeṇa lokenābhreṣaṃ nyeti
children.translated_text: Following the freedom from ruin of sons and cattle, the sacrificer goes without ruin with respect to the heavenly world.

children.text: (GBr_1,3.3r) svargasya lokasyābhreṣam anu tasyārdhasya yogakṣemo 'bhreṣaṃ nyeti yasminn ardhe yajanta iti brāhmaṇam || 3 ||
children.translated_text: Following the freedom from ruin of the heavenly world, the welfare and security of that half goes without ruin — the half in which they sacrifice — thus is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. [3]

body.translated_text: Then <s>Śvetaketu Āruṇeya</s> used to say, upon seeing the <s>Brahman</s> priest speaking: 'Half of this sacrifice has gone away!' Therefore the <s>Brahman</s> priest, during the <s>bahiṣpavamāna</s> (the external Pavamāna chant), [maintains] restraint of speech (<s>vācoyama</s>) by means of the <s>upāṃśu</s> (whispered) and <s>antaryāma</s> (internal) [cups]. And those <s>Ṛcs</s> that belong to the <s>pavamāna</s> [chants] — [he is silent] during those. And those <s>stotras</s> (chants of praise) together with the <s>śastras</s> (recitations), up to the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> (sacrificial exclamation) — [he is silent] during those. If there should be a ritual error (<s>bhreṣa</s>) in the <s>Ṛc</s> [portion], one should offer [an oblation] in the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire [saying] '<s>Oṃ bhūr janat</s>' (Oṃ, of the earth, [the one who] generates). If there should be an error in the <s>Yajus</s> [portion], one should offer in the <s>Dakṣiṇāgni</s> (southern fire) [saying] '<s>Oṃ bhuvo janat</s>' (Oṃ, of the atmosphere, [the one who] generates). If there should be an error in the <s>Sāman</s> [portion], one should offer in the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire [saying] '<s>Oṃ svar janat</s>' (Oṃ, of the sky, [the one who] generates). If there should be an error from an unknown source, from the <s>Brahman</s> [priest's domain], one should offer in the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire alone [saying] '<s>Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svar janad om</s>.' That is the dialogue (<s>vākovākya</s>) pertaining to the <s>Ṛcs</s>, the <s>Yajus</s> formulas, the <s>Sāmans</s>, and the <s>Atharvāṅgirasas</s>. Moreover, the essence (<s>rasa</s>) of the <s>Vedas</s> and the remedy (<s>viriṣṭa</s>) of the sacrifice are joined together [thereby]. As has been said: 'just as with salt' [it pervades everything]. Just as a two-footed man walking, or a two-wheeled chariot moving, goes without ruin, so does his sacrifice go without ruin. Following the freedom from ruin of the sacrifice, the sacrificer goes without ruin. Following the freedom from ruin of the sacrificer, the priests go without ruin. Following the freedom from ruin of the priests, the <s>dakṣiṇās</s> go without ruin.

body.text:
(GBr_1,3.4a) tad yad audumbaryāṃ ma āsiṣṭa hiṅṅ akārṣīn me prāstāvīn ma udagāsīn me subrahmaṇyām āhvāsīd ity udgātre dakṣiṇā nīyante
(GBr_1,3.4b) grahān me 'grahīt prācārīn me 'śuśruvan me samanasas kārṣīd ayākṣīn me 'vaṣaṭkārṣīn ma ity adhvaryave
(GBr_1,3.4c) hotṛṣadana āsiṣṭāyākṣīn me 'śāṃsīn me 'vaṣaṭkārṣīn ma iti hotre
(GBr_1,3.4d) devayajanaṃ me cīkḷpad brahmāsādaṃ me 'sīsṛpad brahmajapān me 'japīt purastāddhomasaṃsthitahomān me 'hauṣīd ayākṣīn me 'śāṃsīn me 'vaṣaṭkārṣīn ma iti brahmaṇe
(GBr_1,3.4e) bhūyiṣṭhena mā brahmaṇākārṣīd iti_
(GBr_1,3.4f) etad vai bhūyiṣṭhaṃ brahma yad bhṛgvaṅgirasaḥ_

children.text: (GBr_1,3.4g) ye 'ṅgirasaḥ sa raso ye 'tharvāṇo ye 'tharvāṇas tadbheṣajam_
children.translated_text: That greatest <s>Brahman</s> (sacred knowledge) is the [tradition of] <s>Bhṛgu</s> and <s>Aṅgiras</s>. Those that are <s>Āṅgirasas</s> — that is the essence (<s>rasa</s>). Those that are <s>Atharvans</s> — that is the medicine (<s>bheṣaja</s>).

children.text: (GBr_1,3.4h) yad bheṣajaṃ tad amṛtaṃ yad amṛtaṃ tad brahma
children.translated_text: That which is medicine is immortality (<s>amṛta</s>); that which is immortality is <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: (GBr_1,3.4i) sa vā eṣa pūrveṣām ṛtvijām ardhabhāgasyārdham itareṣām ardhaṃ brahmaṇa iti brāhmaṇam || 4 ||
children.translated_text: He [the <s>Brahman</s> priest] indeed [receives] half of the half-share of the former [three] priests, and the other half is the <s>Brahman</s> priest's [own share] — thus is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. [4]

body.translated_text: Now, [when someone says:] 'You sat on my <s>audumbarī</s> (fig-wood seat), you performed my <s>hiṅkāra</s> (the syllable <s>hiṃ</s>), you were my <s>prastāvin</s> (leader of the chant), you were my <s>udgātar</s> (chanter), you called out my <s>subrahmaṇyā</s> (invocation)' — the <s>dakṣiṇās</s> are given to the <s>Udgātṛ</s>. 'You drew my cups (<s>grahas</s>), you performed my processions (<s>prācāra</s>), you made [the participants] attentive to me, you made [them] of one mind (<s>samanasas</s>), you carried out my ritual actions, you performed my <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s>' — [<s>dakṣiṇās</s> are given] to the <s>Adhvaryu</s>. 'You sat on my <s>Hotṛ</s>'s seat, you recited for me, you blessed me, you performed my <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s>' — [<s>dakṣiṇās</s> are given] to the <s>Hotṛ</s>. 'You consecrated my sacrificial ground (<s>devayajana</s>), you prepared my <s>brahmāsada</s> (Brahman's seat), you recited my <s>brahmajapa</s> (Brahman's prayers), you offered my <s>purastāddhomas</s> (preliminary offerings) and <s>saṃsthitahomas</s> (concluding offerings), you carried out my ritual actions, you blessed me, you performed my <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s>' — [<s>dakṣiṇās</s> are given] to the <s>Brahman</s> priest. 'May the <s>Brahman</s> priest have performed [his duties] for me with the greatest [knowledge].'

body.text:
(GBr_1,3.5a) devāś ca ha vā asurāś ca saṃgrāmaṃ samayatanta
(GBr_1,3.5b) tatraitās tisro hotrā jihmaṃ pratipedire
(GBr_1,3.5c) tāsām indra ukthāni sāmāni lulopa
(GBr_1,3.5d) tāni hotre prāyacchat_
(GBr_1,3.5e) ājyaṃ ha vai hotur babhūva
(GBr_1,3.5f) pra'ugaṃ potur vaiśvadevaṃ ha vai hotur babhūva
(GBr_1,3.5g) niṣkevalyaṃ neṣṭuḥ_
(GBr_1,3.5h) marutvatīyaṃ ha vai hotur babhūva_
(GBr_1,3.5i) agnimārutam āgnīdhrasya
(GBr_1,3.5j) tasmād etad abhyastataram iva śasyate yad āgnimārutam_
(GBr_1,3.5k) tasmād ete saṃśaṃsukā iva bhavanti yad dhotā potā neṣṭā_

children.text: (GBr_1,3.5l) āgnīdhro mumuhe vasīta
children.translated_text: The <s>Āgnīdhra</s> was confused and remained silent.

children.text: (GBr_1,3.5m) tad brahmeyasāmivāsa
children.translated_text: The <s>Brahman</s> priest was as if possessing the <s>Sāmans</s>.

children.text: (GBr_1,3.5n) tāsām ardhaṃ pratilulopa prathamārhaṇaṃ ca prathamapadaṃ caitad dakṣiṇāṃ caitat pariśiṣeded iti brāhmaṇam || 5 ||
children.translated_text: He plundered half of those [offices], and the first share and the first rank — this is the <s>dakṣiṇā</s>, and this he should set aside — thus is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. [5]

body.translated_text: The <s>Devas</s> and the <s>Asuras</s> indeed joined in battle. Then these three <s>hotrās</s> (priestly offices) went crookedly (<s>jihma</s>). <s>Indra</s> plundered their <s>ukthāni</s> (hymns of praise) and <s>sāmāni</s> (chants). He gave those to the <s>Hotṛ</s>. The <s>ājya</s> (ghee libation recitation) indeed belonged to the <s>Hotṛ</s>. The <s>praüga</s> and <s>vaiśvadeva</s> [recitations] indeed belonged to the <s>Hotṛ</s> [originally to the <s>Potṛ</s>]. The <s>niṣkevalya</s> [belonged] to the <s>Neṣṭṛ</s>. The <s>marutvatīya</s> (hymn to the <s>Maruts</s>) indeed belonged to the <s>Hotṛ</s>. The <s>āgnimāruta</s> (hymn to <s>Agni</s> and the <s>Maruts</s>) [belonged] to the <s>Āgnīdhra</s> (fire-kindler). Therefore that <s>āgnimāruta</s> is recited as if more repeatedly practiced. Therefore these [priests] — the <s>Hotṛ</s>, the <s>Potṛ</s>, and the <s>Neṣṭṛ</s> — are as if in mutual consultation.

body.text:
(GBr_1,3.6a) uddālako ha vā āruṇir udīcyān vṛto dhāvayāṃ cakāra
(GBr_1,3.6b) tasya ha niṣka upāhito babhūvopavādād bibhyato yo mā brāhmaṇo 'nūcāna upavadiṣyati tasmā etaṃ pradāsyamīti
(GBr_1,3.6c) tad dhodīcyān brāhmaṇān bhayaṃ vivedoddālako ha vā ayam āyāti kaurupañcolo brahmā brahmaputraḥ
(GBr_1,3.6d) sa ūrdhvaṃ vṛto na paryādadhīta
(GBr_1,3.6e) kenemaṃ vīreṇa pratisaṃyatāmahā iti
(GBr_1,3.6f) taṃ yata eva prapannaṃ dadhre tata evam anupratipedire te ha svaidāyanaṃ śaunakam ūcuḥ svaidāyana tvaṃ vai no brahmiṣṭho 'sīti
(GBr_1,3.6g) tvayemaṃ vīreṇa pratisaṃyatāmahā iti
(GBr_1,3.6h) taṃ yata eva prapannaṃ dadhre tata evam anupratipedire

children.text: (GBr_1,3.6i) taṃ ha svaidāyanā ity āmantrayām āsa
children.translated_text: He addressed him: 'O <s>Svaidāyana</s>!'

children.text: (GBr_1,3.6j) sa bho gautamasya putreti hāsmā asūyā pratiśrutaṃ pratiśuśrāva
children.translated_text: 'O son of <s>Gautama</s>!' — thus was the jealous reply heard in response.

children.text: (GBr_1,3.6k) sa vai gautamasya putra ūrdhvaṃ vṛto dhāvet || 6 ||
children.translated_text: 'Son of <s>Gautama</s>, indeed, let him go forth debating!' [6]

body.translated_text: <s>Uddālaka Āruṇi</s> indeed, traveling northward, went about conducting debates (<s>vṛta</s>). A gold necklace (<s>niṣka</s>) had been set aside by him, out of fear of reproach, [thinking:] 'To whichever <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, learned in scripture, who defeats me in debate — to him I shall give this.' Then fear seized the northern <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>: 'This <s>Uddālaka</s>, a <s>Kuru-Pañcāla</s>, a <s>Brahman</s>, a son of <s>Brahman</s>, is coming. He, having gone forth debating, would not stop [until victorious]. By what hero shall we confront him?' Those who encountered him wherever he arrived thus submitted to him. They said to <s>Svaidāyana Śaunaka</s>: 'O <s>Svaidāyana</s>, you are indeed the most learned among us in <s>Brahman</s>. By your heroic prowess, confront him.' Those who encountered him wherever he arrived thus submitted to him.

body.text:
(GBr_1,3.7a) yas tad darśapūrṇamāsayo rūpaṃ vidyāt kasmād imāḥ prajāḥ śirastaḥ prathamaṃ lomaśā jāyante kasmād āsām aparam iva śmaśrūṇy upakakṣāṇy anyāni lomāni jāyante
(GBr_1,3.7b) yas tad darśapūrṇamāsayo rūpaṃ vidyāt kasmād imāḥ prājāḥ śirastaḥ prathamaṃ palitā bhavanti kasmād antataḥ sarvā eva palitā bhavanti
(GBr_1,3.7c) yas tad darśapūrṇamāsayo rūpaṃ vidyāt kasmād imāḥ prajā adantikā jāyante kasmād āsām aparam iva jāyante
(GBr_1,3.7d) yas tad darśapūrṇamāsayo rūpaṃ vidyāt kasmād āsāṃ saptavarṣāṣṭavarṣāṇāṃ prabhidyante kasmād āsāṃ punar eva jāyante kasmād antataḥ sarva eva prabhidyante
(GBr_1,3.7e) yas tad darśapūrṇamāsayo rūpaṃ vidyāt kasmād adhare dantāḥ pūrve jāyante para uttare
(GBr_1,3.7f) yas tad darśapūrṇamāsayo rūpaṃ vidyāt kasmād adhare dantāḥ aṇīyāṃso hrasīyāṃsaḥ prathīyāṃso varṣīyāṃsa uttare
(GBr_1,3.7g) yas tad darśapūrṇamāsayo rūpaṃ vidyāt kasmād imau daṃṣṭrau dīrghatarau kasmāt same iva jaṃbhe
(GBr_1,3.7h) yas tad darśapūrṇamāsayo rūpaṃ vidyāt kasmād ime śrotre antarataḥ same iva dīrṇe
(GBr_1,3.7i) yas tad darśapūrṇamāsayo rūpaṃ vidyāt kasmāt pumāṃsaḥ śmaśruvanto 'śmaśruvaḥ striyaḥ_
(GBr_1,3.7j) yas tad darśapūrṇamāsayo rūpaṃ vidyāt kasmād āsāṃ saṃtatam iva śarīraṃ bhavati kasmād āsām asthīni dṛḍhatarāṇīva bhavanti

children.text: (GBr_1,3.7k) yas tad darśapūrṇamāsayo rūpaṃ vidyāt kasmād āsāṃ prathame vayasi retaḥ siktaṃ na saṃbhavati kasmād āsāṃ madhyame vayasi retaḥ siktaṃ saṃbhavati kasmād āsām uttame vayasi retaḥ siktaṃ na saṃbhavati
children.translated_text: He who would know the form of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> [should know]: Why does seed sown in the first stage of life not result in conception? Why does seed sown in the middle stage of life result in conception? Why does seed sown in the last stage of life not result in conception?

children.text: (GBr_1,3.7l) yas tad darśapūrṇamāsayo rūpaṃ vidyāt kasmād idaṃ śiśnam uccaśa eti nīcī padyate [ed. iṃ]
children.translated_text: He who would know the form of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> [should know]: Why does this male organ rise up and fall down?

children.text: (GBr_1,3.7m) kasmāt sakṛd apānam || 7 ||
children.translated_text: Why does it [produce] excretion (<s>apāna</s>) once a day? [7]

body.translated_text: He who would know the form (<s>rūpa</s>) of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new-moon and full-moon sacrifices) [should know]: Why are these creatures born head-first with hair? Why do their beards and other body hair appear to grow later? He who would know the form of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> [should know]: Why do these creatures first become grey-haired on the head? Why do they eventually become entirely grey? He who would know the form of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> [should know]: Why are these creatures born toothless? Why do their [teeth] appear to grow later? He who would know the form of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> [should know]: Why do their [teeth] fall out at seven or eight years of age? Why do they grow back again? Why do they eventually all fall out [permanently]? He who would know the form of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> [should know]: Why are the lower teeth born first and the upper ones later? He who would know the form of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> [should know]: Why are the lower teeth finer, shorter, broader, and more numerous than the upper? He who would know the form of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> [should know]: Why are these two canine teeth (<s>daṃṣṭras</s>) longer, and why are they as if level in the jaw? He who would know the form of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> [should know]: Why are these two ears as if long [channels] on the inside? He who would know the form of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> [should know]: Why do men have beards while women are beardless? He who would know the form of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> [should know]: Why does the body of women appear continuous [without visible joints], and why do their bones appear to be firmer?

body.text:
(GBr_1,3.8a) atha yaḥ purastād aṣṭāv ājyabhāgān vidyān madhyataḥ pañca havirbhāgāḥ ṣaṭ prājāpatyā upariṣṭād aṣṭāv ājyabhāgān vidyāt_
(GBr_1,3.8b) atha yo gāyatrīṃ hariṇīṃ jyotiṣpakṣāṃ sarvair yajñair yajamānaṃ svargaṃ lokam abhivahantīṃ vidyāt_
(GBr_1,3.8c) atha yaḥ apaṅktiṃ pañcapadāṃ saptadaśākṣarāṃ sarvair yajñair yajamānaṃ svargaṃ lokam abhivahantīṃ vidyāt
(GBr_1,3.8d) tasmai ha niṣkaṃ prayacchann uvācānūcāno ha vai svaidāyanāsi suvarṇaṃ vai suvarṇavide dadāmīti
(GBr_1,3.8e) tad upayamya niścakrāma
(GBr_1,3.8f) tatrāpavavrāja yatretaro babhūva
(GBr_1,3.8g) taṃ ha papraccha kim eṣa gautamasya putra iti_
(GBr_1,3.8h) eṣa brahmā brahmāputra iti hovāca yad enaṃ kaś cid upavadetota mīmāṃseta ha vā mūrdhā vā asya vipatet prāṇā vainaṃ jahyur iti
(GBr_1,3.8i) te mitha eva cikrandeyur viprāpavavraja yatretaro babhūva
(GBr_1,3.8j) te prātaḥ samitpāṇaya upodeyur upāyāmo bhavantam iti
(GBr_1,3.8k) kim artham iti

children.text: (GBr_1,3.8l) yān eva no bhavāṃs tān hyaḥ praśnān apṛcchat tān eva no bhavān vyācakṣīteti
children.translated_text: 'Those very questions which you asked us — may you yourself explain them to us.'

children.text: (GBr_1,3.8m) tatheti
children.translated_text: 'So be it.'

children.text: (GBr_1,3.8n) tebhya etān praśnān vyācacaṣṭe || 8 ||
children.translated_text: He expounded those questions to them. [8]

body.translated_text: Now, he who would know, in the beginning, eight shares of <s>ājya</s> (ghee oblations), in the middle five shares of <s>havis</s> (oblations) [and] six <s>prājāpatya</s> (belonging to <s>Prajāpati</s>) [offerings], and at the end eight shares of <s>ājya</s> [would know the sacrifice fully]. And he who would know the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, golden (<s>hariṇī</s>), with wings of light (<s>jyotiṣpakṣā</s>), carrying the sacrificer performing all sacrifices to the heavenly world. And he who would know the <s>Apaṅkti</s> [meter], with five feet (<s>padas</s>), of seventeen syllables, carrying the sacrificer performing all sacrifices to the heavenly world. To him, giving the gold necklace, he said: 'O <s>Svaidāyana</s>, you are indeed learned in scripture! I give gold to one who knows gold!' He accepted it and departed. He went to where the other [<s>Uddālaka</s>] was. He [<s>Uddālaka</s>] asked him: 'What is this, son of <s>Gautama</s>?' 'This is a <s>Brahman</s>, a son of <s>Brahman</s>,' he replied. 'If anyone should challenge him in debate — either his head would split apart, or his vital breaths would leave him!' They cried out to one another in alarm. He [<s>Svaidāyana</s>] departed and went to where the other [<s>Uddālaka</s>] was. In the morning, they approached with fuel-sticks in hand: 'We approach you, sir.' 'For what purpose?'

children.translated_text: (GBr 1,3.9x) Therefore one exhales only once, lest it be permanently swollen or permanently flaccid — thus is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [teaching]. [9]

body.translated_text: (GBr 1,3.9a) Because he first strews the <s>barhis</s> (sacrificial grass) in front of the <s>vedi</s> (altar), therefore these creatures are born hairy from the head first. (GBr 1,3.9b) Because he strews the <s>prastara</s> (grass bundle) as if after [the barhis], therefore their beards, underarm hair, and other body hair grow as if later. (GBr 1,3.9c) Because he draws the <s>prastara</s> forward from the <s>barhis</s>, therefore these creatures first become grey-haired from the head. (GBr 1,3.9d) Because he draws it all through to the end, therefore at the end they become entirely grey. (GBr 1,3.9e) Because the <s>prayājas</s> (fore-offerings) are without <s>puronuvākyā</s> (invitatory verses), therefore these creatures are born without teeth. (GBr 1,3.9f) Because the <s>havīṃṣi</s> (oblations) have <s>puronuvākyā</s>, therefore [teeth] grow as if later for them. (GBr 1,3.9g) Because the <s>anuyājas</s> (after-offerings) are without <s>puronuvākyā</s>, therefore [the teeth] of those who are seven or eight years old fall out. (GBr 1,3.9h) Because the <s>patnīsaṃyājas</s> (wife's offerings) have <s>puronuvākyā</s>, therefore [the teeth] grow again for them. (GBr 1,3.9i) Because the <s>samiṣṭayajus</s> (concluding offering formula) is without <s>puronuvākyā</s>, therefore at the end all [teeth] fall out entirely. (GBr 1,3.9j) Because one recites in <s>Gāyatrī</s> meter and sacrifices with <s>Triṣṭubh</s>, therefore the lower teeth grow first and the upper ones later. (GBr 1,3.9k) Because one recites an <s>ṛc</s> (verse) and sacrifices with a <s>yajus</s> (formula), therefore the lower teeth are thinner, shorter, broader, and the upper ones taller. (GBr 1,3.9l) Because the two <s>āghāras</s> (pourings) are poured forward as longer ones, therefore these two canine teeth are longer. (GBr 1,3.9m) Because the <s>saṃyājya</s> (offering verses) are with proper meter, therefore the two jaws are as if equal. (GBr 1,3.9n) Because he brings together at the fourth <s>prayāja</s>, therefore these two ears are as if equally open on the inside. (GBr 1,3.9o) Because after muttering the <s>japa</s> (whispered prayer) one utters the <s>abhihiṃkāra</s>, therefore men have beards and women are beardless. (GBr 1,3.9p) Because he continuously recites the <s>sāmidhenī</s> (kindling) verses, therefore their body is as if continuous. (GBr 1,3.9q) Because the <s>sāmidhenī</s> verses have wood as their oblation, therefore their bones are as if harder. (GBr 1,3.9r) Because the <s>prayājas</s> have ghee as their oblation, therefore in their first age of life, seed sown does not produce [offspring]. (GBr 1,3.9s) Because in the middle of the oblations they proceed with curds and <s>puroḍāśa</s> (rice cake), therefore in their middle age, seed sown produces [offspring]. (GBr 1,3.9t) Because the <s>anuyājas</s> have ghee as their oblation, therefore in their last age, seed sown does not produce [offspring]. (GBr 1,3.9u) Because at the last <s>anuyāja</s> one exhales once, therefore this male organ rises up and falls down,

children.text: (GBr_1,3.10t) dvyakṣaro vai vaṣaṭkāraḥ saiṣā paṅktiḥ
children.translated_text: (GBr 1,3.10t) The <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> (sacrificial exclamation) has two syllables — that is the <s>Paṅkti</s> [meter].

children.text: (GBr_1,3.10u) pañcapadā saptadaśākṣarā sarvair yajñair yajamānaṃ svargaṃ lokam abhivahati
children.translated_text: (GBr 1,3.10u) With five feet and seventeen syllables, it carries the sacrificer to the heavenly world by means of all sacrifices.

children.text: (GBr_1,3.10v) tad yatrāsyaiśvaryaṃ syād yatra vainam abhivaheyur evaṃvidam eva tatra brahmāṇaṃ vṛṇīyān nānevaṃvidam iti brāhmaṇam || 10 ||
children.translated_text: (GBr 1,3.10v) Where one would have sovereignty, where they would carry one who knows thus — there one should choose such a knower as the <s>Brahmā</s> priest, not one who does not know thus — thus is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [teaching]. [10]

body.translated_text: (GBr 1,3.10a) Now, the eight <s>ājyabhāgas</s> (ghee portions) that are before [the main offerings]: five <s>prayājas</s>, two <s>āghāras</s>, and two <s>ājyabhāgas</s>. The first of the <s>ājyabhāgas</s> belongs to <s>Agni</s>, the second to <s>Soma</s>, [and these are] of the <s>havirbhāgas</s> (oblation portions). (GBr 1,3.10b) For the oblation indeed belongs to <s>Soma</s>. (GBr 1,3.10c) The <s>puroḍāśa</s> (rice cake) belongs to <s>Agni</s>. (GBr 1,3.10d) The <s>puroḍāśa</s> for <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>, and <s>Agni Sviṣṭakṛt</s> — these are the five <s>havirbhāgas</s> in the middle. (GBr 1,3.10e) Now, the six that belong to <s>Prajāpati</s>: the <s>iḍā</s>, the <s>prāśitra</s> (fore-portion), what is set aside for the <s>Āgnīdhra</s> priest, the <s>Brahman</s>'s share, the sacrificer's share, and the <s>anvāhārya</s> (supplementary offering) as the sixth. (GBr 1,3.10f) Now, the eight <s>ājyabhāgas</s> that are after: three <s>anuyājas</s>, four <s>patnīsaṃyājas</s>, and the <s>samiṣṭayajus</s> as the eighth. (GBr 1,3.10g) Now, the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, golden-colored, light-winged, carries the sacrificer to the heavenly world by means of all sacrifices — that is the <s>vedi</s> itself. (GBr 1,3.10h) The eight <s>ājyabhāgas</s> that are before — that is its right wing. (GBr 1,3.10i) The eight <s>ājyabhāgas</s> that are after — that is its left wing. (GBr 1,3.10j) The <s>havīṃṣi</s> (oblations) are the body. (GBr 1,3.10k) The <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire is the hind part. (GBr 1,3.10l) The <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire is the head. (GBr 1,3.10m) The wings are of gold and silver. (GBr 1,3.10n) Because one does not see the sun completely all around in front, therefore the refuse heap is without light. (GBr 1,3.10o) Now, the <s>Paṅkti</s> meter of five feet and seventeen syllables carries the sacrificer to the heavenly world by means of all sacrifices — that is the <s>yājyā</s> (offering verse) itself. (GBr 1,3.10p) Of that, '<s>oṃ śrāvaya</s>' has four syllables. (GBr 1,3.10q) '<s>Astu śrauṣaṭ</s>' has four syllables. (GBr 1,3.10r) '<s>Yaja</s>' has two syllables. (GBr 1,3.10s) '<s>Ye yajāmahe</s>' has five syllables.

body.translated_text: (GBr 1,3.12a) He said: '[The deity] of <s>Rudra</s> [presides over] my cow-pen. (GBr 1,3.12b) Of <s>Manu</s> when the [cow is] called. (GBr 1,3.12c) Of <s>Vāyu</s> when released. (GBr 1,3.12d) Of <s>Virāj</s> when the calf is being led away. (GBr 1,3.12e) Of the <s>Jagatī</s> [meter] when led away. (GBr 1,3.12f) Of the <s>Aśvins</s> when milking. (GBr 1,3.12g) Of <s>Soma</s> when milked. (GBr 1,3.12h) Of <s>Bṛhaspati</s> when setting forth. (GBr 1,3.12i) Of <s>Dyāvāpṛthivī</s> (Heaven and Earth) when being carried. (GBr 1,3.12j) Of <s>Agni</s> when being placed on [the fire]. (GBr 1,3.12k) Of <s>Agni Vaiśvānara</s> when placed on. (GBr 1,3.12l) Of <s>Viṣṇu</s> when being heated. (GBr 1,3.12m) Of the <s>Maruts</s> when heated. (GBr 1,3.12n) Of <s>Pūṣan</s> when boiled over. (GBr 1,3.12o) Of <s>Varuṇa</s> when settled down. (GBr 1,3.12p) Of <s>Sarasvatī</s> when brought back with water. (GBr 1,3.12q) Of <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> when being removed. (GBr 1,3.12r) Of <s>Dhātṛ</s> when removed. (GBr 1,3.12s) Of the <s>Viśvedevas</s> when being taken up. (GBr 1,3.12t) Of <s>Savitṛ</s> when taken up. (GBr 1,3.12u) Of <s>Bṛhaspati</s> when setting forth. (GBr 1,3.12v) Of <s>Dyāvāpṛthivī</s> when being carried. (GBr 1,3.12w) Of <s>Indra</s> when being placed near. (GBr 1,3.12x) Of strength when placed near. (GBr 1,3.12y) The kindling stick belongs to <s>Agni</s>. (GBr 1,3.12z) The first oblation I offered — thereby I established myself in the heavenly world. (GBr 1,3.12aa) When I looked upon the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire, [it was] for the continuity of this world. (GBr 1,3.12bb) The second oblation belongs to <s>Prajāpati</s>. (GBr 1,3.12cc) Therefore it is fuller, for it is [offered] with the mind alone. (GBr 1,3.12dd) When, having offered, I took the ladle upward three times to the north, thereby I propitiated the <s>Rudras</s>. (GBr 1,3.12ee) When, having placed the ladle on the <s>barhis</s> and wiped it, I wiped my hands to the north, thereby I propitiated the plants and trees. (GBr 1,3.12ff) When, having wiped a second time and putting on the sacred thread in the manner of the ancestors, I made the offering of <s>svadhā</s> to the <s>Pitṛs</s> toward the south, thereby I propitiated the <s>Pitṛs</s> (ancestors). (GBr 1,3.12gg) When I ate the first [portion], thereby I propitiated the <s>Prāṇas</s> (vital breaths). (GBr 1,3.12hh) When the second, [I propitiated] the embryos thereby. (GBr 1,3.12ii) Therefore embryos live even without eating. (GBr 1,3.12jj) When I ate all the rest at the end, thereby I propitiated all the <s>Devas</s>. (GBr 1,3.12kk) When I poured down water with the unwashed ladle, thereby I propitiated the serpents and other beings. (GBr 1,3.12ll) When with the washed [ladle], [I propitiated] the serpents and the <s>Puṇyajanas</s> (blessed beings) thereby. (GBr 1,3.12mm) When I poured down water with the ladle behind the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire, thereby I propitiated the <s>Gandharvas</s> and <s>Apsarases</s>.'

children.text: (GBr_1,3.13jj) ānaḍuhenaiva śakṛtpiṇḍenāgnyāyatanāni parilipya homyam upasādya <vāta ā vātu bheṣajam [PS 19.46.7-9]> iti sūktenātmany eva juhuyāt_
children.translated_text: 'Having smeared the fire-sites with a ball of bull's dung, having brought the oblation material near, one should offer into oneself with the <s>sūkta</s> (hymn): "May <s>Vāta</s> (Wind) blow as medicine" [PS 19.46.7-9].'

children.text: (GBr_1,3.13kk) atha prātar agniṃ nirmathya yathāsthānam agnīn upasamādhāya yathāpuraṃ juhuyāt
children.translated_text: 'Then in the morning, having churned a new fire and having re-established the fires in their [proper] places, one should offer as before.'

children.text: (GBr_1,3.13ll) sā me vidyā sā prāyaścittir iti brāhmaṇam || 13 ||
children.translated_text: 'That is my knowledge; that is my expiation' — [thus ends] the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [passage]. || 13 ||

body.translated_text: 'It is exactly so, sir, as you say.' 'But I ask you [a question].' 'Ask, O <s>Prācīnayogya</s>.' 'If one's fires were established in the evening and all were burning, and the washed sacrificial vessels were brought near — and then the southern fire (<s>dakṣiṇāgni</s>) should blaze up [out of control], what danger would come from that?' 'Quickly his wife perishes — [this befalls] one who offers without knowledge.' 'But I offer with knowledge.' 'What is your knowledge? What is your expiation (<s>prāyaścitta</s>)?' 'Having carried [fire] from the <s>Gārhapatya</s> (household fire) to the <s>Dakṣiṇāgni</s> (southern fire), having removed the embers to the east, one should offer with [the words]: "To <s>Prāṇa</s> and <s>Apāna</s>, <s>Svāhā</s>!" Then in the morning, having re-established the fires in their [proper] places, one should offer as before. That is my knowledge; that is my expiation.' 'And if the <s>Āhavanīya</s> (oblation fire) should blaze up — what danger would come from that?' 'Quickly his son perishes — [this befalls] one who offers without knowledge.' 'But I offer with knowledge.' 'What is your knowledge? What is your expiation?' 'Having carried [fire] from the <s>Gārhapatya</s> to the <s>Āhavanīya</s>, having removed the embers to the west, one should offer with [the words]: "To <s>Samāna</s> and <s>Vyāna</s>, <s>Svāhā</s>!" Then in the morning, having re-established the fires in their [proper] places, one should offer as before. That is my knowledge; that is my expiation.' 'And if the <s>Gārhapatya</s> should blaze up — what danger would come from that?' 'Quickly the householder (<s>gṛhapati</s>) perishes — [this befalls] one who offers without knowledge.' 'But I offer with knowledge.' 'What is your knowledge? What is your expiation?' 'Having carried the <s>Āhavanīya</s> together with its ash, bypassing the <s>Dakṣiṇāgni</s> to its south, and re-establishing [it] in the site of the <s>Gārhapatya</s>, then carrying [fire] from there to the <s>Āhavanīya</s>, having removed the embers to the north, one should offer with [the words]: "To <s>Udāna</s> and <s>Rūpa</s>, <s>Svāhā</s>!" Then in the morning, having re-established the fires in their [proper] places, one should offer as before. That is my knowledge; that is my expiation.' 'And if all the fires should blaze up — what danger would come from that?' 'Quickly the householder suffers complete loss — [this befalls] one who offers without knowledge.' 'But I offer with knowledge.' 'What is your knowledge? What is your expiation?' 'Having smeared the fire-sites with a ball of bull's dung, having brought the oblation material near, having churned a new fire, one should offer: "To <s>Prāṇa</s> and <s>Apāna</s>, <s>Svāhā</s>! To <s>Samāna</s> and <s>Vyāna</s>, <s>Svāhā</s>! To <s>Udāna</s> and <s>Rūpa</s>, <s>Svāhā</s>!" Then in the morning, having re-established the fires in their [proper] places, one should offer as before. That is my knowledge; that is my expiation.' 'And if they cannot generate a fire and no wind blows from anywhere — what danger would come from that?' 'His offering and sacrifice become fruitless — [this befalls] one who offers without knowledge.' 'But I offer with knowledge.' 'What is your knowledge? What is your expiation?'

children.text: (GBr_1,3.14cc) sadeṣṭaṃ sadā hutaṃ sadāśitaṃ pāyitam agnihotraṃ bhavati ya evaṃ veda yaś caivaṃvidvān agnihotraṃ juhotīti brāhmaṇam || 14 ||
children.translated_text: His <s>Agnihotra</s> (fire-offering) is always performed, always offered, always eaten [and] drunk — [this is so for] one who knows thus and for one who, having this knowledge, offers the <s>Agnihotra</s>. [Thus ends] the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [passage]. || 14 ||

body.translated_text: 'It is exactly so, O blessed one, as you say.' 'I approach you [as a student].' 'If you had not spoken thus, your head would have split apart.' 'Come, I shall tell you that, so that [your head] shall not split.' He who, having this knowledge, eats and drinks — his speech (<s>vāc</s>) is satisfied thereby. When speech is satisfied, <s>Agni</s> (fire) is satisfied. When <s>Agni</s> is satisfied, the earth (<s>pṛthivī</s>) is satisfied. When the earth is satisfied, the beings dependent upon the earth are satisfied. He who, having this knowledge, eats and drinks — his <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) is satisfied thereby. When <s>prāṇa</s> is satisfied, <s>Vāyu</s> (wind) is satisfied. When <s>Vāyu</s> is satisfied, the atmosphere (<s>antarikṣa</s>) is satisfied. When the atmosphere is satisfied, the beings dependent upon the atmosphere are satisfied. He who, having this knowledge, eats and drinks — his sight (<s>cakṣus</s>) is satisfied thereby. When sight is satisfied, <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun) is satisfied. When <s>Āditya</s> is satisfied, heaven (<s>dyaus</s>) is satisfied. When heaven is satisfied, the beings dependent upon heaven are satisfied. He who, having this knowledge, eats and drinks — his mind (<s>manas</s>) is satisfied thereby. When the mind is satisfied, the Moon (<s>Candramās</s>) is satisfied. When the Moon is satisfied, the waters (<s>āpas</s>) are satisfied. When the waters are satisfied, the beings dependent upon the waters are satisfied. He who, having this knowledge, eats and drinks — his hearing (<s>śrotra</s>) is satisfied thereby. When hearing is satisfied, the directions (<s>diśas</s>) and the intermediate directions are satisfied. When the directions and intermediate directions are satisfied, the beings dependent upon them are satisfied. He who, having this knowledge, eats and drinks — his right hand is [like] the <s>juhū</s> (offering ladle); the left is the <s>upabhṛt</s> (secondary ladle); the throat is the <s>dhruvā</s> (fixed ladle).

children.text: (GBr_1,3.15p) tasya ha prajām itarayoḥ praje sajātatvam upaitām_
children.translated_text: His offspring [absorbed] the offspring of the other two — they came to share the same birth.

children.text: (GBr_1,3.15q) tasmād dvir hotavyaṃ yajuṣā caiva manasā ca
children.translated_text: Therefore one should offer twice — with the <s>Yajus</s> (formula) and with the mind.

children.text: (GBr_1,3.15r) yām eva sa ṛddhim ārdhnot tām ṛdhnoti ya evaṃ veda yaś caivaṃvidvān agnihotraṃ juhotīti brāhmaṇam || 15 ||
children.translated_text: Whatever prosperity he achieved, that same prosperity is achieved by one who knows thus and by one who, having this knowledge, offers the <s>Agnihotra</s>. [Thus ends] the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [passage]. || 15 ||

body.translated_text: The <s>Priyamedhas</s>, descendants of <s>Bharadvāja</s>, considered themselves knowers of sacrifice. They did not approach anyone as a knower of the <s>Veda</s>. They knew everything. They knew [it] all together. [Yet] they did not agree on the <s>Agnihotra</s> alone. One of them offered the <s>Agnihotra</s> once; one [offered] twice; one [offered] thrice. The two others asked the one who offered once: 'To whom do you offer?' [He said:] '<s>Prajāpati</s> alone is all this in its oneness. To <s>Prajāpati</s> alone I offer in the evening; to <s>Prajāpati</s> in the morning.' The two others asked the one who offered twice: 'To which two do you offer?' [He said:] 'To <s>Agni</s> and <s>Prajāpati</s> in the evening; to <s>Sūrya</s> and <s>Prajāpati</s> in the morning.' The two others asked the one who offered thrice: 'To which [deities] do you offer?' [He said:] 'To <s>Agni</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>, and <s>Anumati</s> in the evening; to <s>Sūrya</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>, and <s>Agni Sviṣṭakṛt</s> in the morning.' Among them, the one who offered twice prospered. He became the most [prosperous]. He surpassed the other two in offspring and the other two in glory.

children.text: (GBr_1,3.16t) sā svāhā sā svadhā yajñeṣu vaṣaṭkārabhūtā prayujyate
children.translated_text: That <s>Svāhā</s> — she is <s>Svadhā</s>; in sacrifices she is employed as the <s>Vaṣaṭkāra</s> (sacrificial exclamation).

children.text: (GBr_1,3.16u) tasyā agnir daivatam_
children.translated_text: Her deity is <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: (GBr_1,3.16v) brāhmaṇo rūpam iti brāhmaṇam || 16 ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is her visible form. [Thus ends] the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [passage]. || 16 ||

body.translated_text: Whence did <s>Svāhā</s> originate? By whom was she fashioned? What is her <s>gotra</s> (lineage)? How many syllables [does she have]? How many feet? How many colors? What is her ending? Where does she abide? What is her foundation? Tell [us] of <s>Svāhā</s> — what is her deity and her form? <s>Svāhā</s> was born from truth (<s>satya</s>). She was fashioned by <s>Brahman</s>. She belongs to the <s>gotra</s> of <s>Lāmagāyana</s>. Two syllables. One foot. Three colors: white, lotus(-colored), and golden. She is the unified breath-expiration of all meters in the <s>Vedas</s>; at the end of the sounds, the four <s>Vedas</s> are [her] body. The six auxiliary sciences (<s>Vedāṅgas</s>) [are her limbs]; herbs and trees are [her] body-hair. [Her] two eyes are <s>Sūrya</s> and <s>Candramās</s> (Sun and Moon).

body.translated_text: Now, we shall explain the distribution of the <s>Savanīya</s> (pressing-day) sacrificial animal. Having extracted the portions (<s>avadānas</s>): the two jaws with the tongue [go] to the <s>Prastotṛ</s> (the chanter who introduces). The neck with the hump [goes] to the <s>Pratihartṛ</s> (the respondent). The hawk-[shaped] breast [goes] to the <s>Udgātṛ</s> (the chanter). The right side with the shoulder [goes] to the <s>Adhvaryu</s> (the officiating priest). The left [side goes] to the <s>Upagātṛs</s> (the assistant chanters). The left shoulder [goes] to the <s>Pratiprasthātṛ</s> (the assistant Adhvaryu). The right hip-joint [goes] to the <s>Brahman</s> (the supervisory priest). The rear thigh [goes] to the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> (the Brahman's assistant). The thigh [goes] to the <s>Potṛ</s> (the purifying priest). The left hip-joint [goes] to the <s>Hotṛ</s> (the invoking priest). The rear thigh [goes] to the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> (priest of <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>). The foreleg [goes] to the <s>Acchāvāka</s> (the calling priest). The right foreleg [goes] to the <s>Neṣṭṛ</s> (the leading priest). The left [foreleg goes] to the <s>Sadasya</s> (the hall-priest). The back and the spine [go] to the householder (<s>Gṛhapati</s>). The hind-quarters [go] to the wife (<s>Patnī</s>). She has a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> receive it [on her behalf]. The tip of the stomach, the heart, the kidneys, the fingers, and the right foreleg [go] to the <s>Āgnīdhra</s> (fire-kindler). The left [foreleg goes] to the <s>Ātreya</s>. The right feet [go] to the householder who gives the vow-order. The left feet [go] to the housewife who gives the vow-order. Together with them [comes] the lip [portion]. The householder himself gives instruction regarding it. The collar-bones and three vertebrae [go] to the <s>Grāvastut</s> (praiser of the pressing-stones). Three vertebrae and half the belly [go] to the <s>Unnetṛ</s> (the one who draws up Soma). From there upward [goes] to the <s>Camasādhvaryus</s> (cup-bearing priests); the lung [goes] to the <s>Śamitṛ</s> (the slaughterer). The head [goes] to the <s>Subrahmaṇya</s>. Whoever invites [guests] for the next-day pressing — to him [goes] the hide. Thus indeed thirty-six [portions] are completed. The cow has thirty-six portions. The <s>Bṛhatī</s> [meter] has thirty-six syllables. The heavenly world indeed belongs to the <s>Bṛhat</s> [sāman]. By means of the <s>Bṛhatī</s> the gods sacrifice in the heavenly world. By means of the <s>Bṛhatī</s> they become established in the heavenly world. They become established with offspring and cattle — those who distribute thus. But those who are of improper conduct, or evil-doers, or oblation-stealers, or other people who should disrupt [it] — for them the animal becomes one that disrupts in the same way, and [they become] excluded from heaven. <s>Devabhāga</s>, the seer of <s>Śruti</s>, knew this distribution of the animal. He taught it to <s>Girijā Bābhravya</s> among other men. From him, this [knowledge] came down among men. [Thus ends] the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [passage]. || 18 ||

children.translated_text: Therefore, one should not meditate during divine rites nor study when the sacrifice has concluded—thus is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> (explanation). || 19 ||

body.translated_text: Now, therefore, regarding <s>dīkṣā</s> (consecration). For what reason is one called <s>dīkṣita</s> (consecrated)? Because he dwells in the highest meditation (<s>dhī</s>). Him, being <s>dhīkṣita</s> (one who dwells in meditation), they call <s>dīkṣita</s> indirectly. For the gods are fond of the indirect and averse to the direct. For what reason does the consecrated one not rise to greet others and not offer salutation, yet is one to whom others should rise and offer salutation? Those who are to be risen for and saluted—they are possessed by the <s>Atharvāṅgirasas</s>. What is the <s>Ātharvaṇa</s> aspect of this? That he offers into himself alone, not into another. Thus, of the <s>Ātharvaṇas</s> who perform the <s>odana-sava</s>, one offers into oneself alone, not into another. And what is the <s>Āṅgirasa</s> aspect of this? That he does not take the names of himself or others; thus indeed in that state, the names of oneself and others are not taken. They speak speech that is discerning and delightful. They illuminate the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and delight the <s>Prājāpatya</s>. This is the vow-yielding cow of the <s>Atharvāṅgirasas</s>. For they are dependent on her. For what reason does the consecrated one not eat, and why do they not take his name? He becomes established in food and established in name, they say; those who eat his food eat his sin. And those who take his name strike away the sin of his name. Moreover, they say he becomes an embryo of the <s>Vedas</s>. They say that for him who is unborn, unknown, and has not purchased <s>Soma</s>, food should not be eaten. He is born in the morning of the <s>dīkṣā</s> days; they purchase <s>Soma</s>. They say that for him who is born, known, and has purchased <s>Soma</s>, food may be eaten. For what reason are the <s>saṃsavas</s> (simultaneous pressings) to be avoided? Whichever is more powerful steals the sacrifice of the other. For what reason should one not meditate during divine rites and not study when the sacrifice has concluded? For the very reason of simultaneous pressing. When there is lightning, thunder, and rain, the gods press the <s>Vāyavya</s> offering and consume <s>Soma</s>.
