body.translated_text: The teachers who had returned from their studies sat down. The sacrifice, taking the form of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, approached them as they were about to be consecrated. "If they have thus failed you, come, I shall be the <s>dīkṣā</s> (consecration) in your midst." They said, "We neither know you nor recognize you. For who would be consecrated together with one who is unknown? When you undertake this consecration, you shall not be consecrated again. Or if you consecrate thus, you will then become confused. You will be confused..."

body.text:
(GBr_1,3.21a) sa hovāca dvādaśa ha vai vasūni dīkṣitād utkrāmanti
(GBr_1,3.21b) na ha vai dīkṣito 'gnihotraṃ juhuyāt_
(GBr_1,3.21c) na paurṇamāsena yajñena yajeta
(GBr_1,3.21d) nāmāvāsyena_
(GBr_1,3.21e) asmin vasīta
(GBr_1,3.21f) na pitṛyajñena yajeta
(GBr_1,3.21g) na tatra gacched yatra manasā jigamiṣet_
(GBr_1,3.21h) neṣṭyā yajeta
(GBr_1,3.21i) na vācā yathākathā cid abhibhāṣeta
(GBr_1,3.21j) na mithunaṃ caret_
(GBr_1,3.21k) nānnāsya yathākāmam upayuñjīta
(GBr_1,3.21l) na paśubandhena yajñena yajeta
(GBr_1,3.21m) na tatra gacched yatra cakṣuṣā parāpaśyet
(GBr_1,3.21n) kṛṣṇājinaṃ vasīta
(GBr_1,3.21o) kurīraṃ dhārayet_
(GBr_1,3.21p) muṣṭī kuryāt_
(GBr_1,3.21q) aṅguṣṭhaprabhṛtayas tisra ucchrayet_

children.text: (GBr_1,3.21r) mṛgaśṛṅgaṃ gṛhṇīyāt
children.translated_text: He should take a deer's horn.

children.text: (GBr_1,3.21s) tena kaṣeta_
children.translated_text: With that he should scratch himself.

children.text: (GBr_1,3.21t) atha yasya dīkṣitasya vāg vāyatā syān muṣṭī vā visṛṣṭau sa etāni japet || 21 ||
children.translated_text: And if a consecrated one's speech were to falter or his fists were opened, he should recite these mantras. || 21 ||

body.translated_text: He said: "Twelve treasures (<s>vasūni</s>) indeed depart from the consecrated one. The consecrated one should not offer the <s>Agnihotra</s>. He should not sacrifice with the full-moon sacrifice. Nor with the new-moon sacrifice. He should dwell in this. He should not sacrifice with the ancestor sacrifice. He should not go where he wishes to go in mind. He should not sacrifice with the <s>iṣṭi</s> offering. He should not speak with speech in any manner whatsoever. He should not engage in sexual union. He should not use food as he pleases. Nor with the animal sacrifice."

body.text:
(GBr_1,3.22a) agnihotraṃ ca mā paurṇamāsaś ca yajñaḥ purastāt pratyañcam ubhau kāmaprau bhūtvā kṣityā sahāviśatām_
(GBr_1,3.22b) vasatiś ca māmāvāsyaś ca yajñaḥ paścāt prāñcam ubhāv iti samānam_
(GBr_1,3.22c) manaś ca mā pitṛyajñaś ca yajño dakṣiṇata udañcam ubhāv iti samānam_
(GBr_1,3.22d) vāk ca meṣṭiś cottarato dakṣiṇāñcam ubhāv iti samānam_
(GBr_1,3.22e) retaś ca mānnaṃ ceta ūrdhvam ubhāv iti samānam_

children.text: (GBr_1,3.22f) cakṣuś ca mā paśubandhaś ca yajño 'muto 'rvāñcam ubhau kāmaprau bhūtvākṣityā sahāviśatām iti khalu ha vai dīkṣito ya ātmani vasūni dhatte na caivāsya kā canārtir bhavati na ca yajñaviṣkandham upayāty apahanti punarmṛtyum
children.translated_text: "May sight and the animal sacrifice, from yonder coming hither, both having become desire-fulfilling, enter into me along with imperishability." Indeed, the consecrated one who places these treasures within himself—no affliction befalls him, nor does he encounter obstruction of the sacrifice; he strikes away repeated death.

children.text: (GBr_1,3.22g) apātyeti punarājātim_
children.translated_text: He overcomes rebirth.

children.text: (GBr_1,3.22h) kāmacāro 'sya sarveṣu lokeṣu bhāti ya evaṃ veda yaś caivaṃvidvān dīkṣām upaitīti brāhmaṇam || 22 ||
children.translated_text: He who knows thus, and he who knowing thus undertakes <s>dīkṣā</s> (consecration)—free movement in all worlds shines for him. Thus is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. || 22 ||

body.translated_text: "May the <s>Agnihotra</s> and the full-moon sacrifice, both having become desire-fulfilling, from the front facing backward, enter into me along with the dwelling. May the lodging and the new-moon sacrifice, from behind facing forward, both likewise enter. May mind and the ancestor sacrifice, from the south facing north, both likewise enter. May speech and the <s>iṣṭi</s> offering, from the north facing south, both likewise enter. May semen and food, from above, both likewise enter."

body.text:
(GBr_1,3.23a) atha yasya dīkṣitasyartumatī jāyā syāt pratisnāvā pratisnāvā sarūpavatsāyā goḥ payasi sthālīpākaṃ śrapayitvābhighāryodvāsyoddhṛtyābhihiṃkṛtya garbhavedanapuṃsavanaiḥ saṃpātavantaṃ kṛtvā taṃ paraiva prāśnīyāt_
(GBr_1,3.23b) reto vā annam_

children.text: (GBr_1,3.23c) vṛṣā hiṃkāraḥ_
children.translated_text: The bull is the <s>hiṃkāra</s> (the sound 'hīṃ').

children.text: (GBr_1,3.23d) evaṃ hīśvarā yā dīkṣitāya dīkṣitā jāyā putraṃ labheteti_
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, the consecrated wife of a consecrated one is capable of obtaining a son.

children.text: (GBr_1,3.23e) etenaiva prakrameṇa yajeteti brāhmaṇam || 23 ||
children.translated_text: One should sacrifice by this very procedure—thus is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. || 23 ||

body.translated_text: And if a consecrated one's wife were in her season, having cooked a <s>sthālīpāka</s> (pot-cooked offering) in the milk of a cow that has a calf of the same color, as a surrogate, having poured ghee, having removed it, having taken portions, having uttered <s>hiṃkāra</s>, having mixed it with the <s>garbhavedana</s> (embryo-recognition) and <s>puṃsavana</s> (male-producing) rites, he should eat that as a surplus offering. For semen is food.

body.text: (GBr_1,3.23col) ity atharvavede gopathabrāhmaṇapūrvabhāge tṛtīyaḥ prapāṭhakaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the third chapter (<s>prapāṭhaka</s>) of the first part (<s>pūrvabhāga</s>) of the <s>Gopatha Brāhmaṇa</s> of the <s>Atharvaveda</s>.

body.text:
(GBr_1,4.1a) om ayaṃ vai yajño yo 'yaṃ pavate
(GBr_1,4.1b) tam eta īpsanti ye saṃvatsarāya dīkṣante
(GBr_1,4.1c) teṣāṃ gṛhapatiḥ prathamo dīkṣate_
(GBr_1,4.1d) ayaṃ vai loko gṛhapatiḥ_

children.text: (GBr_1,4.1e) asmin vā idaṃ sarvaṃ loke pratiṣṭhitam_
children.translated_text: In this world, all this is established.

children.text: (GBr_1,4.1f) gṛhapatā u eva sarve sattriṇaḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ
children.translated_text: All the <s>sattra</s>-performers are established in the householder.

children.text: (GBr_1,4.1g) pratiṣṭhāyā evainaṃ tat pratiṣṭhityai dīkṣante || 1 ||
children.translated_text: They consecrate him for the sake of establishment, for firm foundation. || 1 ||

body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>. This sacrifice is indeed the one that purifies. Those who are consecrated for the year seek to obtain it. Among them, the householder (<s>gṛhapati</s>) is consecrated first. This world indeed is the householder.

body.text:
(GBr_1,4.2a) atha brahmāṇaṃ dīkṣayati candramā vai brahmādhidaivaṃ mano 'dhyātmam_
(GBr_1,4.2b) manasaiva tad oṣadhīḥ saṃdadhāti
(GBr_1,4.2c) tad yā oṣadhīr veda sa eva brahmauṣadhīs
(GBr_1,4.2d) tad anena lokena saṃdadhāti
(GBr_1,4.2e) tasmād etāv antareṇānyo na dīkṣeta

children.text: (GBr_1,4.2f) sa yad etāv antareṇānyo dīkṣetemaṃ taṃ lokam oṣadhibhir vyāpādayet_
children.translated_text: If another were to be consecrated between these two, he would destroy this world through the herbs.

children.text: (GBr_1,4.2g) ucchoṣukā ha syus
children.translated_text: They would become dried up.

children.text: (GBr_1,4.2h) tasmād etāv antareṇānyo na dīkṣeta || 2 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore no one else should be consecrated between these two. || 2 ||

body.translated_text: Then he consecrates the <s>Brahman</s> priest. The moon indeed is the <s>Brahman</s> in the divine sphere (<s>adhidaiva</s>), and the mind in the sphere of the self (<s>adhyātma</s>). By mind alone he joins the herbs together. He who knows those herbs is indeed the <s>Brahman</s> of herbs. He joins it with this world. Therefore no one else should be consecrated between these two.

body.text:
(GBr_1,4.3a) athodgātāraṃ dīkṣayati_
(GBr_1,4.3b) ādityo vā udgātādhidaivaṃ cakṣur adhyātmam_
(GBr_1,4.3c) parjanya ādityaḥ
(GBr_1,4.3d) parjanyād adhi vṛṣṭir jāyate
(GBr_1,4.3e) vṛṣṭir eva tad oṣadhīḥ saṃdadhāti
(GBr_1,4.3f) tasmād etāv antareṇānyo na dīkṣeta

children.text: (GBr_1,4.3g) sa yad etāv antareṇānyo dīkṣetemaṃ taṃ lokaṃ varṣeṇa vyāpādayet_
children.translated_text: If another were to be consecrated between these two, he would destroy this world through rain.

children.text: (GBr_1,4.3h) avarṣukā ha syus
children.translated_text: They would become without rain.

children.text: (GBr_1,4.3i) tasmād etāv antareṇānyo na dīkṣeta || 3 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore no one else should be consecrated between these two. || 3 ||

body.translated_text: Then he consecrates the <s>Udgātṛ</s> (chanter). The sun indeed is the <s>Udgātṛ</s> in the divine sphere, and sight in the sphere of the self. <s>Parjanya</s> (the rain cloud) is the sun. From <s>Parjanya</s>, rain is born. Rain indeed joins the herbs together. Therefore no one else should be consecrated between these two.

body.text:
(GBr_1,4.4a) atha hotāraṃ dīkṣayati_
(GBr_1,4.4b) agnir vai hotādhidaivaṃ vāg adhyātmam
(GBr_1,4.4c) annaṃ vṛṣṭiḥ_
(GBr_1,4.4d) vācaṃ caiva tad agniṃ cānnena saṃdādhāti
(GBr_1,4.4e) tasmād etāv antareṇānyo na dīkṣeta

children.text: (GBr_1,4.4f) sa yad etāv antareṇānyo dīkṣetemaṃ taṃ lokam annena vyāpādayet_
children.translated_text: If another were to be consecrated between these two, he would destroy this world through food.

children.text: (GBr_1,4.4g) aśanāyukā ha syus
children.translated_text: They would become hungry.

children.text: (GBr_1,4.4h) tasmād etāv antareṇānyo na dīkṣeta || 4 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore no one else should be consecrated between these two. || 4 ||

body.translated_text: Then he consecrates the <s>Hotṛ</s> (invoker). <s>Agni</s> indeed is the <s>Hotṛ</s> in the divine sphere, and speech in the sphere of the self. Food is rain. He joins both speech and <s>Agni</s> with food. Therefore no one else should be consecrated between these two.

body.text:
(GBr_1,4.5a) athādhvaryuṃ pratiprasthātā dīkṣayati
(GBr_1,4.5b) vāyur vā adhvaryur adhidaivaṃ prāṇo 'dhyātmam
(GBr_1,4.5c) annaṃ vṛṣṭiḥ_
(GBr_1,4.5d) vāyuṃ caiva tat prāṇaṃ cānnena saṃdadhāti
(GBr_1,4.5e) tasmād etāv antareṇānyo na dīkṣeta [ed. etav]

children.text: (GBr_1,4.5f) sa yad etāv antareṇānyo dīkṣetemaṃ taṃ lokaṃ prāṇena vyāpādayet
children.translated_text: If another were to be consecrated between these two, he would destroy this world through breath.

children.text: (GBr_1,4.5g) pramāyukā ha syus
children.translated_text: They would die prematurely.

children.text: (GBr_1,4.5h) tasmād etāv antareṇānyo na dīkṣeta || 5 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore no one else should be consecrated between these two. || 5 ||

body.translated_text: Then the <s>Pratiprasthātṛ</s> consecrates the <s>Adhvaryu</s>. <s>Vāyu</s> indeed is the <s>Adhvaryu</s> in the divine sphere, and breath (<s>prāṇa</s>) in the sphere of the self. Food is rain. He joins both <s>Vāyu</s> and breath with food. Therefore no one else should be consecrated between these two.

body.text:
(GBr_1,4.6a) atha brahmaṇe brāhmaṇācchaṃsinaṃ dīkṣayati_
(GBr_1,4.6b) athodgātre prastotāraṃ dīkṣayati_
(GBr_1,4.6c) atha hotre maitrāvaruṇaṃ dīkṣayati_
(GBr_1,4.6d) athādhvaryave pratiprasthātāraṃ neṣṭā dīkṣayati
(GBr_1,4.6e) sa hainam anu_
(GBr_1,4.6f) eteṣāṃ vai navānāṃ kḷptim anv itare kalpante
(GBr_1,4.6g) nava vai prāṇāḥ
(GBr_1,4.6h) prāṇair yajñas tāyate_
(GBr_1,4.6i) atha brahmaṇe potāraṃ dīkṣayati_
(GBr_1,4.6j) athodgātre pratihartāraṃ dīkṣayati_
(GBr_1,4.6k) atha hotre 'cchāvākaṃ dīkṣayati_
(GBr_1,4.6l) athādhvaryave neṣṭāram unnetā dīkṣayati
(GBr_1,4.6m) sa hainam anu_
(GBr_1,4.6n) atha brahmaṇa āgnīdhraṃ dīkṣyati_
(GBr_1,4.6o) athodgātre subrahmaṇyaṃ dīkṣayati_
(GBr_1,4.6p) atha hotre grāvastutaṃ dīkṣayati_
(GBr_1,4.6q) atha tamanyaḥ snātako vā brahmacārī vā dīkṣayati
(GBr_1,4.6r) na pūtaḥ pāvayed ity āhuḥ

children.text: (GBr_1,4.6s) saiṣānupūrvaṃ dīkṣā
children.translated_text: This is the consecration in proper sequence.

children.text: (GBr_1,4.6t) tad ya evaṃ dīkṣante dīkṣiṣyamāṇā eva te sattriṇāṃ prāyaścittaṃ na vindante
children.translated_text: Those who are consecrated thus, even while being about to be consecrated, do not incur the need for expiation (<s>prāyaścitta</s>) of the <s>sattra</s>-performers.

children.text: (GBr_1,4.6u) sattriṇāṃ prāyaścittam anu tasyārdhasya yogakṣemaḥ kalpate yasminn ardhe dīkṣanta iti brāhmaṇam || 6 ||
children.translated_text: The well-being and security (<s>yogakṣema</s>) of that half in which they are consecrated is arranged according to the expiation of the <s>sattra</s>-performers—thus is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. || 6 ||

body.translated_text: Then for the <s>Brahman</s> priest, he consecrates the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>. Then for the <s>Udgātṛ</s>, he consecrates the <s>Prastotṛ</s>. Then for the <s>Hotṛ</s>, he consecrates the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>. Then for the <s>Adhvaryu</s>, the <s>Neṣṭṛ</s> consecrates the <s>Pratiprasthātṛ</s>. He follows after him. According to the arrangement of these nine, the others are arranged. Nine indeed are the breaths (<s>prāṇas</s>). The sacrifice is extended through the breaths. Then for the <s>Brahman</s>, he consecrates the <s>Potṛ</s>. Then for the <s>Udgātṛ</s>, he consecrates the <s>Pratihartṛ</s>. Then for the <s>Hotṛ</s>, he consecrates the <s>Acchāvāka</s>.

body.text:
(GBr_1,4.7a) śraddhayā vai devā dīkṣaṇīyāṃ niramimatāditeḥ prāyaṇīyām_
(GBr_1,4.7b) somāt krayam_
(GBr_1,4.7c) viṣṇor ātithyam
(GBr_1,4.7d) ādityāt pravargyam_
(GBr_1,4.7e) svadhāyā upasadaḥ_
(GBr_1,4.7f) agnīṣomābhyām aupavasathyam ahaḥ
(GBr_1,4.7g) prātaryāvadbhyo devebhyaḥ prātaranuvākam_
(GBr_1,4.7h) vasubhyaḥ prātaḥsavanam_
(GBr_1,4.7i) rudrebhyo mādhyaṃdinaṃ savanam
(GBr_1,4.7j) ādityebhyas tṛtīyasavanam_
(GBr_1,4.7k) varuṇād avabhṛtham
(GBr_1,4.7l) aditer udayanīyām_
(GBr_1,4.7m) mitrāvaruṇābhyām anūbandhyām_
(GBr_1,4.7n) tvaṣṭus tvāṣṭram_
(GBr_1,4.7o) devībhyo devikābhyo devatāhavīṃṣi
(GBr_1,4.7p) kāmād daśātirātram_

children.text: (GBr_1,4.7q) svargāl lokād udavasānīyām_
children.translated_text: (GBr_1,4.7q) from the heavenly world the <s>udavasānīyā</s> (closing offering).

children.text: (GBr_1,4.7r) tad vā etad agniṣṭomasya janma
children.translated_text: (GBr_1,4.7r) That, verily, is the origin of the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>.

children.text: (GBr_1,4.7s) sa ya evam etad agniṣṭomasya janma vedāgniṣṭomena sātmā saloko bhūtvā devān apy etīti brāhmaṇam || 7 ||
children.translated_text: (GBr_1,4.7s) He who thus knows this origin of the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, having become one in self and one in world with the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, attains the gods — thus is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> teaching. || 7 ||

body.translated_text:
(GBr_1,4.7a) By <s>Śraddhā</s> (faith) indeed the gods fashioned the <s>dīkṣaṇīyā</s> (consecration offering); from <s>Aditi</s> the <s>prāyaṇīyā</s> (opening offering),
(GBr_1,4.7b) from <s>Soma</s> the <s>kraya</s> (purchase of Soma),
(GBr_1,4.7c) from <s>Viṣṇu</s> the <s>ātithya</s> (hospitality offering),
(GBr_1,4.7d) from <s>Āditya</s> the <s>Pravargya</s> (hot-milk ritual),
(GBr_1,4.7e) from <s>Svadhā</s> (self-sustenance) the <s>Upasads</s> (preliminary offerings),
(GBr_1,4.7f) from <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s> the <s>aupavasathya</s> (eve-of-pressing day),
(GBr_1,4.7g) from the gods who come at dawn the <s>prātaranuvāka</s> (morning litany),
(GBr_1,4.7h) from the <s>Vasus</s> the <s>prātaḥsavana</s> (morning pressing),
(GBr_1,4.7i) from the <s>Rudras</s> the <s>mādhyaṃdina savana</s> (midday pressing),
(GBr_1,4.7j) from the <s>Ādityas</s> the <s>tṛtīyasavana</s> (third pressing),
(GBr_1,4.7k) from <s>Varuṇa</s> the <s>Avabhṛtha</s> (concluding bath),
(GBr_1,4.7l) from <s>Aditi</s> the <s>udayanīyā</s> (concluding offering),
(GBr_1,4.7m) from <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> the <s>anūbandhyā</s> (supplementary animal sacrifice),
(GBr_1,4.7n) from <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> the <s>Tvāṣṭra</s> (offering to Tvaṣṭṛ),
(GBr_1,4.7o) from the <s>Devīs</s> (goddesses) and <s>Devikās</s> (minor goddesses) the <s>devatāhavīṃṣi</s> (deity oblations),
(GBr_1,4.7p) from <s>Kāma</s> (desire) the <s>Daśātirātra</s> (ten-night rite),

body.text:
(GBr_1,4.8a) atha yad dīkṣaṇīyayā yajante śraddhām eva tad devīṃ devatāṃ yajante
(GBr_1,4.8b) śraddhā devī devatā bhavanti
(GBr_1,4.8c) śraddhāyā devyāḥ sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ yanti ya etad upayanti_
(GBr_1,4.8d) atha yat prāyaṇīyayā yajante 'ditim eva tad devīṃ devatāṃ yajante
(GBr_1,4.8e) aditir devī devatā bhavanti_
(GBr_1,4.8f) adityā devyāḥ sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ yanti ya etad upayanti_
(GBr_1,4.8g) atha yat krayam upayanti somam eva tad devaṃ devatāṃ yajante
(GBr_1,4.8h) somo devo devatā bhavanti [ed. davatā]
(GBr_1,4.8i) somasya devasya sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ yanti ya etad upayanti_
(GBr_1,4.8j) atha yad ātithyayā yajante viṣṇum eva tad devaṃ devatāṃ yajante
(GBr_1,4.8k) viṣṇur devo devatā bhavanti
(GBr_1,4.8l) viṣṇor devasya sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ yanti ya etad upayanti_
(GBr_1,4.8m) atha yat pravargyam upayanty ādityam eva tad devaṃ devatāṃ yajante_ [ed. davatāṃ]

body.translated_text:
(GBr_1,4.8a) Now, when they sacrifice with the <s>dīkṣaṇīyā</s> (consecration offering), they worship <s>Śraddhā</s> (faith) as the goddess and deity.
(GBr_1,4.8b) <s>Śraddhā</s> becomes the goddess and deity.
(GBr_1,4.8c) They attain union with and sharing the same world as the goddess <s>Śraddhā</s>, those who perform this.
(GBr_1,4.8d) Now, when they sacrifice with the <s>prāyaṇīyā</s> (opening offering), they worship <s>Aditi</s> as the goddess and deity.
(GBr_1,4.8e) <s>Aditi</s> becomes the goddess and deity.
(GBr_1,4.8f) They attain union with and sharing the same world as the goddess <s>Aditi</s>, those who perform this.
(GBr_1,4.8g) Now, when they perform the <s>kraya</s> (purchase of Soma), they worship <s>Soma</s> as the god and deity.
(GBr_1,4.8h) <s>Soma</s> becomes the god and deity. [ed. davatā]
(GBr_1,4.8i) They attain union with and sharing the same world as the god <s>Soma</s>, those who perform this.
(GBr_1,4.8j) Now, when they sacrifice with the <s>ātithya</s> (hospitality offering), they worship <s>Viṣṇu</s> as the god and deity.
(GBr_1,4.8k) <s>Viṣṇu</s> becomes the god and deity.
(GBr_1,4.8l) They attain union with and sharing the same world as the god <s>Viṣṇu</s>, those who perform this.
(GBr_1,4.8m) Now, when they perform the <s>Pravargya</s> (hot-milk ritual), they worship <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun) as the god and deity. [ed. davatāṃ]
(GBr_1,4.8n) <s>Āditya</s> becomes the god and deity.
(GBr_1,4.8o) They attain union with and sharing the same world as the god <s>Āditya</s>, those who perform this.
(GBr_1,4.8p) Now, when they perform the <s>Upasad</s> (preliminary offering), they worship <s>Svadhā</s> (self-sustenance) as the goddess and deity.
(GBr_1,4.8q) <s>Svadhā</s> becomes the goddess and deity.
(GBr_1,4.8r) They attain union with and sharing the same world as the goddess <s>Svadhā</s>, those who perform this.
(GBr_1,4.8s) Now, when they perform the <s>aupavasathya</s> (eve-of-pressing) day, they worship <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s> as the two gods and deities.
(GBr_1,4.8t) <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s> become the two gods and deities.
(GBr_1,4.8u) They attain union with and sharing the same world as the two deities <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>, those who perform this. [ed. 'gnīṣomayor]
(GBr_1,4.8v) Now, when they perform the <s>prātaranuvāka</s> (morning litany), they worship the dawn-coming gods as the deities.
(GBr_1,4.8w) The dawn-coming gods become the deities.
(GBr_1,4.8x) They attain union with and sharing the same world as the dawn-coming gods, those who perform this.
(GBr_1,4.8y) Now, when they perform the <s>prātaḥsavana</s> (morning pressing), they worship the <s>Vasus</s> as the gods and deities.
(GBr_1,4.8z) The <s>Vasus</s> become the gods and deities.
(GBr_1,4.8aa) They attain union with and sharing the same world as the gods the <s>Vasus</s>, those who perform this.
(GBr_1,4.8bb) Now, when they perform the <s>mādhyaṃdina savana</s> (midday pressing), they worship the <s>Rudras</s> as the gods and deities.
(GBr_1,4.8cc) The <s>Rudras</s> become the gods and deities.
(GBr_1,4.8dd) They attain union with and sharing the same world as the gods the <s>Rudras</s>, those who perform this.
(GBr_1,4.8ee) Now, when they perform the <s>tṛtīyasavana</s> (third pressing), they worship the <s>Ādityas</s> as the gods and deities.
(GBr_1,4.8ff) The <s>Ādityas</s> become the gods and deities.
(GBr_1,4.8gg) They attain union with and sharing the same world as the gods the <s>Ādityas</s>, those who perform this.
(GBr_1,4.8hh) Now, when they perform the <s>Avabhṛtha</s> (concluding bath), they worship <s>Varuṇa</s> as the god and deity.
(GBr_1,4.8ii) <s>Varuṇa</s> becomes the god and deity.
(GBr_1,4.8jj) They attain union with and sharing the same world as the god <s>Varuṇa</s>, those who perform this.
(GBr_1,4.8kk) Now, when they sacrifice with the <s>udayanīyā</s> (concluding offering), they worship <s>Aditi</s> as the goddess and deity.
(GBr_1,4.8ll) <s>Aditi</s> becomes the goddess and deity.
(GBr_1,4.8mm) They attain union with and sharing the same world as the goddess <s>Aditi</s>, those who perform this. [ed. ādityā]
(GBr_1,4.8nn) Now, when they sacrifice with the <s>anūbandhyā</s> (supplementary animal sacrifice), they worship <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> as the two gods and deities.
(GBr_1,4.8oo) <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> become the two gods and deities.
(GBr_1,4.8pp) They attain union with and sharing the same world as the two gods <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, those who perform this.
(GBr_1,4.8qq) Now, when they sacrifice with the <s>Tvāṣṭra</s> animal (the animal offering to <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>), they worship <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> as the god and deity.
(GBr_1,4.8rr) <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> becomes the god and deity.
(GBr_1,4.8ss) They attain union with and sharing the same world as the god <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, those who perform this.
(GBr_1,4.8tt) Now, when they offer with the <s>devikā</s> (minor goddess) oblations that are part of the <s>Upasads</s> — <s>Agni</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s> — the goddesses and <s>devikās</s> become the deities.
(GBr_1,4.8uu) They attain union with and sharing the same world as the goddesses and <s>devikā</s> deities, those who perform this.
(GBr_1,4.8vv) Now, when they perform the <s>Daśātirātra</s> (ten-night rite), they worship <s>Kāma</s> (desire) as the god and deity.
(GBr_1,4.8ww) <s>Kāma</s> becomes the god and deity.
(GBr_1,4.8xx) They attain union with and sharing the same world as the god <s>Kāma</s>, those who perform this.
(GBr_1,4.8yy) Now, when they sacrifice with the <s>udavasānīyā</s> (closing offering), they worship the heavenly world as the god and deity.
(GBr_1,4.8zz) The heavenly world becomes the god and deity.
(GBr_1,4.8aaa) They attain union with and sharing the same world as the god, the heavenly world, those who perform this.
(GBr_1,4.8bbb) That, verily, is the origin of the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>.

body.translated_text:
(GBr_1,4.9a) From Day-and-Night indeed the gods fashioned the <s>prāyaṇīya Atirātra</s> (opening overnight rite).
(GBr_1,4.9b) From the half-months the <s>Caturviṃśa</s> (twenty-fourth) day.
(GBr_1,4.9c) From <s>Brahman</s> (sacred power) the <s>Abhiplava</s> (six-day sequence).
(GBr_1,4.9d) From <s>Kṣatra</s> (warrior power) the <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> (six-day sequence).
(GBr_1,4.9e) From <s>Agni</s> the <s>Abhijit</s> (victory day).
(GBr_1,4.9f) From the waters the <s>Svarasāmans</s> (self-sung chants).
(GBr_1,4.9g) From <s>Sūrya</s> (the Sun) the <s>Viṣuvant</s> (solstice day).
(GBr_1,4.9h) The <s>Svarasāmans</s> are stated in reverse order.
(GBr_1,4.9i) From <s>Indra</s> the <s>Viśvajit</s> (all-conquering day).
(GBr_1,4.9j) The <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> and <s>Abhiplava</s> have been stated.
(GBr_1,4.9k) From <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> the two <s>Gavāyuṣī</s> (cow-life days).
(GBr_1,4.9l) From the <s>Viśvedevas</s> (All-Gods) the <s>Daśarātra</s> (ten-day rite).
(GBr_1,4.9m) From the quarters the <s>Dāśarātrika Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s> (ten-day-derived Pṛṣṭhya six-day sequence).
(GBr_1,4.9n) From these worlds the <s>Chandoma</s> (metre-based) three-day rite.
(GBr_1,4.9o) From the <s>Saṃvatsara</s> (year) the tenth day.
(GBr_1,4.9p) From <s>Prajāpati</s> the <s>Mahāvrata</s> (great observance day).

body.translated_text:
(GBr_1,4.10a) Now, when they perform the <s>prāyaṇīya Atirātra</s> (opening overnight rite), they worship Day-and-Night as the two gods and deities.
(GBr_1,4.10b) Day-and-Night become the two gods and deities.
(GBr_1,4.10c) They attain union with and sharing the same world as the two gods Day-and-Night, those who perform this. [ed. 'horātrayor]
(GBr_1,4.10d) Now, when they perform the <s>Caturviṃśa</s> (twenty-fourth) day, they worship the half-months as the gods and deities.
(GBr_1,4.10e) The half-months become the gods and deities.
(GBr_1,4.10f) They attain union with and sharing the same world as the gods the half-months, those who perform this.
(GBr_1,4.10g) Now, when they perform the <s>Abhiplava</s> (six-day sequence), they worship <s>Brahman</s> (sacred power) as the god and deity.
(GBr_1,4.10h) <s>Brahman</s> becomes the god and deity.
(GBr_1,4.10i) They attain union with and sharing the same world as the god <s>Brahman</s>, those who perform this.
(GBr_1,4.10j) Now, when they perform the <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> (six-day sequence), they worship <s>Kṣatra</s> (warrior power) as the god and deity.
(GBr_1,4.10k) <s>Kṣatra</s> becomes the god and deity.
(GBr_1,4.10l) They attain union with and sharing the same world as the god <s>Kṣatra</s>, those who perform this.
(GBr_1,4.10m) Now, when they perform the <s>Abhijit</s> (victory day), they worship <s>Agni</s> as the god and deity.
(GBr_1,4.10n) <s>Agni</s> becomes the god and deity.
(GBr_1,4.10o) They attain union with and sharing the same world as the god <s>Agni</s>, those who perform this.
(GBr_1,4.10p) Now, when they perform the <s>Svarasāmans</s> (self-sung chants), they worship the Waters as the goddesses and deities; the Waters become the goddesses and deities.
(GBr_1,4.10q) They attain union with and sharing the same world as the goddesses the Waters, those who perform this.
(GBr_1,4.10r) Now, when they perform the <s>Viṣuvant</s> (solstice day), they worship <s>Sūrya</s> (the Sun) as the god and deity.
(GBr_1,4.10s) <s>Sūrya</s> becomes the god and deity.
(GBr_1,4.10t) They attain union with and sharing the same world as the god <s>Sūrya</s>, those who perform this.
(GBr_1,4.10u) The <s>Svarasāmans</s> in reverse order have been stated.
(GBr_1,4.10v) Now, when they perform the <s>Viśvajit</s> (all-conquering day), they worship <s>Indra</s> as the god and deity.
(GBr_1,4.10w) <s>Indra</s> becomes the god and deity.
(GBr_1,4.10x) They attain union with and sharing the same world as the god <s>Indra</s>, those who perform this.
(GBr_1,4.10y) The <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> and <s>Abhiplava</s> have been stated.
(GBr_1,4.10z) Now, when they perform the two <s>Gavāyuṣī</s> (cow-life days), they worship <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> as the two gods and deities.
(GBr_1,4.10aa) <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> become the two gods and deities.
(GBr_1,4.10bb) They attain union with and sharing the same world as the two gods <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, those who perform this.
(GBr_1,4.10cc) Now, when they perform the <s>Daśarātra</s> (ten-day rite), they worship the <s>Viśvedevas</s> (All-Gods) as the gods and deities.
(GBr_1,4.10dd) The <s>Viśvedevas</s> become the gods and deities.
(GBr_1,4.10ee) They attain union with and sharing the same world as the gods the <s>Viśvedevas</s>, those who perform this.
(GBr_1,4.10ff) Now, when they perform the <s>Dāśarātrika Pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha</s> (ten-day-derived Pṛṣṭhya six-day sequence), they worship the quarters as the goddesses and deities.
(GBr_1,4.10gg) The quarters become the goddesses and deities.
(GBr_1,4.10hh) They attain union with and sharing the same world as the goddesses the quarters, those who perform this.
(GBr_1,4.10ii) Now, when they perform the <s>Chandoma</s> (metre-based) three-day rite, they worship these worlds as the gods and deities.
(GBr_1,4.10jj) These worlds become the gods and deities.
(GBr_1,4.10kk) They attain union with and sharing the same world as the gods these worlds, those who perform this.
(GBr_1,4.10ll) Now, when they perform the tenth day, they worship the <s>Saṃvatsara</s> (year) as the god and deity.
(GBr_1,4.10mm) The <s>Saṃvatsara</s> becomes the god and deity. [ed. davatā]
(GBr_1,4.10nn) They attain union with and sharing the same world as the god the <s>Saṃvatsara</s>, those who perform this.
(GBr_1,4.10oo) Now, when they perform the <s>Mahāvrata</s> (great observance day), they worship <s>Prajāpati</s> as the god and deity.
(GBr_1,4.10pp) <s>Prajāpati</s> becomes the god and deity. [ed. davatā]
(GBr_1,4.10qq) They attain union with and sharing the same world as the god <s>Prajāpati</s>, those who perform this.
(GBr_1,4.10rr) Now, when they perform the <s>udayanīya Atirātra</s> (concluding overnight rite), they worship the heavenly world as the god and deity.
(GBr_1,4.10ss) The heavenly world becomes the god and deity.
(GBr_1,4.10tt) They attain union with and sharing the same world as the god, the heavenly world, those who perform this.
(GBr_1,4.10uu) That, verily, is the origin of the <s>Saṃvatsara</s> (year-long sacrifice).

children.translated_text: (GBr 1,4.23t) Now, those who are learned and approach [the sacrifice] — just as one crosses from stream to stream, from firm ground to firm ground, from level [ground] to level [ground], from happiness to happiness, from fearlessness to fearlessness — thus indeed these [knowers say]: 'We have partaken of the surplus of the year (<s>saṃvatsara</s>)' — thus is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [teaching]. ||23||

body.translated_text:
(GBr 1,4.24a) <s>Predi</s> from <s>Kauśāmbī</s>, <s>Kausurubindu</s>, lived the life of a student of sacred knowledge (<s>brahmacarya</s>) under <s>Uddālaka Āruṇi</s>.
(GBr 1,4.24b) The teacher asked him: 'Young man, how many days of the year did your father consider [there to be]?'
(GBr 1,4.24c) 'How many indeed?'
(GBr 1,4.24d) 'Ten,' he said.
(GBr 1,4.24e) 'Ten indeed,' he said.
(GBr 1,4.24f) 'The <s>Virāj</s> [meter] has ten syllables; the sacrifice belongs to <s>Virāj</s>.'
(GBr 1,4.24g) 'How many indeed?'
(GBr 1,4.24h) 'Nine,' he said.
(GBr 1,4.24i) 'Nine indeed,' he said.
(GBr 1,4.24j) 'Nine indeed are the vital breaths (<s>prāṇas</s>).'
(GBr 1,4.24k) 'The sacrifice is sustained by the vital breaths.'
(GBr 1,4.24l) 'How many indeed?'
(GBr 1,4.24m) 'Eight,' he said.
(GBr 1,4.24n) 'Eight indeed,' he said.
(GBr 1,4.24o) 'The <s>Gāyatrī</s> [meter] has eight syllables.'
(GBr 1,4.24p) 'The sacrifice is <s>Gāyatrī</s>.'
(GBr 1,4.24q) 'How many indeed?'
(GBr 1,4.24r) 'Seven,' he said.
(GBr 1,4.24s) 'Seven indeed,' he said.
(GBr 1,4.24t) 'Seven are the meters (<s>chandas</s>).'
(GBr 1,4.24u) 'The sacrifice is sustained by the meters.'
(GBr 1,4.24v) 'How many indeed?'
(GBr 1,4.24w) 'Six,' he said.
(GBr 1,4.24x) 'Six indeed,' he said.
(GBr 1,4.24y) 'Six indeed are the seasons.'
(GBr 1,4.24z) '[This is] for the attainment of the seasons.'
(GBr 1,4.24aa) 'How many indeed?'
(GBr 1,4.24bb) 'Five,' he said.
(GBr 1,4.24cc) 'Five indeed,' he said.
(GBr 1,4.24dd) 'The <s>Paṅkti</s> [meter] has five feet.'
(GBr 1,4.24ee) 'The sacrifice belongs to <s>Paṅkti</s>.'
(GBr 1,4.24ff) 'How many indeed?'
(GBr 1,4.24gg) 'Four,' he said.
(GBr 1,4.24hh) 'Four indeed,' he said.
(GBr 1,4.24ii) 'Four indeed are the <s>Vedas</s>.'
(GBr 1,4.24jj) 'The sacrifice is sustained by the <s>Vedas</s>.'
(GBr 1,4.24kk) 'How many indeed?'
(GBr 1,4.24ll) 'Three,' he said.
(GBr 1,4.24mm) 'Three indeed,' he said.
(GBr 1,4.24nn) 'The sacrifice has three pressings (<s>savanas</s>).'
(GBr 1,4.24oo) 'The sacrifice is sustained by the pressings.'
(GBr 1,4.24pp) 'How many indeed?'
(GBr 1,4.24qq) 'Two,' he said.
(GBr 1,4.24rr) 'Two indeed,' he said.
(GBr 1,4.24ss) 'A person (<s>puruṣa</s>) has two feet.'
(GBr 1,4.24tt) 'A person stands on two [feet].'
(GBr 1,4.24uu) 'The person is the sacrifice.'
(GBr 1,4.24vv) 'How many indeed?'

children.translated_text: (GBr 1,5.1p) Thus indeed seven <s>Agniṣṭomas</s> are completed in a month — thus is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [teaching]. ||1||

body.translated_text:
(GBr 1,5.1a) <s>Oṃ</s>. The <s>Abhiplava</s> is a six-day [rite].
(GBr 1,5.1b) For there are six days: <s>Jyotis</s>, <s>Gau</s>, <s>Āyu</s>, <s>Gau</s>, <s>Āyu</s>, <s>Jyotis</s>.
(GBr 1,5.1c) The <s>Abhiplava</s> is a five-day [rite].
(GBr 1,5.1d) For there are five days only.
(GBr 1,5.1e) For the first day is [also] the last day.
(GBr 1,5.1f) The <s>Abhiplava</s> is a four-day [rite].
(GBr 1,5.1g) For there are four <s>stomas</s> (praise-forms): <s>Trivṛt</s>, <s>Pañcadaśa</s>, <s>Saptadaśa</s>, and <s>Ekaviṃśa</s>.
(GBr 1,5.1h) The <s>Abhiplava</s> is a three-day [rite].
(GBr 1,5.1i) Threefold is the repetition: <s>Jyotis</s>, <s>Gau</s>, <s>Āyu</s>.
(GBr 1,5.1j) The <s>Abhiplava</s> is a two-day [rite].
(GBr 1,5.1k) For there are just two <s>sāmans</s> (chants): the <s>Bṛhat</s> and the <s>Rathantara</s>.
(GBr 1,5.1l) The <s>Abhiplava</s> is a one-day [rite].
(GBr 1,5.1m) For it is sustained by the <s>stomas</s> of the one-day [rite].

children.translated_text: (GBr 1,5.2z) Thus indeed, one who knows this used to say this — thus is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [teaching]. ||2||

body.translated_text:
(GBr 1,5.2a) Now then, the footholds of firm ground (<s>gādhapratiṣṭhā</s>).
(GBr 1,5.2b) Those who are consecrated for the year-long [rite] indeed cross an ocean.
(GBr 1,5.2c) For them, the opening <s>Atirātra</s> is the fording-place.
(GBr 1,5.2d) For they cross by means of the fording-place.
(GBr 1,5.2e) Just as one would cross the ocean by a ford — such is that.
(GBr 1,5.2f) The firm ground, the foothold, is the twenty-fourth day — like [a place in] waist-deep or neck-deep [water] from which one might rest and bathe — such is that.
(GBr 1,5.2g) The <s>Abhiplava</s> is the bathing [area].
(GBr 1,5.2h) The <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> [rite] is [also] for bathing.
(GBr 1,5.2i) The firm ground, the foothold, is the <s>Abhijit</s> [day] — like [a place in] waist-deep or neck-deep [water] from which one might rest and bathe — such is that.
(GBr 1,5.2j) The first <s>Svarasāman</s> [day] is 'waist-deep.'
(GBr 1,5.2k) The second is 'knee-deep.'
(GBr 1,5.2l) The third is 'ankle-deep.'
(GBr 1,5.2m) The island, the foothold, is the <s>Viṣuvat</s> (solstice [day]) — like [a place in] waist-deep or neck-deep [water] from which one might rest and bathe — such is that.
(GBr 1,5.2n) The first [<s>Svarasāman</s>] on the return side is 'ankle-deep.'
(GBr 1,5.2o) The second is 'knee-deep.'
(GBr 1,5.2p) The third is 'waist-deep.'
(GBr 1,5.2q) The firm ground, the foothold, is the <s>Viśvajit</s> [day] — like [a place in] waist-deep or neck-deep [water] from which one might rest and bathe — such is that.
(GBr 1,5.2r) The <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> [rite] is for bathing; the <s>Abhiplava</s> is for bathing; the <s>Gavāyuṣī</s> [days] are for bathing; the <s>Daśarātra</s> (ten-day rite) is for bathing.
(GBr 1,5.2s) The firm ground, the foothold, is the <s>Mahāvrata</s> [day] — like [a place in] waist-deep or neck-deep [water] from which one might rest and bathe — such is that.
(GBr 1,5.2t) For them, the closing <s>Atirātra</s> is the fording-place.
(GBr 1,5.2u) For they ascend [from the ocean] by means of the fording-place.
(GBr 1,5.2v) Just as one would emerge from the ocean by a ford — such is that.
(GBr 1,5.2w) Now, <s>Śvetaketu Āruṇeya</s> (son of <s>Āruṇi</s>) used to say: 'I am consecrated for the year-long [rite]!'

body.translated_text:
(GBr 1,5.3a) A person (<s>puruṣa</s>) indeed is the year.
(GBr 1,5.3b) His feet are the opening <s>Atirātra</s>.
(GBr 1,5.3c) For they set forth with their feet; of those [feet], what is white is the form of day.
(GBr 1,5.3d) What is dark is the form of night.
(GBr 1,5.3e) The nails are the form of the <s>nakṣatras</s> (stars).
(GBr 1,5.3f) The body-hairs are [the form] of herbs and trees.
(GBr 1,5.3g) The thighs are the twenty-fourth day.
(GBr 1,5.3h) The chest is the <s>Abhiplava</s>.
(GBr 1,5.3i) The back is the <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> [rite].
(GBr 1,5.3j) The head itself is the <s>Trivṛt</s> [stoma], for the head is indeed threefold: skin, bone, marrow, and brain.
(GBr 1,5.3k) The neck is the <s>Pañcadaśa</s> [stoma], for there are fourteen vertebrae in it;
(GBr 1,5.3l) the vital force is the fifteenth.
(GBr 1,5.3m) Therefore, even with [vertebrae] that are soft, it bears a heavy burden.
(GBr 1,5.3n) Therefore the neck is the <s>Pañcadaśa</s>.
(GBr 1,5.3o) The chest is the <s>Saptadaśa</s> [stoma].
(GBr 1,5.3p) Eight are the ribs on one side, eight are on the other — the chest is the seventeenth.
(GBr 1,5.3q) Therefore the chest is the <s>Saptadaśa</s>.
(GBr 1,5.3r) The belly is the <s>Ekaviṃśa</s> [stoma].
(GBr 1,5.3s) For there are twenty <s>Kuntāpa</s> [entrails] within his belly — the belly is the twenty-first.
(GBr 1,5.3t) Therefore the belly is the <s>Ekaviṃśa</s>.
(GBr 1,5.3u) The sides are the <s>Triṇava</s> [stoma].
(GBr 1,5.3v) Thirteen are the ribs on one side, thirteen on the other — the sides are the <s>Triṇava</s> [twenty-seven].
(GBr 1,5.3w) Therefore the sides are the <s>Triṇava</s>.
(GBr 1,5.3x) The spine is the <s>Trayastriṃśa</s> [stoma].
(GBr 1,5.3y) For there are thirty-two vertebral joints in his back.
(GBr 1,5.3z) The spine is the thirty-third.
(GBr 1,5.3aa) Therefore the spine is the <s>Trayastriṃśa</s>.
(GBr 1,5.3bb) His right arm is the <s>Abhijit</s> [day].
(GBr 1,5.3cc) His three right vital breaths are the <s>Svarasāman</s> [days].
(GBr 1,5.3dd) The self (<s>ātman</s>) is the <s>Viṣuvat</s> (solstice day).
(GBr 1,5.3ee) His three left vital breaths are the <s>Svarasāman</s> [days] on the return side.
(GBr 1,5.3ff) His left arm is the <s>Viśvajit</s> [day].
(GBr 1,5.3gg) The <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> and <s>Abhiplava</s> have been stated.
(GBr 1,5.3hh) The two downward vital breaths are the <s>Gavāyuṣī</s> [days].
(GBr 1,5.3ii) The limbs are the <s>Daśarātra</s> (ten-day rite).

body.translated_text:
(GBr 1,5.4a) A person (<s>puruṣa</s>) indeed is the year.
(GBr 1,5.4b) His <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) is the opening <s>Atirātra</s>.
(GBr 1,5.4c) For they set forth by means of <s>prāṇa</s>.
(GBr 1,5.4d) Speech is the inaugural (<s>ārambhaṇīya</s>) day.
(GBr 1,5.4e) Whatever one undertakes, one undertakes by speech;
(GBr 1,5.4f) by speech alone does one undertake it.
(GBr 1,5.4g) His right hand is the <s>Abhiplava</s>.
(GBr 1,5.4h) This is the morning pressing, this the midday pressing, this the third pressing.
(GBr 1,5.4i) In the seat of the <s>Gāyatrī</s> [meter].
(GBr 1,5.4j) Therefore this [finger] is the shortest of his [fingers].
(GBr 1,5.4k) This is the morning pressing, this the midday pressing, this the third pressing.
(GBr 1,5.4l) In the seat of the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> [meter].
(GBr 1,5.4m) Therefore this [finger] is the longest of his [fingers].
(GBr 1,5.4n) This is the morning pressing, this the midday pressing, this the third pressing.
(GBr 1,5.4o) In the seat of the <s>Jagatī</s> [meter].
(GBr 1,5.4p) Therefore this [finger] is the longest of these two.
(GBr 1,5.4q) This is the morning pressing, this the midday pressing, this the third pressing.
(GBr 1,5.4r) In the seat of the <s>Paṅkti</s> [meter].
(GBr 1,5.4s) Broad indeed is the <s>Paṅkti</s>.
(GBr 1,5.4t) Therefore this [finger] is the broadest of them.
(GBr 1,5.4u) This is the morning pressing, this the midday pressing, this the third pressing.
(GBr 1,5.4v) In the seat of the <s>Virāj</s> [meter].
(GBr 1,5.4w) Food indeed is splendor (<s>śrī</s>).
(GBr 1,5.4x) <s>Virāj</s> is the eating of food.
(GBr 1,5.4y) For the securing of the eating of food [and] of splendor.
(GBr 1,5.4z) Therefore this [finger] is the longest of them.
(GBr 1,5.4aa) This is the morning pressing, this the midday pressing, this the third pressing.
(GBr 1,5.4bb) In the seat of the <s>Atichandas</s> (hyper-meter).
(GBr 1,5.4cc) <s>Atichandas</s> indeed is the seat of the meters.
(GBr 1,5.4dd) Therefore this [the palm] is the broadest board.
(GBr 1,5.4ee) This is the morning pressing, this the midday pressing, this the third pressing.
(GBr 1,5.4ff) From this side and that side is the <s>Abhiplava</s>; from this side the self (<s>ātman</s>) is the <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s>.
(GBr 1,5.4gg) The <s>Abhiplava</s> floats, as it were.
(GBr 1,5.4hh) The <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> stands firm, as it were.
(GBr 1,5.4ii) For one floats, as it were, with the limbs.
(GBr 1,5.4jj) One stands firm, as it were, with the self.
(GBr 1,5.4kk) His right ear is the <s>Abhijit</s> [day].
(GBr 1,5.4ll) The white of his right eye is the first <s>Svarasāman</s> [day].
(GBr 1,5.4mm) The dark [part] is the second.
(GBr 1,5.4nn) The pupil is the third.
(GBr 1,5.4oo) The two nostrils are the <s>Viṣuvat</s> (solstice day); the pupil itself is the first <s>Svarasāman</s> on the return side.
(GBr 1,5.4pp) The dark [part] is the second.
(GBr 1,5.4qq) The white is the third.
(GBr 1,5.4rr) His left ear is the <s>Viśvajit</s> [day].
(GBr 1,5.4ss) The <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> and <s>Abhiplava</s> have been stated.
(GBr 1,5.4tt) The two downward vital breaths are the <s>Gavāyuṣī</s> [days].
(GBr 1,5.4uu) The limbs are the <s>Daśarātra</s> (ten-day rite).

body.translated_text: The <s>puruṣa</s> (man/person) is indeed the year. '<s>Puruṣa</s>' is one; 'year' is one — therein they are equal. Two day-and-nights belong to the year; two <s>prāṇas</s> (vital breaths) belong to this person — therein they are equal. Three indeed are the seasons of the year; three are these <s>prāṇas</s> of the person — therein they are equal. Six indeed are the seasons of the year; six are these <s>prāṇas</s> of the person — therein they are equal. Seven indeed are the seasons of the year; seven are these <s>prāṇas</s> of the person — therein they are equal. Twelve months belong to the year; twelve are these <s>prāṇas</s> of the person — therein they are equal. Thirteen months belong to the year; thirteen are these <s>prāṇas</s> of the person — therein they are equal. Twenty-four half-months belong to the year; this person is twenty-four — twenty fingers and four limbs — therein they are equal. Twenty-six half-months belong to the year; this person is twenty-six — 'in twenty-six is the firm ground' — therein they are equal. Three hundred and sixty day-and-nights belong to the year; exactly that many are the <s>prāṇas</s> of the person — therein they are equal. Seven hundred and twenty days and nights belong to the year; exactly that many are the bones and marrows of the person — therein they are equal. Fourteen hundred and forty half-days and half-nights belong to the year; exactly that many are the gross flesh-parts of the person — therein they are equal. Two thousand eight hundred and eighty quarter-days and quarter-nights belong to the year; exactly that many are the sinews and tendons of the person — therein they are equal. Ten thousand eight hundred <s>muhūrtas</s> (moments) belong to the year; exactly that many are the fine membranes of the person — therein they are equal. However many <s>muhūrtas</s>, fifteen times that many are the <s>prāṇas</s>; however many <s>prāṇas</s>, fifteen times that many are the <s>apānas</s>; however many <s>apānas</s>, fifteen times that many are the <s>vyānas</s>; however many <s>vyānas</s>, fifteen times that many are the <s>samānas</s>; however many <s>samānas</s>, fifteen times that many are the <s>udānas</s>; however many <s>udānas</s>, fifteen times that many are the 'and-so-forths'; however many 'and-so-forths,' that many are the 'just-nows'; however many 'just-nows,' that many are the sweat-ducts; however many sweat-ducts, that many are the quick-passages; however many quick-passages, that many are the hair-pores; however many hair-pores, fifteen times that many are the rain-streams that fall — that is the measure of a hundred <s>krośas</s>. And this is stated by the <s>Ṛc</s>: 'Apart from exertion, going about, whether sitting or even sleeping — how many times does a person breathe in and breathe out in a day-and-night in a moment? One hundred times one hundred, in the course of a year, eight hundred <s>muhūrtas</s> — which they call of the year — in a day-and-night equally, how many times does a person breathe in and breathe out?' — thus is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. || 5 ||

children.translated_text: They approach thirty <s>ṣaḍahas</s> (six-day periods) before the <s>viṣuvat</s>, thirty after.

children.text: (GBr_1,5.6g) saiṣā saṃvatsarasya samatā
children.translated_text: This is the symmetry of the year.

children.text: (GBr_1,5.6h) sa ya evam etāṃ saṃvatsarasya samatāṃ veda saṃvatsareṇa sātmā saloko bhūtvā devān apyetīti brahmaṇam || 6 ||
children.translated_text: He who knows thus this symmetry of the year — having become one in self and world with the year, he goes to the gods' — thus is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. || 6 ||

body.translated_text: The symmetry of the year is to be known — thus indeed said <s>Vāsyu</s>: 'They approach one <s>atirātra</s> before the <s>viṣuvat</s> (solstice), one after. They approach fifty-three <s>agniṣṭomas</s> before the <s>viṣuvat</s>, fifty-three after. They approach one hundred and twenty <s>ukthyas</s> before the <s>viṣuvat</s>, one hundred and twenty after. They approach six <s>ṣoḍaśins</s> before the <s>viṣuvat</s>, six after.

children.text: (GBr_1,5.7s) sa ya evam etān yajñakramān veda yajñena sātmā saloko bhūtvā devān apyetīti brāhmaṇam || 7 ||
children.translated_text: He who knows thus these sequences of sacrifices — having become one in self and world with the sacrifice, he goes to the gods' — thus is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. || 7 ||

body.translated_text: Now then, the sequence of sacrifices: The establishment of fires (<s>agnyādheya</s>); from the establishment of fires, the full offering (<s>pūrṇāhuti</s>); from the full offering, the <s>agnihotra</s>; from the <s>agnihotra</s>, the new-and-full-moon sacrifices; from the new-and-full-moon sacrifices, the first-fruits offering (<s>āgrayaṇa</s>); from the first-fruits offering, the four-monthly sacrifices (<s>cāturmāsya</s>); from the four-monthly sacrifices, the animal sacrifice (<s>paśubandha</s>); from the animal sacrifice, the <s>agniṣṭoma</s>; from the <s>agniṣṭoma</s>, the royal consecration (<s>rājasūya</s>); from the royal consecration, the <s>vājapeya</s>; from the <s>vājapeya</s>, the horse sacrifice (<s>aśvamedha</s>); from the horse sacrifice, the human sacrifice (<s>puruṣamedha</s>); from the human sacrifice, the all-sacrifice (<s>sarvamedha</s>); from the all-sacrifice, those with <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fees); from those with <s>dakṣiṇā</s>, those without <s>dakṣiṇā</s>;

children.text: (GBr_1,5.8z) tad yā dakṣiṇā ānayat tābhir ātmānaṃ niṣkrīṇīya
children.translated_text: Thus, having given himself [and attained] infinity, he attained infinity. Then, with whatever <s>dakṣiṇā</s> he brought, with those he redeemed himself.

children.text: (GBr_1,5.8aa) tasmād etena jyotiṣṭomenāgniṣṭomenātmaniṣkrayaṇena sahasradakṣiṇena pṛṣṭhaśamanīyena tvareta
children.translated_text: Therefore, one should hasten with this <s>jyotiṣṭoma</s>, an <s>agniṣṭoma</s>, a self-redemption with a thousand <s>dakṣiṇā</s>, a back-pacifying [sacrifice].

children.text: (GBr_1,5.8bb) yo hy aniṣṭvā pṛṣṭhaśamanīyena praityātmānaṃ so 'niṣkrīya praitīti brāhmaṇam || 8 ||
children.translated_text: For he who departs without having sacrificed with the back-pacifying [rite] departs without having redeemed himself — thus is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. || 8 ||

body.translated_text: <s>Prajāpati</s> desired: 'May I attain infinity.' He established the sacred fires and sacrificed with the full offering. He saw only the end. He sacrificed with the <s>agnihotra</s> — he saw only the end. He sacrificed with the new-and-full-moon offerings — he saw only the end. He sacrificed with the first-fruits offering — he saw only the end. He sacrificed with the four-monthly offerings — he saw only the end. He sacrificed with the animal sacrifice — he saw only the end. He sacrificed with the <s>agniṣṭoma</s> — he saw only the end. He sacrificed with the royal consecration and assumed the name 'king' — he saw only the end. He sacrificed with the <s>vājapeya</s> and assumed the name 'emperor' — he saw only the end. He sacrificed with the horse-sacrifice and assumed the name 'self-ruler' — he saw only the end. He sacrificed with the human-sacrifice and assumed the name 'universal ruler' — he saw only the end. He sacrificed with the all-sacrifice and assumed the name 'all-ruler' — he saw only the end. He sacrificed with continuous [sessions] with <s>dakṣiṇā</s> — he saw only the end. He sacrificed with continuous [sessions] without <s>dakṣiṇā</s> — he saw only the end. He sacrificed at the end with a <s>sattra</s> (sacrificial session) having <s>atirātras</s> on both sides. He gave speech to the <s>hotṛ</s>, breath to the <s>adhvaryu</s>, sight to the <s>udgātṛ</s>, mind to the <s>brahman</s>, his limbs to the assistant priests, his self to the assembled [priests].

children.translated_text: 'By the sound <s>hiṃ</s>,' one should say.

children.text: (GBr_1,5.9u) saiṣā saṃvatsare yajñakratūnām apītiḥ
children.translated_text: This is the entry into the sacrificial rites in [the course of] a year.

children.text: (GBr_1,5.9v) sa ya evam etāṃ saṃvatsare yajñakratūnām apītiṃ veda yajñena sātmā saloko bhūtvā devān apy etīti brāhmaṇam || 9 ||
children.translated_text: He who knows thus this entry into the sacrificial rites in a year — having become one in self and world with the sacrifice, he goes to the gods' — thus is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. || 9 ||

body.translated_text: When those who sit for a year undertake the consecration (<s>dīkṣā</s>) for a year — how does their <s>agnihotra</s> remain uninterrupted? 'By observance (<s>vrata</s>),' one should say. How does their new-moon [sacrifice] remain uninterrupted? 'By curds and a sacrificial cake,' one should say. How does their full-moon [sacrifice] remain uninterrupted? 'By ghee and a sacrificial cake,' one should say. How does their first-fruits offering remain uninterrupted? 'By a <s>Soma</s> oblation,' one should say. How do their four-monthly sacrifices remain uninterrupted? 'By the milk offering,' one should say. How does their animal sacrifice remain uninterrupted? 'By an animal and a sacrificial cake,' one should say. How does their <s>Soma</s> sacrifice remain uninterrupted? 'By the <s>grahas</s> (cups),' one should say. How does their household sacrifice remain uninterrupted? 'By the grain-porridge offerings,' one should say. How does their ancestor-sacrifice remain uninterrupted? 'By the <s>aupāsana</s> (domestic fire) offerings,' one should say. How does their sexual union remain uninterrupted?

children.translated_text: (GBr 1,5.10jj) This indeed is the <s>Viśvajit</s> which is the equivalent of the thousand-year [sacrifice].

children.text: (GBr_1,5.10kk) eṣa ha prajānāṃ prajāpatir yad viśvajid iti brāhmaṇam || 10 ||
children.translated_text: (GBr 1,5.10kk) This [<s>Viśvajit</s>] is the <s>Prajāpati</s> (Lord of Creatures) of [all] creatures — thus is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [teaching]. [10]

body.translated_text: (GBr 1,5.10a) The gods indeed consecrated themselves for a thousand-year [sacrifice]. (GBr 1,5.10b) Five hundred years had passed for them, and then all this became exhausted — the <s>stomas</s> (praise-forms), the <s>pṛṣṭhas</s> (back-chants), and the <s>śastras</s> (recitations). (GBr 1,5.10c) The gods deliberated: 'Let us find that sacrificial rite which is the equivalent of the thousand-year [sacrifice]. (GBr 1,5.10d) For what man is there who could sacrifice with a thousand-year [sacrifice]?' (GBr 1,5.10e) They saw, in the middle of the sacrifice, that which is unwearied (<s>ayātayāma</s>). (GBr 1,5.10f) With that unwearied [element], they saw the distribution that was in the <s>Veda</s> in five [parts] — in the <s>Ṛc</s>, the <s>Yajus</s>, the <s>Sāman</s>, the peaceful (<s>śānta</s>), and the terrible (<s>ghora</s>). (GBr 1,5.10g) These indeed are the five exclamations (<s>vyāhṛtis</s>): '<s>O śrāvaya</s>' (Make him hear!), '<s>Astu śrauṣaṭ</s>' (Let him hear!), '<s>Yaja</s>' (Sacrifice!), '<s>Ye yajāmahe</s>' (We who sacrifice), and '<s>Vauṣaṭ</s>!' (GBr 1,5.10h) The gods deliberated: 'Let us find that sacrificial rite which is the equivalent of the thousand-year [sacrifice]. (GBr 1,5.10i) For what man is there who could sacrifice with a thousand-year [sacrifice]?' (GBr 1,5.10j) Then they saw the <s>Tāpaścit</s> (fire-piling penance) as the direct equivalent of the thousand-year [sacrifice]. (GBr 1,5.10k) For these same <s>stomas</s> are [in it], these same <s>pṛṣṭhas</s>, these same <s>śastras</s>. (GBr 1,5.10l) He indeed proceeds for twelve months with consecrations (<s>dīkṣās</s>), for twelve months with preparatory rites (<s>upasads</s>), and for twelve months with pressings (<s>sutyas</s>). (GBr 1,5.10m) And because he proceeds for twelve months with consecrations and twelve months with preparatory rites, thereby he attains the Fire and the Sun (<s>Agni</s> and <s>Arka</s>). (GBr 1,5.10n) And because he proceeds for twelve months with pressings, thereby he attains this great recitation (<s>Mahad Uktham</s>). (GBr 1,5.10o) The gods deliberated: 'Let us find that sacrificial rite which is the equivalent of the thousand-year [sacrifice]. (GBr 1,5.10p) For what man is there who could sacrifice with a thousand-year [sacrifice]?' (GBr 1,5.10q) Then they saw the year-long [sacrifice] (<s>saṃvatsara</s>) as the direct equivalent of the <s>Tāpaścit</s>. (GBr 1,5.10r) For these same <s>stomas</s> are [in it], these same <s>pṛṣṭhas</s>, these same <s>śastras</s>. (GBr 1,5.10s) The gods deliberated: 'Let us find that sacrificial rite which is the equivalent of the thousand-year [sacrifice]. (GBr 1,5.10t) For what man is there who could sacrifice with a thousand-year [sacrifice]?' (GBr 1,5.10u) Then they saw the twelve-day [sacrifice] (<s>dvādaśāha</s>) as the direct equivalent of the year-long [sacrifice]. (GBr 1,5.10v) For these same <s>stomas</s> are [in it], these same <s>pṛṣṭhas</s>, these same <s>śastras</s>. (GBr 1,5.10w) He indeed proceeds for twelve days with consecrations, for twelve days with preparatory rites, and for twelve days with pressings. (GBr 1,5.10x) And because he proceeds for twelve days with consecrations and twelve days with preparatory rites, thereby he attains the Fire and the Sun. (GBr 1,5.10y) And because he proceeds for twelve days with pressings, thereby he attains this great recitation. (GBr 1,5.10z) The gods deliberated: 'Let us find that sacrificial rite which is the equivalent of the thousand-year [sacrifice]. (GBr 1,5.10aa) For what man is there who could sacrifice with a thousand-year [sacrifice]?' (GBr 1,5.10bb) Then they saw the <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> six-day [rite] (<s>ṣaḍaha</s>) as the direct equivalent of the twelve-day [sacrifice]. (GBr 1,5.10cc) For these same <s>stomas</s> are [in it], these same <s>pṛṣṭhas</s>, these same <s>śastras</s>. (GBr 1,5.10dd) The gods deliberated: 'Let us find that sacrificial rite which is the equivalent of the thousand-year [sacrifice]. (GBr 1,5.10ee) For what man is there who could sacrifice with a thousand-year [sacrifice]?' (GBr 1,5.10ff) Then they saw the <s>Viśvajit</s> (all-conquering [rite]) as the direct equivalent of the <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> six-day [rite]. (GBr 1,5.10gg) For these same <s>stomas</s> are [in it], these same <s>pṛṣṭhas</s>, these same <s>śastras</s>. (GBr 1,5.10hh) The gods deliberated: 'Let us find that sacrificial rite which is the equivalent of the thousand-year [sacrifice].'

children.translated_text: (GBr 1,5.11i) He indeed is the learned, omniscient <s>Brahmā</s> priest who knows the [lore of] <s>Bhṛgu</s> and <s>Aṅgiras</s>.

children.translated_text: (GBr 1,5.11j) These indeed are the pacifiers and protectors of all this.
