children.translated_text: (GBr 1,5.11k) Therefore the <s>Brahmā</s> priest has [the <s>Hotṛ</s>] recite at the <s>Bahiṣpavamāna</s> (outer purification chant). [11]

body.translated_text: (GBr 1,5.11a) <s>Prajāpati</s> indeed spoke to <s>Puruṣa Nārāyaṇa</s>: 'Sacrifice! Sacrifice!' (GBr 1,5.11b) He replied: 'You keep saying "Sacrifice! Sacrifice!" to me. (GBr 1,5.11c) Three times already have the <s>Vasus</s> injured me at the morning pressing, the <s>Rudras</s> at the midday pressing, and the <s>Ādityas</s> at the third pressing. (GBr 1,5.11d) The blessings are merely of the sacrificial ground — "for the sacrificial ground" — such are the blessings. I indeed know this: in the sacrifice the <s>Vasus</s> [injure] at the morning pressing, the <s>Rudras</s> at the midday pressing, and the <s>Ādityas</s> at the third pressing. The blessings are merely of the sacrificial ground — "for the sacrificial ground" — such are the blessings. Knowing ones should surely make you perform the sacrifice. (GBr 1,5.11e) Those indeed are ignorant where the <s>Hotṛ</s> does not know the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, the <s>Adhvaryu</s> does not know the <s>Yajurveda</s>, the <s>Udgātṛ</s> does not know the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, and the <s>Brahmā</s> priest does not know the <s>Atharvaveda</s> (<s>Bhṛgv-Aṅgiras</s>). (GBr 1,5.11f) Sacrifice indeed! Come, I shall tell you that. (GBr 1,5.11g) Just as a jewel on a thread — the thread is these <s>Ukthya</s> days; or rather, like a thread on a jewel.' (GBr 1,5.11h) Therefore, one who is omniscient should be made the <s>Brahmā</s> priest.

body.text:
(GBr_1,5.12a) śyeno 'si gāyatrachandā
(GBr_1,5.12b) anu tvārabhe
(GBr_1,5.12c) svasti mā saṃpārayeti
(GBr_1,5.12d) sa yad āha śyeno 'sīti somaṃ vā etad āha_
(GBr_1,5.12e) eṣa ha vā agnir bhūtvāsmiṃl loke saṃśāyayati
(GBr_1,5.12f) tad yat saṃśāyayati tasmāc cheyanas
(GBr_1,5.12g) tac cheyanasya śyenatvam_
(GBr_1,5.12h) sa yad āha gāyatrachandā anutvārabha iti gāyatreṇa chandasā vasurbhir devaiḥ prātaḥsavane 'smiṃl loke 'gniṃ santam anvārabhate
(GBr_1,5.12i) sa yad āha svasti mā saṃpārayeti gāyatreṇaiva chandasā vasubhir devaiḥ prātaḥsavane 'smiṃl loke 'gninā devena svasti mā saṃpārayeti gāyatreṇaivainaṃ tac chandasā vasubhir devaiḥ prātaḥsavane 'smiṃl loke 'gninā devena svasti saṃpadyate ya evaṃ veda
body.translated_text: (GBr 1,5.12a) 'You are the eagle (<s>Śyena</s>), of the <s>Gāyatrī</s> meter.' (GBr 1,5.12b) 'I take hold of you.' (GBr 1,5.12c) 'Carry me safely across!' (GBr 1,5.12d) When he says 'You are the eagle,' he is addressing <s>Soma</s>. (GBr 1,5.12e) For this [<s>Soma</s>] indeed, having become <s>Agni</s>, causes [beings] to rest in this world. (GBr 1,5.12f) Because he causes to rest (<s>saṃśāyayati</s>), therefore he is <s>Śeyana</s> (resting one). (GBr 1,5.12g) That is the eagle-nature (<s>śyenatva</s>) of the eagle. (GBr 1,5.12h) When he says 'Of the <s>Gāyatrī</s> meter, I take hold of you' — by the <s>Gāyatrī</s> meter, with the <s>Vasu</s> gods, at the morning pressing, in this world, he takes hold of <s>Agni</s> who abides [here]. (GBr 1,5.12i) When he says 'Carry me safely across' — by the <s>Gāyatrī</s> meter itself, with the <s>Vasu</s> gods, at the morning pressing, in this world, through the god <s>Agni</s>, 'Carry me safely across' — thus by the <s>Gāyatrī</s> meter, with the <s>Vasu</s> gods, at the morning pressing, in this world, through the god <s>Agni</s>, he is safely carried across — he who knows thus.

body.text:
(GBr_1,5.13a) atha mādhyaṃdine pavamāne vācayati samrāḍ asi triṣṭupchandā
(GBr_1,5.13b) anu tvārabhe
(GBr_1,5.13c) svasti mā saṃpārayeti
(GBr_1,5.13d) sa yad āha samrāḍ asīti somaṃ vā etad āha_
(GBr_1,5.13e) eṣa ha vai vāyurbhūtvāntarikṣaloke samrājati
(GBr_1,5.13f) tad yat samrājati tasmāt samrāṭ
(GBr_1,5.13g) tat samrājasya samrāṭtvam_

children.text: (GBr_1,5.13h) sa yad āha triṣṭupchandā anu tvārabha iti traiṣṭubhena chandasā rudrair devair mādhyaṃdine savane 'ntarikṣaloke vāyuṃ santam anvārabhate
children.translated_text: (GBr 1,5.13h) When he says 'Of the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> meter, I take hold of you' — by the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> meter, with the <s>Rudra</s> gods, at the midday pressing, in the intermediate space, he takes hold of <s>Vāyu</s> who abides [there].

children.text: (GBr_1,5.13i) sa yad āha svasti mā saṃpārayeti traiṣṭubhenaiva chandasā rudrair devair mādhyaṃdine savane antarikṣaloke vāyunā devena svasti mā saṃpārayeti
children.translated_text: (GBr 1,5.13i) When he says 'Carry me safely across' — by the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> meter, with the <s>Rudra</s> gods, at the midday pressing, in the intermediate space, through the god <s>Vāyu</s>, 'Carry me safely across' [he says].

children.text: (GBr_1,5.13j) traiṣṭubhenaivainaṃ tac chandasā rudrair devair mādhyaṃdine savane antarikṣaloke vāyunā devena svasti saṃpadyate ya evaṃ veda || 13 ||
children.translated_text: (GBr 1,5.13j) By the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> meter itself, with the <s>Rudra</s> gods, at the midday pressing, in the intermediate space, through the god <s>Vāyu</s>, he is safely carried across — he who knows thus. [13]

body.translated_text: (GBr 1,5.13a) Then at the midday <s>Pavamāna</s> (purification chant), [the <s>Brahmā</s>] has [the <s>Hotṛ</s>] recite: 'You are the sovereign (<s>Samrāj</s>), of the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> meter.' (GBr 1,5.13b) 'I take hold of you.' (GBr 1,5.13c) 'Carry me safely across!' (GBr 1,5.13d) When he says 'You are the sovereign,' he is addressing <s>Soma</s>. (GBr 1,5.13e) For this [<s>Soma</s>] indeed, having become <s>Vāyu</s>, rules as sovereign in the intermediate space (<s>antarikṣa</s>). (GBr 1,5.13f) Because he rules as sovereign (<s>samrājati</s>), therefore he is the <s>Samrāj</s>. (GBr 1,5.13g) That is the sovereignty of the sovereign.

body.text:
(GBr_1,5.14a) athārbhave pavamāne vācayati svaro 'si gayo 'si jagacchandā
(GBr_1,5.14b) anu tvārabhe
(GBr_1,5.14c) svasti mā saṃpārayeti
(GBr_1,5.14d) sa yad āha svaro 'sīti somaṃ vā etad āha_
(GBr_1,5.14e) eṣa ha vai sūryo bhūtvāmuṣmiṃl loke svarati
(GBr_1,5.14f) tad yat svarati tasmāt svaras
(GBr_1,5.14g) tat svarasya svaratvam_
(GBr_1,5.14h) sa yad āha gayo 'sīti somaṃ vā etad āha_
(GBr_1,5.14i) eṣa ha vai candramā bhūtvā sarvāṃl lokān gacchati
(GBr_1,5.14j) tad yad gacchati tasmād gayas

children.text: (GBr_1,5.14k) tad gayasya gayatvam_
children.translated_text: (GBr 1,5.14k) That is the song-nature of the song.

children.text: (GBr_1,5.14l) sa yad āha jagacchandā anu tvārabha iti jāgatena chandasādityair devais tṛtīyasavane 'muṣmiṃl loke sūryaṃ santam anvārabhate
children.translated_text: (GBr 1,5.14l) When he says 'Of the <s>Jagatī</s> meter, I take hold of you' — by the <s>Jagatī</s> meter, with the <s>Āditya</s> gods, at the third pressing, in that [heavenly] world, he takes hold of <s>Sūrya</s> who abides [there].

children.text: (GBr_1,5.14m) sa yad āha svasti mā saṃpārayeti jāgatenaiva chandasādityair devais tṛtīyasavane 'muṣmiṃl loke sūryeṇa devena svasti mā saṃpārayeti jāgatenaivainaṃ tac chandasādityair devais tṛtīyasavane 'muṣmiṃl loke sūryeṇa devena svasti saṃpadyate ya evaṃ veda || 14 ||
children.translated_text: (GBr 1,5.14m) When he says 'Carry me safely across' — by the <s>Jagatī</s> meter, with the <s>Āditya</s> gods, at the third pressing, in that [heavenly] world, through the god <s>Sūrya</s>, 'Carry me safely across' — thus by the <s>Jagatī</s> meter itself, with the <s>Āditya</s> gods, at the third pressing, in that [heavenly] world, through the god <s>Sūrya</s>, he is safely carried across — he who knows thus. [14]

body.translated_text: (GBr 1,5.14a) Then at the <s>Ārbhava</s> (third) <s>Pavamāna</s>, [the <s>Brahmā</s>] has [the <s>Hotṛ</s>] recite: 'You are the <s>Svara</s> (sound), you are the <s>Gaya</s> (song), of the <s>Jagatī</s> meter.' (GBr 1,5.14b) 'I take hold of you.' (GBr 1,5.14c) 'Carry me safely across!' (GBr 1,5.14d) When he says 'You are the sound,' he is addressing <s>Soma</s>. (GBr 1,5.14e) For this [<s>Soma</s>] indeed, having become <s>Sūrya</s> (the Sun), resounds in that [heavenly] world. (GBr 1,5.14f) Because he resounds (<s>svarati</s>), therefore he is <s>Svara</s>. (GBr 1,5.14g) That is the sound-nature of the sound. (GBr 1,5.14h) When he says 'You are the song,' he is addressing <s>Soma</s>. (GBr 1,5.14i) For this [<s>Soma</s>] indeed, having become <s>Candramā</s> (the Moon), goes to all the worlds. (GBr 1,5.14j) Because he goes (<s>gacchati</s>), therefore he is <s>Gaya</s>.

body.text:
(GBr_1,5.15a) atha saṃsthite saṃsthite savane vācayati mayi bhargo mayi maho mayi yaśo mayi sarvam iti
(GBr_1,5.15b) pṛthivy eva bhargo 'ntarikṣa eva maho dyaur eva yaśo 'pa eva sarvam
(GBr_1,5.15c) agnir eva bhargo vāyur eva maha āditya eva yaśaś candramā eva sarvam_ [ed. ādityā]
(GBr_1,5.15d) vasava eva bhargo rudrā eva maha ādityā eva yaśo viśvedevā eva sarvam_
(GBr_1,5.15e) gāyatry eva bhargas triṣṭub eva maho jagaty eva yaśo 'nuṣṭub eva sarvam_
(GBr_1,5.15f) prācy eva bhargaḥ pratīcy eva maha udīcy eva yaśo dakṣiṇaiva sarvam_
(GBr_1,5.15g) vasanta eva bhargo grīṣma eva maho varṣā eva yaśaḥ śarad eva sarvam_
(GBr_1,5.15h) trivṛd eva bhargaḥ pañcadaśa eva mahaḥ saptadaśa eva yaśa ekaviṃśa eva sarvam

children.text: (GBr_1,5.15i) ṛgveda eva bhargo yajurveda eva mahaḥ sāmaveda eva yaśo brahmaveda eva sarvam_
children.translated_text: (GBr 1,5.15i) The <s>Ṛgveda</s> is splendor, the <s>Yajurveda</s> is greatness, the <s>Sāmaveda</s> is glory, and the <s>Brahmaveda</s> (<s>Atharvaveda</s>) is everything.

children.text: (GBr_1,5.15j) hotaiva bhargo 'dhvaryur eva maha udgātaiva yaśo brahmaiva sarvam_
children.translated_text: (GBr 1,5.15j) The <s>Hotṛ</s> is splendor, the <s>Adhvaryu</s> is greatness, the <s>Udgātṛ</s> is glory, and the <s>Brahmā</s> [priest] is everything.

children.text: (GBr_1,5.15k) vāg eva bhargaḥ prāṇa eva mahaś cakṣur eva yaśo mana eva sarvam || 15 ||
children.translated_text: (GBr 1,5.15k) Speech (<s>Vāk</s>) is splendor, breath (<s>Prāṇa</s>) is greatness, sight (<s>Cakṣus</s>) is glory, and mind (<s>Manas</s>) is everything. [15]

body.translated_text: (GBr 1,5.15a) Then, when each pressing is completed, [the <s>Brahmā</s>] has [the <s>Hotṛ</s>] recite: 'In me [be] splendor (<s>bhargas</s>), in me [be] greatness (<s>mahas</s>), in me [be] glory (<s>yaśas</s>), in me [be] everything (<s>sarvam</s>).' (GBr 1,5.15b) The earth is splendor, the intermediate space is greatness, heaven is glory, the waters are everything. (GBr 1,5.15c) <s>Agni</s> is splendor, <s>Vāyu</s> is greatness, <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun) is glory, <s>Candramā</s> (the Moon) is everything. (GBr 1,5.15d) The <s>Vasus</s> are splendor, the <s>Rudras</s> are greatness, the <s>Ādityas</s> are glory, the <s>Viśvedevas</s> (All-gods) are everything. (GBr 1,5.15e) The <s>Gāyatrī</s> is splendor, the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> is greatness, the <s>Jagatī</s> is glory, the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> is everything. (GBr 1,5.15f) The eastern [direction] is splendor, the western is greatness, the northern is glory, the southern is everything. (GBr 1,5.15g) Spring is splendor, summer is greatness, the rains are glory, autumn is everything. (GBr 1,5.15h) The <s>Trivṛt</s> (ninefold) is splendor, the <s>Pañcadaśa</s> (fifteenfold) is greatness, the <s>Saptadaśa</s> (seventeenfold) is glory, and the <s>Ekaviṃśa</s> (twenty-onefold) is everything.

body.text: (GBr_1,5.16a) sa yad āha mayi bharga iti pṛthivīm evaital lokānām ahāgniṃ devānāṃ vasūn devān devagaṇānāṃ gāyatraṃ chandasāṃ prācīṃ diśāṃ vasantam ṛtūnāṃ trivṛtaṃ stomānām ṛgvedaṃ vedānāṃ hautraṃ hotrakāṇāṃ vācam indriyāṇām || 16 ||
body.translated_text: (GBr 1,5.16a) When he says 'In me [be] splendor' — he thereby [invokes] the earth among the worlds, <s>Agni</s> among the gods, the <s>Vasus</s> among the divine hosts, the <s>Gāyatra</s> among the meters, the eastern among the directions, spring among the seasons, the <s>Trivṛt</s> among the <s>stomas</s>, the <s>Ṛgveda</s> among the <s>Vedas</s>, the <s>Hautra</s> (office of the <s>Hotṛ</s>) among the priestly functions, and speech among the faculties. [16]

body.text: (GBr_1,5.17a) sa yad āha mayi maha ity antarikṣam evaital lokānām āha vāyuṃ devānāṃ rudrān devān devagaṇānāṃ traiṣṭubhaṃ chandasāṃ pratīcīṃ diśāṃ grīṣmam ṛtūnāṃ pañcadaśaṃ stomānāṃ yajurvedaṃ vedānām ādhvaryavaṃ hotrakāṇāṃ prāṇam indriyāṇām || 17 ||
body.translated_text: (GBr 1,5.17a) When he says 'In me [be] greatness' — he thereby [invokes] the intermediate space among the worlds, <s>Vāyu</s> among the gods, the <s>Rudras</s> among the divine hosts, the <s>Traiṣṭubha</s> among the meters, the western [direction] among the directions, summer among the seasons, the <s>Pañcadaśa</s> among the <s>stomas</s>, the <s>Yajurveda</s> among the <s>Vedas</s>, the <s>Ādhvaryava</s> (office of the <s>Adhvaryu</s>) among the priestly functions, and breath among the faculties. [17]

body.text: (GBr_1,5.18a) sa yad āha mayi yaśa iti divam evaital lokānām āhādityaṃ devānām ādityān devagaṇānāṃ jāgataṃ chandasām udīcīṃ diśāṃ varṣā ṛtūnāṃ saptadaśaṃ stomānāṃ sāmavedaṃ vedānām audgātraṃ hotrakāṇāṃ cakṣur indriyāṇām || 17 ||
body.translated_text: (GBr 1,5.18a) When he says 'In me [be] glory' — he thereby [invokes] heaven among the worlds, <s>Āditya</s> among the gods, the <s>Ādityas</s> among the divine hosts, the <s>Jāgata</s> among the meters, the northern [direction] among the directions, the rains among the seasons, the <s>Saptadaśa</s> among the <s>stomas</s>, the <s>Sāmaveda</s> among the <s>Vedas</s>, the <s>Audgātra</s> (office of the <s>Udgātṛ</s>) among the priestly functions, and sight among the faculties. [17]

body.text: (GBr_1,5.19a) sa yad āha mayi sarvam ity apa evaital lokānām āha candramasaṃ devānāṃ viśvān devān devagaṇānām ānuṣṭubhaṃ chandasāṃ dakṣiṇāṃ diśāṃ śaradam ṛtūnām ekaviṃśaṃ stomānāṃ brahmavedaṃ vedānāṃ brahmatvaṃ hotrakāṇāṃ mana indriyāṇām || 18 ||
body.translated_text: (GBr 1,5.19a) When he says 'In me [be] everything' — he thereby [invokes] the waters among the worlds, <s>Candramā</s> (the Moon) among the gods, the <s>Viśvedevas</s> (All-gods) among the divine hosts, the <s>Ānuṣṭubha</s> among the meters, the southern [direction] among the directions, autumn among the seasons, the <s>Ekaviṃśa</s> among the <s>stomas</s>, the <s>Brahmaveda</s> (<s>Atharvaveda</s>) among the <s>Vedas</s>, the <s>Brahmatva</s> (office of the <s>Brahmā</s>) among the priestly functions, and mind among the faculties. [18]

body.text:
(GBr_1,5.20a) sa vā eṣa daśadhā catuḥ saṃpadyate
(GBr_1,5.20b) daśa ca ha vai catur virājo 'kṣarāṇi
(GBr_1,5.20c) taṃ garbhā upajīvanti
(GBr_1,5.20d) śrīr vai virāḍ
(GBr_1,5.20e) yaśo 'nnādyam_

children.text: (GBr_1,5.20f) śriyam eva tad virājaṃ yaśasy annādyo pratiṣṭhāpayati
children.translated_text: (GBr 1,5.20f) He thereby establishes <s>Śrī</s>, the <s>Virāj</s>, in glory and food.

children.text: (GBr_1,5.20g) pratiṣṭhantīr idaṃ sarvam anupratiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: (GBr 1,5.20g) As [these correspondences] become established, all this is established along with them.

children.text: (GBr_1,5.20h) pratitiṣṭhati prajayā paśubhir ya evaṃ veda || 20 ||
children.translated_text: (GBr 1,5.20h) He becomes established with offspring and cattle — he who knows thus. [20]

body.translated_text: (GBr 1,5.20a) This indeed amounts to four sets of ten. (GBr 1,5.20b) For ten times four are the syllables of the <s>Virāj</s> [meter]. (GBr 1,5.20c) Embryos live by it. (GBr 1,5.20d) <s>Śrī</s> (prosperity) is the <s>Virāj</s>. (GBr 1,5.20e) Glory and food [come from it].

body.text:
(GBr_1,5.21a) anarvāṇaṃ ha vai devaṃ dadhyaṅṅ āṅgirasa upasīdaṃ ha yajñasya śnuṣṭiṃ samaśnavāmaha iti
(GBr_1,5.21b) sa dadhyaṅṅ āṅgiraso 'bravīd yo vai saptadaśaṃ prajāpatiṃ yajñe 'nvitaṃ veda nāsya yajño riṣyate
(GBr_1,5.21c) na yajñapatiṃ riṣyanta iti
(GBr_1,5.21d) tā vā etāḥ pañca vyāhṛtayo bhavanty o śrāvayāstu śrauṣaḍ yaja ye yajāmahe vauṣaḍ iti
(GBr_1,5.21e) sa dadhyaṅṅ āṅgiraso 'bravīn na vayaṃ vidmo yadi brāhmaṇāḥ smo yady abrāhmaṇāḥ smo yadi tasyarṣeḥ smo vānyasyeti_
(GBr_1,5.21f) anarvāṇaś ca ha vā ṛtāvantaś ca pitaraḥ svadhāyām āvṛṣāyanta vayaṃ vadāmahai vayaṃ vadāmahā iti

children.text: (GBr_1,5.21g) so 'yāt svāyaṃbhuvo vā ṛtāvanto madayātāṃ na vayaṃ vadāmahā iti
children.translated_text: He [<s>Anarvāṇa</s>] went forth [saying]: 'O <s>Svāyambhuva</s>! Let the <s>Ṛtāvants</s> (truth-possessing ones) be delighted. We shall not speak.'

children.text: (GBr_1,5.21h) tasmāt pravare pravriyamāṇe vācayed devāḥ pitara iti tisraḥ_
children.translated_text: Therefore, when the <s>Pravara</s> (lineage declaration) is being recited, one should recite three [invocations]: '<s>Devāḥ</s>' (gods), '<s>Pitaraḥ</s>' (ancestors) [and a third].

children.text: (GBr_1,5.21i) ya eti saṃyajati sa bhavati yaś ca na brūte yaś ca na brūta iti brāhmaṇam || 21 ||
children.translated_text: He who performs the <s>saṃyāja</s> (joint sacrifice) becomes [successful], both he who speaks and he who does not speak — thus is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [teaching]. [21]

body.translated_text: <s>Dadhyaṅ Āṅgirasa</s> approached the divine <s>Anarvāṇa</s>, [saying]: 'May I attain the fullness of the sacrifice.' <s>Dadhyaṅ Āṅgirasa</s> said: 'He who knows the seventeen-fold <s>Prajāpati</s> as pervading the sacrifice — his sacrifice is not harmed, nor is the lord of the sacrifice harmed.' These five <s>vyāhṛtis</s> (sacred utterances) exist: '<s>O śrāvaya</s>' (make him hear), '<s>Astu śrauṣaṭ</s>' (let him listen), '<s>Yaja</s>' (sacrifice), '<s>Ye yajāmahe</s>' (we who sacrifice), and '<s>Vauṣaṭ</s>' (the offering call). <s>Dadhyaṅ Āṅgirasa</s> said: 'We do not know whether we are <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> or non-<s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, whether we belong to that <s>Ṛṣi</s> or to another.' <s>Anarvāṇa</s> and the <s>Ṛtāvants</s> (truth-possessing) ancestors, delighting in <s>Svadhā</s> (ancestral oblation), proclaimed: 'Let us speak, let us speak!'

body.text:
(GBr_1,5.22a) sāvitraṃ ha smaitaṃ pūrve purastāt paśum ālabhanta ity etarhi prājāpatyam_
(GBr_1,5.22b) yo hy eva savitā sa prajāpatir iti vadantas
(GBr_1,5.22c) tasmād u samupyāgnīṃs tena yajeran_
(GBr_1,5.22d) te samānadhiṣṇyā eva syur okhāsaṃbharaṇīyāyāḥ_
(GBr_1,5.22e) ukhāsaṃbharaṇīyāyāṃ vinyupayāgnīṃs tayā yajeran_
(GBr_1,5.22f) te nānādhiṣṇyā eva syur ā dīkṣaṇīyāyāḥ_
(GBr_1,5.22g) dīkṣaṇīyāyāṃ saṃnyupyāgnīṃs tayā yajeran_
(GBr_1,5.22h) te samānadhiṣṇyā eva syur odavasānīyāyāḥ_
(GBr_1,5.22i) udavasānīyāyāṃ vinyupyāgnīṃs tayā yajeran_
(GBr_1,5.22j) te nānādhiṣṇyā eva syuḥ_
(GBr_1,5.22k) atha yadi yajamānasyopatapet pārśvato 'gnīn ādhāya tāvad āsīta yāvad agadaḥ syāt_
(GBr_1,5.22l) yadi preyāt svair eva tam agnibhir dahet_

children.text: (GBr_1,5.22m) aśavāgnibhir itare yajamānā āsata iti vadantas
children.translated_text: The other <s>Yajamānas</s> (sacrificers) sit with impure fires, they say.

children.text: (GBr_1,5.22n) tasya tad eva brāhmaṇaṃ yad adaḥ puraḥsavane
children.translated_text: The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> explanation for that is the same as what was given above in the <s>Puraḥsavana</s> (preliminary pressing) section.

children.text: (GBr_1,5.22o) pitṛmedha āśiṣo vyākhyātāḥ || 22 ||
children.translated_text: The blessings of the <s>Pitṛmedha</s> (ancestral sacrifice) have been explained. [22]

body.translated_text: The ancients formerly offered the preliminary animal sacrifice as <s>Sāvitra</s> (dedicated to <s>Savitṛ</s>); now it is <s>Prājāpatya</s> (dedicated to <s>Prajāpati</s>), for they say: 'He who is <s>Savitṛ</s> is indeed <s>Prajāpati</s>.' Therefore, having heaped together the fires, they should sacrifice with that [fire]. They would then share the same fire-seat, until the <s>Ukhāsaṃbharaṇīyā</s> (fire-pot collection ceremony). At the <s>Ukhāsaṃbharaṇīyā</s>, having separated the fires, they should sacrifice with that. They would then have separate fire-seats, until the <s>Dīkṣaṇīyā</s> (consecration ceremony). At the <s>Dīkṣaṇīyā</s>, having heaped together the fires, they should sacrifice with that. They would then share the same fire-seat, until the <s>Udavasānīyā</s> (concluding ceremony). At the <s>Udavasānīyā</s>, having separated the fires, they should sacrifice with that. They would then have separate fire-seats. Now, if the <s>Yajamāna</s> (sacrificer) should fall ill, having established the fires to the side, he should wait until he recovers. If he should die, they should cremate him with his own fires.

body.text:
(GBr_1,5.23a) sāyaṃprātarhomau sthālīpāko navaś ca yaḥ | baliś ca pitṛyajñaś cāṣṭakā saptamaḥ paśuḥ || ity ete pākayajñāḥ
(GBr_1,5.23b) agnyādheyam agnihotraṃ paurṇamāsyamāvāsye | naveṣṭiś cāturmāsyāni paśubandho 'tra saptamaḥ || ity ete haviryajñāḥ
(GBr_1,5.23c) agniṣṭomo 'tyagniṣṭoma ukthyaḥ ṣoḍaśimāṃs tataḥ | vājapeyo 'tirātraś cāptoryāmātra saptamaḥ || ity ete sutyāḥ
(GBr_1,5.23d) ke svid devā pravovājāḥ ke svid devā abhidyavaḥ | ke svid devā haviṣmantaḥ kiṃ svij jigāti sumnayuḥ ||
body.translated_text: The evening and morning oblations, the <s>Sthālīpāka</s> (pot-cooking), the new-moon [offering], <s>Bali</s> (offering), <s>Pitṛyajña</s> (ancestor sacrifice), the seventh is <s>Aṣṭakā</s>, and the animal [sacrifice] — these are the <s>Pākayajñas</s> (cooked oblations). The <s>Agnyādheya</s> (fire-establishment), <s>Agnihotra</s> (fire oblation), <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> (full-moon) and <s>Amāvāsyā</s> (new-moon offerings), <s>Naveṣṭi</s> (new-grain offering), <s>Cāturmāsyas</s> (seasonal offerings), and the seventh is <s>Paśubandha</s> (animal sacrifice) — these are the <s>Haviryajñas</s> (oblation sacrifices). <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, <s>Atyagniṣṭoma</s>, <s>Ukthya</s>, <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s>, then <s>Vājapeya</s>, <s>Atirātra</s>, and the seventh is <s>Aptoryāma</s> — these are the <s>Sutyās</s> (Soma pressings). 'Who are the gods that are foremost in battle? Who are the gods that shine upon heaven? Who are the gods that receive oblations? What goes forth desiring favor?'

body.text: (GBr_1,5.23e) ṛtava eva pravovājā māsā devā abhidyavaḥ | ardhamāsā haviṣmantas taj jigāti sunmayuḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'The seasons (<s>Ṛtus</s>) indeed are foremost in battle, the months are the gods that shine upon heaven, the half-months receive oblations, and that [sacrifice] goes forth desiring favor.'

body.text: (GBr_1,5.23f) kati svid rātrayaḥ katy ahāni kati stotrāṇi kati śastrāṇy asya | kati svit savanāḥ saṃvatsarasya stotriyāḥ padākṣarāṇi katy asya ||
body.translated_text: 'How many nights, how many days, how many <s>Stotras</s> (hymns of praise), how many <s>Śastras</s> (recitations) does it have? How many <s>Savanas</s> (pressings) in the year, and how many <s>Stotriya</s> (hymn-text) <s>Padākṣaras</s> (word-syllables) does it have?'

body.text: (GBr_1,5.23g) <dvāv atirātrau ṣaṭ śatam agniṣṭomā dve viṃśatiśate ukthyānāṃ | dvādaśa ṣoḍaśinaḥ ṣaṣṭiḥ ṣaḍahā vaiṣuvataṃ ca [VaitS 31.15]> ||
body.translated_text: 'Two <s>Atirātras</s>, six hundred <s>Agniṣṭomas</s>, twenty-two hundred <s>Ukthyas</s>, twelve <s>Ṣoḍaśins</s>, sixty <s>Ṣaḍahas</s> (six-day periods), and the <s>Viṣuvat</s> (solstice day)' [VaitS 31.15].

body.text: (GBr_1,5.23h) ahānyasya viṃśatiśatāni trīṇy ahaś caikaṃ tāvad asya | saṃvatsarasya savanāḥ sahasram asīti trīṇi ca saṃstutasya ||
body.translated_text: 'Its days are twenty-three hundred and one additional day; the <s>Savanas</s> (pressings) of the year are one thousand and eighty-three of the fully praised [sacrifice].'

body.text: (GBr_1,5.23i) ṣaṭṣaṣṭiś ca dve ca śate bhavata stutaśastrāṇām ayutaṃ caikam asya | stotriyāś ca navatisahasrā dve niyute navatiś cāti ṣaṭ ca ||
body.translated_text: 'Sixty-six and two hundred are the <s>Stuta-Śastras</s> (praised recitations), and one <s>Ayuta</s> (ten-thousand) [of syllables] it has. The <s>Stotriyas</s> (hymn-texts) are ninety thousand, two <s>Niyutas</s> (millions), ninety, and six more.'

body.text: (GBr_1,5.23j) aṣṭau śatāny ayutāni triṃśac caturnavatiś ca padāny asya | saṃvatsarasya kavibhir mitasyaitāvatī madhyamā devamātrā ||
body.translated_text: 'Eight hundred <s>Ayutas</s> (ten-thousands), thirty, and ninety-four are its <s>Padas</s> (metrical feet). Of the year measured by the sages, such is the middle divine measure.'

body.text: (GBr_1,5.23k) ayutam ekaṃ prayutāni triṃśad dve niyute tathā hy anusṛṣṭāḥ | aṣṭau śatāni nava cākṣarāṇy etāvān ātmā paramaḥ prajāpateḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'One <s>Ayuta</s> (ten-thousand), thirty <s>Prayutas</s> (hundred-thousands), and two <s>Niyutas</s> (millions) — thus have they been set forth. Eight hundred and nine are the syllables (<s>Akṣaras</s>). Such is the supreme self of <s>Prajāpati</s>.'

body.text: (GBr_1,5.23l) ādyaṃ vaṣaṭkāraḥ pradānāntam etam agniṣṭome parvaśaḥ sādhu kḷptam | saubheṣajaṃ chanda īpsan yad agnau catuḥśataṃ bahudhā hūyate yat ||
body.translated_text: 'The <s>Vaṣaṭkāra</s> (offering call) is the beginning, and the offering is the end; in the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, this is well arranged section by section. Desiring the healing meter in the fire, the four hundred [oblations] that are offered in many ways.'

body.text: (GBr_1,5.23m) prātaḥsavana stuta ekaviṃśo gāyatrastomamita eka eva | mādhyaṃdinaḥ saptadaśena kḷptas trayastriṃśena savanaṃ tṛtīyam || 23 ||
body.translated_text: 'In the morning pressing, the <s>Ekaviṃśa</s> (twenty-one-fold) is praised, measured by the <s>Gāyatra Stoma</s>, being one alone. The midday [pressing] is arranged with the seventeen-fold, and the third pressing with the thirty-three-fold.' [23]

body.text: (GBr_1,5.24a) śraddhāyāṃ retas tapasā tapasvī vaiśvānaraḥ siṣice 'patyam īpsan | tato jajñe lokajit somajambhā ṛṣer ṛṣir aṅgirāḥ saṃnabhūva ||
body.translated_text: <s>Vaiśvānara</s> (the universal fire), performing <s>Tapas</s> (austerity) with <s>Tapas</s>, desiring offspring, deposited his seed in <s>Śraddhā</s> (faith). From that was born the world-conquering, <s>Soma</s>-consuming one; from <s>Ṛṣi</s> to <s>Ṛṣi</s>, <s>Aṅgiras</s> came into being.

body.text: (GBr_1,5.24b) ṛṣer yajñasya caturvidhasya śraddhāṃ yaḥ śreyasīṃ lokam amuṃ jigāya | yasmai vedāḥ prasṛtāḥ somabindu yuktā vahanti sukṛtām u lokam ||
body.translated_text: He who, through faith, conquered the superior world of the four-fold <s>Ṛṣi</s>-sacrifice — to him the <s>Vedas</s>, set forth with drops of <s>Soma</s>, yoked, carry [him] to the world of the meritorious.

body.text: (GBr_1,5.24c) ṛco 'sya bhāgāṃś caturo vahanty ukthaśastraiḥ pramudo modamānāḥ | grahair havirbhiś ca kṛtākṛtaś ca yajūṃṣi bhāgāṃś caturo vahanti ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Ṛcs</s> (verses) carry his four portions with <s>Uktha</s> (laudatory) recitations, rejoicing with delight. Through <s>Grahas</s> (Soma cups) and <s>Havis</s> (oblations), both fashioned and unfashioned, the <s>Yajus</s> (sacrificial formulas) carry four portions.

body.text: (GBr_1,5.24d) audumbaryāṃ sāmaghoṣeṇa tāvat saviṣṭutibhiś ca stomaiḥ chandasā | sāmāni bhāgāṃś caturo vahanti gītyā stomena saha prastāvena ca ||
body.translated_text: On the <s>Audumbarī</s> (fig-wood altar), with the sound of <s>Sāman</s> (chant), with the <s>Viṣṭutis</s> (special praises) and <s>Stomas</s> (praise-forms), with <s>Chandas</s> (meter) — the <s>Sāmans</s> (chants) carry four portions, through song, <s>Stoma</s>, and <s>Prastāva</s> (introductory chant).

body.text: (GBr_1,5.24e) prāyaścittair bheṣajaiḥ saṃstuvanto 'tharvāṇo 'ṅgirasaś ca śāntāḥ | brahmā brahmatvena pramudo modamānā asaṃsṛṣṭān bhāgāṃś caturo vahanti ||
body.translated_text: Praising with <s>Prāyaścittas</s> (expiations) and remedies, the <s>Atharvans</s> and <s>Aṅgirases</s>, pacified, <s>Brahmā</s> (the Brahman priest), rejoicing with delight through his office, carries four unseparated portions.

body.text: (GBr_1,5.24f) yo brahmavit so 'bhikaro 'stu vaḥ śivo dhiyā dhīro rakṣatu dharmam etam | mā vaḥ pramattām amṛtāc ca yajñāt karmāc ca yenān aṅgiraso 'piyāsīt ||
body.translated_text: May he who knows <s>Brahman</s> be a benefactor to you; may the auspicious one protect this <s>Dharma</s> (sacred law) with wisdom, O wise one. May you not fall away from immortality, from the sacrifice, and from the rite by which the <s>Aṅgirases</s> attained [the goal].

body.text: (GBr_1,5.24g) māyuṃ daśaṃ māruśastāḥ prameṣṭā mā me bhūr yuktā vidahātha lokān | divyaṃ bhayaṃ rakṣata dharmam udyataṃ yajñaṃ kālāśa stutigopanāyanam ||
body.translated_text: May the ten not be destroyed, may the <s>Praṃeṣṭhā</s> (supreme lord) not be assailed by weapons! May my yoked [fires] not burn away the worlds! Protect the divine, fearsome, upraised <s>Dharma</s> — the sacrifice, the vessel of praise led by Time.

body.text: (GBr_1,5.24h) hotā ca maitrāvaruṇaś ca pādam acchāvākaḥ saha grāvastutaikam | ṛgbhi stuvanto 'harahaḥ pṛthivyā agniṃ pādaṃ brahmaṇā dhārayanti ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Hotṛ</s> and the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> [hold] one <s>Pāda</s> (quarter), the <s>Acchāvāka</s> together with the <s>Grāvastut</s> [hold] one. Praising day after day with <s>Ṛcs</s> (verses) upon the earth, they uphold the quarter of <s>Agni</s> through <s>Brahman</s> (sacred knowledge).

body.text: (GBr_1,5.24i) adhvaryuḥ pratiprasthātā neṣṭonnetā nihitaṃ pādam ekam | sam antarikṣaṃ yajuṣā stuvanto vāyuṃ pādaṃ brahmaṇā dhārayanti ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Adhvaryu</s>, the <s>Pratiprasthātṛ</s>, the <s>Neṣṭṛ</s>, and the <s>Unnetṛ</s> [hold] one established <s>Pāda</s> (quarter). Praising the atmosphere with <s>Yajus</s> (sacrificial formulas), they uphold the quarter of <s>Vāyu</s> through <s>Brahman</s>.

body.text: (GBr_1,5.24j) sāmnodgātā chādayann apramatta audumbaryāṃ stobhadeyaḥ sagadgadaḥ | vidvān prastotā vidahātha suṣṭutiṃ subrahmaṇyaḥ pratihartātha yajñe ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Udgātṛ</s>, covering [the world] with <s>Sāman</s> (chant), unwavering, upon the <s>Audumbarī</s> (fig-wood seat), the giver of <s>Stobhas</s> (interjections), with faltering voice — the knowing <s>Prastotṛ</s> (leader of chanting), may he perform the laudation well; the <s>Subrahmaṇya</s> and the <s>Pratihartṛ</s> [serve] in the sacrifice.

body.text: (GBr_1,5.24k) sāmnā divy ekaṃ nihitaṃ stuvantaḥ sūryaṃ pādaṃ brahmaṇā dhārayanti | brahmā haikaṃ brāhmaṇācchaṃsinaḥ saha potāgnīdhro nihitaṃ pādam ekam ||
body.translated_text: Praising with <s>Sāman</s> (chant), they uphold one [quarter] established in heaven — the quarter of <s>Sūrya</s> (the Sun) through <s>Brahman</s>. The <s>Brahmā</s> (Brahman priest) with the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>, together with the <s>Potṛ</s> and the <s>Agnīdhra</s> [hold] one established <s>Pāda</s> (quarter).

body.text: (GBr_1,5.24l) atharvabhir aṅgirobhiś ca gupto 'psu candraṃ pādaṃ brahmaṇā dhārayanti | ṣoḍaśikaṃ hotrakā abhiṣṭuvanti vedeṣu yuktāḥ prapṛthak caturdhā ||
body.translated_text: Protected by the <s>Atharvans</s> and <s>Aṅgirases</s>, they uphold the quarter of <s>Candra</s> (the Moon) in the waters through <s>Brahman</s>. The <s>Hotṛkas</s> (assistant priests) praise with the sixteen-fold [<s>Stoma</s>], yoked to the <s>Vedas</s>, separately in four ways.

body.text: (GBr_1,5.24m) manīṣiṇo dīkṣitāḥ śraddadhānā hotāro guptā abhivahanti yajñam | dakṣiṇato brahmaṇasyoṃ janad ity etāṃ vyāhṛtiṃ japan ||
body.translated_text: The wise ones, consecrated, full of faith — the <s>Hotṛs</s> (invoking priests), protected, carry the sacrifice forward. To the south of <s>Brahmā</s>, murmuring '<s>Oṃ janat</s>' — this <s>Vyāhṛti</s> (sacred utterance) they recite.

body.text: (GBr_1,5.24n) saptadaśaṃ sadasyaṃ taṃ kīrtayanti purā viduḥ | aṣṭādaśī dīkṣitā dīkṣitānāṃ yajñe patnī śraddadhāneha yuktā ||
body.translated_text: The seventeenth, the <s>Sadasya</s> (assembly priest), him they proclaim — the ancients knew [this]. The eighteenth is the <s>Dīkṣitā</s> (consecrated wife) among the consecrated; in the sacrifice, the wife, faithful, is yoked here.

body.text: (GBr_1,5.24o) ekonaviṃśaḥ śamitā babhūva viṃśo yajñe gṛhapatir eva sunvan | ekaviṃśatir evaiṣāṃ saṃsthāyām aṅgiro vaha ||
body.translated_text: The nineteenth is the <s>Śamitṛ</s> (slaughterer); the twentieth in the sacrifice is the <s>Gṛhapati</s> (householder) himself, pressing [the Soma]. Twenty-one in all — at the conclusion, O <s>Aṅgiras</s>, carry [the sacrifice forward].

body.text: (GBr_1,5.24p) vedair abhiṣṭuto loko nānāveśāparājitaḥ | || 24 ||
body.translated_text: The world praised by the <s>Vedas</s>, of manifold dwelling-places, unconquered. [24]

body.text: (GBr_1,5.25a) sapta sutyāḥ sapta ca pākayajñāḥ haviryajñāḥ sapta tathaikaviṃśatiḥ | sarve te yajñā aṅgiraso 'piyanti nūtanā yān ṛṣayo sṛjanti ye ca sṛṣṭāḥ purāṇaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: Seven <s>Sutyās</s> (Soma sacrifices), seven <s>Pākayajñas</s> (cooked oblations), and seven <s>Haviryajñas</s> (oblation sacrifices) — thus twenty-one in all. All these sacrifices lead to the <s>Aṅgirases</s> — both the new ones that the <s>Ṛṣis</s> create and those created by the ancients.

body.text: (GBr_1,5.25b) eteṣu vedeṣv api caikam evāpavrajam ṛtvijāṃ saṃbharanti | kṛṭstṛpāt sacate tām aśastiṃ viṣkandham enaṃ visṛtaṃ prajāsu ||
body.translated_text: In these <s>Vedas</s>, they gather even a single retirement of the <s>Ṛtvijs</s> (priests). He who falls short from the ritual incurs that censure — an injury spread among the people.

body.text: (GBr_1,5.25c) nivartante dakṣiṇā nīyamānāḥ sute some vitate yajñatantre | moghāśiṣo yanty anivartamānā aniṣṭayajñā na taranti lokān ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Dakṣiṇās</s> (ritual fees) return when being led away; when <s>Soma</s> is pressed and the sacrificial thread is spread — those of vain hopes depart without returning; those whose sacrifices are incomplete do not cross over the worlds.

body.text: (GBr_1,5.25d) dvādaśavarṣaṃ brahmacaryaṃ pṛthag vedeṣu tat smṛtam | evaṃ vyavasthitā vedāḥ sarva eva svakarmasu ||
body.translated_text: Twelve years of <s>Brahmacarya</s> (studentship) is prescribed separately in each <s>Veda</s>. Thus the <s>Vedas</s> are established, each in its own ritual functions.

body.text: (GBr_1,5.25e) santi caiṣāṃ samānāḥ mantrāḥ kalpāś ca brāhmaṇāni ca | vyavasthānaṃ tu tat sarvaṃ pṛthagvedeṣu tat smṛtam ||
body.translated_text: And they have common <s>Mantras</s>, <s>Kalpas</s> (ritual procedures), and <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> (explanatory texts). But all that distinction is prescribed separately in each <s>Veda</s>.

body.text: (GBr_1,5.25f) ṛgvedasya pṛthivī sthānam antarikṣasthāno 'dhvaraḥ | dyau sthānaṃ sāmavedasyāpo bhṛgvaṅgirasāṃ smṛtam ||
body.translated_text: The abode of the <s>Ṛgveda</s> is the earth; the <s>Yajurveda</s> has the atmosphere as its abode. Heaven is the abode of the <s>Sāmaveda</s>; the waters are declared to be [the abode] of the <s>Bhṛgus</s> and <s>Aṅgirases</s> (i.e., the <s>Atharvaveda</s>).

body.text: (GBr_1,5.25g) agnir devata ṛgvedasya yajurvedo vāyudevataḥ | ādityaḥ sāmavedasya candramā vaidyutaś ca bhṛgvaṅgirasām ||
body.translated_text: <s>Agni</s> is the deity of the <s>Ṛgveda</s>; the <s>Yajurveda</s> has <s>Vāyu</s> as its deity. <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun) is [the deity] of the <s>Sāmaveda</s>; <s>Candramā</s> (the Moon) and <s>Vaidyuta</s> (Lightning) are [the deities] of the <s>Bhṛgus</s> and <s>Aṅgirases</s>.

body.text: (GBr_1,5.25h) trivṛtstoma ṛgvedasya yajūṃṣi pañcadaśena saha jajñire | saptadaśena sāmaveda ekaviṃśo brahmasaṃmitaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Trivṛt Stoma</s> (nine-fold praise) belongs to the <s>Ṛgveda</s>; the <s>Yajus</s> (sacrificial formulas) were born together with the fifteen-fold [<s>Stoma</s>]. The <s>Sāmaveda</s> [has] the seventeen-fold; the twenty-one-fold corresponds to <s>Brahman</s> (the <s>Atharvaveda</s>).

body.text: (GBr_1,5.25i) vāg adhyātmam ṛgvedasya yajuṣāṃ prāṇa ucyate | cakṣuṣī sāmavedasya mano bhṛgvaṅgirasāṃ smṛtam ||
body.translated_text: Speech (<s>Vāc</s>) is the inner correspondent (<s>Adhyātman</s>) of the <s>Ṛgveda</s>; <s>Prāṇa</s> (breath) is said to be [that] of the <s>Yajus</s>. The eyes are [that] of the <s>Sāmaveda</s>; the mind (<s>Manas</s>) is declared to be [that] of the <s>Bhṛgus</s> and <s>Aṅgirases</s>.

body.text: (GBr_1,5.25j) ṛgbhiḥ saha gāyatraṃ jāgatam āhur yajūṃṣi traiṣṭubhena saha jajñire | uṣṇikkakubhyāṃ bhṛgvaṅgiraso jagatyā sāmāni kavayo vadanti ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Gāyatra</s> [meter] is said to accompany the <s>Ṛcs</s> (verses); the <s>Jāgata</s> — the <s>Yajus</s> (formulas) were born together with the <s>Traiṣṭubha</s> [meter]. The <s>Bhṛgus</s> and <s>Aṅgirases</s> [accompany] the <s>Uṣṇik</s> and <s>Kakubh</s> [meters]; the sages say the <s>Sāmans</s> [accompany] the <s>Jagatī</s>.

body.text: (GBr_1,5.25k) ṛgbhiḥ pṛthivīṃ yajuṣāntarikṣaṃ sāmnā divaṃ lokajit somajambhāḥ | atharvabhir aṅgirobhiś ca gupto yajñaś catuṣpād divam udvaheta ||
body.translated_text: With the <s>Ṛcs</s> (verses) [one wins] the earth, with the <s>Yajus</s> (formulas) the atmosphere, with the <s>Sāman</s> (chant) heaven — the world-conquering, <s>Soma</s>-consuming ones. Protected by the <s>Atharvans</s> and <s>Aṅgirases</s>, the four-footed sacrifice ascends to heaven.

body.text: (GBr_1,5.25l) ṛgbhiḥ suśasto yajuṣā pariṣkṛtaḥ saviṣṭutaḥ sāmajit somajambhāḥ | atharvabhir aṅgirobhiś ca gupto yajñaś catuṣpād divam āruroha ||
body.translated_text: Well-praised with <s>Ṛcs</s> (verses), adorned with <s>Yajus</s> (formulas), glorified with <s>Viṣṭuti</s> (special praise), <s>Soma</s>-consuming, the <s>Sāma</s>-conquering [sacrifice] — protected by the <s>Atharvans</s> and <s>Aṅgirases</s>, the four-footed sacrifice has ascended to heaven.

body.text: (GBr_1,5.25m) ṛco vidvān pṛthivīṃ veda saṃprati yajūṃṣi vidvān bṛhad antarikṣam | divaṃ veda sāmago yo vipaścit sarvān lokān yad bhṛgvaṅgirovit ||
body.translated_text: He who knows the <s>Ṛcs</s> (verses) knows the earth fully; he who knows the <s>Yajus</s> (formulas) [knows] the vast atmosphere. He who knows the <s>Sāman</s> (chant), the wise one, knows heaven. He who knows the <s>Bhṛgus</s> and <s>Aṅgirases</s> (i.e., the <s>Atharvaveda</s>) [knows] all the worlds.

body.text: (GBr_1,5.25n) yāṃś ca grāme yāṃś cāraṇye japanti mantrān nārthān bahudhā janāsaḥ | sarve te yajñā aṅgiraso 'piyanti nūtanā sā hi gatir brahmaṇo yāvarārdhyā ||
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>Mantras</s> (sacred formulas) people recite in the village or in the forest, for various purposes — all those sacrifices lead to the <s>Aṅgirases</s>; the new ones too — for that is the path of <s>Brahman</s>, reaching to the farthest end.

body.text: (GBr_1,5.25o) triviṣṭapaṃ tridivaṃ nākam uttamaṃ tam etayā trayyā vidyayaiti | ata uttare brahmalokā mahānto 'tharvaṇām aṅgirasāṃ ca sā gatiḥ || atharvaṇām aṅgirasāṃ ca sā gatir iti brāhmaṇam || 25 ||
body.translated_text: <s>Triviṣṭapa</s> (the triple heaven), <s>Tridiva</s> (the three heavens), the highest <s>Nāka</s> (firmament) — one reaches that through this threefold knowledge (<s>Trayī Vidyā</s>). Beyond that are the great <s>Brahmaloka</s>s (worlds of <s>Brahman</s>) — that is the destination of the <s>Atharvans</s> and <s>Aṅgirases</s>. That is the destination of the <s>Atharvans</s> and <s>Aṅgirases</s> — thus is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [teaching]. [25]

body.text: (GBr_1,5.25col) ity atharvavede gopathabrāhmaṇapūrvabhāge pañcamaḥ prapāṭhakaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fifth <s>Prapāṭhaka</s> (chapter) of the <s>Pūrvabhāga</s> (first part) of the <s>Gopatha Brāhmaṇa</s> of the <s>Atharvaveda</s>.

body.text: (GBr_1col) iti pūrvabrāhmaṇaṃ samāptam
body.translated_text: Thus the <s>Pūrva Brāhmaṇa</s> (first Brāhmaṇa) is completed.

children.translated_text: (GBr 2,1.1dd) Twelve indeed are the months of the year.

children.translated_text: (GBr 2,1.1ee) By that he pleases the year indeed.

children.translated_text: (GBr 2,1.1ff) And he thereby establishes the year for him, for the attainment of the heavenly world. [1]

body.translated_text:
(GBr 2,1.1a) Now, when he removes a blade of grass from the <s>brahmasadana</s> (seat of the Brahman priest), he thereby purifies it.
(GBr 2,1.1b) Then he sits down [saying]: 'I sit in the seat of <s>Arvāgvasu</s>.'
(GBr 2,1.1c) <s>Arvāgvasu</s> was indeed the <s>Brahman</s> priest of the gods; <s>Parāgvasu</s> [was that] of the <s>Asuras</s>.
(GBr 2,1.1d) Him indeed he first seats.
(GBr 2,1.1e) 'May he extend the sacrifice unharmed' — thus.
(GBr 2,1.1f) Then, having sat down, he mutters: '<s>Bṛhaspati</s> is the <s>Brahman</s>.'
(GBr 2,1.1g) <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, son of <s>Aṅgiras</s>, was indeed the <s>Brahman</s> priest of the gods.
(GBr 2,1.1h) In him indeed he seeks permission; when the consecrated waters are being led forth, he restrains speech until the exclamation at the <s>haviṣkṛta</s> (preparation of the oblation).
(GBr 2,1.1i) This indeed is the door of the sacrifice.
(GBr 2,1.1j) This he makes not empty.
(GBr 2,1.1k) And when the offering has been made, at the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> (offering to the properly-offered), from the authorization of the after-offerings — thus.
(GBr 2,1.1l) This indeed is the second door of the sacrifice.
(GBr 2,1.1m) This he makes not empty.
(GBr 2,1.1n) When the enclosing sticks are placed around, [it is] for the protection of the sacrifice.
(GBr 2,1.1o) He places the enclosing sticks for the self-possession of the sacrifice.
(GBr 2,1.1p) He wipes the enclosing sticks.
(GBr 2,1.1q) He purifies them indeed.
(GBr 2,1.1r) Three times the middle one.
(GBr 2,1.1s) Three are these vital breaths.
(GBr 2,1.1t) He conquers the vital breaths indeed.
(GBr 2,1.1u) Three times the southern one.
(GBr 2,1.1v) Three indeed are the worlds.
(GBr 2,1.1w) He conquers the worlds indeed.
(GBr 2,1.1x) Three times the northern one.
(GBr 2,1.1y) Three indeed are the divine worlds.
(GBr 2,1.1z) He conquers the divine worlds indeed.
(GBr 2,1.1aa) Three times he fans [the fire]; three indeed are the paths leading to the gods.
(GBr 2,1.1bb) These he conquers.
(GBr 2,1.1cc) These are indeed twelve.

(GBr 2,1.2a) <s>Prajāpati</s> excluded <s>Rudra</s> from the sacrifice.
(GBr 2,1.2b) He [<s>Rudra</s>] desired:
(GBr 2,1.2c) 'May this intention of him who excluded me from the sacrifice not succeed.'
(GBr 2,1.2d) He, straining against the sacrifice, pierced it.
(GBr 2,1.2e) That which was pierced, he cut off.
(GBr 2,1.2f) That became the <s>prāśitra</s> (fore-portion for the Brahman priest).
(GBr 2,1.2g) He [<s>Prajāpati</s>] lifted it up.
(GBr 2,1.2h) He offered it to <s>Bhaga</s>.
(GBr 2,1.2i) He [<s>Bhaga</s>] looked upon it.
(GBr 2,1.2j) His eyes fell out.
(GBr 2,1.2k) Therefore they say: '<s>Bhaga</s> is indeed blind.'
(GBr 2,1.2l) He does not obtain even that which he desires.
(GBr 2,1.2m) He offered it to <s>Savitṛ</s>.
(GBr 2,1.2n) He [<s>Savitṛ</s>] received it; it cut off his hands.
(GBr 2,1.2o) Golden [hands] were made for him.

body.translated_text:
(GBr 2,1.3a) And they say: 'In the stomach of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.'
(GBr 2,1.3b) 'Self within self — do not harm my self!' <s>Svāhā</s>!
(GBr 2,1.3c) Food is indeed the self of all beings; by that he pacified it.
(GBr 2,1.3d) He consecrates the <s>prāśitra</s>: 'That fire named <s>Nṛmaṇas</s> which has entered the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> — in him may this <s>prāśitra</s> be well-offered for me; may it not harm me in the highest heaven' [PS 20.57.15] — thus.
(GBr 2,1.3e) He eats it with the entire <s>Brahman</s> (sacred knowledge).
(GBr 2,1.3f) Therefore it did not harm him.
(GBr 2,1.3g) Therefore, whoever is most learned in the <s>Vedas</s>, him one should make the <s>Brahman</s> priest.
(GBr 2,1.3h) <s>Bṛhaspati</s> is indeed the entirety of sacred knowledge.
(GBr 2,1.3i) With the entire sacred knowledge he raises the sacrifice from the south.

children.text: (GBr_2,1.4aa) sa hi brahmiṣṭhaḥ
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,1.4aa) For he is the most learned in the <s>Vedas</s>.

children.text: (GBr_2,1.4bb) sa yajñaṃ pāhi sa yajñapatiṃ pāhi sa māṃ pāhi sa māṃ karmaṇyaṃ pāhīty āha
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,1.4bb) 'Protect the sacrifice! Protect the lord of the sacrifice! Protect me! Protect me in my ritual action!' — he says.

children.text: (GBr_2,1.4cc) yajñāya ca yajamānāya ca paśūnām āptyai || 4 ||
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,1.4cc) For the sake of the sacrifice and the sacrificer, and for the obtainment of cattle. [4]

body.translated_text:
(GBr 2,1.4a) He carries it forward.
(GBr 2,1.4b) He carries it by the proper path.
(GBr 2,1.4c) The sacrifice is indeed cut asunder when the <s>prāśitra</s> is carried around.
(GBr 2,1.4d) When he says: 'O <s>Brahman</s>, I shall proceed' — <s>Bṛhaspati</s> is indeed the entirety of sacred knowledge.
(GBr 2,1.4e) With the entire sacred knowledge he joins the sacrifice from the south.
(GBr 2,1.4f) And now, wherever the <s>Brahman</s> priest is, there the sacrifice rests; wherever the <s>Brahman</s> is, there the sacrifice is established.
(GBr 2,1.4g) From there he takes hold of it.
(GBr 2,1.4h) If he were to move his hand, he would tremble.
(GBr 2,1.4i) If [he were to move] his head, he would have a headache.
(GBr 2,1.4j) If he were to sit silently, the sacrifice would be unaccomplished.
(GBr 2,1.4k) He should say: 'It is established!'
(GBr 2,1.4l) For the sacrifice rests in speech.

body.text: (GBr_2,1.5a) na vai paurṇamāsyāṃ nāmāvāsyāyāṃ dakṣiṇā dīyante

children.text: (GBr_2,1.5b) ya eṣa odanaḥ pacyate dakṣiṇaiṣā dīyate yajñasyarddhyai_
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,1.5b) The rice porridge that is cooked — that is the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> given for the success of the sacrifice.

children.text: (GBr_2,1.5c) iṣṭī vā etena yad yajate 'tho vā etena pūrtī ya eṣa odanaḥ pacyate_
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,1.5c) That by which he sacrifices is the <s>iṣṭi</s> (offering); and the rice porridge that is cooked is the <s>pūrti</s> (charitable gift).

children.text: (GBr_2,1.5d) eṣa ha vā iṣṭāpūrtī ya enaṃ pacati || 5 ||
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,1.5d) He who cooks it — for him these are the <s>iṣṭāpūrta</s> (merit from sacrifice and charity). [5]

body.translated_text: (GBr 2,1.5a) No <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee) is given at the full-moon or new-moon [sacrifice].

body.text:
(GBr_2,1.6a) dvayā vai devā yajamānasya gṛham āgacchanti somapā anye 'somapā anye
(GBr_2,1.6b) hutādo 'nye 'hutādo 'nye_
(GBr_2,1.6c) ete vai devā ahutādo yad brāhmaṇāḥ_
(GBr_2,1.6d) etaddevatya eṣa yaḥ purānījānaḥ_
(GBr_2,1.6e) ete ha vā etasya prajāyāḥ paśūnām īśate
(GBr_2,1.6f) te 'syāprītā iṣam ūrjam ādāyāpakrāmanti
(GBr_2,1.6g) yad anvāhāryam anvāharati tān eva tena prīṇāti
(GBr_2,1.6h) dakṣiṇataḥsadbhyaḥ parihartavā āha

children.text: (GBr_2,1.6i) dakṣiṇāvataiva yajñena yajate_
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,1.6i) He sacrifices with a sacrifice that has <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (fees) indeed.

children.text: (GBr_2,1.6j) āhutibhir eva devān hutādaḥ prīṇāti dakṣiṇābhir manuṣyadevān_
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,1.6j) By oblations he pleases the gods who partake of offerings; by <s>dakṣiṇās</s> (fees) [he pleases] the human-gods (i.e. <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>).

children.text: (GBr_2,1.6k) te 'smai prītā iṣam ūrjaṃ niyacchanti || 6 ||
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,1.6k) They, being pleased, bestow nourishment and strength upon him. [6]

body.translated_text:
(GBr 2,1.6a) Two kinds of gods come to the house of the sacrificer: some are <s>Soma</s>-drinkers, others are non-<s>Soma</s>-drinkers.
(GBr 2,1.6b) Some partake of oblations, others do not partake of oblations.
(GBr 2,1.6c) These gods who do not partake of oblations are the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>.
(GBr 2,1.6d) This [oblation] has them as its deities — that which [is offered] before the <s>anīja</s> (offering).
(GBr 2,1.6e) They indeed are the lords of his offspring and cattle.
(GBr 2,1.6f) They, displeased, depart taking away nourishment and strength.
(GBr 2,1.6g) When he offers the <s>anvāhārya</s> (supplementary offering), by that he pleases them.
(GBr 2,1.6h) It should be served to those seated on the south — he says.

body.text:
(GBr_2,1.7a) devāś ca ha vā asurāś cāspardhanta
(GBr_2,1.7b) te devāḥ prajāpatim evābhyayajanta_
(GBr_2,1.7c) anyo 'nyasyāsann asurā ajuhavus
(GBr_2,1.7d) te devā etam odanam apaśyan_
(GBr_2,1.7e) taṃ prajāpataye bhāgam anuniravapan_
(GBr_2,1.7f) taṃ bhāgaṃ paśyan prajāpatir devān upāvartata
(GBr_2,1.7g) tato devā abhavan parāsurāḥ
(GBr_2,1.7h) sa ya evaṃvidvān etam odanaṃ pacati bhavaty ātmanā parāsyāpriyo bhrātṛvyo bhavati
(GBr_2,1.7i) prajāpatir vai devebhyo bhāgadheyāni vyakalpayat
(GBr_2,1.7j) so 'manyatātmānam antaragām iti
(GBr_2,1.7k) sa etam odanam abhaktam apaśyat
(GBr_2,1.7l) tam ātmane bhāgaṃ niravapat
(GBr_2,1.7m) prajāpater vā eṣa bhāgaḥ_

(GBr_2,1.7q) akṣito 'si_
(GBr_2,1.7r) akṣityai tvā
(GBr_2,1.7s) mā me kṣeṣṭhā amutrāmuṣmiṃl loka iha ca
(GBr_2,1.7t) prāṇāpanau me pāhi

(GBr_2,1.7v) udānarūpe me pāhi_
(GBr_2,1.7w) ūrg asi_
(GBr_2,1.7x) ūrjaṃ me dhehi
(GBr_2,1.7y) kurvato me mā kṣeṣṭhāḥ_

children.text: (GBr_2,1.7z) dadato me mopadasaḥ
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,1.7z) 'May no failure befall me who give!'

children.text: (GBr_2,1.7aa) prajāpatim ahaṃ tvayā samakṣam ṛdhyāsam iti
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,1.7aa) 'May I prosper in the sight of <s>Prajāpati</s> through you!'

children.text: (GBr_2,1.7bb) prajāpatim eva samakṣam ṛdhnoti ya evaṃ veda ya evaṃ veda || 7 ||
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,1.7bb) He prospers in the sight of <s>Prajāpati</s> — whoever knows thus, whoever knows thus. [7]

body.translated_text:
(GBr 2,1.7a) The gods and the <s>Asuras</s> were in rivalry.
(GBr 2,1.7b) The gods worshipped <s>Prajāpati</s> alone.
(GBr 2,1.7c) The <s>Asuras</s> offered oblations to one another.
(GBr 2,1.7d) The gods perceived this rice porridge.
(GBr 2,1.7e) They offered a portion of it to <s>Prajāpati</s>.
(GBr 2,1.7f) Seeing that portion, <s>Prajāpati</s> turned toward the gods.
(GBr 2,1.7g) Thereupon the gods prevailed; the <s>Asuras</s> were defeated.
(GBr 2,1.7h) He who, knowing thus, cooks this rice porridge, he prevails by himself; his hostile rival is defeated.
(GBr 2,1.7i) <s>Prajāpati</s> distributed the sacrificial portions among the gods.
(GBr 2,1.7j) He thought: 'I have been left out.'
(GBr 2,1.7k) He perceived this rice porridge as unassigned.
(GBr 2,1.7l) He claimed it for himself.

body.text:
(GBr_2,1.8a) ye vā iha yajñair ārdhnuvaṃs teṣām etāni jyotīṃṣi yāny amūni nakṣatrāṇi
(GBr_2,1.8b) tan nakṣatrāṇāṃ nakṣatratvaṃ yan na kṣīyanti
(GBr_2,1.8c) darśapūrṇamāsau vai yajñasyāvasānadarśau

children.text: (GBr_2,1.8d) ye vā aniṣṭvā darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ somena yajante teṣām etāni jyotīṃṣi yāny amūni nakṣatrāṇi patantīva
children.translated_text: Those who, without having sacrificed with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new and full moon rites), sacrifice with <s>Soma</s> — their lights are those stars (<s>nakṣatras</s>) that appear to fall.

children.text: (GBr_2,1.8e) tad yathā ha vā idam aspaṣṭāvasāne nehāvasāsyasi nehāvasāsyasīti nonudyanta evaṃ haivaite 'muṣmāṃl lokān nonudyante
children.translated_text: Just as here in this world, at an unclear resting place, one is pushed on saying 'You shall not rest here! You shall not rest here!' — even so are these pushed from the other world.

children.text: (GBr_2,1.8f) ta ete pracyavante || 8 ||
children.translated_text: They fall away. ||8||

body.translated_text:
(GBr 2,1.8a) Those who prospered here through sacrifices — theirs are those lights which are those stars.
(GBr 2,1.8b) The starhood of the stars consists in this: that they do not perish (<s>na kṣīyanti</s>).
(GBr 2,1.8c) The new-moon and full-moon sacrifices are indeed the resting places of the sacrifice.

body.text:
(GBr_2,1.9a) yasya havir niruptaṃ purastāc candramā abhyudiyāt tāṃs tredhā tāṇḍulān vibhajet_
(GBr_2,1.9b) ye madhyamās tān agnaye dātre 'ṣṭākapālaṃ nirvapet_
(GBr_2,1.9c) ye sthaviṣṭhās tān indrāya prādātre dadhani carum_
(GBr_2,1.9d) ye kṣodiṣṭhās tān viṣṇave śipiviṣṭāya śṛte carum_ [ed. kṣodisthās, corr. Patyal]
(GBr_2,1.9e) paśavo vā ete 'tiricyante
(GBr_2,1.9f) tān evāpnoti
(GBr_2,1.9g) tān avarunddhe_
(GBr_2,1.9h) agnir vai madhyamasya dātendro vai jyeṣṭhasya pradātā

children.text: (GBr_2,1.9i) yad evedaṃ kṣudraṃ paśūnāṃ tad viṣṇoḥ śipiviṣṭam_
children.translated_text: Whatever is small among cattle, that belongs to <s>Viṣṇu Śipiviṣṭa</s>.

children.text: (GBr_2,1.9j) tad evāpnoti
children.translated_text: He obtains that very thing.

children.text: (GBr_2,1.9k) paśūn evāvarunddhe || 9 ||
children.translated_text: He secures the cattle indeed. ||9||

body.translated_text:
If the moon rises before the <s>havis</s> (oblation) has been poured, one should divide the rice grains into three parts:
the medium ones he should offer as an eight-potsherds cake (<s>aṣṭākapāla</s>) to <s>Agni</s> the Giver;
the largest ones he should offer as a porridge (<s>caru</s>) in curds to <s>Indra</s> the Bestower;
the smallest ones he should offer as a porridge in cooked milk to <s>Viṣṇu Śipiviṣṭa</s>.
These are indeed the cattle that are left over.
He obtains them.
He secures them.
<s>Agni</s> is indeed the giver of the middle, <s>Indra</s> is the bestower of the greatest.

body.text:
(GBr_2,1.10a) yā pūrvā paurṇamāsī sānumatiḥ_
(GBr_2,1.10b) yottarā rākā
(GBr_2,1.10c) yā pūrvāmāvāsyā sā sinīvālī yottarā sā kuhūḥ_
(GBr_2,1.10d) candramā eva dhātā ca vidhātā ca
(GBr_2,1.10e) yat pūrṇo 'nyāṃ vasaty apūrṇo 'nyāṃ tan mithunam_

children.text: (GBr_2,1.10f) yat paśyaty anyāṃ nānyāṃ tan mithunam_
children.translated_text: That it is seen on one night and not on another — that is a pairing.

children.text: (GBr_2,1.10g) yad amāvāsyāyāś candramā adhi prajāyate tan mithunam_
children.translated_text: That from the new-moon night the moon is reborn — that is a pairing.

children.text: (GBr_2,1.10h) tasmād evāsmai mithunāt paśūn prajanayati || 10 ||
children.translated_text: From this very pairing he begets cattle for him. ||10||

body.translated_text:
The earlier full-moon day is <s>Anumati</s>;
the later one is <s>Rākā</s>.
The earlier new-moon day is <s>Sinīvālī</s>; the later one is <s>Kuhū</s>.
The moon itself is <s>Dhātṛ</s> (the Creator) and <s>Vidhātṛ</s> (the Ordainer).
That it dwells full on one night and not full on another — that is a pairing (<s>mithuna</s>).

body.text:
(GBr_2,1.11a) na dve yajeta
(GBr_2,1.11b) yat pūrvayā saṃprati yatetottarayā chambaṭkuryāt_
(GBr_2,1.11c) yad uttarayā saṃprati yajeta pūrvayā chambaṭkuryāt_
(GBr_2,1.11d) neṣṭir bhavati na yajñas
(GBr_2,1.11e) tad anu hrītamukhy apagalbho jāyate_
(GBr_2,1.11f) ekām eva yajeta
(GBr_2,1.11g) pragalbho haiva jāyate_
(GBr_2,1.11h) anādṛtya tad dve yajeta
(GBr_2,1.11i) yajñamukham eva pūrvayālabhate yajata uttarayā
(GBr_2,1.11j) devatā evaṃ pūrvayāpnotīndriyam uttaryā

children.text: (GBr_2,1.11k) devalokam eva pūrvayāvarunddhe manuṣyalokam uttarayā bhūyaso yajñakratūn upaitya_
children.translated_text: With the earlier he secures the world of the gods, with the later the world of men, having attained more sacrificial rites.

children.text: (GBr_2,1.11l) eṣā ha vai sumanā nāmeṣṭiḥ_
children.translated_text: This is indeed the <s>iṣṭi</s> (offering) called <s>Sumanā</s> (well-minded).

children.text: (GBr_2,1.11m) yam adyejānaṃ paścāc candramā abhyudiyād asmā asmiṃl loka ārdhukaṃ bhavati || 11 ||
children.translated_text: If the moon rises after the one sacrificing today — for him there is prosperity in this world. ||11||

body.translated_text:
One should not sacrifice on both days.
If one were to succeed with the earlier day, the later would be spoiled;
if one were to sacrifice successfully on the later, the earlier would be spoiled.
There is neither sacrifice nor <s>yajña</s> (rite).
Thereafter, a shamefaced and timid son is born.
One should sacrifice on one day only.
Then indeed a bold son is born.
Disregarding that, one may sacrifice on both days:
with the earlier one he obtains the opening of the sacrifice, and sacrifices with the later;
with the earlier he obtains the deities, with the later, vital power.

body.text:
(GBr_2,1.12a) agnāvaiṣṇavam ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvaped darśapūrṇamāsāv āripsamāṇaḥ_
(GBr_2,1.12b) agnir vai sarvā devatā viṣṇur yajñaḥ_
(GBr_2,1.12c) devatāś caiva yajñaṃ cārabhata ṛddhyai_
(GBr_2,1.12d) ṛdhnoty eva_
(GBr_2,1.12e) ubhau sahārambhāv ity āhuḥ_
(GBr_2,1.12f) udin nu śṛṅge sito mucyata iti
(GBr_2,1.12g) darśo vā etayoḥ pūrvaḥ paurṇamāsa uttaraḥ_
(GBr_2,1.12h) atha yat parastāt paurṇamāsa ārabhyate tad yathā pūrvaṃ kriyate

children.text: (GBr_2,1.12i) tad yat paurṇamāsam ārabhamāṇaḥ sarasvatyai caruṃ nirvapet sarasvate dvādaśakapālam amāvāsyā vai sarasvatī paurṇamāsaḥ sarasvān iti_
children.translated_text: When one beginning the <s>Paurṇamāsa</s> offers a porridge to <s>Sarasvatī</s> and a twelve-potsherds cake to <s>Sarasvat</s> — for the new moon is <s>Sarasvatī</s> and the full moon is <s>Sarasvat</s>.

children.text: (GBr_2,1.12j) ubhāv evainau sahārabhata ṛddhyai_
children.translated_text: He takes hold of both of them together, for prosperity.

children.text: (GBr_2,1.12k) ṛdhnoty eva || 12 ||
children.translated_text: He prospers indeed. ||12||

body.translated_text:
One who desires to undertake the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> should offer an eleven-potsherds cake to <s>Agni-Viṣṇu</s>.
<s>Agni</s> indeed is all the deities, <s>Viṣṇu</s> is the sacrifice.
He takes hold of both the deities and the sacrifice, for prosperity.
He prospers indeed.
They say: 'Both should be undertaken together.'
'Indeed, the horn being raised, the white one is released.'
Of these two, <s>Darśa</s> (new moon) is the first, <s>Paurṇamāsa</s> (full moon) is the second.
But when one begins with the <s>Paurṇamāsa</s> subsequently, it is as if done first.

body.text:
(GBr_2,1.13a) agnaye pathikṛte 'ṣṭākapālaṃ nirvaped yasya prajñāteṣṭir atipadyate
(GBr_2,1.13b) bahiṣpathaṃ vā eṣa eti yasya prajñāteṣṭir atipadyate_
(GBr_2,1.13c) agnir vai devānāṃ pathikṛt
(GBr_2,1.13d) tam eva bhāgadheyenopāsarat

children.text: (GBr_2,1.13e) sa enaṃ panthānam apinayati_
children.translated_text: He leads him along the path.

children.text: (GBr_2,1.13f) anaḍvān dakṣiṇā
children.translated_text: An ox is the sacrificial fee (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>).

children.text: (GBr_2,1.13g) sa hi panthānam abhivahati || 13 ||
children.translated_text: For it draws along the path. ||13||

body.translated_text:
One whose known <s>iṣṭi</s> (offering) fails should offer an eight-potsherds cake to <s>Agni Pathikṛt</s> (the Path-maker).
For one whose known offering fails goes off the path.
<s>Agni</s> is indeed the path-maker of the gods.
Him he approaches with his share of the offering.

body.text:
(GBr_2,1.14a) agnaye vratapataye 'ṣṭākapālaṃ nirvaped ya āhitāgniḥ san pravaset_
(GBr_2,1.14b) bahu vā eṣa vratam atipātayati ya āhitāgniḥ san pravasati vratye 'hani striyaṃ vopaiti māṃsaṃ vāśnāti_

children.text: (GBr_2,1.14c) agnir vai devānāṃ vratapatiḥ_
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s> is indeed the lord of observances of the gods.

children.text: (GBr_2,1.14d) agnim etasya vratam agāt
children.translated_text: The observance of this one has gone to <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: (GBr_2,1.14e) tasmād etasya vratam ālambhayate || 14 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore he restores his observance. ||14||

body.translated_text:
One who, having established the sacred fires (<s>āhitāgni</s>), goes on a journey should offer an eight-potsherds cake to <s>Agni Vratapati</s> (Lord of Observances).
For one who, having established the fires, goes on a journey, approaches a woman on an observance day, or eats meat — he violates the observance greatly.

body.text:
(GBr_2,1.15a) agnaye vratabhṛte 'ṣṭākapālaṃ nirvaped ya āhitāgnir ārtijam aśru kuryāt_
(GBr_2,1.15b) ānīto vā eṣa devānāṃ ya āhitāgnis
(GBr_2,1.15c) tasmād etenāśru na kartavyam_
(GBr_2,1.15d) na hi devā aśru kurvanti_

children.text: (GBr_2,1.15e) agnir vai devānāṃ vratabhṛt_
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s> is indeed the bearer of observances of the gods.

children.text: (GBr_2,1.15f) agnim etasya vratam agāt
children.translated_text: The observance of this one has gone to <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: (GBr_2,1.15g) tasmād etasya vratam ālambhayate || 15 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore he restores his observance. ||15||

body.translated_text:
One who, having established the sacred fires, sheds tears of grief should offer an eight-potsherds cake to <s>Agni Vratabhṛt</s> (Bearer of Observances).
For one who has established the fires is brought near to the gods.
Therefore he should not shed tears,
for the gods do not shed tears.

children.translated_text: It is a released animal (<s>anusṛṣṭa</s>).

children.text: (GBr_2,1.16h) anusṛṣṭa iva hy etasya somapītho yasya pitā pitāmahaḥ somaṃ na pibati
children.translated_text: For the <s>Soma</s>-drinking of one whose father and grandfather have not drunk <s>Soma</s> is as if released (permitted).

children.text: (GBr_2,1.16i) tasmād eṣa eva tasyā devatāyāḥ paśūnāṃ samṛddhaḥ || 16 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore he is indeed prosperous in cattle of that deity. ||16||

body.translated_text:
One whose father and grandfather have not drunk <s>Soma</s> should sacrifice an ox released for <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>.
For one whose father and grandfather have not drunk <s>Soma</s> is diminished in vital power and strength.
Because the offering is to <s>Indra</s>, it endows him with vital power and strength.
For one whose father and grandfather have not drunk <s>Soma</s> is diminished in divine power and strength.
Because the offering is to <s>Agni</s> — and <s>Agni</s> is indeed all the deities —
he thereby endows him with all the deities.

children.text: (GBr_2,1.17z) sa hi saṃvatsarasya pratimā
children.translated_text: For he is the counterpart of the year.

children.text: (GBr_2,1.17aa) reta eva hy eṣo 'prajātaḥ
children.translated_text: For he is indeed the seed that has not yet been born.

children.text: (GBr_2,1.17bb) prajātyai || 17 ||
children.translated_text: For procreation. ||17||

body.translated_text:
The gods ran a race when the plants were ripe.
<s>Indra</s> knew: '<s>Agni</s> will certainly win these first.'
He said: 'Whichever of us two wins first, let that be ours together.'
<s>Agni</s> won them.
Then <s>Indra</s> won along with him.
Therefore this offering, though being for <s>Indra-Agni</s>, is called <s>Āgni-Aindra</s>.
At that time there was one ear of barley, one of rice, one of beans, one of sesame.
Then the <s>Viśvedevas</s> (All-gods) said: 'We shall spread these; let there be a share for us.'
Therefore the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> offering is for abundance.
Moreover, it spreads by this very means.
It should be in milk, for the sake of the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> character.

children.translated_text: He drove them away with the <s>Apratiratham</s>.

children.text: (GBr_2,1.18q) tasmād brahmāpratirathaṃ japann eti
children.translated_text: Therefore the <s>Brahman</s> priest goes reciting the <s>Apratiratham</s>.

children.text: (GBr_2,1.18r) yad brahmāpratirathaṃ japann eti yajñasyābhijityai rakṣasām apahatyai rakṣasām apahatyai || 18 ||
children.translated_text: That the <s>Brahman</s> priest goes reciting the <s>Apratiratham</s> is for the victory of the sacrifice and for the destruction of the <s>Rakṣas</s> (demons), for the destruction of the <s>Rakṣas</s>. ||18||

body.translated_text:
Now this is the <s>Apratiratham</s> (invincible): '<s>Indra's</s> arms are mighty, bull-like' —
With this indeed <s>Indra</s> conquered the <s>Asuras</s>.
The sacrificer who uses this becomes invincible and conquers his rival.
One should offer it in battle; one becomes invincible.
With this indeed <s>Bharadvāja</s> girded <s>Pratardana</s>.
He became a ruler (<s>rāṣṭrin</s>).
Whomever one desires to be a ruler, him one should gird with this.
He becomes a ruler.
With this indeed <s>Indra</s> conquered the <s>Virāj</s> (sovereign meter).
He recites ten verses.
The <s>Virāj</s> has ten syllables; with this the sacrificer conquers his <s>Virāj</s>-related rival.

children.translated_text: Now, that the two concluding offerings (<s>saṃyājyā</s>) are in the <s>Virāj</s> meter — food indeed is prosperity, and the <s>Virāj</s> is food — is for the securing of food and prosperity.

children.text: (GBr_2,1.19s) atha yan nava prayājā navānuyājā aṣṭau havīṃṣi vājinaṃ navamaṃ tan nakṣatrīyāṃ virājam āpnoti_
children.translated_text: Now, that there are nine fore-offerings and nine after-offerings, eight oblations, and the <s>Vājina</s> as the ninth — thereby one attains the <s>Virāj</s> associated with the <s>nakṣatras</s> (lunar mansions).

children.text: (GBr_2,1.19t) atho āhur daśanīṃ virājam iti prayājānuyājā havīṃṣy āghārāv ājyabhāgāv iti || 19 ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, they say it is the <s>Virāj</s> of ten: the fore-offerings, after-offerings, oblations, the two pourings, and the two portions of clarified butter (<s>ājyabhāgas</s>). ||19||

body.translated_text:
Now, here is the performance of the <s>Cāturmāsya</s> (seasonal) sacrifices.
One should perform the <s>Cāturmāsyas</s> on the full-moon day of <s>Phālgunī</s>.
For the full moon of <s>Phālgunī</s> is the mouth of the year; the later <s>Phālgunī</s> stars are the mouth, the earlier ones the tail.
Just as the two ends of something rolled up would meet, even so the two ends of the year come together.
When one sacrifices with the <s>Cāturmāsyas</s> on the full moon of <s>Phālgunī</s>, one yokes the year from its very mouth.
Moreover, these <s>Cāturmāsyas</s> are healing sacrifices.
Therefore they are performed at the junctions of the seasons.
For disease arises at the junctions of the seasons.

children.translated_text: (GBr 2,1.20u) Moreover, the <s>Vājins</s> are the divine horses.

children.text: (GBr_2,1.20v) atra devāḥ sāśvā abhīṣṭāḥ prītā bhavanti_
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,1.20v) Here the gods together with their horses become worshipped and gratified.

children.text: (GBr_2,1.20w) atha yat parastāt paurṇamāsena yajate tathā hāsya pūrvapakṣe vaiśvadeveneṣṭaṃ bhavati || 20 ||
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,1.20w) And when he sacrifices afterwards with the full-moon [offering], thus his offering through the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> is accomplished in the bright fortnight. [20]

body.translated_text: (GBr 2,1.20a) Now, when he sacrifices to <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s> first among the deities — <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s> are indeed the mouth of the gods. (GBr 2,1.20b) He thereby gratifies the gods through the mouth. (GBr 2,1.20c) And when he sacrifices to <s>Savitṛ</s> — that [sun] which shines yonder is <s>Savitṛ</s>. (GBr 2,1.20d) He thereby gratifies that very one. (GBr 2,1.20e) And when he sacrifices to <s>Sarasvatī</s> — speech indeed is <s>Sarasvatī</s>. (GBr 2,1.20f) He thereby gratifies speech. (GBr 2,1.20g) And when he sacrifices to <s>Pūṣan</s> — that [sun] which shines yonder is <s>Pūṣan</s>. (GBr 2,1.20h) He thereby gratifies that very one. (GBr 2,1.20i) And when he sacrifices to the <s>Maruts</s> of their own might (<s>svatavas</s>) — the <s>Maruts</s> of their own might are indeed terrible. (GBr 2,1.20j) He thereby gratifies them. (GBr 2,1.20k) And when he sacrifices to the <s>Viśve Devāḥ</s> (All-gods) — these <s>Viśve Devāḥ</s> are all the gods. (GBr 2,1.20l) He thereby gratifies them. (GBr 2,1.20m) And when he sacrifices to <s>Dyāvāpṛthivī</s> (Heaven and Earth) — <s>Dyāvāpṛthivī</s> are indeed the [two] foundations. (GBr 2,1.20n) [He does this] for the sake of a firm foundation. (GBr 2,1.20o) And when he sacrifices to the <s>Vājins</s> (prize-winners) — the <s>Vājins</s> are indeed the animals. (GBr 2,1.20p) He thereby gratifies the animals. (GBr 2,1.20q) Moreover, the <s>Vājins</s> are the seasons. (GBr 2,1.20r) He thereby gratifies the seasons. (GBr 2,1.20s) Moreover, the <s>Vājins</s> are the meters. (GBr 2,1.20t) He thereby gratifies the meters.

children.text: (GBr_2,1.21q) atha yan nava prayājā navānuyājā navaitāni havīṃṣi
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,1.21q) And there are nine fore-offerings (<s>prayājas</s>), nine after-offerings (<s>anuyājas</s>), and nine oblations.

children.text: (GBr_2,1.21r) samānāni tv eva pañca saṃcarāṇi havīṃṣi bhavanti pauṣṇāntāni
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,1.21r) Five of the oblations, however, are of the same [type], being shared offerings (<s>saṃcarāṇi</s>), ending with [the offering to] <s>Pūṣan</s>.

children.text: (GBr_2,1.21s) teṣām uktaṃ brāhmaṇam || 21 ||
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,1.21s) Their <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [teaching] has been stated. [21]

body.translated_text: (GBr 2,1.21a) Through the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> offering indeed, <s>Prajāpati</s> created creatures. (GBr 2,1.21b) Those [creatures], having been created but not yet released, ate the barley of <s>Varuṇa</s>. (GBr 2,1.21c) <s>Varuṇa</s> bound them with the fetters of <s>Varuṇa</s> (<s>varuṇapāśa</s>). (GBr 2,1.21d) Those creatures, approaching their father <s>Prajāpati</s>, beseeched him: 'Find that sacrificial rite by which, having sacrificed, you may gratify <s>Varuṇa</s>. (GBr 2,1.21e) When <s>Varuṇa</s> is gratified, (GBr 2,1.21f) may we be completely freed from the fetters of <s>Varuṇa</s> and from all evil.' (GBr 2,1.21g) Then <s>Prajāpati</s> saw that sacrificial rite — the <s>Varuṇapraghāsas</s> (rites for appeasing <s>Varuṇa</s>). (GBr 2,1.21h) He brought it forth. (GBr 2,1.21i) With it he sacrificed. (GBr 2,1.21j) Having sacrificed with it, he gratified <s>Varuṇa</s>. (GBr 2,1.21k) <s>Varuṇa</s>, gratified, freed the creatures from the fetters of <s>Varuṇa</s> and from all evil. (GBr 2,1.21l) The offspring of him who knows thus are indeed freed from the fetters of <s>Varuṇa</s> and from all evil — (GBr 2,1.21m) he who knows thus. (GBr 2,1.21n) And when they lead forth the fire — the very [fire] which they churn at the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>, that they lead forth. (GBr 2,1.21o) The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [teaching] regarding that which is churned has been stated. (GBr 2,1.21p) And as for the seventeen kindling verses (<s>sāmidhenīs</s>), the two <s>ājyabhāga</s> offerings with closing [formulas], the two <s>Virāj</s> [verses], and the concluding offerings (<s>saṃyājyas</s>) — their <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [teaching] has been stated.

children.text: (GBr_2,1.22o) ukthyā vājinaḥ_
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,1.22o) The <s>Ukthya</s> [rite follows, with] the <s>Vājins</s>.

children.text: (GBr_2,1.22p) atha yad apsu varuṇaṃ yajati sva evainaṃ tad āyatane prīṇāti_
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,1.22p) And when he sacrifices to <s>Varuṇa</s> in the waters, he thereby gratifies him in his own abode.

children.text: (GBr_2,1.22q) atha yat parastāt paurṇamāsena yajate tathā hāsya pūrvapakṣe varuṇapraghāsair iṣṭaṃ bhavati || 22 ||
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,1.22q) And when he sacrifices afterwards with the full-moon [offering], thus his offering through the <s>Varuṇapraghāsas</s> is accomplished in the bright fortnight. [22]

body.translated_text: (GBr 2,1.22a) Now, the <s>Aindrāgna</s> [cake] on twelve potsherds (<s>dvādaśakapāla</s>) — <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> are strength and splendor. (GBr 2,1.22b) He thereby establishes strength in splendor. (GBr 2,1.22c) And as for the <s>Vāruṇī āmikṣā</s> (curdled milk for <s>Varuṇa</s>) — <s>Indra</s> indeed is <s>Varuṇa</s>. (GBr 2,1.22d) And he partakes of milk offerings. (GBr 2,1.22e) Therefore the <s>Vāruṇī āmikṣā</s>. (GBr 2,1.22f) And as for the <s>Mārutī payasyā</s> (milk-offering for the <s>Maruts</s>) — the <s>Maruts</s> abide in the waters. (GBr 2,1.22g) For the waters are milk. (GBr 2,1.22h) Moreover, the <s>Maruts</s> are associated with <s>Indra</s>; the milk is of <s>Indra</s>. (GBr 2,1.22i) Therefore the <s>Mārutī payasyā</s>. (GBr 2,1.22j) And as for the <s>Kāya ekakapāla</s> (single-potsherd cake for <s>Ka</s>) — <s>Prajāpati</s> is <s>Ka</s> ('Who?'). (GBr 2,1.22k) It is for the attainment of <s>Prajāpati</s>. (GBr 2,1.22l) Or, 'Ka' is the name of happiness (<s>sukha</s>). (GBr 2,1.22m) He thereby places happiness upon himself. (GBr 2,1.22n) And when he gives a pair of cattle, that is the form of procreation.

children.text: (GBr_2,1.23v) atha yad vaiśvakarmaṇa ekakapālo 'sau vai viśvakarmā yo 'sau tapati_
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,1.23v) And as for the <s>Vaiśvakarmaṇa ekakapāla</s> (single-potsherd cake for <s>Viśvakarman</s>) — <s>Viśvakarman</s> is that [sun] which shines yonder.

children.text: (GBr_2,1.23w) etam eva tena prīṇāti_
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,1.23w) He thereby gratifies that very one.

children.text: (GBr_2,1.23x) atha yad ṛṣabhaṃ dadāty aindro ha yajñakratuḥ || 23 ||
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,1.23x) And when he gives a bull, the sacrificial rite is indeed of <s>Indra</s>. [23]

body.translated_text: (GBr 2,1.23a) This sacrificial rite, the <s>Sākamedhas</s>, is indeed of <s>Indra</s>. (GBr 2,1.23b) Just as a great king, having deployed army divisions before him, would travel along a safe path — so too he sacrifices to the deities beforehand. (GBr 2,1.23c) Just as there is the <s>Mahāvrata</s> of the <s>Soma</s> [sacrifice] yonder, so too is this <s>Iṣṭi-Mahāvrata</s> (great vow of the <s>iṣṭi</s>). (GBr 2,1.23d) And when he sacrifices first among the deities to <s>Agni Anīkavat</s> (Agni with a vanguard) — <s>Agni</s> is indeed the mouth of the gods. (GBr 2,1.23e) He thereby gratifies the gods through the mouth. (GBr 2,1.23f) And when at midday he sacrifices to the <s>Maruts Sāṃtapanas</s> (scorching Maruts) — the <s>Maruts Saṃtapanas</s> are indeed [the Maruts] of <s>Indra</s>. (GBr 2,1.23g) The midday [pressing] is of <s>Indra</s>. (GBr 2,1.23h) Therefore he sacrifices to them as connected with <s>Indra</s>. (GBr 2,1.23i) And when in the evening they proceed with the <s>Gṛhamedha</s> (householder's sacrifice) — the <s>Gṛhamedha</s> is indeed a rite for prosperity (<s>puṣṭikarma</s>). (GBr 2,1.23j) In the evening comes the prosperity of cattle. (GBr 2,1.23k) Therefore in the evening they proceed with the <s>Gṛhamedha</s>. (GBr 2,1.23l) And when the next day they proceed with the remnant of the <s>Gṛhamedha</s> mixed [with offerings], with a full ladle — they thereby extend the morning rite by means of the previous day's rite. (GBr 2,1.23m) And when in the morning he sacrifices to the playful <s>Maruts</s> (<s>Maruts Krīḍinas</s>) — the playful <s>Maruts</s> are indeed [those] of <s>Indra</s>. (GBr 2,1.23n) Therefore he sacrifices to them as connected with <s>Indra</s>. (GBr 2,1.23o) And when they lead forth the fire — the very [fire] which they churn at the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>, that they lead forth. (GBr 2,1.23p) The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [teaching] regarding that which is churned has been stated. (GBr 2,1.23q) And as for the seventeen kindling verses, the two <s>ājyabhāga</s> offerings with closing [formulas], the two <s>Virāj</s> [verses], and the concluding offerings — their <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [teaching] has been stated. (GBr 2,1.23r) And there are nine fore-offerings, nine after-offerings, and eight oblations; six of the oblations, however, are of the same [type], being shared offerings, ending with [the offering to] <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>. (GBr 2,1.23s) Their <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [teaching] has been stated. (GBr 2,1.23t) And when he sacrifices to <s>Mahendra</s> (Great <s>Indra</s>) last — the chief indeed takes the end portion. (GBr 2,1.23u) Therefore he sacrifices to him last.

children.text: (GBr_2,1.24q) ṣaḍ vā ṛtavaḥ_
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,1.24q) Six indeed are the seasons.

children.text: (GBr_2,1.24r) ṛtavaḥ pitaraḥ
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,1.24r) The seasons are the ancestors.

children.text: (GBr_2,1.24s) pitṝṇām āptyai || 24 ||
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,1.24s) [This is] for the attainment of the ancestors. [24]

body.translated_text: (GBr 2,1.24a) And when in the afternoon they proceed with the ancestor-sacrifice (<s>Pitṛyajña</s>) — the afternoon is the portion of the ancestors (<s>Pitṛs</s>). (GBr 2,1.24b) Therefore in the afternoon they proceed with the ancestor-sacrifice. (GBr 2,1.24c) They say: 'Since the ancestors have the dark fortnight as their portion, why do they sacrifice to them in the bright fortnight?' (GBr 2,1.24d) These ancestors are indeed gods. (GBr 2,1.24e) Therefore they sacrifice to them in the bright fortnight. (GBr 2,1.24f) And when he recites one kindling verse three times — the ancestors are single (<s>sakṛt</s>). (GBr 2,1.24g) Therefore he recites one kindling verse three times. (GBr 2,1.24h) And when he does not utter the ancestral lineage (<s>ārṣeya</s>) of the sacrificer — lest he should harm the sacrificer. (GBr 2,1.24i) And when he invokes '<s>Soma</s> accompanied by the ancestors,' 'the ancestors seated on the <s>barhis</s> (sacred grass),' 'the fire-consumed ancestors' — (GBr 2,1.24j) some do not invoke their own glory, saying 'This is the glory of the sacrificer,' but the established [practice] is that he should invoke. (GBr 2,1.24k) For this is the glory of <s>Agni</s>. (GBr 2,1.24l) He calls out 'Oṃ <s>Svadhā</s>!' (GBr 2,1.24m) The response is '<s>Astu Svadhā</s>!' (Let there be the <s>Svadhā</s> offering!) (GBr 2,1.24n) For <s>Svadhā</s> is the [offering call] of the ancestors. (GBr 2,1.24o) And when he removes the [bundles of] <s>barhis</s> (sacred grass) from the fore-offerings and after-offerings — offspring are indeed the <s>barhis</s>; lest he should place offspring among the ancestors. (GBr 2,1.24p) These indeed amount to six.
