children.text: (GBr_2,1.25bb) atha yad antata ādityeṣṭyā yajatīyaṃ vā aditiḥ_
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,1.25bb) And when at the end he sacrifices with the <s>Ādityeṣṭi</s> (offering to <s>Āditya</s>) — this [earth] indeed is <s>Aditi</s>.

children.text: (GBr_2,1.25cc) asyām evainam antataḥ pratiṣṭhāpayati_
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,1.25cc) He thereby establishes him upon this [earth] at the end.

children.text: (GBr_2,1.25dd) atha yat parastāt paurṇamāsena yajate tathā hāsya pūrvapakṣe sākamedhair iṣṭaṃ bhavati || 25 ||
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,1.25dd) And when he sacrifices afterwards with the full-moon [offering], thus his offering through the <s>Sākamedhas</s> is accomplished in the bright fortnight. [25]

body.translated_text: (GBr 2,1.25a) And when the two <s>ājyabhāga</s> (clarified butter portions) offerings contain [words] of 'living' — he thereby gives life to the sacrificer. (GBr 2,1.25b) And when there are three offering-verses (<s>yājyās</s>) for each oblation — with the first he invites them. (GBr 2,1.25c) With the second he makes them come. (GBr 2,1.25d) With the third he verily bestows [the offering upon them]. (GBr 2,1.25e) Moreover, he thereby distinguishes the sacrifice to the gods from the ancestor-sacrifice. (GBr 2,1.25f) The ancestor-sacrifice is indeed established in the south. (GBr 2,1.25g) They thereby make it established in the north. (GBr 2,1.25h) And when he sacrifices to <s>Agni Kavyavāhana</s> (Agni the carrier of offerings to the ancestors) last — this is the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> (making the offering succeed) of the ancestors. (GBr 2,1.25i) Therefore he sacrifices to <s>Agni Kavyavāhana</s> last. (GBr 2,1.25j) And when, having invoked the <s>Iḍā</s> (libation) and smelled it, they do not eat — the <s>Iḍā</s> is indeed the animals. (GBr 2,1.25k) Lest he should harm the animals. (GBr 2,1.25l) And when at the <s>Sūktavāka</s> (praise recitation) he recites the blessings for the sacrificer — lest he should harm the sacrificer. (GBr 2,1.25m) And when they do not perform the concluding sacrifice with the wife — lest he should harm the wife. (GBr 2,1.25n) And when they purify [themselves] with the strainer (<s>pavitravat</s>) — the waters are peace and medicine. (GBr 2,1.25o) This peace and medicine is performed at the end of the sacrifice. (GBr 2,1.25p) And when the <s>Adhvaryu</s> makes offerings (<s>nipṛṇāti</s>) to the ancestors — the living ones indeed, following the ancestors, the human ancestors flow along. (GBr 2,1.25q) Moreover, he thereby distinguishes the sacrifice to the gods from the ancestor-sacrifice. (GBr 2,1.25r) The ancestor-sacrifice is indeed established in the south. (GBr 2,1.25s) They thereby make it established in the north. (GBr 2,1.25t) And when, going eastward, they approach the sun (<s>Āditya</s>) — <s>Āditya</s> is the world of the gods. (GBr 2,1.25u) The ancestors are the world of the ancestors. (GBr 2,1.25v) They thereby cross from the world of the ancestors to the world of the gods. (GBr 2,1.25w) And when, going southward, they approach the fires — they thereby perform their share among the gods at the end with delight. (GBr 2,1.25x) And when, going northward, they sacrifice with the <s>Traiyambaka</s> offerings — they thereby gratify <s>Rudra</s> in his own direction. (GBr 2,1.25y) Moreover, he thereby distinguishes the sacrifice to the gods from the ancestor-sacrifice. (GBr 2,1.25z) The ancestor-sacrifice is indeed established in the south. (GBr 2,1.25aa) They thereby make it established in the north.

body.translated_text:
(GBr 2,1.26a) He attains the thirteenth month when he sacrifices with the <s>Śunāsīrya</s> sacrifice.
(GBr 2,1.26b) The year is as extensive as this thirteenth month.
(GBr 2,1.26c) Now, when they lead the fire forth, that very [fire] which they churn at the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> — that indeed they lead forth.
(GBr 2,1.26d) When it is churned, its <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [explanation] has been stated.
(GBr 2,1.26e) If it is not churned, the full-moon [sacrifice] becomes the basic framework.
(GBr 2,1.26f) The full-moon [sacrifice] is the foundation.
(GBr 2,1.26g) For the sake of foundation indeed. Now, when he sacrifices to <s>Vāyu</s> — <s>Vāyu</s> is indeed <s>prāṇa</s> (breath).
(GBr 2,1.26h) By that he pleases <s>prāṇa</s> indeed.
(GBr 2,1.26i) Now, when he sacrifices to <s>Śunāsīra</s> — <s>Śunāsīra</s> is indeed the year.
(GBr 2,1.26j) By that he pleases the year indeed.
(GBr 2,1.26k) Now, when he sacrifices to <s>Sūrya</s> — that <s>Sūrya</s> is the one who shines yonder.
(GBr 2,1.26l) Him indeed he pleases by that.
(GBr 2,1.26m) Now, when he gives a white [cow] as <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee), thereby he makes the form of that [<s>Sūrya</s>].
(GBr 2,1.26n) Now, when they perform the <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiation) as a substitute, they perform an auspicious rite indeed.
(GBr 2,1.26o) It is the pacification of the sacrifice, for the healing of the sacrificer.
(GBr 2,1.26p) By these <s>Cāturmāsya</s> (seasonal) sacrifices, the gods attained all desires, all offerings, and all immortality.
(GBr 2,1.26q) This <s>Prajāpati</s>, the year, is the twenty-fourth — that is, the <s>Cāturmāsya</s> sacrifices.
(GBr 2,1.26r) Of him, the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> is the mouth.
(GBr 2,1.26s) The <s>Varuṇapraghāsas</s> are the arms.
(GBr 2,1.26t) <s>Prāṇa</s>, <s>Apāna</s>, and <s>Vyāna</s> — these are the three offerings.
(GBr 2,1.26u) The <s>Mahāhavis</s> (great oblation) is the self.
(GBr 2,1.26v) The <s>Śunāsīrya</s> is the foundation.
(GBr 2,1.26w) This <s>Prajāpati</s>, the year, is indeed the <s>Cāturmāsya</s> sacrifices.
(GBr 2,1.26x) <s>Prajāpati</s> is everything.
(GBr 2,1.26y) The <s>Cāturmāsya</s> sacrifices are everything.
(GBr 2,1.26z) By everything he attains everything — whoever knows thus, and whoever, knowing thus, sacrifices with the <s>Cāturmāsya</s> sacrifices.

children.text: (GBr_2,2.1z) yonīn vā eṣa kāmyān paśūn ālabhate yo 'niṣṭvaindrāgnena kāmyaṃ paśum ālabhata iṣṭvālambhaḥ samṛddhyai || 1 ||
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,2.1z) He indeed offers optional animals without foundation who offers an optional animal without first offering the <s>Aindrāgna</s> [animal]. One should offer [the optional animal] only after offering [the <s>Aindrāgna</s>], for the sake of success. [1]

body.translated_text:
(GBr 2,2.1a) <s>Oṃ</s> — The fires of one who has established the sacred fires desire flesh.
(GBr 2,2.1b) They first contemplate the sacrificer himself.
(GBr 2,2.1c) He who offers this <s>Aindrāgna</s> (dedicated to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>) animal every sixth month, thereby ransoms himself who has been seized by <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>.
(GBr 2,2.1d) He who desires long life should offer it.
(GBr 2,2.1e) <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> are indeed <s>prāṇa</s> (in-breath) and <s>apāna</s> (out-breath).
(GBr 2,2.1f) He thereby places <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s> in himself.
(GBr 2,2.1g) He becomes long-lived.
(GBr 2,2.1h) He who desires offspring should offer it.
(GBr 2,2.1i) <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> are indeed <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>.
(GBr 2,2.1j) <s>Prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s> — offspring are born following them.
(GBr 2,2.1k) He becomes rich in offspring.
(GBr 2,2.1l) He who desires cattle should offer it.
(GBr 2,2.1m) <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> are indeed <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>.
(GBr 2,2.1n) <s>Prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s> — cattle are born following them.
(GBr 2,2.1o) He becomes rich in cattle.
(GBr 2,2.1p) He who desires 'May I be free from disease in the world of the ancestors' should offer a green parrot of <s>Yama</s>, or a hornless [goat].
(GBr 2,2.1q) By this indeed <s>Yama</s> prospered in the other world.
(GBr 2,2.1r) He prospers in the world of the ancestors.
(GBr 2,2.1s) He who desires offspring should offer a mare dedicated to <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>.
(GBr 2,2.1t) <s>Prajāpati</s>, desiring to create offspring, did not find a second mate.
(GBr 2,2.1u) He perceived this mare of <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>.
(GBr 2,2.1v) For <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> is the generator of forms.
(GBr 2,2.1w) By that he created offspring.

children.translated_text: (GBr 2,2.2h) Therefore, whoever among those who have made the <s>Tānūnaptra</s> covenant first betrays, he comes to ruin.

children.text: (GBr_2,2.2i) yat tānūnaptraṃ samavadyati bhrātṛvyābhibhūtyai
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,2.2i) When one recites the <s>Tānūnaptra</s> [formula], it is for the overpowering of rivals.

children.text: (GBr_2,2.2j) bhavaty ātmanā parāsyāpriyo bhrātṛvyo bhavati || 2 ||
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,2.2j) He prevails by himself; his hostile rival is defeated. [2]

body.translated_text:
(GBr 2,2.2a) The gods split into five groups: <s>Agni</s> with the <s>Vasus</s>, <s>Soma</s> with the <s>Rudras</s>, <s>Indra</s> with the <s>Maruts</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s> with the <s>Ādityas</s>, and <s>Bṛhaspati</s> with the <s>Viśvedevas</s> (All-gods).
(GBr 2,2.2b) The gods said: 'We are subject to the <s>Asuras</s>, our rivals, because we are disunited among ourselves.'
(GBr 2,2.2c) 'Let us pledge together these dear bodies of ours.'
(GBr 2,2.2d) They pledged them together.
(GBr 2,2.2e) From those [pledged bodies came] an agreement: 'Whoever among us first betrays another [shall suffer].'
(GBr 2,2.2f) Because the bodies were pledged together, that is the nature of the <s>Tānūnaptra</s> (body-protection covenant) as <s>Tānūnaptra</s>.
(GBr 2,2.2g) Thereupon the gods prevailed; the <s>Asuras</s> were defeated.

children.translated_text: (GBr 2,2.3z) 'May the lord of consecration approve my consecration, may the lord of austerity [approve] my austerity; may I attain truth straightway; place me in the auspicious' — he says. This is according to the <s>Yajus</s> formula. [3]

body.translated_text:
(GBr 2,2.3a) He recites five times.
(GBr 2,2.3b) The sacrifice is fivefold.
(GBr 2,2.3c) For they pledged those [bodies] in five ways.
(GBr 2,2.3d) 'For <s>Āpati</s> (the lord) I take you,' he says.
(GBr 2,2.3e) <s>Āpati</s> is indeed <s>prāṇa</s> (breath).
(GBr 2,2.3f) By that he pleases <s>prāṇa</s> indeed.
(GBr 2,2.3g) 'For <s>Paripati</s> (the lord all around),' he says.
(GBr 2,2.3h) <s>Paripati</s> is indeed the mind.
(GBr 2,2.3i) By that he pleases the mind indeed.
(GBr 2,2.3j) '<s>Tānūnaptra</s>,' he says.
(GBr 2,2.3k) For those bodies were indeed pledged together.
(GBr 2,2.3l) 'For the <s>Śākvara</s>,' he says.
(GBr 2,2.3m) For they were pledged together for power.
(GBr 2,2.3n) 'For the mightiest of might (<s>Śakmanas</s>),' he says.
(GBr 2,2.3o) For they pledged together the mightiest part of themselves.
(GBr 2,2.3p) 'Unassailable,' he says.
(GBr 2,2.3q) For this is indeed unassailable.
(GBr 2,2.3r) 'Unassailable,' he says.
(GBr 2,2.3s) For this is indeed unassailable.
(GBr 2,2.3t) 'The vigor of the gods,' he says.
(GBr 2,2.3u) For this is indeed the vigor of the gods.
(GBr 2,2.3v) 'Protector from calumny,' he says.
(GBr 2,2.3w) For this indeed protects from calumny.

children.translated_text: (GBr 2,2.4r) 'Seeking wealth, seeking goods, I urge [you] to <s>Bhaga</s> (good fortune).'

children.text: (GBr_2,2.4s) ṛtam ṛtavādibhyo namo dive namaḥ pṛthivyā iti
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,2.4s) 'Truth to the truth-speakers! Homage to heaven! Homage to earth!'

children.text: (GBr_2,2.4t) dyāvāpṛthivībhyām eva namaskṛtyāsmiṃl loke pratitiṣṭhati pratitiṣṭhati || 4 ||
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,2.4t) Having made obeisance to heaven and earth, he becomes established in this world. [4]

body.translated_text:
(GBr 2,2.4a) The gods, having made ghee into a weapon, struck <s>Soma</s>.
(GBr 2,2.4b) The <s>sruc</s> ladles [are] the arms.
(GBr 2,2.4c) Therefore the <s>sruc</s> ladles do not destroy the <s>Soma</s> oblation.
(GBr 2,2.4d) [Otherwise] <s>Soma</s> would be killed.
(GBr 2,2.4e) Therefore the <s>sruc</s> ladles and the ghee were brought close together.
(GBr 2,2.4f) Close indeed is that which they perform when they perform the <s>Tānūnaptra</s>.
(GBr 2,2.4g) 'Shoot by shoot, O god <s>Soma</s>, may you swell for <s>Indra</s>, the knower of the single treasure' — he says.
(GBr 2,2.4h) Whatever of him diminishes and wastes, that they replenish by this.
(GBr 2,2.4i) 'May <s>Indra</s> swell for you; may you swell for <s>Indra</s>' — he says.
(GBr 2,2.4j) Both <s>Indra</s> and <s>Soma</s> they replenish indeed.
(GBr 2,2.4k) 'Replenish us, your friends, with true wisdom, with offspring, and with wealth' — he says.
(GBr 2,2.4l) The <s>Ṛtvijs</s> (priests) are indeed his friends.
(GBr 2,2.4m) Them he replenishes by this.
(GBr 2,2.4n) 'Hail to you, O god <s>Soma</s>! May I partake of the overflowing at the pressing' — he says.
(GBr 2,2.4o) He pronounces this as a blessing.
(GBr 2,2.4p) Those who replenish <s>Soma</s> move forth from this world.
(GBr 2,2.4q) For <s>Soma</s>, when replenished, has the atmosphere as his deity.

body.translated_text:
(GBr 2,2.5a) '<s>Makha</s>' — this is a name of the sacrifice, because of its power to prevent defects.
(GBr 2,2.5b) 'Defect' is said to mean 'gap' (<s>kha</s>).
(GBr 2,2.5c) '<s>Ma</s>' is the prohibition of that.
(GBr 2,2.5d) '[The sacrifice] shall not make a gap.'
(GBr 2,2.5e) For a sacrifice with gaps, like a broken vessel, leaks out.
(GBr 2,2.5f) A gap arises from disrespect between the priest and the sacrificer.
(GBr 2,2.5g) Or also from their mutual disregard, from the non-employment of <s>mantras</s>, ritual procedures (<s>Kalpa</s>), and <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [texts], or from the non-giving of prescribed <s>dakṣiṇās</s>, or from deficiency or excess, or from the failure to perform <s>prāyaścittas</s> (expiations) when portents and prodigies occur.
(GBr 2,2.5h) All this is entrusted to the <s>Brahman</s> [priest].
(GBr 2,2.5i) The <s>Brahman</s> priest who knows, who knows the <s>Bhṛgu-Aṅgiras</s> [tradition], who studies correctly, who has completed <s>brahmacarya</s> (Vedic studentship), whose limbs are neither deficient nor excessive, who is vigilant — he protects the sacrifice.
(GBr 2,2.5j) Through his negligence, or indeed through his absence, just as a broken ship in a deep great body of water would sink, becoming a share for fish, turtles, porpoises, crocodiles, <s>makaras</s> (sea-monsters), crabs, and <s>piśācas</s> (demons), and for other scavengers —
(GBr 2,2.5k) Even so, a sacrifice that is cut, broken, ruined, beset by portents and prodigies, manifold, and unconsecrated by the <s>Atharva</s> [rites] becomes a share for <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, and <s>Piśācas</s>, and for other scavengers.
(GBr 2,2.5l) On this there are also verses:
(GBr 2,2.5m) 'The sacrifice, cut, broken, and ruined, scattered in many ways — seizing the wealth of <s>iṣṭāpūrta</s> (sacrificial and charitable merit), it falls upon the sacrificer.'

body.text:
(GBr_2,2.5n) ṛtvijāṃ ca vināśāya rājño janapadasya ca | saṃvatsaraviriṣṭaṃ tad yatra yajño viriṣyate || [ed. viraṣyate, corrected p. 302]
(GBr_2,2.5o) dakṣiṇāpravaṇībhūto yajño dakṣiṇataḥ smṛtaḥ | hīnāṅgo rakṣasāṃ bhāgo brahmavedād asaṃskṛtaḥ ||
body.translated_text:
(GBr 2,2.5n) 'And for the destruction of the priests, the king, and the people — that is the year-long calamity wherever the sacrifice is ruined.'
(GBr 2,2.5o) 'A sacrifice inclined toward <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (fees) is remembered as [proper]; deficient in limbs, it becomes the share of <s>Rākṣasas</s> when unconsecrated by the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>.'

body.text: (GBr_2,2.5p) catuṣpāt sakalo yajñaś cāturhautravinirmitaḥ | caturvidhai sthito mantrair ṛtvigbhir vedapāragaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: (GBr 2,2.5p) 'The sacrifice, four-footed and complete, is fashioned by the fourfold priesthood (<s>Cāturhautra</s>); it stands established by mantras of four kinds, [recited] by priests who have mastered the <s>Vedas</s>.'

body.text:
(GBr_2,2.5q) prāyaścittair anudhyānair anujñānānumantraṇaiḥ | homaiś ca yajñavibhraṃśaṃ sarvaṃ brahmā prapūrayed || iti
(GBr_2,2.5r) tasmād yajamāno bhṛgvaṅgirovidam eva tatra brahmāṇaṃ vṛṇīyāt
(GBr_2,2.5s) sa hi yajñaṃ tārayatīti brāhmaṇam || 5 ||
body.translated_text:
(GBr 2,2.5q) 'By <s>prāyaścittas</s> (expiations), by meditations, by permissions, and by consecrating formulas, and by oblations — the <s>Brahman</s> priest should fill up every breach of the sacrifice.' Thus.
(GBr 2,2.5r) Therefore, the sacrificer should choose as the <s>Brahman</s> priest one who knows the <s>Bhṛgu-Aṅgiras</s> [tradition].
(GBr 2,2.5s) For he carries the sacrifice across — thus is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [teaching]. [5]

children.text: (GBr_2,2.6ii) śiro ha vā etad yajñasya yat pravargyas
children.translated_text: The <s>Pravargya</s> is indeed the head of the sacrifice.

children.text: (GBr_2,2.6jj) tasmāt pravargyavataiva yājayen nāpravagyeṇa
children.translated_text: Therefore one should have the sacrifice performed only with the <s>Pravargya</s>, never without it.

children.translated_text: And this [verse] has been recited in connection with it: '<s>Catvāri śṛṅgā</s>' (Four horns [has he]) [PS 8.13.3]. [6]

body.translated_text: The sacrifice (<s>Yajña</s>) indeed departed from the gods, [saying]: 'I shall not be food for you.' 'No,' the gods said, 'you shall indeed be food for us.' The gods tore it apart. When torn apart, it did not suffice for them. The gods said: 'Torn apart like this, it will surely not be enough for us. Come, let us reassemble it.' They reassembled it. Having reassembled it, they said: 'O <s>Aśvins</s>, heal this!' For the <s>Aśvins</s> are indeed the physicians of the gods. The <s>Aśvins</s> are the <s>Adhvaryus</s> (officiating priests). Therefore the <s>Adhvaryus</s> prepare the <s>Gharma</s> (hot milk offering). Having prepared it, the two said: 'O <s>Brahman</s> (priest), we shall proceed with the <s>Gharma</s>. O <s>Hotṛ</s>, praise the <s>Gharma</s>! O <s>Udgātṛ</s>, sing the <s>Sāmans</s>!' 'Proceed with the <s>Gharma</s>!' — he [the Brahman priest] gives permission. For they proceed when authorized by <s>Brahman</s>. For <s>Brahman</s> is indeed the lord of authorizations — for the sake of being impelled by <s>Savitṛ</s>. [With the mantras] '<s>Gharmaṃ tapāmi</s>' (I heat the <s>Gharma</s>) [PS 5.16.2], '<s>Brahma jajñānam</s>' (<s>Brahman</s> born first) [PS 5.2.2], '<s>Iyaṃ pitryā rāṣṭry etv agre</s>' (May this ancestral dominion go forth first) [PS 5.2.1] — one should attend to the <s>Gharma</s> being heated, reciting in the manner of a <s>Śastra</s> (recitation), by half-verses, without the call and response. [One should recite] with verses that are metrically complete. That indeed is the perfection of the sacrifice which is metrically complete. Whatever rite being performed is accompanied by an <s>Ṛc</s> or <s>Yajus</s> — he who knows thus reaches the far shore of that sacrifice safely. The <s>Gharma</s> is indeed a divine union (<s>Devamithuna</s>). Therefore they perform it in concealment. For union is performed in concealment — thus they call this the divine union. Its <s>Gharma</s> (pot) is the phallus; the two hooves are the two testicles; the <s>Upayamanī</s> (supporting vessel) is the two hip-bones; the milk is the semen. That seed, made of <s>Brahman</s>, he places in <s>Agni</s>, the divine womb, for procreation. That <s>Agni</s>, the divine womb, made of <s>Ṛcs</s>, made of <s>Yajus</s>, made of <s>Sāmans</s>, made of <s>Brahman</s>, made of immortality, made of oblations, endowed with all faculties — the <s>Yajamāna</s> (sacrificer) goes upward to the heavenly world. They say: 'One should not perform the <s>Pravargya</s> at the first sacrifice, for the subsequent sacrificial rites would turn away from him.' But one who is learned and versed in the <s>Vedas</s> may freely perform the <s>Pravargya</s> for him. For it is known that [the <s>Pravargya</s>] is the self (<s>Ātman</s>) of the sacrifice. He who sacrifices without the <s>Pravargya</s> sacrifices with a headless sacrifice.

children.text: (GBr_2,2.7w) tān upasadbhir evaibhyo lokebhyo nudamānā āyan_
children.translated_text: Driving [the <s>Asuras</s>] away from these worlds with the <s>Upasads</s>, they advanced.

children.text: (GBr_2,2.7x) tato devā abhavan parāsurāḥ
children.translated_text: Then the gods prevailed, and the <s>Asuras</s> were vanquished.

children.text: (GBr_2,2.7y) sarvebhya evaibhyo lokebhyo bhrātṛvyaṃ nudamāna eti ya evaṃvidvān upasadam upaiti || 7 ||
children.translated_text: He who, knowing thus, performs the <s>Upasad</s>, drives away his rival from all these worlds. [7]

body.translated_text: The gods and the <s>Ṛṣis</s> were arrayed in battle against the <s>Asuras</s>. The <s>Asuras</s> had these fortresses that had been conquered back: an iron one [on] earth, a silver one [in] the atmosphere, a golden one [in] heaven. The gods were defeated in every encounter. They realized: 'We have no secure base; therefore we are defeated.' They fashioned these [ritual] enclosures in return: the <s>Havirdhāna</s> (Soma shed) from heaven, the <s>Āgnīdhra</s> (fire-kindler's shed) from the atmosphere, and the <s>Sadas</s> (assembly hall) from earth. The gods said: 'Let us approach with the <s>Upasad</s> (siege ceremony), for by the <s>Upasad</s> one conquers a great fortress.' They drove them out from these worlds — with one [<s>Upasad</s>] from yonder world, with one from the atmosphere, with one from earth. Therefore they say: 'By the <s>Upasad</s> one conquers a great fortress.' Driven out from these worlds, [the <s>Asuras</s>] entered the seasons (<s>Ṛtus</s>). They approached as six. [The gods] drove them out from the seasons with the <s>Upasads</s> — with two from yonder world, with two from the atmosphere, with two from earth. Driven out from the seasons, they entered the year (<s>Saṃvatsara</s>). They approached as twelve. [The gods] drove them out from the year with the <s>Upasads</s> — with four from yonder world, with four from the atmosphere, with four from earth. Driven out from the year, they entered day and night. When [the gods] approached in the evening, with that they repelled them by night; when in the morning, by day. Therefore a cow's udder fills with milk in the evening for the morning [milking], and in the morning for the evening [milking].

children.translated_text: These very worlds are indeed the <s>Sādhya</s> gods (gods to be won).

children.text: (GBr_2,2.8l) sa ya evam etānt sādhyān veda sidhyaty asmai
children.translated_text: He who thus knows these <s>Sādhyas</s> — for him they are fulfilled.

children.text: (GBr_2,2.8m) sidhyaty amuṣmai sidhyaty asmai lokāya ya evaṃvidvān upasadam upaiti || 8 ||
children.translated_text: He prospers in yonder world, he prospers in this world — he who, knowing thus, performs the <s>Upasad</s>. [8]

body.translated_text: There should not be twelve <s>Upasads</s> for the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>. Without pacification, they would wear out [the sacrificer]. Nor [should there be only] three for the <s>Ahīna</s> (multi-day sacrifice). The sacrificial rite above being weightier, it would press down — just as a heavy load would break the neck, causing injury. For the <s>Ahīna</s> of twelve days, one should perform [twelve <s>Upasads</s>] — for firm support and stability. For the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> there should be three <s>Upasads</s> — for pacification and to prevent wearing out. Those gods did not dare to enter these worlds [held by] the <s>Asuras</s>. They entered them with <s>Agni</s> as their leader. That the <s>Agni</s> mantras are at the beginning of the <s>Upasads</s> — just as a landowner leads [people] into his field, so indeed they go, leading [the sacrificer] into these worlds with <s>Agni</s> as their leader. He who knows the <s>Sādhya</s> gods — for him they are fulfilled.

body.translated_text: Now, when the <s>Adhvaryu</s> says: 'O <s>Āgnīdhra</s>, announce the wives of the gods! O <s>Subrahmaṇya</s>, call the <s>Subrahmaṇyā</s> [invocation]!' — then, standing west of the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire, facing east, without eating, the <s>Āgnīdhra</s> announces the wives of the gods: '<s>Pṛthivī</s> (Earth) is the wife of <s>Agni</s>. <s>Vāc</s> (Speech) is the wife of <s>Vāta</s> (Wind). <s>Senā</s> (Army) is the wife of <s>Indra</s>. <s>Dhenā</s> (Nourishing Speech) is the wife of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>. <s>Pathyā</s> (the Way) is the wife of <s>Pūṣan</s>. <s>Gāyatrī</s> (meter) is the wife of the <s>Vasus</s>. <s>Triṣṭubh</s> (meter) is the wife of the <s>Rudras</s>. <s>Jagatī</s> (meter) is the wife of the <s>Ādityas</s>. <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> (meter) is the wife of <s>Mitra</s>. <s>Virāj</s> (meter) is the wife of <s>Varuṇa</s>. <s>Paṅkti</s> (meter) is the wife of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. <s>Dīkṣā</s> (consecration) is the wife of King <s>Soma</s>.' He who, knowing thus, as <s>Āgnīdhra</s> announces the wives of the gods — he surpasses his rivals, his rivals do not surpass him, he rises above his rivals. [9]

body.translated_text: Just as a chariot moves by resting on one spoke after another, so the sacrifice proceeds by resting on one body (<s>Tanū</s>) after another. Before the commencement [of the ritual], oblations should be offered at the <s>Āgnīdhrīya</s> fire. <s>Vāsiṣṭha Sātyahavya</s> indeed said this: 'When "<s>Askan Soma</s>" (the Soma has reached [the pressing stone]) is uttered, do not be alarmed — proceed! For it was just this morning that I stabilized the <s>Soma</s>.' The <s>Soma</s> does not spill for one who, knowing thus, drinks <s>Soma</s>. He would sit on a seat and drink <s>Soma</s> mixed with barley meal. [He said:] 'I indeed know the sacrifice from all sides — I who know these [rites]. It will not harm me.' Neither the drinking of <s>Soma</s> nor the beverage harms one who, knowing thus, drinks <s>Soma</s>. When they asked him: 'Why do you sit on a seat and drink <s>Soma</s> mixed with barley meal?' — he said: 'I establish the sacrifice in the deities.' The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who knows thus, for whom such a knower offers an expiation for a flaw in the sacrifice — he establishes the sacrifice in the deities. One should offer in return for the flaw of the sacrifice, for the sake of restoring it to its proper source. The sacrifice has indeed thirty-three bodies: twenty-nine are <s>Stoma</s>-portions, three are <s>Savanas</s> (pressings), and the sacrifice itself is the fourth. By the <s>Stoma</s>-portions one employs the <s>Stoma</s>-portions, by the <s>Savanas</s> the <s>Savanas</s>, by the sacrifice the sacrifice. All the bodies of his sacrifice become employed, all attained, all secured. 'At the impulse of the divine <s>Savitṛ</s>, [we praise] <s>Bṛhaspati</s> with praise.' Whatever <s>Savitṛ</s> impelled for the gods, by that they prospered. Impelled by <s>Savitṛ</s>, they praise, and they prosper. His <s>Stomas</s> (praises) prosper in the sacrifice.

children.translated_text: Having obtained it, one should touch the hospitality offering (<s>Ātithya</s>) with these very [mantras]: '<s>Yajñena yajñam ayajanta devāḥ</s>' (The gods worshipped the sacrifice with sacrifice) [ŚS 7.5.1]. [11]

body.translated_text: The gods and the <s>Asuras</s> were indeed in rivalry. The gods were performing the same things in the sacrifice [as the <s>Asuras</s>]. Whatever the gods did, the <s>Asuras</s> did the same. They could not achieve any distinction. The gods said: 'Come, let us take this sacrifice beyond and above the <s>Asuras</s>; we shall overpower them.' Having concealed it with these [mantras], they departed [reciting]: '<s>Yajūṃṣi yajñe samidhaḥ svāhā</s>' (The <s>Yajus</s> formulas are the fuel-sticks in the sacrifice; <s>Svāhā</s>!). They extended the sacrifice beyond and above the <s>Asuras</s>. The <s>Asuras</s> could not find their sacrifice. Then the gods prevailed, and the <s>Asuras</s> were vanquished. He who, knowing thus, extends the sacrifice beyond and above the <s>Asuras</s> — he prevails by himself, and his hostile rival is defeated. One should offer with these very [mantras], four by four, reciting them in sequence, when the sacrifice has gone awry. One should offer before the morning <s>Anuvāka</s> (recitation). For the sacrifice is as extensive as this sacrifice [itself]; he takes possession of it. He becomes possessed of the sacrifice; the other becomes without sacrifice. One should offer with these very [mantras] before the twelve-day [sacrifice]. This indeed is the manifest twelve-day [sacrifice]. Having obtained it, one should offer with these very [mantras].

body.translated_text:
When one knows, 'O <s>Brahman</s> priest, the <s>Soma</s> has spilled,' he consecrates the offering with this verse: '<s>Savitṛ</s>, the god, has now become worthy of praise; now he is to be invoked by men during the day; he who distributes treasures among men — may he bestow upon us the best wealth' [ṚV 4.54.1].
With the seven verses beginning '<s>ye agnayo apsv antar</s>' [ŚS 3.21.1] he makes seven oblations.
Whatever of his has been spilled, that he thereby restores to <s>Agni</s>.
For <s>Agni</s> is the foundation of well-performed oblations.
Then, moving about, he offers the oblations of spatterings with '<s>drapsaś caskanda</s>' [ṚV 10.17.11].
Whatever drops of his spatter while pressing <s>Soma</s>, or the stalks — those he thereby restores in the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire.
For the <s>Āhavanīya</s> is the foundation of oblations.
With '<s>yas te drapsa skandati</s>' [ṚV 10.17.12a] —
for a drop (<s>stoka</s>) is indeed a <s>drapsa</s>.

body.translated_text:
The seers did not see <s>Indra</s> face to face.
Only <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> saw him face to face.
He was afraid: 'May he not tell the other seers.'
He said: 'I shall tell you a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> (sacred teaching) whereby peoples having you as their priest shall be born.'
'But do not tell the other seers.'
To him he proclaimed these <s>Stomabhāgas</s> (praise-portions).
Thereafter peoples having <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> as their priest were born.
The <s>stoma</s> (praise) is indeed theirs; these are their portions.
That is the <s>Stomabhāga</s>-nature of the <s>Stomabhāgas</s>.
'You are a ray (<s>raśmi</s>), for the abode (<s>kṣaya</s>) I consecrate you' —
the abode is the gods;
to the gods he thus declares the sacrifice.
'You are departure (<s>preti</s>), for the law (<s>dharma</s>) I consecrate you' —
the law is humans;
to humans he thus declares the sacrifice.
'You are succession (<s>anviti</s>), you are junction (<s>saṃdhi</s>), you are counter-support (<s>pratidhi</s>)' —
three are the worlds;
in the worlds he thus establishes the sacrifice.
'You are support (<s>viṣṭambha</s>)' —
he thereby secures rain.
'You are the covering of the days (<s>prāvaḥ ahnāṃsi</s>)' — he thereby makes a pairing.
'You are the eager one (<s>uśik</s>), you are the beacon (<s>praketa</s>), you are the well-shining one (<s>suditi</s>)' —
eight <s>Vasus</s>, eleven <s>Rudras</s>, twelve <s>Ādityas</s>, Speech as the thirty-second, melody (<s>svara</s>) as the thirty-third — thirty-three gods.
To the gods he thus declares the sacrifice.
'You are vigor (<s>ojas</s>), for the ancestors (<s>Pitṛs</s>) I consecrate you' —
he thereby extends strength to the ancestors.
'You are the thread (<s>tantu</s>), for the offspring I consecrate you' —
he thereby extends the offspring and cattle.
'You are the wealthy one (<s>revat</s>), for the plants I consecrate you' —
he thereby establishes the sacrifice in the plants.
'You are the army-vanquisher (<s>pṛtanāṣāṭ</s>), for the cattle I consecrate you' —
he thereby extends the offspring and cattle.
'You are the victorious one (<s>abhijit</s>)' —
the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> (sixteenth <s>stoma</s>) is indeed the thunderbolt.
That thunderbolt is turned away.
Therefore it is separated from the others.

body.translated_text:
'You are the overlord (<s>adhipati</s>), you are the upholder (<s>dharuṇa</s>), you are the gliding one (<s>saṃsarpa</s>), you are the life-giver (<s>vayodhā</s>)' —
breath, downward breath, sight, hearing — these vital airs approach a person.
For procreation indeed.
'You are the threefold (<s>trivṛt</s>), you are the expanding one (<s>pravṛt</s>), you are the self-turning one (<s>svavṛt</s>), you are the follower (<s>anuvṛt</s>)' —
he thereby makes a pairing.
'You are the climbing one (<s>āroha</s>), you are the sprouting one (<s>praroha</s>), you are the re-growing one (<s>saṃroha</s>), you are the follower-growth (<s>anuroha</s>)' —
that is <s>Prajāpati</s> himself.
'You are the wealth-possessing one (<s>vasuka</s>), you are the wealth-grasper (<s>vasyaṣṭi</s>), you are the beauty-adorned (<s>veṣaśrī</s>)' —
that is establishment indeed.
'You are the stepping forth (<s>ākrama</s>), you are the crossing over (<s>saṃkrama</s>), you are the ascending (<s>utkrama</s>), you are the ascent (<s>utkrānti</s>)' —
that is prosperity indeed.
For whatever <s>Savitṛ</s> impelled for the gods, by that they prospered.
Impelled by <s>Savitṛ</s>, they recite the praises.
They prosper.
'Praised for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>' —
for <s>Bṛhaspati Āṅgirasa</s> is the <s>Brahman</s> priest of the gods.
Then, with <s>Anumati's</s> approval: '<s>Oṃ bhūḥ janat</s>' — at the morning pressing.
Guarded on both sides by the <s>ṛcs</s> (verses), guarded by the <s>Atharvāṅgiras</s> hymns — 'Praised!'
'<s>Oṃ bhuvaḥ janat</s>' — at the midday pressing.
Guarded on both sides by the <s>yajus</s> (formulas), guarded by the <s>Atharvāṅgiras</s>.
'Praised!' — '<s>Oṃ svaḥ janat</s>' — at the third pressing.
Guarded on both sides by the <s>sāmans</s> (chants), guarded by the <s>Atharvāṅgiras</s> — 'Praised!' indeed.

body.translated_text:
He who knows both the outgoing and returning <s>Stomabhāgas</s> should be the <s>Brahman</s> priest when two rival <s>Soma</s> sacrifices are performed simultaneously.
'Praised for vigor, praised for nourishment, praised! Of god <s>Savitṛ</s>, at the impelling, <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>, you the <s>Vasus</s>, you the gods, the <s>Rudras</s>, you the gods, the <s>Ādityas</s>, you the gods, the <s>Sādhyas</s>, you the gods, the <s>Āptyas</s>, you the gods, the <s>Viśvedevas</s>, you the gods, all gods — from all sides we invoke you' [VaitS 17.7].
'For our people may there be exclusive possession' [cf. PS 5.4.9c].
'From here may he create heroic power' [PS 5.4.9d].
These are indeed the outgoing and returning <s>Stomabhāgas</s>.
Reciting them, he should look down upon the rival's <s>Brahman</s> priest from above.
Thereupon their <s>Brahman</s> priest falls headfirst.
Thereupon the sacrifice falls.
Thereupon the sacrificer falls.
When the sacrificer falls headfirst, that country in whose half they sacrifice falls headfirst.
The gods and the <s>Asuras</s> once performed two rival <s>Soma</s> sacrifices.
Now <s>Bṛhaspati Āṅgirasa</s> was the <s>Brahman</s> priest of the gods.
He, reciting the outgoing and returning <s>Stomabhāgas</s>, looked down upon the <s>Brahman</s> priest of the <s>Asuras</s> from above.

body.translated_text:
The gods lost the sacrifice.
They won it back from the <s>Āgnīdhra</s> (fire-kindler's shed).
That is this unconquered part of the sacrifice — the <s>Āgnīdhra</s>.
When one distributes the <s>dhiṣṇya</s> fires from the <s>Āgnīdhra</s>, from that very place one extends the sacrifice again,
for the sake of victory.
Indeed, those who go out for the <s>Bahiṣpavamāna</s> (external purification chant) depart.
When the <s>Bahiṣpavamāna</s> has been praised, he says:
'O <s>Āgnīdh</s>! Distribute the fires, strew the <s>barhis</s> (sacred grass), prepare the sacrificial cakes!'
They come back extending the sacrifice unconquered.
For two pressings he distributes with embers, for the third pressing with sticks — for the sake of brilliance.
Moreover, it comes together in this way.
From the south, the <s>Rakṣas</s> (demons) sought to destroy the sacrifice of the gods.

body.translated_text:
Now they ask: 'Why are the <s>pravṛtāhutis</s> (ongoing oblations) offered only in the <s>Soma</s> sacrifice (<s>adhvara</s>) and not in the <s>haviryajña</s> (oblation sacrifice)?'
For the <s>haviryajña</s> is an incomplete worship of the gods.
But this alone is the complete worship of the gods — the <s>Soma</s> sacrifice.
Therefore the <s>pravṛtāhutis</s> are offered only in the <s>Soma</s> sacrifice.
'May I be pleasing to <s>Vāc</s> (Speech), pleasing to <s>Vācaspati</s> (Lord of Speech)! O divine <s>Vāc</s>, whatever is the sweetest of speech, in that place me! <s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Vāc</s>! <s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Vācaspati</s>! <s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Sarasvatī</s>! <s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Sarasvatī</s>!' — he offers with the <s>svāhā</s> call at the beginning.
Therefore, from this point onward, <s>Vāc</s>, once released, carries the sacrifice; the mind carries the later part.
For the mind is pleased by the mind.
But some offer seven oblations, saying 'Seven meters are set in motion, one per mantra.'
Just as a girdle is cast around for the separation of the pure and impure, even so are these laid down for the separation of the pure and impure, for the separation of the sacrifice.
For to the east of the <s>dhiṣṇya</s> fires are the worlds of the gods; to the west, of men.
Therefore, those drinking <s>Soma</s> should not approach the <s>dhiṣṇya</s> fires going eastward,
for that belongs to the people;
for they ascend to the world of the gods.
The <s>Āgnīdhra</s> and the <s>Sadas</s> (assembly hall) are their foundation and impelling place.
He who moves about without knowing this suffers harm.
But he who moves about with knowledge does not suffer harm from the <s>dhiṣṇya</s> fires. ||17||

<s>Prajāpati</s> is indeed the sacrifice.
In him are all desires, all offerings, all immortality.
These <s>dhiṣṇya</s> fires are his guardians.
About to enter the <s>Sadas</s>, one pays homage to them,
saying '<s>Namaḥ, namaḥ</s>' (Salutation, salutation).
For the gods do not go beyond a salutation.
They, when saluted, let the doer pass.

body.translated_text: He who knows the <s>Gandharvas</s> of the assembly hall does not suffer affliction in the assembly. One about to crawl into the assembly hall should say, 'Homage to the Observer (<s>Upadraṣṭṛ</s>).' <s>Agni</s> indeed is the observer; to him he surrenders himself. He lives his full life and does not perish before old age—whoever knows thus. Having crawled into the assembly hall, he should say, 'Homage to the Listener (<s>Upaśrotṛ</s>).' <s>Vāyu</s> indeed is the listener. To him he surrenders himself. He lives his full life and does not perish before old age—whoever knows thus. While moving through the assembly hall, he should say, 'Homage to the Proclaimer (<s>Anukhyātṛ</s>).' <s>Āditya</s> (the sun) indeed is the proclaimer. To him he surrenders himself. He lives his full life and does not perish before old age—whoever knows thus. Having entered the assembly hall, he should say, 'Homage to the Observer.' The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> (priest) indeed is the observer. To him he surrenders himself. He lives his full life and does not perish before old age—whoever knows thus. These are the <s>Gandharvas</s> of the assembly hall. He who, not knowing these <s>Gandharvas</s> of the assembly hall, enters the assembly hall—he suffers affliction in the assembly. But he who moves about knowing this does not suffer affliction in the assembly. By this the <s>Aṅgirasas</s> indeed traversed the entire assembly hall. They do not suffer affliction in the assembly. And for those whom one desires not to suffer affliction in the assembly, one should recite this around the entire assembly hall for them.

body.translated_text: They say: 'Since the sacrifice belongs to <s>Indra</s>, why is it that at the morning pressing, only two of those who have set forth offer directly with <s>Aindrī</s> (Indra-related) verses—the <s>Hotṛ</s> and the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>?' The <s>Hotṛ</s> offers with '<s>idaṃ te somyaṃ madhu</s>' (ṚV 8.65.8). The <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> offers with '<s>indra tvā vṛṣabhaṃ vayam</s>' (ṚV 3.40.1). The others offer with verses to various deities. How then do theirs become <s>Aindrī</s>? The <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> offers with '<s>mitraṃ vayaṃ havāmahe</s>' (ṚV 1.23.4a), '<s>varuṇaṃ somapītaye</s>' (ṚV 1.23.4b). Whatever has the quality of drinking is an <s>Aindra</s> form. By that he pleases <s>Indra</s>. The <s>Potṛ</s> offers with '<s>maruto yasya hi kṣaye</s>' (ṚV 1.86.1a), '<s>sa sugopātamo janaḥ</s>' (ṚV 1.86.1c). <s>Indra</s> indeed is the protector (<s>gopā</s>). That is an <s>Aindra</s> form. By that he pleases <s>Indra</s>. The <s>Neṣṭṛ</s> offers with '<s>agne patnīr ihā vaha</s>' (ṚV 1.22.9a), '<s>tvaṣṭāraṃ somapītaye</s>' (ṚV 1.22.9c). Whatever has the quality of drinking is an <s>Aindra</s> form. By that he pleases <s>Indra</s>. The <s>Āgnīdhra</s> offers with '<s>ukṣānnāya vaśānnāya</s>' (ṚV 8.43.11a), '<s>somapṛṣṭhāya vedhase</s>' (ṚV 8.43.11b). <s>Indra</s> indeed is the ordainer (<s>vedhās</s>). That is an <s>Aindra</s> form. By that he pleases <s>Indra</s>. '<s>prātaryāvabhir ā gataṃ devebhir jenyāvasū indrāgnī somapītaye</s>' (ṚV 8.38.7)—the <s>Acchāvāka</s>'s verse is self-accomplished. Thus these become <s>Aindrī</s>.

children.text: (GBr_2,2.21k) indro vai prātaḥsavanaṃ nābhyajayat
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> did not win the morning pressing.

children.text: (GBr_2,2.21l) sa etābhir mādhyaṃdinaṃ savanam abhyatṛṇat
children.translated_text: With these verses he overcame the midday pressing.

children.text: (GBr_2,2.21m) tad yad etābhir mādhyaṃdinaṃ savanam abhyatṛṇat tasmād etā abhitṛṇavatyo bhavanti || 21 ||
children.translated_text: Because with these he overcame (<s>abhyatṛṇat</s>) the midday pressing, therefore these are the <s>abhitṛṇavatī</s> (victory) verses. || 21 ||

body.translated_text: At the midday pressing, all of those who have set forth offer directly with <s>Aindrī</s> verses. Some say, with <s>abhitṛṇavatī</s> (victory) verses. The <s>Hotṛ</s> offers with '<s>pibā somam abhi yam ugra tardaḥ</s>' (ṚV 6.17.1). The <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> offers with '<s>sa īṃ pāhi ya ṛjīṣī tarutraḥ</s>' (ṚV 6.17.2). The <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> offers with '<s>evā pāhi pratnathā mandatu tvā</s>' (ṚV 6.17.3). The <s>Potṛ</s> offers with '<s>arvāṅ ehi somakāmaṃ tvāhuḥ</s>' (ṚV 1.104.9). The <s>Neṣṭṛ</s> offers with '<s>tavāyaṃ somas tvam ehy arvāṅ</s>' (ṚV 3.35.6). The <s>Acchāvāka</s> offers with '<s>indrāya somāḥ pradivo vidānāḥ</s>' (ṚV 3.36.2). The <s>Āgnīdhra</s> offers with '<s>āpūrṇo asya kalaśaḥ svāhā</s>' (ṚV 3.32.15). Thus these become <s>abhitṛṇavatī</s> verses.

children.text: (GBr_2,2.22x) yan nānādevatyās tenānyā devatāḥ prīṇāti
children.translated_text: Because they are addressed to various deities, he thereby pleases other deities as well.

children.text: (GBr_2,2.22y) yad u jagatprāsāhā jāgatam u vai tṛtīyasavanam_
children.translated_text: Because they are in the <s>Jagatī</s> meter, which predominates, the third pressing is indeed <s>Jāgata</s> (of the Jagatī).

children.text: (GBr_2,2.22z) tṛtīyasavanasya samaṣṭyai || 22 ||
children.translated_text: For the completion of the third pressing. || 22 ||

body.translated_text: They say: 'Since the third pressing belongs to <s>Indra</s> and the <s>Ṛbhus</s>, why does only one of those who have set forth at the third pressing offer directly with <s>Aindrārbhavī</s> verses—the <s>Hotṛ</s> alone, with "<s>indra ṛbhubhir vājavadbhiḥ samukṣitam</s>" (ṚV 3.60.5)?' The others offer with verses to various deities. How then do theirs become <s>Aindrārbhavī</s>? The <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> offers with '<s>indrāvaruṇā sutapāv imaṃ sutam</s>' (ṚV 6.68.10), '<s>yuvo ratho adhvaro devavītaye</s>'—'he carries many things.' That is the form of the <s>Ṛbhus</s>. The <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> offers with '<s>indraś ca somaṃ pibataṃ bṛhaspataye</s>' (ṚV 4.50.10a), '<s>ā vāṃ viśantv indavaḥ svābhuvaḥ</s>' (ṚV 4.50.10c)—'he carries many things.' That is the form of the <s>Ṛbhus</s>. The <s>Potṛ</s> offers with '<s>ā vo vahantu saptayo raghuṣyadaḥ</s>' (ṚV 1.85.6a), '<s>raghupatvānaḥ pra jigāta bāhubhiḥ</s>' (ṚV 1.85.6b)—'he carries many things.' That is the form of the <s>Ṛbhus</s>. The <s>Neṣṭṛ</s> offers with '<s>ameva naḥ suhavā ā hi gantana</s>' (ṚV 2.36.3)—'come' implies many. That is the form of the <s>Ṛbhus</s>. The <s>Acchāvāka</s> offers with '<s>indrāviṣṇū pibataṃ madhvo asya</s>' (ṚV 6.69.7a), '<s>ā vām andhāṃsi madirāṇy agman</s>' (ṚV 6.69.7c)—'he carries many things.' That is the form of the <s>Ṛbhus</s>. The <s>Āgnīdhra</s> offers with '<s>imaṃ stomam arhate jātavedase</s>' (ṚV 1.94.1a), '<s>ratham iva saṃ mahemā manīṣayā</s>' (ṚV 1.94.1b)—'he carries many things.' That is the form of the <s>Ṛbhus</s>. Thus these become <s>Aindrārbhavī</s>.

children.translated_text: But even if something has been seen by oneself, one does not trust the testimony of many people.

children.text: (GBr_2,2.23i) tasmād vicakṣaṇavatīṃ vācaṃ bhāṣante canasitavatīm_
children.translated_text: Therefore they speak speech that is discerning and delightful.

children.text: (GBr_2,2.23j) satyottarā haivaiṣāṃ vāg uditā bhavati || 23 ||
children.translated_text: Their speech, once uttered, is established in truth. || 23 ||

body.translated_text: They speak speech that is discerning and delightful. They illuminate the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. They delight the <s>Prājāpatya</s>. They speak truth. This among humans is truth—that which is sight (<s>cakṣus</s>). Therefore they say of one who has seen, 'He saw truly (<s>adrāk</s>).' When he says, 'I have seen (<s>adrākṣam</s>),' people believe him.

body.text:
(GBr_2,2.24a) samṛtayajño vā eṣa yad darśapūrṇamāsau
(GBr_2,2.24b) kasya vāva devā yajñam āgacchanti kasya vā na
(GBr_2,2.24c) bahūnāṃ vā etad yajamānānāṃ sāmānyam ahas

children.translated_text: He who seizes the deities on the day before—to his sacrifice they come on the next day.

children.text: (GBr_2,2.24f) tasmād vihavyasya catasra ṛco japet_
children.translated_text: Therefore one should recite the four verses of <s>Vihavya</s>.

children.text: (GBr_2,2.24g) yajñavido hi manyante eva soma eva samṛta iti yajño yajñena samṛtaḥ || 24 ||
children.translated_text: The knowers of sacrifice consider: <s>Soma</s> alone is the meeting point; sacrifice meets sacrifice. || 24 ||

body.translated_text: The <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new and full moon rites) are indeed a sacrifice that meets another sacrifice. To whose sacrifice do the gods come, and to whose do they not? The day is common to many sacrificers. Therefore one should seize the deities on the day before.

body.text: (GBr_2,2.24col) ity atharvavede gopathabrāhmaṇottarabhāge dvitīyaḥ prapāṭhakaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the second chapter (<s>prapāṭhaka</s>) of the later part (<s>uttarabhāga</s>) of the <s>Gopatha Brāhmaṇa</s> of the <s>Atharvaveda</s>.

children.text: (GBr_2,3.1i) tad āhuḥ ko nu somasya sviṣṭakṛdbhāga iti
children.translated_text: They ask: 'What then is the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> (well-offered) portion of <s>Soma</s>?'

children.text: (GBr_2,3.1j) yad eva somasyāgne vīhīty anuvaṣaṭkaroti tenaiva saṃsthitān somān bhakṣayantīty āhuḥ
children.translated_text: They say: when he utters <s>anuvaṣaṭ</s> with '<s>somasyāgne vīhi</s>,' by that very means they consume the completed <s>Soma</s> offerings.

children.text: (GBr_2,3.1k) sa u eṣa somasya sviṣṭakṛdbhāgo yad anuvaṣaṭkaroti || 1 ||
children.translated_text: This is indeed the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> portion of <s>Soma</s>—the <s>anuvaṣaṭkāra</s>. || 1 ||

body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>. The <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> is indeed the vessel of the gods. When he utters <s>vaṣaṭ</s>, he satisfies the deities with the vessel of the gods. And when they are thirsting at the conclusion, he satisfies them likewise; thus he satisfies the deities when he utters <s>anuvaṣaṭ</s>. Just as here one satisfies horses or cows again with a subsequent feeding, even so he satisfies the deities when he utters <s>anuvaṣaṭ</s>. They say: 'Attend to these fires'—meaning the <s>dhiṣṇya</s> hearths. Why then does he offer into the first fire and utter <s>vaṣaṭ</s> at the first? Because when he utters <s>anuvaṣaṭ</s> with '<s>somasyāgne vīhi</s>,' by that very <s>vaṣaṭ</s> utterance he pleases the <s>dhiṣṇya</s> hearths. And they say that those for whom <s>anuvaṣaṭ</s> is not uttered consume the <s>Soma</s> offerings after the conclusion of the rite.

children.text: (GBr_2,3.2q) brahma tapasīti_
children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s> in <s>tapas</s> (austerity).

children.text: (GBr_2,3.2r) etā eva tad devatāḥ pratiṣṭhānyāḥ pratitiṣṭhantīr idaṃ sarvam anu pratitiṣṭhati [ed. pratisthānyāḥ, corr. Patyal]
children.translated_text: These deities being established, all this that rests upon them becomes established accordingly.

children.text: (GBr_2,3.2s) pratitiṣṭhati prajayā paśubhir ya evaṃ veda || 2 ||
children.translated_text: He becomes established in progeny and cattle—whoever knows thus. || 2 ||

body.translated_text: The <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> is indeed the thunderbolt (<s>vajra</s>). Whomever one hates, meditating upon him in mind, one should utter <s>vaṣaṭ</s>. Upon him one places the thunderbolt. He utters '<s>ṣaṭ</s>' (six) in the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s>. Six are the seasons. For the attainment of the seasons. He utters '<s>vauṣaṭ</s>.' '<s>Vau</s>' means 'these,' and the seasons are six. He thereby places this in the seasons. He establishes it in the seasons. And the teacher <s>Vaida</s> said: 'By this he establishes six things.' Heaven is established in the atmosphere. The atmosphere in the earth. The earth in the waters. The waters in truth (<s>satya</s>). Truth in <s>Brahman</s>.

body.text:
(GBr_2,3.3a) trayo vai vaṣaṭkārāḥ_
(GBr_2,3.3b) vajro dhāmacchad riktaḥ
(GBr_2,3.3c) sa yad evoccair balaṃ vaṣaṭkaroti sa vajras
(GBr_2,3.3d) taṃ taṃ praharati dviṣate bhrātṛvyāya vadhaṃ yo 'sya stṛtyas tasmai starītave
(GBr_2,3.3e) tasmāt sa bhrātṛvyavatā vaṣaṭkṛtyaḥ_
(GBr_2,3.3f) atha yaḥ samaḥ saṃtato nirhāṇacchatsva dhāmacchat
(GBr_2,3.3g) taṃ taṃ prajāś ca paśavaś cānūpatiṣṭhante
(GBr_2,3.3h) tasmāt sa prajākāmena paśukāmena vaṣaṭkṛtyaḥ_
(GBr_2,3.3i) atha yenaiva ṣaḍ aparādhnoti sa riktaḥ_
(GBr_2,3.3j) riṇakty ātmānaṃ riṇakti yajamānam_
(GBr_2,3.3k) pāpīyān vaṣaṭkartā bhavati pāpīyān yasmai vaṣaṭkaroti
(GBr_2,3.3l) tasmāt tasyāśāṃ neyāt
(GBr_2,3.3m) kiṃ svit sa yajamānasya pāpabhadram ādriyeteti ha smāha yo 'sya vaṣaṭkartā bhavati_
(GBr_2,3.3n) atraivainaṃ yathā kāmayeta tathā kuryāt_
(GBr_2,3.3o) yaṃ kāmayeta yathaivānījāno 'bhūt tathaivejānaḥ syād iti yathaivāsyarcaṃ brūyāt tathaivāsya vaṣaṭkuryāt
(GBr_2,3.3p) samānam evainaṃ tat karoti
(GBr_2,3.3q) yaṃ kāmayeta pāpīyān syād ity uccaistarām asyarcaṃ brūyān nīcaistarāṃ vaṣaṭkuryāt
(GBr_2,3.3r) pāpīyāṃsam evainaṃ tat karoti

children.text: (GBr_2,3.3s) yaṃ kāmayeta śreyān syād iti nīcaistarām asyarcaṃ brūyād uccaistarāṃ vaṣaṭkuryāt_
children.translated_text: For him whom one wishes to become better — one should recite his <s>Ṛc</s> (verse) softer and utter the <s>Vaṣaṭkāra</s> louder.

children.text: (GBr_2,3.3t) śreyāṃsam evainaṃ tat karoti
children.translated_text: That makes him better.

children.text: (GBr_2,3.3u) śriya evainaṃ tac chriyam ādadhāti || 3 ||
children.translated_text: It places him in glory, in prosperity. [3]

body.translated_text: There are indeed three kinds of <s>Vaṣaṭkāra</s> (offering call): the <s>Vajra</s> (thunderbolt), the <s>Dhāmacchat</s> (abode-covering), and the <s>Rikta</s> (empty). When he utters the <s>Vaṣaṭkāra</s> loudly and with force, that is the <s>Vajra</s>. With that he strikes at his hateful rival — a blow for his enemy, to lay him low. Therefore that [<s>Vaṣaṭkāra</s>] should be uttered by one who has a rival. Now, the one that is even, continuous, and gradually diminishing is the <s>Dhāmacchat</s> (abode-covering). With that, offspring and cattle follow him. Therefore that should be uttered by one desiring offspring and cattle. Now, the one by which he errs in six ways is the <s>Rikta</s> (empty). It empties [ruins] oneself, it empties the <s>Yajamāna</s> (sacrificer). The utterer of the <s>Vaṣaṭkāra</s> becomes worse off, and he for whom he utters it becomes worse off. Therefore one should not entertain hopes regarding that. 'What evil or good of the <s>Yajamāna</s> should one attend to?' — thus asks the one who is his <s>Vaṣaṭkāra</s> utterer. In this matter, one may do as one desires. For him whom one wishes to remain just as he was before the sacrifice — one should utter the <s>Vaṣaṭkāra</s> at the same [pitch] as one recites his <s>Ṛc</s> (verse). That makes him remain the same. For him whom one wishes to become worse off — one should recite his <s>Ṛc</s> louder and utter the <s>Vaṣaṭkāra</s> softer. That makes him worse off.

body.text:

children.translated_text: The <s>Vaṣaṭkāra</s> should be continuous with the <s>Ṛc</s> (verse),

children.text: (GBr_2,3.4e) saṃtatyai
children.translated_text: for the sake of continuity.

children.text: (GBr_2,3.4f) saṃdhīyate prajayā paśubhir ya evaṃ veda || 4 ||
children.translated_text: He is joined with offspring and cattle — whoever knows thus. [4]

body.translated_text: For whichever deity the oblation has been taken up, one should utter the <s>Vaṣaṭkāra</s> while meditating on that deity with the mind. Thereby one directly pleases the deity. One grasps the deity face to face.

body.text:
(GBr_2,3.5a) vajro vai vaṣaṭkāraḥ
(GBr_2,3.5b) sa u eṣa prahṛto 'śānto dīdāya tasya ha na sarva eva śāntiṃ veda no pratiṣṭhām_
(GBr_2,3.5c) tasmād dhāpy etarhi bhūyān iva mṛtyus
(GBr_2,3.5d) tasya haiṣaiva śāntir eṣā pratiṣṭhā yad vāg iti
(GBr_2,3.5e) vaṣaṭkṛtya vāg ity anumantrayate
(GBr_2,3.5f) vaṣaṭkāra mā māṃ pramṛkṣo māhaṃ tvāṃ pramṛkṣaṃ bṛhatā mana upahvaye vyānena śarīraṃ pratiṣṭhāsi pratiṣṭhāṃ gaccha pratiṣṭhāṃ mā gamayed iti [ed. pratiṣṭhīsi, corrected p. 302]
(GBr_2,3.5g) tad u smāha dīrgham evaitait sadaprabhv ojaḥ saha oja ity anumantrayeta_

children.text: (GBr_2,3.5h) ojaś ca ha vai sahaś ca vaṣaṭkārasya priyatame tanvau
children.translated_text: <s>Ojas</s> (strength) and <s>Sahas</s> (might) are indeed the two dearest bodies of the <s>Vaṣaṭkāra</s>.

children.text: (GBr_2,3.5i) priyābhyām eva tat tanūbhyāṃ samardhayati
children.translated_text: Through those two dear bodies he brings it to fulfillment.

children.text: (GBr_2,3.5j) priyayā tanvā samṛdhyate ya evaṃ veda || 5 ||
children.translated_text: Through [its] dear body he is fulfilled — whoever knows thus. [5]

body.translated_text: The <s>Vaṣaṭkāra</s> is indeed a <s>Vajra</s> (thunderbolt). Once hurled, it blazes, unpacified; and no one knows fully its pacification or its resting place. Therefore even now, death seems to be more [prevalent]. Its pacification and resting place is this — the word '<s>Vāk</s>' (speech). After uttering the <s>Vaṣaṭkāra</s>, one murmurs '<s>Vāk</s>' (speech) [as a pacification]: 'O <s>Vaṣaṭkāra</s>, do not destroy me; may I not destroy you. With the <s>Bṛhat</s> [<s>Sāman</s>] I invoke [you] with my mind. Through <s>Vyāna</s> (diffused breath) you are the foundation of the body. Go to your resting place; may it lead me to a firm resting place.' And he also said: 'One should murmur this [invocation] for a long time, constantly, with power: "<s>Ojas</s> (strength), <s>Sahas</s> (might), <s>Ojas</s> (strength)!"'

body.text:
(GBr_2,3.6a) vāk ca vai prāṇāpānau ca vaṣaṭkāras
(GBr_2,3.6b) te vaṣaṭkṛte vaṣaṭkṛte vyutkrāmanti
(GBr_2,3.6c) tān anumantrayate vāg ojaḥ saha ojo mayi prāṇāpānāv iti
(GBr_2,3.6d) vācaṃ caiva tat prāṇāpānau ca hotātmani pratiṣṭhāpayati
(GBr_2,3.6e) sarvam āyur eti
(GBr_2,3.6f) na purā jarasaḥ pramīyate ya evaṃ veda
(GBr_2,3.6g) <śaṃ no bhava hṛda ā pīta indo piteva soma sūnave suśevaḥ | sakheva sakhya uruśaṃsa dhīraḥ pra ṇa āyur jīvase soma tārīḥ [ṚV 8.48.4, VaitS 19.18]>_ity ātmānaṃ pratyabhimṛśati_
(GBr_2,3.6h) īśvaro vā eṣo 'pratyabhimṛṣṭo yajamānasyāyuḥ pratyavahartum anarhan mā bhakṣayed iti

children.text: (GBr_2,3.6i) tad yad etena pratyabhimṛśaty āyur evāsmai tat pratirate_
children.translated_text: When he touches himself with this [verse], thereby he secures life for himself.

children.text: (GBr_2,3.6j) āpyāyasva saṃ te payāṃsīti dvābhyāṃ camasān āpyāyayanty abhirūpābhyām_
children.translated_text: '<s>Āpyāyasva sam te payāṃsi</s>' (Swell up, let your streams of milk [flow together]) — with these two [verses] they make the <s>Camasas</s> (Soma cups) swell, with verses that are metrically appropriate.

children.text: (GBr_2,3.6k) yad yajñe 'bhirūpaṃ tat samṛddham || 6 ||
children.translated_text: That which is metrically appropriate in the sacrifice is [ritually] complete. [6]

body.translated_text: Speech (<s>Vāc</s>) and <s>Prāṇa-Apāna</s> (inhalation and exhalation) are indeed the <s>Vaṣaṭkāra</s>. At every uttering of the <s>Vaṣaṭkāra</s>, they depart. He [the <s>Hotṛ</s>] invokes them [back]: '<s>Vāc</s> (Speech), <s>Ojas</s> (strength), <s>Sahas</s> (might), <s>Ojas</s> (strength) — may <s>Prāṇa</s> and <s>Apāna</s> [be] in me!' Thereby the <s>Hotṛ</s> re-establishes speech and <s>Prāṇa-Apāna</s> in himself. He lives a full life. He does not die before old age — whoever knows thus. [With the verse:] '<s>Śaṃ no bhava hṛda ā pīta Indo</s>' (Be auspicious to us, O <s>Indra</s>, drunk into the heart; like a father to a son, O <s>Soma</s>, be gracious; like a friend to a friend, O widely-praised wise one, extend our life for living, O <s>Soma</s>) [ṚV 8.48.4] — with this he touches himself. For if not touched [with this mantra], [the <s>Vaṣaṭkāra</s>] is capable of carrying away the life of the <s>Yajamāna</s> (sacrificer), [as if saying:] 'Let not one unworthy consume me.'

body.text:
(GBr_2,3.7a) prāṇā vā ṛtuyājās
(GBr_2,3.7b) tad yad ṛtuyājaiś caranti prāṇān eva tad yajamāne dadhati
(GBr_2,3.7c) ṣaḍ ṛtuneti yajanti

(GBr_2,3.7f) apānam eva tad yajamāne dadhati

(GBr_2,3.7h) vyānam eva tad yajamāne dadhati

(GBr_2,3.7j) tato 'nyatra guṇitas
(GBr_2,3.7k) tathā ha yajamānaḥ sarvam āyur ety asmiṃl loka ārdhnoti_
(GBr_2,3.7l) āpnoty amṛtatvam akṣitaṃ svarge loke
(GBr_2,3.7m) te vā ete prāṇā eva yad ṛtuyājās
(GBr_2,3.7n) tasmād anavānaṃ tato yajanti [ed. anavānanto, corr. Patyal]
(GBr_2,3.7o) prāṇānāṃ santatyai
(GBr_2,3.7p) santantā iva hīme prāṇāḥ_
(GBr_2,3.7q) atho ṛtavo vā ṛtuyājāḥ

children.text: (GBr_2,3.7r) saṃsthānuvaṣaṭkāraḥ_ [ed. anuvaṣaṭkuāro]
children.translated_text: The concluding <s>Anuvaṣaṭkāra</s> (secondary offering call) [is for] completion.

children.text: (GBr_2,3.7s) yo 'trānuvaṣaṭkuryād asaṃsthitān ṛtūn saṃsthāpayet_
children.translated_text: He who utters the <s>Anuvaṣaṭkāra</s> here would bring the incomplete seasons to completion.

children.text: (GBr_2,3.7t) yas taṃ tatra brūyād asaṃsthitān ṛtūn samatiṣṭhipad duḥṣamaṃ bhaviṣyatīti śaśvat tathā syāt || 7 ||
children.translated_text: If someone were to say to him: 'He brought the incomplete seasons to completion; there will be disorder' — it would always be so. [7]

body.translated_text: The <s>Ṛtuyājas</s> (seasonal offerings) are indeed the vital breaths (<s>Prāṇas</s>). When they perform the <s>Ṛtuyājas</s>, they thereby place the vital breaths in the <s>Yajamāna</s> (sacrificer). When they offer [saying] 'to the six seasons' — thereby they place <s>Prāṇa</s> (inbreath) in the <s>Yajamāna</s>. When they offer 'with four seasons' — thereby they place <s>Apāna</s> (outbreath) in the <s>Yajamāna</s>. When twice 'to the seasons' at the end — thereby they place <s>Vyāna</s> (diffused breath) in the <s>Yajamāna</s>. That [breath], gathered together and distributed threefold, is <s>Prāṇa</s>, <s>Apāna</s>, and <s>Vyāna</s>. Beyond that, it is multiplied further. Thus the <s>Yajamāna</s> lives a full life, prospers in this world, and attains immortality and imperishability in the heavenly world. These <s>Ṛtuyājas</s> are indeed the vital breaths. Therefore they sacrifice without fasting, for the continuity of the breaths — for these breaths are indeed continuous. Moreover, the seasons are the <s>Ṛtuyājas</s>.

body.text:
(GBr_2,3.8a) tad āhur yad dhotā yakṣad dhotā yakṣad iti maitrāvaruṇo hotre preṣyaty atha kasmād ahotṛbhyaḥ sadbhyo hotrāśaṃsibhyo hotā yakṣad dhotā yakṣad iti preṣyatīti

(GBr_2,3.8c) vāg yakṣad vāg yakṣad iti_
(GBr_2,3.8d) atho sarve vā ete sapta hotāro 'pi vā ṛcābhyuditaṃ sapta hotāra ṛtuthā yajantīti_

(GBr_2,3.8k) yo vai bhakṣayet prāṇo bhakṣaḥ prāṇa ātmānam antaragād iti tathaiva bhavati

children.text: (GBr_2,3.8l) limped ivaivāvajighred atra ca dvidevatyeṣu ceti
children.translated_text: One should merely sniff [the offering], as it were, here and in the <s>Dvidevatya</s> (two-deity oblations).

children.text: (GBr_2,3.8m) tad u tatra śāsanaṃ vedayante_
children.translated_text: And they teach this instruction for that [procedure].

children.text: (GBr_2,3.8n) atha yad abhū vyabhicarato nānyonyam anuprapadyete adhvaryū tasmād ṛtur ṛtuṃ nānuprapadyate || 8 ||
children.translated_text: Now, when the two <s>Adhvaryus</s> go astray and do not follow one another, therefore season does not follow season [in proper order]. [8]

body.translated_text: They ask: 'When the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> (priest of <s>Mitra-Varuṇa</s>) commands the <s>Hotṛ</s>, saying "<s>Hotā yakṣat, hotā yakṣat</s>" (May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship, may the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship), why does he command "May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship" to those who are not [themselves the] <s>Hotṛ</s>, [but rather] the <s>Hotrāśaṃsins</s> (assistant <s>Hotṛ</s> priests)?' <s>Vāc</s> (Speech) is indeed the <s>Hotṛ</s>; <s>Vāc</s> is all the <s>Ṛtvijs</s> (priests). [It means:] 'May <s>Vāc</s> worship, may <s>Vāc</s> worship.' Moreover, all these are the seven <s>Hotṛs</s>; indeed, it has been declared by the <s>Ṛc</s> (verse): 'The seven <s>Hotṛs</s> sacrifice according to the seasons.' Now, the twelve [verses] that follow are for avoiding <s>Jāmitā</s> (injurious repetition). They are twelve. Twelve months make the year. The year is <s>Prajāpati</s>. <s>Prajāpati</s> is the sacrifice. If one who would consume [the Soma] here, and someone were to say to him: 'The drink is unpacified, without the <s>Anuvaṣaṭkāra</s>; your self has gone inward; you will not live' — so it would be. He who would consume [the Soma] — the breath is the drink; the breath [has gone] inward — it becomes exactly so.

children.text: (GBr_2,3.9aa) prajāpatir hi tam abhijighrati_
children.translated_text: For <s>Prajāpati</s> smells [revives] him.

children.text: (GBr_2,3.9bb) atho khalv āhur eko vai prajāpater vrataṃ bibharti gaur eva
children.translated_text: Moreover, they say: 'Only the cow (<s>Gau</s>) bears the vow of <s>Prajāpati</s>.'

children.text: (GBr_2,3.9cc) tad ubhaye paśava upajīvanti ye ca grāmyā ye cāraṇyā iti || 9 ||
children.translated_text: Both kinds of animals subsist on her — those that are domestic and those that are wild. [9]

body.translated_text: When <s>Prajāpati</s> created the creatures, he created them exhausted. He revived them with the <s>Hiṃkāra</s> (the syllable 'Hīṃ'). The creatures seized a horse. For the sacrifice is indeed bound when the oblations are cooked, when the <s>Soma</s> is pressed, when the animal is seized. With the <s>Hiṃkāra</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s> smells what has been killed — for the non-killing of the sacrifice, for the attainment of the sacrifice, for the virility of the sacrifice. Therefore the <s>Hiṃkāra</s> is uttered. Therefore, he who among fathers is concerned about his sons becomes the most excellent. For <s>Prajāpati</s> smells [revives] him. When a bird sits on an egg that does not hatch, she too utters the <s>Hiṃkāra</s>. Moreover, they say: 'A great <s>Ṛṣi</s> first saw that which is to be sung at the beginning of the sacrifice.' The <s>Hiṃkāra</s> is indeed that which is to be sung at the beginning of the sacrifice. The gods and <s>Ṛṣis</s> said: 'Let him be <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> (the best), he who first saw what is to be sung at the beginning of the sacrifice.' The <s>Hiṃkāra</s> is indeed that which is to be sung at the beginning of the sacrifice. Thereby he became the most excellent among the gods. He by whom one is most excellent, by that one is <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> (the best). Therefore, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> of the <s>Vāsiṣṭha</s> lineage should not be excluded from the <s>Dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee). Thus his <s>Hiṃkāra</s> is pleased. Now, when the gods and <s>Ṛṣis</s> saw the <s>Ṛc</s> and <s>Sāman</s>, they indeed saw them [together]. Where they saw them, from there they milked all the milking. These <s>Ṛc</s> and <s>Sāman</s>, being milked out and exhausted, are replenished by the <s>Hiṃkāra</s>. Through the <s>Hiṃkāra</s>, the <s>Ṛc</s> and <s>Sāman</s>, made full, yield their milking for the <s>Yajamāna</s> (sacrificer). Therefore the <s>Adhvaryus</s> press the <s>Soma</s> after uttering the <s>Hiṃkāra</s>. The <s>Udgātṛs</s> praise with <s>Sāman</s> after uttering the <s>Hiṃkāra</s>. The <s>Uktha</s> chanters perform their priestly function with <s>Ṛcs</s> after uttering the <s>Hiṃkāra</s>. The <s>Atharvans</s> perform the office of <s>Brahmā</s> after uttering the <s>Hiṃkāra</s>. Therefore the <s>Hiṃkāra</s> is uttered.

children.text: (GBr_2,3.10ee) etad vai tac chandaś chandasi pratiṣṭhāpayati
children.translated_text: This indeed is establishing meter upon meter.

children.text: (GBr_2,3.10ff) kalpayaty eva devaviśo ya evaṃ veda
children.translated_text: He arranges the divine clans (<s>Devaviśas</s>) — whoever knows thus.

children.text: (GBr_2,3.10gg) tad apy eṣābhyanūktā yad gāyatre adhi gāyatram āhitam iti || 10 ||
children.translated_text: And this [verse] has been recited in connection with it: '<s>Yad gāyatre adhi gāyatram āhitam</s>' (That which in the <s>Gāyatrī</s> is placed upon the <s>Gāyatrī</s>). [10]

body.translated_text: The divine clans (<s>Devaviśas</s>) should be arranged, they say. Meter should be established upon meter. [The <s>Hotṛ</s>] calls out '<s>Śaṃsāvom</s>' (Let us recite, <s>Oṃ</s>) at the morning pressing with three syllables. '<s>Śaṃsāvo daiva</s>' (Recite, O divine one) — the <s>Adhvaryu</s> responds with five syllables. That makes eight syllables. The <s>Gāyatrī</s> indeed has eight syllables. Thus they fashioned the <s>Gāyatrī</s> at the beginning of the morning pressing. '<s>Ukthaṃ vācī</s>' (The <s>Uktha</s> [is] in speech) — he says after reciting, with four syllables. '<s>Om ukthaśāḥ</s>' (<s>Oṃ</s>, O <s>Uktha</s>-reciter) — the <s>Adhvaryu</s> responds with four syllables. That makes eight syllables. The <s>Gāyatrī</s> indeed has eight syllables. Thus they fashioned the <s>Gāyatrī</s> on both sides of the morning pressing. '<s>Adhvaryo śaṃsāvom</s>' (O <s>Adhvaryu</s>, let us recite, <s>Oṃ</s>) — he calls out at the midday pressing with six syllables. '<s>Śaṃsāvo daiva</s>' (Recite, O divine one) — the <s>Adhvaryu</s> responds with five syllables. That makes eleven syllables. The <s>Triṣṭubh</s> indeed has eleven syllables. Thus they fashioned the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> at the beginning of the midday pressing. '<s>Ukthaṃ vācīndrāya</s>' (The <s>Uktha</s> [is] in speech, for <s>Indra</s>) — he says after reciting, with six syllables. '<s>Om ukthaśā yaja</s>' (<s>Oṃ</s>, O <s>Uktha</s>-reciter, sacrifice) — the <s>Adhvaryu</s> responds with five syllables. That makes eleven syllables. The <s>Triṣṭubh</s> indeed has eleven syllables. Thus they fashioned the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> on both sides of the midday pressing. '<s>Adhvaryo śaṃśaṃsāvom</s>' (O <s>Adhvaryu</s>, let us recite and recite, <s>Oṃ</s>) — he calls out at the third pressing with seven syllables. '<s>Śaṃsavo daiva</s>' (Recite, O divine one) — the <s>Adhvaryu</s> responds with five syllables. That makes twelve syllables. The <s>Jagatī</s> indeed has twelve syllables. Thus they fashioned the <s>Jagatī</s> at the beginning of the third pressing. '<s>Ukthaṃ vācīndrāya devebhyaḥ</s>' (The <s>Uktha</s> [is] in speech, for <s>Indra</s> and the gods) — he says after reciting, with nine syllables. '<s>Om ukthaśāḥ</s>' (<s>Oṃ</s>, O <s>Uktha</s>-reciter) — the <s>Adhvaryu</s> responds with three syllables. That makes twelve syllables. The <s>Jagatī</s> indeed has twelve syllables. Thus they fashioned the <s>Jagatī</s> on both sides of the third pressing.

children.text: (GBr_2,3.11dd) yady api chandaḥ prātaḥsavane yujyetārdharcaśa eva tasya śaṃsyaṃ gāyatryā rūpeṇa_
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,3.11dd) Even if a meter is employed at the morning pressing, its recitation should be in half-verses, in the form of <s>Gāyatrī</s>.

children.text: (GBr_2,3.11ff) na triṣṭubjagatyāv etasmin sthāne 'rdharcaśasye yat kiṃ cic chandaḥ prātaḥsavane yujyetāṃ paccha evainayoḥ śasyam iti sā sthitiḥ || 11 ||
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,3.11ff) <s>Triṣṭubh</s> and <s>Jagatī</s> [meters] in this place [should be recited] in half-verses; whatever meter is employed at the morning pressing — its recitation should follow the same [pattern]. That is the established rule. [11]

body.translated_text:
(GBr 2,3.11a) Now, these various meters are like pits in between.
(GBr 2,3.11b) Now, these two are the most mighty and powerful deities, not the intermediate ones.
(GBr 2,3.11c) By means of these two he proceeds.
(GBr 2,3.11d) That is the leaping-over-the-pit, a form of ascent, leading to heaven.
(GBr 2,3.11e) He should cross over without a cart.
(GBr 2,3.11f) The <s>Praṇava</s> (<s>Oṃ</s>) is indeed immortality.
(GBr 2,3.11g) By immortality indeed he crosses over death.
(GBr 2,3.11h) Just as one would cross a pit by means of a harrow or a bamboo pole, so he extends [the recitation] by means of the <s>Praṇava</s>.
(GBr 2,3.11i) The <s>Praṇava</s> is indeed <s>Brahman</s>.
(GBr 2,3.11j) By <s>Brahman</s> indeed he extends <s>Brahman</s> for him.
(GBr 2,3.11k) The <s>Praṇava</s> should be pure (<s>śuddha</s>) for those desiring offspring.
(GBr 2,3.11l) Ending in 'm' for those desiring a firm foundation.
(GBr 2,3.11m) 'The <s>Praṇava</s> should end in m' — thus some say.
(GBr 2,3.11n) But the established [view] is 'pure.'
(GBr 2,3.11o) The <s>Praṇava</s> has been investigated.
(GBr 2,3.11p) Now therefore, here pure, here full — thus.
(GBr 2,3.11q) The <s>Praṇava</s> should be pure.
(GBr 2,3.11r) 'In the middle of the <s>Śastra</s> (recitation) and the <s>Anuvacana</s> (repetition)' — thus <s>Kauṣītaki</s> used to say.
(GBr 2,3.11s) Thus it is in the collected [tradition].
(GBr 2,3.11t) Ending in 'm' [is used] at the conclusion.
(GBr 2,3.11u) Conclusion is indeed foundation.
(GBr 2,3.11v) For the sake of foundation indeed.
(GBr 2,3.11w) And for the attainment of both desires.
(GBr 2,3.11x) These are indeed the two currents of meters — the lower meter and the higher meter flow past.
(GBr 2,3.11y) His life is not harmed thereby.
(GBr 2,3.11z) A meter that has been carried beyond [its proper place] among the meters — upon whomever he hates, him he should mentally pierce.
(GBr 2,3.11aa) In the cutting of the meters, it either flows away or crumbles.
(GBr 2,3.11bb) Three times the first, three times the last he recites — thereby he binds the sacrificial grass of the sacrifice.
(GBr 2,3.11cc) For stability, for strength, for non-disintegration.

(GBr_2,3.12a) athāta ekāhasya prātaḥsavanam_
(GBr_2,3.12b) prajāpatiṃ ha vai yajñaṃ tanvānaṃ bahiṣpavamāna eva mṛtyur mṛtyupāśena pratyupākrāmata
(GBr_2,3.12c) sa āgneyyā gāyatryājyaṃ pratyapadyata
(GBr_2,3.12d) mṛtyur vāva taṃ paśyan prajāpatiṃ paryakrāmat
(GBr_2,3.12e) taṃ sāmājyeṣṭhasīdat
(GBr_2,3.12f) sa vāyavyā pra"ugaṃ pratyapadyata
(GBr_2,3.12g) mṛtyur vāva taṃ paśyan prajāpatiṃ paryakrāmat
(GBr_2,3.12h) taṃ mādhyaṃdine pavamāne 'sīdat
(GBr_2,3.12i) sa aindryā triṣṭubhā marutvatīyaṃ pratyapadyata
(GBr_2,3.12j) mṛtyur vāva taṃ paśyan prajāpatiṃ paryakrāmat
(GBr_2,3.12k) sa tenaiva draviṇe pūrvo niṣkevalyasya stotriyam āsīdat

children.text: (GBr_2,3.12n) mṛtyur anavakāśam apādravad aśaṃsad itaro niṣkevalyam_
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,3.12n) <s>Mṛtyu</s> ran away having found no opportunity; the other [<s>Prajāpati</s>] recited the <s>Niṣkevalya</s> [<s>Śastra</s>].

children.text: (GBr_2,3.12o) tasmād ekam evokthaṃ hotā marutvatīyena pratipadyate niṣkevalyam eva_
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,3.12o) Therefore, the <s>Hotṛ</s> (invoking priest) begins with the <s>Marutvatīya</s> and recites only one <s>Uktha</s> (praise) — the <s>Niṣkevalya</s> alone.

children.text: (GBr_2,3.12p) atra hi prajāpatiṃ mṛtyur vyajahāt || 12 ||
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,3.12p) For here <s>Mṛtyu</s> abandoned <s>Prajāpati</s>. [12]

body.translated_text:
(GBr 2,3.12a) Now therefore, the morning pressing of the one-day [<s>Soma</s> sacrifice].
(GBr 2,3.12b) When <s>Prajāpati</s> was extending the sacrifice, <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death) approached him with the noose of death at the <s>Bahiṣpavamāna</s> [<s>Stotra</s>] itself.
(GBr 2,3.12c) He warded [Death] off with the <s>Ājya</s> (ghee recitation) in the <s>Gāyatrī</s> [meter] dedicated to <s>Agni</s>.
(GBr 2,3.12d) <s>Mṛtyu</s>, seeing <s>Prajāpati</s>, went around him.
(GBr 2,3.12e) He [Death] sat down at the <s>Sāma</s>-led <s>Ājya</s>.
(GBr 2,3.12f) He [<s>Prajāpati</s>] warded [Death] off with the <s>Praüga</s> [recitation] dedicated to <s>Vāyu</s>.
(GBr 2,3.12g) <s>Mṛtyu</s>, seeing <s>Prajāpati</s>, went around him.
(GBr 2,3.12h) He sat down at the midday <s>Pavamāna</s> [<s>Stotra</s>].
(GBr 2,3.12i) He [<s>Prajāpati</s>] warded [Death] off with the <s>Marutvatīya</s> [recitation] in the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> [meter] dedicated to <s>Indra</s>.

body.translated_text:
(GBr 2,3.13a) He said to <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>: 'You two, gather for us this limb of the sacrifice — the <s>Maitrāvaruṇīya</s> [recitation].'
(GBr 2,3.13b) 'So be it,' they said.
(GBr 2,3.13c) Those two, becoming united and powerful, overcame <s>Mṛtyu</s> by force.
(GBr 2,3.13d) They indeed gathered for him this limb of the sacrifice — the <s>Maitrāvaruṇīya</s>.
(GBr 2,3.13e) Therefore the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> [priest] recites the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> hymns at the morning pressing.
(GBr 2,3.13f) For they indeed gathered this limb of the sacrifice for him.
(GBr 2,3.13g) Or rather, when he recites the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> hymns: 'At the rising of the sun we would worship you two with obeisances, O <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, and with oblations' —

(GBr 2,3.14a) He said to <s>Indra</s>: 'You gather for us this limb of the sacrifice — the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsīya</s> [recitation].'
(GBr 2,3.14b) 'With whom [as companion]?' [asked <s>Indra</s>].
(GBr 2,3.14c) 'With <s>Sūrya</s> (the Sun),' [he replied].
(GBr 2,3.14d) 'So be it,' they said.
(GBr 2,3.14e) Those two, becoming united and powerful, overcame <s>Mṛtyu</s> by force.
(GBr 2,3.14f) They indeed gathered for him this limb of the sacrifice — the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsīya</s>.
(GBr 2,3.14g) Therefore the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> [priest] recites the hymns to <s>Indra</s> and those with <s>Sūrya</s> as their limbs at the morning pressing.
(GBr 2,3.14h) For they indeed gathered this limb of the sacrifice for him.
(GBr 2,3.14i) Or rather, when he recites the hymns to <s>Indra</s> with <s>Sūrya</s> as their limbs —

body.translated_text:
(GBr 2,3.17a) They indeed kill <s>Soma</s> when they press him.
(GBr 2,3.17b) They indeed kill the sacrifice when the <s>dakṣiṇās</s> (sacrificial fees) are led away.
(GBr 2,3.17c) They indeed empower the sacrifice thereby.
(GBr 2,3.17d) That is the nature of <s>dakṣiṇās</s> as <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (i.e., empowering).
(GBr 2,3.17e) The midday pressing is indeed the heavenly world.
(GBr 2,3.17f) When the <s>dakṣiṇās</s> are led away at the midday pressing, [it is] for the attainment of the heavenly world.
(GBr 2,3.17g) Much should be given.
(GBr 2,3.17h) The sacrificer thereby constructs a bridge.
(GBr 2,3.17i) For ascending to the heavenly world, for the advancement of offspring.
(GBr 2,3.17j) He offers two [oblations] in the <s>Gārhapatya</s> [fire].

(GBr 2,3.18a) He gives first to the <s>Agnīdh</s> (fire-kindler).

(GBr 2,3.18c) By the mouth of the sacrifice he thereby accomplishes the mouth of the sacrifice.
(GBr 2,3.18d) He gives to the <s>Brahman</s> [priest].
(GBr 2,3.18e) The <s>Brahman</s> belongs to <s>Prajāpati</s>.
(GBr 2,3.18f) By that he pleases <s>Prajāpati</s> indeed.
(GBr 2,3.18g) He gives to the <s>Ṛtvijs</s> (priests).
(GBr 2,3.18h) By that he pleases the <s>Hotrā</s> (priestly office) indeed.
(GBr 2,3.18i) He gives to the <s>Sadasyas</s> (assembly priests).
(GBr 2,3.18j) By that he purchases the right to drink <s>Soma</s>.
(GBr 2,3.18k) For he who does not deserve [it] should purchase the right to drink <s>Soma</s> by that.
(GBr 2,3.18l) What he gives to one of priestly lineage (<s>Ārṣeya</s>) who has heard [the Vedas] — by that [he gains] the world of the gods.

body.translated_text:
When he gives a cow — for the cow belongs to the <s>Viśvedevas</s> (All-gods) —
he thereby attains the dear abode of all the gods.
When he gives a goat — for the goat belongs to <s>Agni</s> —
he thereby attains the dear abode of <s>Agni</s>.
When he gives a sheep, he thereby conquers what pertains to sheep.
When he gives cooked food, he thereby redeems the flesh.
When he gives a cart or a chariot, he thereby gives his body.
When he gives a garment, he thereby gives <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
When he gives gold, he thereby makes his life longer.
When he gives a horse — for the horse belongs to <s>Sūrya</s> —
he thereby attains the dear abode of <s>Sūrya</s>.
At least something should be given to the <s>Pratihartṛ</s> (respondent priest).
For the <s>Pratihartṛ</s> belongs to <s>Rudra</s>.
He thereby appeases <s>Rudra</s>.
If he were to give to the <s>Pratihartṛ</s> from the middle portion, he would follow <s>Rudra</s> from the middle.
<s>Svarbhānu</s> the <s>Asura</s> struck the sun with darkness.
<s>Atri</s> drove it away.
<s>Atri</s> perceived that.

body.translated_text:
Now, regarding the midday pressing of the one-day rite.
The <s>Ṛk</s> (verse) and the <s>Sāman</s> (chant) were here.
She was indeed named <s>Ṛk</s>.
The <s>Sāman</s> was named <s>Ama</s>.
The <s>Ṛk</s> and <s>Sāman</s> said to each other: 'Let us come together as a pair for procreation.'
'No,' said the <s>Sāman</s>,
'for my greatness is greater than this.'
Being two, they spoke to each other.
They did not agree.
Being three, they spoke.
Because being three they spoke, therefore it came together with three.

It should be recited with a medium voice.
He thereby prepares his self. He recites the <s>Anurūpa</s>.
The offspring is the <s>Anurūpa</s>.
Therefore they make the <s>Anurūpa</s> a likeness.
A likeness indeed is born in his offspring, not an unlike one.
Therefore they make the <s>Anurūpa</s> a likeness.
It should be recited in a somewhat louder voice.
He thereby makes his offspring better.
He recites the <s>Dhāyyā</s>.

body.translated_text:
Now they ask: 'To which deity does the sacrifice belong?'
One should say: 'To <s>Indra</s>.'
For when the sacrifice belongs to <s>Indra</s>, the other deities follow according to their share — at the morning pressing, in the <s>Marutvatīya</s>, and at the third pressing.
But what is above the <s>Marutvatīya</s> belongs exclusively to <s>Indra</s>.
Therefore all recite the <s>Niṣkevalya</s> (exclusive hymns).
The <s>Niṣkevalya</s> hymns are indeed the form of the heavenly world.
Moreover, the <s>Niṣkevalya</s> — in the beginning there was only one pressing, the morning pressing.
Then <s>Prajāpati</s> desired:

'<s>kas tam indra tvāvasum</s>' [ṚV 7.32.14] is the <s>Pragātha</s> in <s>Bārhatī</s> meter.
Above that is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> passage.

With '<s>uśannu ṣu ṇaḥ sumanā upāke</s>' [ṚV 4.20.4] he offers.
He thereby gives each deity its proper share.
