body.translated_text:
The <s>Stotriya</s> and <s>Anurūpa</s> of the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> are: '<s>taṃ vo dasmam ṛtīṣaham</s>' [ṚV 8.88.1] and '<s>tat tvā yāmi suvīryam</s>' [ṚV 8.3.9].
'<s>ud u tye madhumattamā giraḥ</s>' [ṚV 8.3.15] is the <s>Pragātha</s> in <s>Bārhatī</s> meter.
Cattle indeed are the <s>Pragātha</s>.
Cattle are the melody (<s>svara</s>).
For the obtainment of cattle.
The <s>Bṛhatī</s> is indeed the middle of all meters.
The midday pressing is the middle of the pressings.
He thus fulfills the middle by the middle.
'<s>indraḥ pūrbhid ātirad dāsam arkaiḥ</s>' [ṚV 3.34.1] is the opening of the <s>Uktha</s>.
'<s>ud u brahmāṇy airata śravasyā</s>' [ṚV 7.23.1] is the concluding portion (<s>paryāsa</s>).
With '<s>eved indraṃ vṛṣaṇaṃ vajrabāhum</s>' [ṚV 7.23.6a] he encloses.
'<s>vasiṣṭhāso abhy arcanty arkaiḥ</s>' [ṚV 7.26.6b] —
for the <s>arka</s> is food.
He thereby bestows upon him the eating of food.
'<s>sa na stuto vīravad dhātu gomat</s>' [ṚV 7.26.6c] —
for the <s>arka</s> is food.
He thereby wishes for him offspring and cattle.
'<s>yūyaṃ pāta svastibhiḥ sadā naḥ</s>' [ṚV 7.26.6d] — this is endowed with blessings and perfected in form.
This is the perfection of the sacrifice — that it is perfected in form, that the ritual being performed is accompanied by <s>ṛc</s> and <s>yajus</s> verses.
He who knows this, and the knower who as <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> encloses with this verse, safely reaches the far shore of the sacrifice.
With '<s>ṛjīṣī vajrī vṛṣabhas turāṣāṭ</s>' [ṚV 5.40.4] he offers.
He thereby pleases each deity according to its share.
Having made the <s>vaṣaṭ</s> call, he makes the <s>anuvaṣaṭ</s> call.

The <s>Stotriya</s> and <s>Anurūpa</s> of the <s>Acchāvāka</s> are: '<s>tarobhir vo vidadvasum</s>' [ṚV 8.66.1] and '<s>taraṇir it siṣāsati</s>' [ṚV 7.32.20].
'<s>ud in nv asya ricyate</s>' [ṚV 7.32.12] is the <s>Pragātha</s> in <s>Bārhatī</s> meter.
Its <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> explanation has been stated.
'<s>bhūya id vāvṛdhe vīryāya</s>' [ṚV 6.30.1] is the opening of the <s>Uktha</s>.
'<s>imām ū ṣu prabhṛtiṃ sātaye dhāḥ</s>' [ṚV 3.36.1] is the concluding portion.
He takes out the tenth verse.
For this is the seer-hymn of <s>Ghora Āṅgirasa</s> — lest it burn the sacrifice while being recited.
With '<s>pibā vardhasva tava ghā sutāsaḥ</s>' [ṚV 3.36.3] he offers.
He thereby pleases each deity according to its share.
Having made the <s>vaṣaṭ</s> call, he makes the <s>anuvaṣaṭ</s> call.

body.translated_text:
Now, 'O <s>Adhvaryu</s>, let us recite!' — for the <s>Stotriya</s>, the <s>Anurūpa</s>, the <s>Pragātha</s>, the opening of the <s>Uktha</s>, and the <s>Paridhānīya</s> — they invite five times.
Five-footed is the <s>Paṅkti</s> meter.
The sacrifice is of <s>Paṅkti</s> form.
All recite <s>Triṣṭubh</s> verses dedicated to <s>Indra</s>,
for the midday pressing belongs to <s>Indra</s> and to <s>Triṣṭubh</s>.
All enclose with <s>Samavatī</s> verses.
That they enclose with <s>Samavatī</s> verses — for the concluding portion (<s>paryāsa</s>) is the end, and the final result (<s>udarka</s>) is the end.
By the end he thereby encloses the end.
All offer with <s>Madvatī</s> (intoxicating) verses.
That they offer with <s>Madvatī</s> verses means they all offer with verses that have <s>Soma</s> pressed, <s>Soma</s> drunk, and fitting form.
What is fitting in form in the sacrifice is perfected.
All make the <s>anuvaṣaṭ</s> call.
The <s>anuvaṣaṭ</s> call is for the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> (the 'well-offered' oblation),
lest the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> intervene.
The midday pressing is the world of the atmosphere.

body.translated_text:
Now, regarding the <s>Aupāsana</s> (subsidiary rite): at the third pressing, they worship — thereby he pleases the ancestors (<s>Pitṛs</s>).
The <s>Āgnīdhra</s> priest offers the <s>Pātnīvata</s> (wife's portion) in a low voice.
For the <s>Pātnīvata</s> is the seed.
Seed is indeed deposited in a low voice, as it were.
He does not make the <s>anuvaṣaṭ</s> call for it, lest he 'establish' the seed once deposited.
For seed that is deposited and unsettled is indeed productive.
The <s>anuvaṣaṭ</s> call is indeed a settling.
Therefore he does not make the <s>anuvaṣaṭ</s> call.
Sitting in the lap of the <s>Neṣṭṛ</s> priest or at the end of the <s>dhiṣṇya</s> fire, he partakes.
For the <s>Neṣṭṛ</s> is the share-bearer of the wives.
The <s>Agnīdh</s> deposits the seed in the wives.
From the seed deposited, offspring are born.
For the procreation of offspring.

body.translated_text:
Now they offer the <s>Śākala</s> oblations.
Just as a snake frees itself from its old skin, or a reed from <s>muñja</s> grass, even so those who offer the <s>Śākala</s> oblations are freed from all evil.
In the <s>Droṇakalaśa</s> (wooden trough) are the parched grains.
They take them with their hands.
For the parched grains are cattle.
They scatter them at the edge of the ashes of the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire.
For the <s>Āhavanīya</s> is the womb of cattle.
He thereby places them in their own pen, without escape.
Then, turning to the left, they replenish the <s>Soma</s> stalks in water.
They seat them within the <s>Vedi</s> (altar).
For that is the abode of <s>Soma</s>.
The <s>Adhvaryu</s>, having filled the cups with water from the <s>Cātvāla</s> (pit) on the western side, placing them facing north, distributes green grass over them.
For when the waters and plants come together, then <s>Soma</s> becomes complete.
They lead them away with a verse to <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

body.translated_text:
A stench indeed carries the <s>Adhvaryu</s> and the sacrificer in the other world.
If they were to carry him to the <s>Avabhṛtha</s> (concluding bath) without anointing him with curds, it would make him like a corpse stinking.
But when they carry him to the <s>Avabhṛtha</s> having anointed him with curds, they thereby complete him entirely with his origin.
They gather prosperity.
With '<s>abhūd devaḥ savitā vandyo nunaḥ</s>' [ṚV 4.54.1] he offers.
He thereby gathers him complete, with all his joints.
With three verses —
for the sacrifice is threefold.
He makes additional oblations with <s>Drapsavatī</s> (drop-containing) verses.
He thereby gathers him complete, with all his limbs.
He makes additional oblations with <s>Saumī</s> (Soma-related) verses.
He thereby gathers him complete, with his self.
He makes additional oblations with five verses.
For the sacrifice is of <s>Paṅkti</s> (fivefold) form.
He thereby secures the sacrifice.
The person (<s>puruṣa</s>) is of fivefold form.
He thereby obtains the person.

<s>Agni</s> is indeed <s>Yama</s>; this earth is <s>Yamī</s>.
The sacrificer takes on a debt to <s>Yama</s> when he strews the <s>Vedi</s> (altar) with plants.
If he were to depart without fasting upon it, they would punish him in the other world.
With the verse '<s>apamityam apratīttam</s>' [PS 16.49.10] — 'what is to be measured out and not repaid' — he fasts upon the <s>Vedi</s>.
Having paid off the accumulated debt to <s>Yama</s> right here, becoming free from debt, he goes to the heavenly world.
The <s>Hotṛ</s> priest says: '<s>viśvalopa viśvadāvasya tvāsañ juhomi</s>' [TS 3.3.8.2].
For the non-defeat of the sacrificer.

body.translated_text:
On the arrangement of days, on the <s>Ekāṣṭakā</s> (eighth day after full moon), having baked a cake on four dishes, one should in the morning fast with it upon a thicket.
If it burns, it is equal to merit.
If it does not burn, it is equal to sin.
With this knowledge indeed the <s>Aṅgirasas</s> of old undertook the long sacrificial session (<s>Dīrghasattra</s>).
He who, knowing the witness, the listener, and the proclaimer, sacrifices — he is united with his <s>iṣṭāpūrta</s> (merit of sacrifice and pious works) in the other world.
<s>Agni</s> is indeed the witness.
<s>Vāyu</s> is the listener.
<s>Āditya</s> (the Sun) is the proclaimer.
He who, knowing these, sacrifices — he is united with his <s>iṣṭāpūrta</s> in the other world.
With '<s>ayaṃ no nabhasas patiḥ</s>' [PS 19.16.17] he speaks.
<s>Agni</s> is indeed the lord of the sky.
He thereby says to <s>Agni</s>: 'Protect us!'
With '<s>sa tvaṃ no nabhasas patiḥ</s>' [cf. TS 3.3.8.6] he speaks.
<s>Vāyu</s> is indeed the lord of the sky.
He thereby says to <s>Vāyu</s>: 'Protect us!'
With '<s>deva saṃsphāna</s>' [TS 3.3.8.6] he speaks.
<s>Āditya</s> is indeed the divine expander.
He thereby says to <s>Āditya</s>: 'Protect us!'
With '<s>ayaṃ te yoniḥ</s>' [PS 3.34.1] he should place the fire upon the fire-sticks (<s>araṇī</s>).
Now they say: if the fire placed upon the fire-sticks should perish, his fire would fail.
He would have to re-establish the fires.
'O <s>Agni</s>, with your sacrificial body, enter me, abide in me.'

body.translated_text: He who knows the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> as 'of one day' (<s>sāhna</s>) attains the fellowship and shared world of the one-day <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>—whoever knows thus. He who shines yonder—he is the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, he is the 'one-day.' They should complete it together with the day. For this is indeed called 'of one day.' They should perform it without haste. Because they perform the first two pressings without haste, therefore the eastern regions are densely inhabited. But because they perform the third pressing with haste, therefore the western regions have long wilderness stretches. Just as at the morning pressing, so at the midday pressing, so at the third pressing— thus the sacrificer does not die prematurely. Therefore they should perform it without haste. When this sun rises in the morning, it shines most gently. Therefore one should recite at the morning pressing with the gentlest voice. When it reaches its height, it shines more strongly. Therefore one should recite at the midday pressing with a stronger voice. And when it comes closest, it shines most strongly. Therefore one should recite at the third pressing with the strongest voice. Thus one should recite, if one can control one's voice. For speech is the recitation (<s>śastra</s>). But with whatever increasingly elevated voice one is able to bring it to completion, with that one should begin. That indeed becomes better recited. This sun indeed never sets and never rises. When people think it sets in the west, having reached the end of the day, it reverses itself— it places the day below and the night above. This sun indeed never sets and never rises. When people think it rises in the east, having reached the end of the night, it reverses itself— it places the night below and the day above.

body.translated_text: Now, regarding the third pressing of the one-day rite. The gods and <s>Asuras</s> contended in these worlds. The gods conquered the <s>Asuras</s>. Those defeated ones took refuge at the junction of day and night. <s>Indra</s> said: 'These <s>Asuras</s> have taken refuge at the junction of day and night. Who will rise up with me against these <s>Asuras</s>?' 'I will,' said <s>Agni</s>. 'I will,' said <s>Varuṇa</s>. 'I will,' said <s>Bṛhaspati</s>. 'I will,' said <s>Viṣṇu</s>. Rising up, they drove them out from the junction of day and night. Because they rose up and drove them from the junction of day and night, therefore it is called <s>Utthā</s> (the rising). He who knows thus indeed rises up and strikes down the hostile rival. <s>Agni</s>, having become a horse, ran forth first. Because <s>Agni</s> as a horse ran forth first, therefore they introduce the <s>Uktha</s> recitations with <s>Āgneyī</s> (Agni-related) verses. Because <s>Agni</s> as a horse ran forth first, therefore [there is] the horse-offering. Because five deities rose up, therefore five deities are recited in the <s>Uktha</s>. Speech is <s>Agni</s>. Breath is <s>Varuṇa</s>. Mind is <s>Indra</s>. Sight is <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.

children.text: (GBr_2,4.12j) ye ha vā enaṃ pañcabhiḥ prāṇaiḥ samīryotthāpayan_
children.translated_text: Those who stirred him up and raised him with the five breaths—

children.text: (GBr_2,4.12k) tā u evaitāḥ pañca devatā ukthe śasyante || 12 ||
children.translated_text: These are the five deities that are recited in the <s>Uktha</s>. || 12 ||

body.translated_text: <s>Prajāpati</s> created the other gods from these five breaths. And whatever exists in fivefold form. Having created them, he became exhausted. The gods said: 'This father, the beneficent one, has become enfeebled. Let us stir him up again and raise him.' He, having declared his being (<s>sattva</s>), stands forth. If indeed even one of a purified family sacrifices with the <s>Saṃdhyukṣa</s> (twilight sprinkling), his being indeed declares itself and he stands forth. He who is <s>Prajāpati</s> is the sacrifice.

body.text:
(GBr_2,4.13a) tad āhur yad dvayor devatayo stuvata indrāgnyor ity atha kasmād bhūyiṣṭhā devatā ukthe śasyanta iti_ [ed. bhūyiṣṭho, corr. Patyal]
(GBr_2,4.13b) anto vā āgnimārutam antar ukthāny anta āśvinam_

children.text: (GBr_2,4.13c) kanīyasīṣu devatāsu stuvate tiṣṭheti_
children.translated_text: 'He stands firm while chanting for the lesser deities.'

children.text: (GBr_2,4.13d) atha kasmād bhūyiṣṭho devatā ukthe śasyanta iti
children.translated_text: Then why are more deities recited in the <s>Uktha</s>?

children.text: (GBr_2,4.13e) dve dve ukthamukhe bhavatas tad yad dve dve || 13 ||
children.translated_text: Two by two become the openings of the <s>Uktha</s>; that is why two by two. || 13 ||

body.translated_text: They ask: 'If one chants for two deities, <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, then why are more deities recited in the <s>Uktha</s>?' The <s>Āgnimaruta</s> is within, the <s>Uktha</s> recitations are within, the <s>Āśvina</s> is within.

body.text:

children.translated_text: Two are recited together—the <s>Aindra</s> and the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> become one <s>Aindrāvaiṣṇava</s>.

body.translated_text: Now, the <s>Uktha</s> of the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> priest is <s>Aindrāvaruṇa</s> (belonging to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>), the <s>Uktha</s> of the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> is <s>Aindrābārhaspatya</s> (belonging to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Bṛhaspati</s>), and the <s>Uktha</s> of the <s>Acchāvāka</s> is <s>Aindrāvaiṣṇava</s> (belonging to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>). Two are recited together—the <s>Aindra</s> and the <s>Vāruṇa</s> become one <s>Aindrāvaruṇa</s>. Two are recited together—the <s>Aindra</s> and the <s>Bārhaspatya</s> become one <s>Aindrābārhaspatya</s>.

body.translated_text: Now, the <s>Uktha</s> of the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> is <s>Aindrāvaruṇa</s>. It is introduced by the verse '<s>indrāvaruṇā sutapāv imaṃ sutaṃ somaṃ pibataṃ madyaṃ dhṛtavratau</s>' (ŚS 7.58.1, ṚV 6.68.10). For the third pressing is intoxicating in character. '<s>ehy ū ṣu bravāṇi te</s>' (ṚV 6.16.16), '<s>āgnir agāmi bhārataḥ</s>' (ṚV 6.16.19)—these are the <s>Stotriya</s> and <s>Anurūpa</s> of the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>. '<s>carṣaṇīdhṛtaṃ maghavānam ukthyam</s>' (ṚV 3.51.1) is the opening of the <s>Uktha</s>. Above that is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> passage. '<s>astabhnād dyām asuro viśvavedāḥ</s>' (ṚV 8.42.1) is the <s>Vāruṇa</s> recitation-portion (<s>sāṃśaṃsika</s>). 'I will,' <s>Varuṇa</s> said. For the combined recitation of the two deities, for the extended recitation. '<s>indrāvaruṇā yuvam adhvarāya naḥ</s>' (ṚV 7.82.1) is the concluding portion (<s>paryāsa</s>) in the <s>Aindrāvaruṇa</s>. This is the permanent <s>Uktha</s> of the <s>Aindrāvaruṇa</s>. He thereby establishes it in its own abode, in its own foundation. These deities, having become a pair, conquered. Having conquered— and also for the procreation of the paired couple. It has one additional foot (<s>ekapādinī</s>). With the one-footed verse, the <s>Hotṛ</s> encloses. Where the <s>Hotṛ</s>'s recitations of the <s>Hotraka</s> priests are yoked, that is accomplished. Indeed, '<s>ā vāṃ rājānāv adhvare vavṛtyām</s>' (ṚV 7.84.1). Thus one should make the concluding portion an exclusive hymn, a complete hymn. A complete hymn indeed follows in the latter two. He offers with '<s>indrāvaruṇā madhumattamasya</s>' (ŚS 7.58.2, ṚV 6.68.11). He thereby gives each deity its proper share.

body.translated_text: Now, the <s>Uktha</s> of the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> is <s>Aindrābārhaspatya</s>. It is introduced by the verse '<s>indraś ca somaṃ pibataṃ bṛhaspate 'smin yajñe mandasānā vṛṣaṇvasū</s>' (ṚV 4.50.10). For the third pressing is intoxicating in character. '<s>vayam u tvām apūrvya</s>' (ṚV 8.21.1), '<s>yo na idamidaṃ purā</s>' (ṚV 8.21.9)—these are the <s>Stotriya</s> and <s>Anurūpa</s> of the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>. '<s>pra maṃhiṣṭhāya bṛhate bṛhadraye</s>' (ṚV 1.57.1) is the opening of the <s>Uktha</s>. It is <s>Aindra</s> in <s>Jagatī</s> meter. Animals belong to the <s>Jagatī</s>. For the obtainment of animals. The third pressing is indeed <s>Jāgata</s>. It has the form of the third pressing. '<s>udapruto na vayo rakṣamāṇāḥ</s>' (ṚV 10.68.1) is the <s>Bārhaspatya</s> recitation-portion. 'I will,' said <s>Bṛhaspati</s>. For the combined recitation of the two deities, for the extended recitation. '<s>acchā ma indraṃ matayaḥ svarvidaḥ</s>' (ṚV 10.43.1) is the concluding portion in the <s>Aindrābārhaspatya</s>. This is the permanent <s>Uktha</s> of the <s>Aindrābārhaspatya</s>. He thereby establishes it in its own abode, in its own foundation. These deities, having become a pair, conquered. Having conquered— and also for the procreation of the paired couple. With '<s>bṛhaspatir naḥ pari pātu paścāt</s>' (ṚV 10.42.11a) he encloses in the <s>Aindrābārhaspatya</s>. He thereby establishes the sacrifice in <s>Indra</s> and <s>Bṛhaspati</s>. '<s>utottarasmād adharād aghāyor indraḥ purastād uta madhyato naḥ sakhā sakhibhyo varivaḥ kṛṇotu</s>' (ṚV 10.42.11bcd)— he thereby invokes blessings from all directions, not seasonal. Whatever desire he desires, that desire is fulfilled for him—whoever knows thus, and whoever, knowing thus, as <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>, encloses with this. He offers with '<s>bṛhaspate yuvam indraś ca vasvaḥ</s>' (ṚV 7.97.10). He thereby gives each deity its proper share. Having uttered <s>vaṣaṭ</s>, he utters <s>anuvaṣaṭ</s>.

body.translated_text:
(GBr 2,4.17a) Now, the <s>Uktha</s> (praise) of the <s>Acchāvāka</s> [priest] belongs to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>: '<s>Indra</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>, lords of intoxication among intoxicants, come to drink this <s>Soma</s>, bringing wealth' [ṚV 6.69.3] — thus it is declared by the <s>Ṛk</s> verse.
(GBr 2,4.17b) For the third pressing is indeed associated with intoxication.
(GBr 2,4.17c) 'Come then, O <s>Indra</s>, praised one' [ṚV 8.98.7] and 'This is for you, O <s>Indra</s>, praised one' [ṚV 8.13.4] — these are the <s>Stotriya</s> and <s>Anurūpa</s> of the <s>Acchāvāka</s>.
(GBr 2,4.17d) '<s>Ṛtu</s>, the begetter, from her, the waters round about' [ṚV 2.13.1] — this is the <s>Ukthamukha</s> (opening of the praise).
(GBr 2,4.17e) Its <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [explanation] has been stated.
(GBr 2,4.17f) 'Now let no mortal withhold, seeking to give' [ṚV 7.100.1] — this is the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> (hymn to <s>Viṣṇu</s>), the shared praise.
(GBr 2,4.17g) 'I also' — thus <s>Viṣṇu</s> said.
(GBr 2,4.17h) For the shared praise of both deities, so that neither is over-praised.
(GBr 2,4.17i) 'I unite you both by deed and by offering' [ṚV 6.69.1] — this is the <s>Paryāsa</s> (concluding portion) dedicated to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
(GBr 2,4.17j) This is his permanent <s>Uktha</s> to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
(GBr 2,4.17k) He thereby establishes it in its own abode, in its own foundation.
(GBr 2,4.17l) These two deities, having become a pair, conquered.
(GBr 2,4.17m) For the sake of conquest indeed.
(GBr 2,4.17n) And for the procreation of the pair, the couple.
(GBr 2,4.17o) 'You both have conquered; you are never conquered' [ṚV 6.69.8, PS 20.16.3, ŚS 7.44.1] — with this verse to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s> he encloses [the recitation].
(GBr 2,4.17p) He thereby establishes the sacrifice in <s>Indra</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
(GBr 2,4.17q) 'O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>, drink of the sweetness of this [<s>Soma</s>]' [ṚV 6.69.7] — with this he offers.
(GBr 2,4.17r) He thereby gives each deity its proper share.
(GBr 2,4.17s) After the <s>Vaṣaṭ</s> call, he makes the <s>Anuvaṣaṭ</s> call.

children.text: (GBr_2,4.18aa) sa etaiḥ pañcabhir ukthair etāḥ pañca diśa āpnoti
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,4.18aa) By these five <s>Ukthas</s> he attains these five directions.

children.translated_text: (GBr 2,4.18bb) Whatever form and measure these worlds have — by that form, by that measure, he prospers in these worlds; he prospers in these worlds. [18]

body.translated_text:
(GBr 2,4.18a) Now, 'O <s>Adhvaryu</s>, let us recite' — for the <s>Stotriya</s>, the <s>Anurūpa</s>, the <s>Ukthamukha</s>, and the <s>Paridhānīya</s> — they invite [the priest] four times each.
(GBr 2,4.18b) Four indeed are the directions.
(GBr 2,4.18c) Thereby they become established in the directions.
(GBr 2,4.18d) And cattle are four-footed.
(GBr 2,4.18e) For the obtainment of cattle.
(GBr 2,4.18f) And the <s>Hotraka</s> [recitations] at the third pressing have four parts.
(GBr 2,4.18g) Therefore four [times].
(GBr 2,4.18h) All recite <s>Traiṣṭubha</s> and <s>Jāgata</s> [hymns].
(GBr 2,4.18i) For the third pressing has the <s>Jāgata</s> form.
(GBr 2,4.18j) And yet these are in <s>Triṣṭubh</s>.
(GBr 2,4.18k) For at the morning pressing's <s>Marutvatīya</s> and at the third pressing, the recitation of the <s>Hotraka</s> priests is as if unestablished.
(GBr 2,4.18l) The third pressing is indeed a pressing that has lost its essential quality.
(GBr 2,4.18m) And that <s>Triṣṭubh</s> meter, being unwearied and radiant, is one that has not lost its essential quality.
(GBr 2,4.18n) Thereby the pressing gains its essential quality.
(GBr 2,4.18o) They all enclose with <s>Samavatī</s> [verses].
(GBr 2,4.18p) When they enclose with <s>Samavatī</s> verses — the <s>Paryāsa</s> is the end, the conclusion is the end, and one's wife is the end — indeed, for the purpose of encompassing.
(GBr 2,4.18q) By the end he encloses the end.
(GBr 2,4.18r) All offer with <s>Madvatī</s> (intoxication) [verses].
(GBr 2,4.18s) When they offer with <s>Madvatī</s> verses, they all offer with verses that speak of pressing, of drinking, and that are fitting.
(GBr 2,4.18t) Whatever is fitting in the sacrifice is successful.
(GBr 2,4.18u) All make the <s>Anuvaṣaṭ</s> call.
(GBr 2,4.18v) The <s>Anuvaṣaṭ</s> call follows the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> offering.
(GBr 2,4.18w) 'Lest the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> intervene.'
(GBr 2,4.18x) That yonder world is the third pressing.
(GBr 2,4.18y) Its five directions —

(GBr_2,4.19a) tad āhuḥ kiṃ ṣoḍaśinaḥ ṣoḍaśitvam_
(GBr_2,4.19b) ṣoḍaśa stotrāṇi ṣoḍaśa śastrāṇi ṣoḍaśabhir akṣarair ādatte

body.translated_text:
(GBr 2,4.19a) They ask: 'What is the sixteenfold nature of the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> (sixteenth <s>Stotra</s>)?'
(GBr 2,4.19b) Sixteen <s>Stotras</s> (chants), sixteen <s>Śastras</s> (recitations), and with sixteen syllables he takes [the <s>Graha</s>].
(GBr 2,4.19c) Two syllables indeed are in excess when the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> is completed in <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> [meter].
(GBr 2,4.19d) These two are the breasts of speech.
(GBr 2,4.19e) They are truth and untruth.
(GBr 2,4.19f) Truth protects him; untruth does not harm him — whoever knows thus, whoever knows thus. [19]

body.text: (GBr_2,4.19col) ity atharvavede gopathabrāhmaṇottarabhāge caturthaḥ prapāṭhakaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus in the <s>Atharvaveda</s>, in the <s>Gopatha Brāhmaṇa</s>, the fourth section (<s>prapāṭhaka</s>) of the latter part (<s>uttarabhāga</s>) [ends].

children.text: (GBr_2,5.1t) śarvarāṇi khalu ha vā asyaitāni chandāṃsīti ha smāha_
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,5.1t) 'These are indeed his night-meters, the <s>Śarvara</s> [meters]' — thus one used to say.

children.text: (GBr_2,5.1u) etāni ha vā indraṃ rātryās tamaso mṛtyor abhipatyāvārayan_
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,5.1u) These [meters] indeed, having rescued <s>Indra</s> from the night's darkness and death, protected him.

children.text: (GBr_2,5.1v) tad apiśarvarāṇām apiśarvaratvam || 1 ||
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,5.1v) That is the nature of the <s>Apiśarvaras</s> as <s>Apiśarvara</s>. [1]

body.translated_text:
(GBr 2,5.1a) <s>Oṃ</s> — The gods indeed took refuge in the day; the <s>Asuras</s> in the night.
(GBr 2,5.1b) They were of equal strength.
(GBr 2,5.1c) They did not overcome [each other].
(GBr 2,5.1d) <s>Indra</s> said: 'Who [will go] with me? Let us pursue these <s>Asuras</s> into the night.'
(GBr 2,5.1e) Among the gods he did not find [a companion].
(GBr 2,5.1f) They were afraid of the night, of darkness, of death.
(GBr 2,5.1g) For night is like darkness.
(GBr 2,5.1h) Death is indeed darkness.
(GBr 2,5.1i) Therefore, even today, one who walks at night is more afraid than one who walks even a short distance [in the day].
(GBr 2,5.1j) The meters indeed accompanied him.
(GBr 2,5.1k) Because the meters accompanied him, therefore <s>Indra</s> and the meters carry the night.
(GBr 2,5.1l) No <s>Nivid</s> (invocatory formula) is recited, no <s>Puroruc</s> (introductory praise), no <s>Dhāyyā</s> (meditation verse), no other deity —
(GBr 2,5.1m) For <s>Indra</s> and the meters alone carry the night.
(GBr 2,5.1n) With <s>Paryāyas</s> (rotating stanzas) they drove them round by round.
(GBr 2,5.1o) Because they drove them round by round with <s>Paryāyas</s>, therefore [they are called] <s>Paryāyas</s>.
(GBr 2,5.1p) That is the nature of <s>Paryāyas</s> as <s>Paryāya</s>.
(GBr 2,5.1q) With the first <s>Paryāyas</s> they drove them from the first part of the night; with the middle ones from the middle of the night; with the last ones from the latter part of the night.
(GBr 2,5.1r) 'We have become the [night's] companions throughout the dark night' — they said.
(GBr 2,5.1s) Because they said 'We have become the companions throughout the dark night' — that is the nature of the <s>Apiśarvaras</s> as <s>Apiśarvara</s>.

children.translated_text: (GBr 2,5.2f) Whatever garments, gold, jewels, and personal possessions they had — those they recovered by that.

children.translated_text: (GBr 2,5.2g) He takes away the wealth of one who hates him; he expels him from all these worlds — whoever knows thus. [2]

body.translated_text:
(GBr 2,5.2a) When they chant the first <s>Paryāyas</s>, they recover the first portions.
(GBr 2,5.2b) Whatever mind-wishes they had — those they recovered by that.
(GBr 2,5.2c) When they chant the middle <s>Paryāyas</s>, they recover the middle portions.
(GBr 2,5.2d) Whatever horses and cattle they had — those they recovered by that.

children.text: (GBr_2,5.3ee) tad āhur atha kasmād uttamāt pratīhārād āhūya sāmnā śastram upasaṃtanvantīti || 3 ||
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,5.3ee) They ask: 'Why do they extend the recitation with the <s>Sāman</s>, having called [the response] from the last <s>Pratihāra</s> (response)?'  [3]

body.translated_text:
(GBr 2,5.3a) 'The day has the <s>Pavamāna</s> [<s>Stotra</s>],' they say, 'but the night does not have the <s>Pavamāna</s>.'
(GBr 2,5.3b) 'How do both have the <s>Pavamāna</s>?'
(GBr 2,5.3c) 'By what do the two become equal sharers?'
(GBr 2,5.3d) When they chant and recite: 'For <s>Indra</s>, for the intoxicating drink, this pressed [<s>Soma</s>], O <s>Vasu</s>, this pressed one, this blind one, by strength pressed' — by that the night has the <s>Pavamāna</s>.
(GBr 2,5.3e) By that both have the <s>Pavamāna</s>.
(GBr 2,5.3f) By that the two become equal sharers.
(GBr 2,5.3g) 'The day has fifteen <s>Stotras</s> (chants),' they say, 'but the night does not have fifteen <s>Stotras</s>.'
(GBr 2,5.3h) 'How do both have fifteen <s>Stotras</s>?'
(GBr 2,5.3i) 'By what do the two become equal sharers?'
(GBr 2,5.3j) Twelve are the <s>Apiśarvara</s> <s>Stotras</s>.
(GBr 2,5.3k) With three deities, at the junction [of day and night], they chant to the <s>Rathantara</s> [<s>Sāman</s>] for the <s>Āśvina</s> [rite].
(GBr 2,5.3l) By that the night has fifteen <s>Stotras</s>.
(GBr 2,5.3m) By that both have fifteen <s>Stotras</s>.
(GBr 2,5.3n) By that the two become equal sharers.
(GBr 2,5.3o) They chant with a measured [number]; they recite with an unmeasured [number].
(GBr 2,5.3p) What is measured is the past; what is unmeasured is the future.
(GBr 2,5.3q) He would obtain the unmeasured — therefore he over-recites the <s>Stoma</s> (praise).
(GBr 2,5.3r) The offspring surpass his self; the cattle [surpass] him.
(GBr 2,5.3s) That by which they surpass his self — that they replenish by this.
(GBr 2,5.3t) Now, all this is twofold: moisture and splendor.
(GBr 2,5.3u) And that is obtained by day and night.
(GBr 2,5.3v) For the obtainment of moisture and splendor.
(GBr 2,5.3w) They recite <s>Gāyatra</s> <s>Stotriyas</s> and <s>Anurūpas</s>.
(GBr 2,5.3x) The <s>Gāyatrī</s> is indeed splendor.
(GBr 2,5.3y) Night is darkness and evil.
(GBr 2,5.3z) By that splendor they cross over the darkness and evil.
(GBr 2,5.3aa) They recite the repetitions (<s>Punarādāya</s>).
(GBr 2,5.3bb) For thus the <s>Sāma</s>-singers chant.

children.text: (GBr_2,5.4ii) net prāṇebhya ātmānam antaragād iti || 4 ||
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,5.4ii) Lest he exclude his self from the vital breaths. [4]

body.translated_text:
(GBr 2,5.4a) The <s>Puruṣa</s> (Person) is indeed the sacrifice.
(GBr 2,5.4b) His head is the <s>Havirdhāna</s> (oblation-cart shed).
(GBr 2,5.4c) His mouth is the <s>Āhavanīya</s> [fire].
(GBr 2,5.4d) His belly is the <s>Sadas</s> (assembly hall).
(GBr 2,5.4e) Food is the <s>Ukthas</s> (praises).
(GBr 2,5.4f) His arms are the <s>Mārjālīya</s> and the <s>Āgnīdhrīya</s> [fire-halls].
(GBr 2,5.4g) The deities here — they are the <s>Dhiṣṇya</s> (subsidiary) fires within the <s>Sadas</s>.
(GBr 2,5.4h) His feet are the <s>Gārhapatya</s> and the <s>Vrataśrapaṇa</s> (cooking fire for the vow) — and then further:
(GBr 2,5.4i) His mind is the <s>Brahman</s> [priest].
(GBr 2,5.4j) His <s>prāṇa</s> (in-breath) is the <s>Udgātṛ</s> (chanter).
(GBr 2,5.4k) His <s>apāna</s> (out-breath) is the <s>Prastotṛ</s> (leader of the chant).
(GBr 2,5.4l) His <s>vyāna</s> (diffused breath) is the <s>Pratihartṛ</s> (respondent).
(GBr 2,5.4m) His speech is the <s>Hotṛ</s> (invoker).
(GBr 2,5.4n) His eye is the <s>Adhvaryu</s> [priest].
(GBr 2,5.4o) His offspring is the <s>Sadasya</s> (assembly priest).
(GBr 2,5.4p) His limbs are the <s>Hotrāśaṃsins</s> (assistant invokers).
(GBr 2,5.4q) His self (<s>ātman</s>) is the sacrificer.
(GBr 2,5.4r) When the <s>Adhvaryu</s> initiates the <s>Stotra</s> [saying] '<s>Soma</s> is being purified,' he thereby joins the eye with the vital breaths.
(GBr 2,5.4s) When the <s>Prastotṛ</s> addresses the <s>Brahman</s> [priest]: 'O <s>Brahman</s>, we shall chant; O <s>Praśāstṛ</s>' — the mind becomes the leader.
(GBr 2,5.4t) 'With the mind as our guide, may we chant with the <s>Stoma</s>' — of these vital breaths.
(GBr 2,5.4u) He thereby joins the vital breaths with the mind.
(GBr 2,5.4v) When the <s>Brahman</s> [priest] approves aloud [saying] 'It has been chanted!' — the mind is indeed the <s>Brahman</s>.
(GBr 2,5.4w) He thereby joins the mind with the vital breaths.
(GBr 2,5.4x) When the <s>Prastotṛ</s> begins the chant, he thereby joins the <s>apāna</s> with the vital breaths.
(GBr 2,5.4y) When the <s>Pratihartṛ</s> responds, he thereby joins the <s>vyāna</s> with the <s>apāna</s>.
(GBr 2,5.4z) When the <s>Udgātṛ</s> chants the <s>Udgītha</s>, he thereby joins the <s>samāna</s> (equalizing breath) with the vital breaths.
(GBr 2,5.4aa) When the <s>Hotṛ</s> extends the recitation with the <s>Sāman</s>, speech is indeed the <s>Hotṛ</s>; he thereby joins speech with the vital breaths.
(GBr 2,5.4bb) When the <s>Sadasya</s> approaches the <s>Brahman</s> — offspring is indeed the <s>Sadasya</s>; he thereby attains offspring.
(GBr 2,5.4cc) When the <s>Hotrāśaṃsins</s> create the <s>Sāma</s>-connection — the limbs are indeed the <s>Hotrāśaṃsins</s>; he thereby joins his limbs with the vital breaths.
(GBr 2,5.4dd) When the sacrificer attends the <s>Stotra</s> — the self is indeed the sacrificer; he thereby prepares his self.
(GBr 2,5.4ee) Therefore, one should not make him hear [the call] outside the sacrificial enclosure.
(GBr 2,5.4ff) [The sun] should not rise [upon him during the rite].

children.text: (GBr_2,5.5z) ārebhantaḥ śayīran_
children.translated_text: They should lie down holding onto [the fires].

children.text: (GBr_2,5.5aa) tān ha taḥ śreṣṭho vā iti pāpmā nābhivṛkṇoti
children.translated_text: Then the evil one (<s>Pāpman</s>) does not cut down the best [among them].

children.text: (GBr_2,5.5bb) te tamaḥ pāpmānam apāghnate te tamaḥ pāpmānamapāghnate || 5 ||
children.translated_text: They drove away the darkness and evil; they drove away the darkness and evil. [5]

body.translated_text: In the first <s>Paryāyas</s> (rounds of praise) they praise, in the first <s>Padas</s> (metrical feet) they thunder — thereby they drive out the <s>Asuras</s> from the first [part of the] night. In the middle <s>Paryāyas</s> they praise, in the middle <s>Padas</s> they thunder — thereby they drive out the <s>Asuras</s> from the middle [part of the] night. In the last <s>Paryāyas</s> they praise, in the last <s>Padas</s> they thunder — thereby they drive out the <s>Asuras</s> from the last [part of the] night. Just as one repeatedly sweeps evil out toward the door, so with the <s>Stotriya</s> and <s>Anurūpa</s> (hymn-text and its counterpart), they drive out the <s>Asuras</s> through day and night. They recite <s>Gāyatrī</s> [verses] — for the <s>Gāyatrī</s> is spiritual splendor (<s>Tejas</s>) and <s>Brahmavarcas</s> (Brahmanical radiance). Thereby they place splendor and <s>Brahmavarcas</s> in the <s>Yajamāna</s> (sacrificer). After reciting <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses, they recite <s>Jagatī</s> verses. The <s>Jagatī</s> is indeed <s>Brahman</s> (sacred knowledge). Through <s>Brahman</s> they place <s>Brahmavarcas</s> in the <s>Yajamāna</s>. They call out between the <s>Gāyatrī</s> and <s>Jagatī</s> [verses]. Thereby they make the meters of diverse powers. After reciting <s>Jagatī</s> verses, they recite <s>Triṣṭubh</s> verses. The <s>Jagatī</s> is indeed cattle. With the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> they surround the cattle [with protection]. The <s>Triṣṭubh</s> is indeed strength and vigor. Thereby he establishes strength in vigor at the end. The <s>Triṣṭubh</s> <s>Yājyā</s> (offering) verses should be complete — with Soma-plant, with sweetness, with pressed juice, with drinking — well-formed and auspicious. This is indeed the form of the night [ritual]. One should stay awake through the night. For as long as they are neither praising nor reciting, the <s>Asuras</s> and <s>Rakṣases</s> (demons) are able to lead the sacrifice astray. Therefore they should announce: 'Kindle the <s>Āhavanīya</s>, the <s>Āgnīdhrīya</s>, the <s>Gārhapatya</s>, and the <s>Dhiṣṇya</s> fires — make them blaze!'

children.text: (GBr_2,5.6l) tayendram abhyaṣiñcan_
children.translated_text: With that they anointed <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: (GBr_2,5.6m) tato vai sa devānāṃ śreṣṭho 'bhavat_
children.translated_text: Thereby he became the most excellent among the gods.

children.text: (GBr_2,5.6n) śreṣṭhaḥ svānāṃ cānyeṣāṃ ca bhavati ya evaṃ veda yaś caivaṃvidvānt sautrāmaṇyābhiṣicyate || 6 ||
children.translated_text: He becomes the most excellent among his own and others — whoever knows thus and whoever, knowing thus, is consecrated with the <s>Sautrāmaṇī</s>. [6]

body.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> indeed slew <s>Viśvarūpa</s>, the son of <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>. <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, his son having been slain, brought out the <s>Soma</s> away from <s>Indra</s>, with intent to curse him. <s>Indra</s>, having made a sacrifice-entry, forcibly drank the <s>Soma</s>. He burst forth in all directions [became ill]. Therefore <s>Soma</s> should not be drunk by one who has not been invited. His <s>Soma</s>-drinking becomes destructive. From his mouth, from his vital breaths, glory (<s>Śrī</s>) and fame departed upward. They entered the cattle. Therefore cattle possess fame. He who knows thus attains fame. Then the <s>Aśvins</s> and <s>Sarasvatī</s> prepared this sacrifice for him — the <s>Sautrāmaṇī</s> — as a remedy.

children.text: (GBr_2,5.7z) etad vā etasya sāmna uktham eṣā pratiṣṭhā
children.translated_text: This is indeed the <s>Uktha</s> (laudatory recitation) of this <s>Sāman</s>; this is its foundation.

children.text: (GBr_2,5.7aa) trayastriṃśaṃ grahaṃ gṛhṇāti
children.translated_text: He draws the thirty-third <s>Graha</s> (Soma cup),

children.text: (GBr_2,5.7bb) sāmnaḥ pratiṣṭhāyai pratiṣṭhāyai || 7 ||
children.translated_text: for the firm foundation of the <s>Sāman</s>, for a firm foundation. [7]

body.translated_text: Then the <s>Brahmā</s> (priest) sings the <s>Sāman</s> (chant). <s>Kṣatra</s> (ruling power) is indeed the <s>Sāman</s>. With <s>Kṣatra</s> he thereby consecrates him. Moreover, the <s>Sāman</s> is indeed sovereign rule (<s>Sāmrājya</s>). With <s>Sāmrājya</s> he leads him to <s>Sāmrājya</s>. Moreover, the <s>Sāman</s> is the essence of all the <s>Vedas</s>. With the essence of all the <s>Vedas</s> he consecrates him. He sings in the <s>Bṛhatī</s> [meter]. In the <s>Bṛhatī</s>, that <s>Āditya</s> (Sun) shines, established in glory and in a firm foundation. He sings in the <s>Aindrī Bṛhatī</s> (the <s>Bṛhatī</s> belonging to <s>Indra</s>). This sacrificial rite, the <s>Sautrāmaṇī</s>, belongs to <s>Indra</s>. He who now sacrifices is in the abode of <s>Indra</s>. He pleases him in his own abode. Now why are they called <s>Saṃśāna</s> (sharpening [<s>Sāmans</s>])? With these <s>Sāmans</s> the gods sharpened <s>Indra</s> with <s>Indriya</s> (vital power) and <s>Vīrya</s> (heroic strength). Likewise the <s>Yajamānas</s> (sacrificers) sharpen [themselves] with these very <s>Sāmans</s>, with vital power and heroic strength. The <s>Sāmans</s> are [named] <s>Saṃśravase</s> (for hearing together), <s>Viśravase</s> (for hearing widely), <s>Satyaśravase</s> (for hearing truth), and <s>Śravase</s> (for fame). He establishes him in these very worlds. [The <s>Sāman</s>] has four endings (<s>Nidhanas</s>). Four are the directions. In the directions they are established. Moreover, cattle are four-footed — for the attainment of cattle. They ask: 'When this <s>Sāman</s> is sung, where is its <s>Uktha</s> (laudatory recitation)? What is its foundation?' 'Three [groups of] eleven gods,' they say.

children.text: (GBr_2,5.8ff) svargam eva tal lokaṃ rohati
children.translated_text: He thereby ascends to the heavenly world.

children.text: (GBr_2,5.8gg) viṣṇoḥ śipiviṣṭavatīṣu bṛhad uttamaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: In the [verses] relating to <s>Viṣṇu Śipiviṣṭa</s> (Viṣṇu the ray-covered), the <s>Bṛhat</s> [<s>Sāman</s>] is the highest.

children.text: (GBr_2,5.8hh) svargam eva tal lokaṃ rūḍhvā bradhnasya viṣṭapam atikrāmaty atikrāmati || 8 ||
children.translated_text: Having ascended to the heavenly world, he crosses over to the seat (<s>Viṣṭapa</s>) of <s>Bradhna</s> (the Sun); he crosses beyond. [8]

body.translated_text: <s>Prajāpati</s> desired: 'May I obtain <s>Vāja</s> (nourishment/prize) and the heavenly world.' He saw this <s>Vājapeya</s> (drink of nourishment). The <s>Vājapeya</s> is indeed that [Sun] which shines there. Through the <s>Vājapeya</s>, the <s>Yajamāna</s> (sacrificer) attains <s>Vāja</s> (nourishment) and the heavenly world. At the morning pressing, [verses] containing [the word] '<s>Śukra</s>' (bright) and '<s>Jyotis</s>' (light) are used — through them he attains spiritual splendor (<s>Tejas</s>) and <s>Brahmavarcas</s> (Brahmanical radiance). At the midday pressing, [verses] containing '<s>Vāja</s>' (nourishment) [are used] — for the attainment of the heavenly world. At the third pressing, [verses] containing '<s>Anna</s>' (food), '<s>Gaṇa</s>' (multitude), and '<s>Paśu</s>' (cattle) are used — through them he attains abundance. Everything is seventeen-fold. <s>Prajāpati</s> is indeed seventeen-fold. He attains <s>Prajāpati</s>. The <s>Ṛtvijs</s> (priests) wear golden garlands. Thereby the form of greatness is fashioned: 'May this be my radiance in yonder world.' For gold is light. With light he envelops him. They run a chariot race. They make the <s>Yajamāna</s> (sacrificer) rise up [calling out]: 'He ascends to the firmament (<s>Nāka</s>), he ascends to equal greatness, he ascends to universal greatness, he ascends to all-encompassing greatness!' They thereby remove him from the world of men. 'At the impulse of the divine <s>Savitṛ</s>, may I ascend to the heavenly world, to the highest firmament!' — the <s>Brahmā</s> (priest) climbs the chariot wheel. Impelled by <s>Savitṛ</s>, he thus climbs. Moreover, the <s>Brahmā</s> is <s>Prajāpati</s>. He impels him from above [like] a thunderbolt toward <s>Prajāpati</s> — for the conquest of the firmament (<s>Nāka</s>), for the continuity of prizes (<s>Vājins</s>). He sings the <s>Vāji-Sāman</s> (chant of the prize-winner). He becomes possessed of <s>Vāja</s> (nourishment). <s>Vāja</s> is indeed the heavenly world.

children.translated_text: Now, just as in another sacrifice the <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> follows the <s>Viśvajit</s> (all-conquering) pattern — how is it so here?

children.translated_text: This [<s>Aptoryāma</s>] is the father of sacrifices.

children.text: (GBr_2,5.9y) tad yathā śreṣṭhini saṃvaśreyur api vidviṣāṇā evam evaitac chreṣṭhino vaśeyānnam annasyānucaryāya kṣamante || 9 ||
children.translated_text: Just as [people] would submit to the most excellent, even those who are hostile — likewise they submit to the most excellent; foods tolerate the pursuit of food. [9]

body.translated_text: Now concerning the <s>Aptoryāma</s> (attainment of all). When <s>Prajāpati</s> created the creatures, he created them exhausted. Once created, they went away. They did not return. He seized them with one <s>Stoma</s> (praise-form). They exceeded [it]. [He seized them] with two. [He seized them] with all. Therefore [it is called] <s>Sarvastoma</s> (all-<s>Stomas</s>). He seized them with one <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> (back-chant). They exceeded [it]. [He seized them] with two. [He seized them] with all. Therefore [it is called] <s>Sarvapṛṣṭha</s> (all-<s>Pṛṣṭhas</s>). The surplus <s>Uktha</s> (laudatory recitation) they restrained with the <s>Vāravantīya</s> [<s>Sāman</s>]. Therefore it has the surplus <s>Uktha</s>. Therefore [it includes] the <s>Vāravantīya</s>. Because he, having attained [them], restrained them — therefore [it is called] <s>Aptoryāma</s> (attainment and restraint). Moreover, they say: '<s>Aptu</s>' means creatures. [It means] 'the controlling (<s>Yamana</s>) of creatures' — thus it has been said. The creatures on the <s>Barhis</s> (sacred grass) would consume [offerings]. Then he sacrifices with this [rite]. It has eight <s>Pṛṣṭhas</s> (back-chants).

children.translated_text: The <s>Yājyā</s> (offering) verses are in the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> meter.

children.text: (GBr_2,5.10v) yatra hatas tat prajā aśanāyantīḥ pipāsantīḥ saṃruddhā sthitā babhūvus tā haivainā etābhir yathaukasaṃ vyavasāyayāṃ cakāra
children.translated_text: There, the creatures, hungry and thirsty, obstructed and standing still, having been slain — with these very [verses] he settled them each in their own home.

children.text: (GBr_2,5.10w) tasmād etā yājyā bhavanti tasmād etā yājyā bhavanti || 10 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore these are the <s>Yājyā</s> (offering) verses; therefore these are the <s>Yājyā</s> verses. [10]

body.translated_text: Just as in the other day [of the sacrifice] the first of the <s>Uktha</s> recitations belongs to <s>Agni</s>, so also here the first belongs to <s>Agni</s>. The two that follow belong to <s>Indra</s>. These [all] belong to <s>Indra</s>. The <s>Uktha</s> of the <s>Acchāvāka</s> (priest) belongs to <s>Indra-Viṣṇu</s>. The surplus <s>Ukthas</s> are of four offerings each. <s>Ukthas</s> are indeed cattle. Cattle are indeed four-fold. Moreover, cattle are four-footed — for the attainment of cattle. These <s>Stotriya-Anurūpa</s> (hymn-text and counterpart) [verses] are <s>Tṛcas</s> (verse-triplets) to be recited by half-verses. The half-verse is indeed a firm foundation — for the sake of establishment. Then, of these same <s>Āśvina</s> (relating to the <s>Aśvins</s>) hymns, he recites two [hymns] together as one offering, one each day. The <s>Aśvins</s> are indeed the physicians of the gods. Therefore he recites the <s>Āśvina</s> hymns. They gave [the sacrificer] to the <s>Aśvins</s> [saying]: 'Heal him.' The concluding verses (<s>Paridhānīyās</s>) belong to <s>Kṣetrapati</s> (lord of the field). There, the creatures, hungry and thirsty, obstructed and standing still, having been slain — with these [verses] he made them drink and satiated them, each in their own field. Moreover, this earth is indeed the field — [thinking]: 'On this [earth], made free from distress, we shall finally be established.'

body.translated_text: Now concerning the multi-day [sacrifice] (<s>Anekāhika</s>). They make the <s>Stotriya</s> (hymn-text) of tomorrow the <s>Anurūpa</s> (counterpart) of today's <s>Stotriya</s> at the morning pressing. They thereby extend the <s>Ahīna</s> (multi-day sacrifice). For the continuity of the <s>Ahīna</s>. Just as a one-day [sacrifice] has its <s>Soma</s> pressed, so the <s>Ahīna</s> has its <s>Soma</s> pressed. Just as the <s>Savanas</s> (pressings) of a one-day sacrifice come to completion successively, so the days of the <s>Ahīna</s> come to completion successively. When they make the <s>Stotriya</s> of tomorrow the <s>Anurūpa</s> of today's <s>Stotriya</s> at the morning pressing — they make the day the <s>Anurūpa</s> of the day. With the following day they lay hold of the next day. But not so at the midday pressing. The <s>Pṛṣṭhas</s> (back-chants) are indeed glory (<s>Śrī</s>).

body.translated_text: Now, regarding the introductory (<s>ārabhaṇīya</s>) verses. '<s>ṛjunītī no varuṇa</s>'—for the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>: '<s>mitro nayatu vidvān</s>' (ṚV 1.90.1). The <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> is indeed the leader of the <s>Hotraka</s> recitations. Therefore this verse contains a leader (<s>praṇetṛ</s>). '<s>indraṃ vo viśvatas pari</s>' (ṚV 1.7.10a)—for the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>. '<s>havāmahe janebhyaḥ</s>' (ṚV 1.7.10b)—with this they call forth <s>Indra</s> day after day. No one else seizes <s>Indra</s> from them at the calling, when one who knows thus recites this day after day as the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>. '<s>yat soma ā sute naraḥ</s>' (ṚV 7.94.10a)—for the <s>Acchāvāka</s>. '<s>indrāgnī ajohavuḥ</s>' (ṚV 7.94.10b)—with this they call forth <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> day after day.

body.translated_text: Now, regarding the concluding (<s>paridhānīya</s>) verses. '<s>te syāma deva varuṇa</s>' (ṚV 7.66.9a)—for the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>. '<s>iṣaṃ svaś ca dhīmahi</s>' (ṚV 7.66.9b)—'<s>iṣam</s>' (nourishment) refers to this world, '<s>svar</s>' (heaven) refers to that world. He thereby takes hold of both these worlds. '<s>vy antarikṣam atirat</s>' (ṚV 8.14.7a)—for the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>. It is an opening triplet (<s>vivat tṛca</s>). With these he opens up the heavenly world. '<s>made somasya rocanendro yad abhinad valam</s>' (ṚV 8.14.7bc). Those who are consecrated are indeed seekers of gain. Therefore this verse contains <s>Vala</s>. '<s>ud gā ājad aṅgirobhya āviṣ kṛṇvan guhā satīḥ | arvāñcaṃ nunude valam</s>' (ṚV 8.14.8). With this he secures gain for them. '<s>indreṇa rocanā divo dṛḍhāni dṛṃhitāni ca | sthirāṇi na parāṇude</s>' (ṚV 8.14.9). With this he secures the heavenly world day after day. '<s>āhaṃ sarasvatīvatoḥ</s>' (ṚV 8.38.10a)—for the <s>Acchāvāka</s>.

children.text: (GBr_2,5.14y) atha samānya eva hotrakāṇāṃ paridhānīyā bhavanti || 14 ||
children.translated_text: And the <s>Paridhānīya</s> verses of the <s>Hotraka</s> priests are the same. || 14 ||

body.translated_text: The <s>Paridhānīya</s> verses of the <s>Hotraka</s> priests are of both kinds—those for the multi-day (<s>ahīna</s>) conclusion and those of the one-day (<s>ekāhina</s>) rite. The <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> encloses with one-day verses. Thereby he does not fall from this world. The <s>Acchāvāka</s> with multi-day verses. For the attainment of the heavenly world. The <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> with both kinds. Thus he, grasping both, goes to this world and that world; and also to the multi-day and the one-day; and also to the year-long rite and the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>; and also to the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> and the <s>Acchāvāka</s>. Thus he, grasping both, goes. Now, at the third pressing, the <s>Hotraka</s> priests enclose with one-day verses. Thereby he does not fall from this world. The <s>Acchāvāka</s> with multi-day verses. For the completion of the heavenly world. The <s>Hotṛ</s> may freely recite what the <s>Hotraka</s> priests would recite on the previous day. For what the <s>Hotṛ</s> is, that are the <s>Hotraka</s> priests. The breath (<s>prāṇa</s>) is indeed the <s>Hotṛ</s>, the limbs are the <s>Hotraka</s> priests. This common breath pervades the limbs. Therefore the <s>Hotṛ</s> may freely recite what the <s>Hotraka</s> priests would recite on the previous day. For what the <s>Hotṛ</s> is, that are the <s>Hotraka</s> priests. The self (<s>ātman</s>) is indeed the <s>Hotṛ</s>, the limbs are the <s>Hotraka</s> priests. The ends of the limbs are indeed the same. Therefore the <s>Hotṛ</s> may freely recite what the <s>Hotraka</s> priests would recite on the previous day.

body.translated_text: The <s>Stotriya</s> of the next day is made the <s>Anurūpa</s> (corresponding hymn) of today's <s>Stotriya</s> at the morning pressing. They thereby weave the multi-day rite (<s>ahīna</s>). For the continuity of the multi-day rite. These <s>Hotraka</s> priests, having recited the <s>Stotriya</s> of the six-day cycle at the morning pressing, recite the multi-day hymns (<s>ahīna-sūktas</s>) at the midday pressing. '<s>ā satyo yātu maghavāṃ ṛjīṣī</s>' (ṚV 4.16.1)—the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>'s is truthful (<s>satyavat</s>). '<s>asmā id u pra tavase turāya</s>' (ṚV 1.16.1)—for the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>. '<s>śāsad vahnir duhitur naptyaṃ gāt</s>' (ṚV 3.31.1)—for the <s>Acchāvāka</s>. They ask: 'Why does the <s>Acchāvāka</s> recite this hymn containing <s>vahni</s> (the drawer) at both, at the departing days and at the homeward days?' Because the <s>Acchāvāka</s> as a Bahvṛca is indeed powerful. The drawer (<s>vahni</s>) indeed carries the loads to which he is yoked. Therefore the <s>Acchāvāka</s> recites this hymn containing <s>vahni</s> at both the departing and homeward days. These are recited on five days: the twenty-fourth, the <s>Abhijit</s>, the <s>Viṣuvat</s>, the <s>Viśvajit</s>, and the <s>Mahāvrata</s>. These are called the multi-day hymns (<s>ahīna-sūktas</s>). For in these nothing is omitted. These days indeed go forward without return. Therefore these are recited on these days. When they recite these, that is the form of the heavenly world. Or when they recite these, they call forth <s>Indra</s> by them, as a bull to a cow. The gods and ancient sages said: 'Let us extend the sacrifice with what is common.' They perceived this commonality of the sacrifice— common <s>Pragāthas</s>, common opening verses, common hymns.

body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>. <s>Viśvāmitra</s> first perceived these <s>saṃpāta</s> (confluence) hymns: '<s>evā tvām indra vajrinn atra</s>' (ṚV 4.19.1), '<s>yan na indro jujuṣe yac ca vaṣṭi</s>' (ṚV 4.22.1), '<s>kathā mahām avṛdhat kasya hotuḥ</s>' (ṚV 4.23.1). Those seen by <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, <s>Vāmadeva</s> released. <s>Viśvāmitra</s> reflected: 'The <s>saṃpāta</s> hymns that I perceived, <s>Vāmadeva</s> has released them. What hymns then shall I release as <s>saṃpāta</s> counterparts?' He released these hymns as <s>saṃpāta</s> counterparts: '<s>sadyo ha jāto vṛṣabhaḥ kanīnaḥ</s>' (ṚV 3.48.1), '<s>ud u brahmāṇy airata śravasyā</s>' (ṚV 7.23.1), '<s>abhi taṣṭeva dīdhayā manīṣām</s>' (ṚV 3.38.1)—these are <s>Viśvāmitra</s>'s. '<s>indraḥ pūrbhid ātirad dāsam arkaiḥ</s>' (ṚV 3.34.1), '<s>ya eka id dhavyaś carṣaṇīnām</s>' (ṚV 6.22.1), '<s>yas tigmaśṛṅgo vṛṣabho na bhīmaḥ</s>' (ṚV 7.19.1)—these are <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>'s. '<s>imām ū ṣu prabhṛtiṃ sātaye dhāḥ</s>' (ṚV 3.36.1), '<s>icchanti tvā somyāsaḥ sakhāyaḥ</s>' (ṚV 3.30.1), '<s>śāsad vahnir duhitur naptyaṃ gāt</s>' (ṚV 3.31.1)—these are <s>Bharadvāja</s>'s. By these <s>saṃpāta</s> hymns, these sages attained these worlds. Because they attained (<s>samapatan</s>), therefore they are called <s>saṃpātas</s>. That is the <s>saṃpāta</s>-nature of the <s>saṃpātas</s>. Then, from these three <s>saṃpāta</s> hymns, the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> recites one each day in reverse order: '<s>evā tvām indra vajrinn atra</s>' (ṚV 4.19.1) on the first day; '<s>yan na indro jujuṣe yac ca vaṣṭi</s>' (ṚV 4.22.1) on the second; '<s>kathā mahām avṛdhat kasya hotuḥ</s>' (ṚV 4.23.1) on the third. Likewise the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> recites three <s>saṃpātas</s> one each day in reverse order: '<s>indraḥ pūrbhid ātirad dāsam arkaiḥ</s>' (ṚV 3.34.1) on the first day; '<s>ya eka id dhavyaś carṣaṇīnām</s>' (ṚV 6.22.1) on the second; '<s>yas tigmaśṛṅgo vṛṣabho na bhīmaḥ</s>' (ṚV 7.19.1) on the third. Likewise the <s>Acchāvāka</s> recites three <s>saṃpātas</s> one each day in reverse order: '<s>imām ū ṣu prabhṛtiṃ sātaye dhāḥ</s>' (ṚV 3.36.1) on the first day; '<s>icchanti tvā somyāsaḥ sakhāyaḥ</s>' (ṚV 3.30.1) on the second; '<s>śāsad vahnir duhitur naptyaṃ gāt</s>' (ṚV 3.31.1) on the third. These are nine and three recited daily—they total twelve. Twelve are the months of the year. The year is <s>Prajāpati</s>. <s>Prajāpati</s> is the sacrifice. He thereby attains the year, <s>Prajāpati</s>, the sacrifice. Becoming established day by day in that year, in <s>Prajāpati</s>, in the sacrifice, they go forth. They become established. All this becomes established accordingly. He becomes established in progeny and cattle—whoever knows thus.

body.translated_text:
The <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> recites '<s>ko adya naryo devakāmaḥ</s>' [ṚV 4.25.1].
The <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> recites '<s>vane na vā yo ny adhāyi cākan</s>' [ṚV 10.29.1].
The <s>Acchāvāka</s> recites '<s>ā yāhy arvāṅ upa vandhureṣṭhāḥ</s>' [ṚV 3.43.1].
These are indeed the 'sowings' (<s>āvapana</s>).
With these very sowings the gods and the seers went to the heavenly world.
Even so the sacrificers, with these very sowings, go to the heavenly world.
The <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> recites '<s>sadyo ha jāto vṛṣabhaḥ kanīnaḥ</s>' [ṚV 3.48.1] day after day, before the <s>saṃpātas</s> (junctions).
This <s>sūkta</s> (hymn) leads to heaven.
With this hymn the gods and seers went to the heavenly world.
Even so the sacrificers go to the heavenly world with this very hymn.
It contains a bull — it has cattle.
For the obtainment of cattle.
It has five verses.
For the <s>Paṅkti</s> (five-foot meter) is food.
For the securing of food.
With '<s>ariṣṭair naḥ pathibhiḥ pārayantā</s>' [ṚV 6.69.1d] — he recites this day after day for the attainment of heaven.
The <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> recites '<s>ud u brahmāṇy airata śravasyā</s>' [ṚV 7.23.1].
This hymn is perfected, rich in sacred formulas.
With this hymn the gods and seers went to the heavenly world.
Even so the sacrificers go to the heavenly world with this very hymn.
It has six verses.
Six indeed are the seasons.
For the obtainment of the seasons.
He recites it day after day after the <s>saṃpātas</s>.
The <s>Acchāvāka</s> recites '<s>abhi taṣṭeva dīdhayā manīṣām</s>' [ṚV 3.38.1a].
He recites day after day; he addresses — that is its form.
'<s>abhi priyāṇi marmṛśat parāṇi</s>' [ṚV 3.38.1c] —
for the distant days are the dear ones.
Touching those very days, they go, taking hold of them.
For the heavenly world is beyond this world.
They thereby touch the heavenly world.
'<s>kavīṃr icchāmi saṃdṛśe sumedhāḥ</s>' [ṚV 3.38.1d] —
those who have departed before by this path are indeed the sages (<s>kavis</s>); he thereby addresses them.
Moreover, it has ten verses — ten indeed are the vital breaths.
By the breath he thereby attains it.
For the continuity of the vital breaths.
Moreover, it has ten verses.
Ten are the vital breaths in a person.
Ten are the heavenly worlds.
He thereby attains both the vital breaths and the heavenly worlds.
Established in the vital breaths and in the heavenly worlds, they proceed.
Moreover, it has ten verses.
The <s>Virāj</s> has ten syllables.
This earth is indeed the foundation of the heavenly world.
He thereby establishes this in that foundation.

body.translated_text:
The <s>Pragāthas</s> containing '<s>kad</s>' (who) — '<s>kas tam indra tvāvasum</s>' [ṚV 7.32.14], '<s>kan navyo atasīnām</s>' [ṚV 8.3.13], '<s>kad ū nv asyākṛtam</s>' [ṚV 8.66.9] — are recited day after day.
<s>Ka</s> (who) is indeed <s>Prajāpati</s>.
For the attainment of <s>Prajāpati</s>.
That they contain '<s>kad</s>' — that is the form of the heavenly world.
Moreover, that they contain '<s>kad</s>' —
<s>Kam</s> is indeed food.
For the securing of food.
Moreover, that they contain '<s>kad</s>' —
<s>Kam</s> is indeed happiness.
For the securing of food.
Moreover, day after day they employ the pacified <s>Ahīna</s> hymns.
They pacify them with the <s>Pragāthas</s> containing '<s>kad</s>'.
Those, being pacified, become happiness (<s>kam</s>) for them.
Those, being pacified, carry them to the heavenly world.
They should recite hymn-opening verses in <s>Triṣṭubh</s> meter.
Some recite them before the <s>Pragāthas</s>, calling them <s>Dhāyyā</s> verses.
But one should not do so.
For the <s>Hotṛ</s> is the ruling power (<s>kṣatra</s>), the <s>Hotraka</s> priests are the common people (<s>viś</s>).
They would thereby make the common people go against the ruling power —
that would be harmful.
One should know: 'These are <s>Triṣṭubh</s> hymn-opening verses.'
Just as one would cross the ocean, even so do those float along who undertake a year-long session or a twelve-day rite.
Just as those desiring to cross would board a ship with <s>Airāvatī</s> (the elephant goddess), even so those desiring heaven mount upon these <s>Triṣṭubh</s> verses.
For this meter, having conveyed one to the heavenly world, does not turn back.
For it is the most powerful.
One should not invite apart from them.
For the meter is the same.

body.translated_text:
The <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> recites day after day before the <s>saṃpātas</s>: '<s>apendra prāco maghavann amitrān</s>' [PS 19.16.8a] —
'Drive away the enemies before us, O <s>Maghavan</s>! Drive away those behind, O conqueror! Drive away those from the north, drive away the base ones! That we may rejoice in your wide shelter' [PS 19.16.8bcd].
This is the form of fearlessness.
For one seeks fearlessness, as it were.
The <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> recites '<s>brahmaṇā te brahmayujā yunajmi</s>' [ṚV 3.35.5].
He recites this day after day — it contains 'yoking.'
For the <s>Ahīna</s> (multi-day rite) is as if yoked.
That is the form of the <s>Ahīna</s>.
The <s>Acchāvāka</s> recites day after day: '<s>uruṃ no lokam anu neṣi</s>' [ṚV 6.47.8] —
'Lead us' — for the <s>Ahīna</s> is indeed a journey.
That is the form of the <s>Ahīna</s>.
'Lead us' — that is the form of the <s>Sattrāyaṇa</s> (sacrificial session journey); <s>Indra</s> becomes like one dwelling in a house for them.
Just as a cow goes to a known cow-pen, or a bull to a cow, even so <s>Indra</s> comes to their sacrifice.

body.translated_text:
Now, regarding the yoking and unyoking of the <s>Ahīna</s>.
With '<s>vy antarikṣam atirat</s>' [ṚV 8.14.7a] he yokes the <s>Ahīna</s>.
With '<s>eved indram</s>' [ṚV 7.23.6a] he unyokes.
With '<s>nūnaṃ sā te</s>' [ṚV 2.11.21] he yokes the <s>Ahīna</s>.
With '<s>nū ṣṭutaḥ</s>' [ṚV 4.16.21] he unyokes.
He who knows both the yoking and unyoking is indeed worthy to extend the <s>Ahīna</s> thread.
This is his yoking; this is his unyoking.
Now, if on the first day they were to enclose with single-day verses on the twenty-fourth day, they would bring the sacrifice to completion on the very first day and would not perform the <s>Ahīna</s> rite.
But if they were to enclose with <s>Ahīna</s> concluding verses, then just as a yoked animal not being unyoked would be exhausted, so the sacrificers would be exhausted.
They would not perform the <s>Ahīna</s> rite.
But when they enclose with both types — just as one on a long journey would go from unyoking place to unyoking place, even so is this.
They should enclose with matching verses.
Now they say: one may extend the <s>stoma</s> (praise) by one or two verses.
There are long wilderness stretches.
Where the <s>stoma</s> is extended by many verses — 'let me quickly offer food to the gods.'
With unlimited verses at the latter two pressings — for the heavenly world is unlimited.
For the attainment of the heavenly world.
Just as one would quickly give to one who whinnies and thirsts, even so is this.
They should enclose with matching verses.

body.translated_text:
(GBr 2,6.6a) They ask: 'How is it that the <s>Hotṛ</s> has two <s>Ukthas</s> (praises) and one <s>Sūkta</s> (hymn), while the <s>Hotrā</s> (assistant priests) have one <s>Uktha</s> each and two <s>Sūktas</s>?'
(GBr 2,6.6b) That one who shines yonder [the sun] is indeed the <s>Hotṛ</s>.
(GBr 2,6.6c) He is indeed one.
(GBr 2,6.6d) Therefore he has one <s>Sūkta</s>.
(GBr 2,6.6e) Since, when pierced, he appears as if two —
(GBr 2,6.6f) his splendor is the disc, his radiance another; one is bright, the other is dark.
(GBr 2,6.6g) Therefore he has two <s>Ukthas</s>.
(GBr 2,6.6h) The rays are indeed the <s>Hotrās</s> (assistant priests).
(GBr 2,6.6i) They are one each.
(GBr 2,6.6j) Therefore they have one <s>Uktha</s> each.
(GBr 2,6.6k) Since each individual ray has two colors, therefore they have two <s>Sūktas</s>.
(GBr 2,6.6l) The year is indeed the <s>Hotṛ</s>.
(GBr 2,6.6m) It is indeed one.
(GBr 2,6.6n) Therefore it has one <s>Sūkta</s>.
(GBr 2,6.6o) Since its days are of two kinds — some cold, some hot — therefore it has two <s>Ukthas</s>.
(GBr 2,6.6p) The seasons are indeed the <s>Hotrās</s>.
(GBr 2,6.6q) They are one each.
(GBr 2,6.6r) Therefore they have one <s>Uktha</s> each.
(GBr 2,6.6s) Since each season has two months, therefore they have two <s>Sūktas</s>.
(GBr 2,6.6t) The person (<s>puruṣa</s>) is indeed the <s>Hotṛ</s>.
(GBr 2,6.6u) He is indeed one.
(GBr 2,6.6v) Therefore he has one <s>Sūkta</s>.
(GBr 2,6.6w) Since the person is one way facing backward and another way facing forward, therefore he has two <s>Ukthas</s>.
(GBr 2,6.6x) The limbs are indeed the <s>Hotrās</s>.
(GBr 2,6.6y) They are one each.
(GBr 2,6.6z) Therefore they have one <s>Uktha</s> each.
(GBr 2,6.6aa) Since each limb has a luster, therefore they have two <s>Sūktas</s>.
(GBr 2,6.6bb) They ask: 'When the <s>Hotṛ</s> has two <s>Ukthas</s> and one <s>Sūkta</s>, and the <s>Hotrās</s> have one <s>Uktha</s> each and two <s>Sūktas</s>, how is that equal?'
(GBr 2,6.6cc) 'Because they offer with two-deity [verses], and because the <s>Hotrās</s> have two <s>Sūktas</s>' — thus one should say.
(GBr 2,6.6dd) They ask: 'When at the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> sacrifice two <s>Ukthas</s> of the <s>Hotṛ</s> are in excess, how are the <s>Hotrās</s> not cut off from that?'
(GBr 2,6.6ee) 'Because they offer with two-deity [verses], and because the <s>Hotrās</s> have two <s>Sūktas</s>' — thus one should say.
(GBr 2,6.6ff) They say: 'At the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> sacrifice, all deities and all meters are replenished.'
(GBr 2,6.6gg) 'Then with which meter do they lead forth the unwearied <s>Ukthas</s>? With which deity?'
(GBr 2,6.6hh) 'With the <s>Gāyatra</s> meter and with <s>Agni</s> as the deity' — thus one should say.
(GBr 2,6.6ii) When the gods were extending the sacrifice, the <s>Asura-Rākṣasas</s> attacked at the joints of the sacrifice: 'We shall destroy their sacrifice at the third pressing.'
(GBr 2,6.6jj) At the third pressing the sacrifice is the swiftest and strongest.
(GBr 2,6.6kk) 'Let us spread out and destroy their sacrifice.'
(GBr 2,6.6ll) They yoked <s>Varuṇa</s> to the south,
(GBr 2,6.6mm) <s>Bṛhaspati</s> to the middle,
(GBr 2,6.6nn) <s>Viṣṇu</s> to the north.
(GBr 2,6.6oo) They [each] said: 'We are each alone.'
(GBr 2,6.6pp) 'We cannot withstand this.'
(GBr 2,6.6qq) 'Let a second be praised, by whom together we may prevail.'
(GBr 2,6.6rr) <s>Indra</s> said to them: 'You are all my companions.'
(GBr 2,6.6ss) They all, with <s>Indra</s> as companion,

body.translated_text:
(GBr 2,6.7a) They lead forth the <s>Uktha</s> of the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> [priest] with <s>Āgneya</s> (verses to <s>Agni</s>).
(GBr 2,6.7b) <s>Agni</s> is indeed virility.
(GBr 2,6.7c) By virility indeed they lead it forth for him.
(GBr 2,6.7d) The <s>Aindrāvāruṇa</s> is recited in accompaniment.
(GBr 2,6.7e) <s>Indra</s> is indeed virility.
(GBr 2,6.7f) <s>Varuṇa</s> is sovereignty.
(GBr 2,6.7g) The <s>Ukthas</s> (praises) are cattle.
(GBr 2,6.7h) By virility and sovereignty he seizes cattle on both sides.
(GBr 2,6.7i) For stability.
(GBr 2,6.7j) For non-departure.
(GBr 2,6.7k) They lead forth the <s>Uktha</s> of the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> with <s>Aindrī</s> (verses to <s>Indra</s>).
(GBr 2,6.7l) <s>Indra</s> is indeed virility.
(GBr 2,6.7m) By virility indeed they lead it forth for him.
(GBr 2,6.7n) The <s>Aindrābārhaspatya</s> is recited in accompaniment.
(GBr 2,6.7o) <s>Indra</s> is indeed virility.
(GBr 2,6.7p) <s>Bṛhaspati</s> is <s>Brahman</s> (sacred knowledge).
(GBr 2,6.7q) The <s>Ukthas</s> are cattle.
(GBr 2,6.7r) By virility and <s>Brahman</s> he seizes cattle on both sides.
(GBr 2,6.7s) For stability.
(GBr 2,6.7t) For non-departure.
(GBr 2,6.7u) They lead forth the <s>Uktha</s> of the <s>Acchāvāka</s> with <s>Aindrī</s> (verses to <s>Indra</s>).
(GBr 2,6.7v) <s>Indra</s> is indeed virility.
(GBr 2,6.7w) By virility indeed they lead it forth for him.
(GBr 2,6.7x) The <s>Aindrāvaiṣṇava</s> is recited in accompaniment.
(GBr 2,6.7y) <s>Indra</s> is indeed virility.
(GBr 2,6.7z) <s>Viṣṇu</s> is the sacrifice.
(GBr 2,6.7aa) The <s>Ukthas</s> are cattle.
(GBr 2,6.7bb) By virility and sacrifice he seizes cattle on both sides and finally establishes them in sovereignty.
(GBr 2,6.7cc) Therefore the <s>Kṣatriya</s> is the greatest lord of cattle.
(GBr 2,6.7dd) He is the ruler, the bestower; to whom it is given, the <s>Vedas</s> are secured.
(GBr 2,6.7ee) These <s>Aindrī</s> and <s>Jāgatī</s> [hymns] they recite.
(GBr 2,6.7ff) And by these the third pressing is [made] one with <s>Indra</s>; by these the pressing is in <s>Jagatī</s> [meter].
(GBr 2,6.7gg) These are indeed the steadfast <s>Ukthas</s> — the <s>Nābhānediṣṭha</s>, the <s>Vālakhilya</s>, the <s>Vṛṣākapi</s>, and the <s>Evayāmarut</s>.
(GBr 2,6.7hh) Therefore they should be approached together.
(GBr 2,6.7ii) 'This seed, shed together, is successful; let it generate as one.'
(GBr 2,6.7jj) Those who do not approach these together — it would be as if one were to scatter seed that has been shed, or dismember a child that has been born limb by limb; such would be the result.
(GBr 2,6.7kk) Therefore they should be approached together.
(GBr 2,6.7ll) 'This seed, shed together, is successful; let it generate as one.'
(GBr 2,6.7mm) He recites the <s>Śilpas</s> (ornamental passages), the divine <s>Śilpas</s>.
(GBr 2,6.7nn) It is by imitation of these [divine] <s>Śilpas</s> that human <s>Śilpa</s> (craft/art) is attained.
(GBr 2,6.7oo) An elephant, a metal vessel, a garment, gold, a mule-drawn chariot — these are <s>Śilpa</s>.
(GBr 2,6.7pp) <s>Śilpa</s> is attained by him — whoever knows thus.

body.translated_text:
(GBr 2,6.8a) He recites the <s>Nābhānediṣṭha</s> [hymn].
(GBr 2,6.8b) The <s>Nābhānediṣṭha</s> is indeed seed.
(GBr 2,6.8c) He thereby prepares his seed.
(GBr 2,6.8d) That becomes mixed with seed.
(GBr 2,6.8e) 'Coming together with seed upon the earth, he sprinkled it' [ṚV 10.61.7b] — thus.
(GBr 2,6.8f) For the success of the seed indeed.
(GBr 2,6.8g) He recites it with <s>Ārāśaṃsa</s> (praise verses).
(GBr 2,6.8h) Offspring are indeed men (<s>naras</s>).
(GBr 2,6.8i) Recitation is speech.
(GBr 2,6.8j) He thereby places speech in the offspring.
(GBr 2,6.8k) Therefore these offspring are born speaking.
(GBr 2,6.8l) Some recite it before the <s>Pragāthas</s>, saying: 'Speech has its source in front.'
(GBr 2,6.8m) Others [recite it] after, saying: 'Speech has its source above.'
(GBr 2,6.8n) He should recite it in the middle.
(GBr 2,6.8o) For this speech has its source in the middle.
(GBr 2,6.8p) From above it is as if nearer.
(GBr 2,6.8q) The <s>Hotṛ</s>, having recited it in the form of seed, hands it to the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> [priest].
(GBr 2,6.8r) 'Prepare the vital breaths for this one!'
(GBr 2,6.8s) He recites the <s>Vālakhilya</s> [hymns].
(GBr 2,6.8t) The <s>Vālakhilyas</s> are indeed the vital breaths.
(GBr 2,6.8u) He thereby prepares his vital breaths.
(GBr 2,6.8v) He recites them in alternation.
(GBr 2,6.8w) For the vital breaths are in alternation.
(GBr 2,6.8x) <s>Prāṇa</s> (in-breath) with <s>apāna</s> (out-breath).
(GBr 2,6.8y) <s>Apāna</s> with <s>vyāna</s> (diffused breath).
(GBr 2,6.8z) He alternates by the verse-foot in the first <s>Sūkta</s>.
(GBr 2,6.8aa) By the half-verse in the second.
(GBr 2,6.8bb) By the whole verse in the third.
(GBr 2,6.8cc) When he alternates in the first <s>Sūkta</s>, he thereby separates speech and mind.
(GBr 2,6.8dd) In the second, he separates sight and hearing.
(GBr 2,6.8ee) In the third, he separates the vital breaths and the self.
(GBr 2,6.8ff) He should alternate at will.
(GBr 2,6.8gg) Otherwise the <s>Pragāthas</s> do not work properly.
(GBr 2,6.8hh) He should alternate by exceeding [the normal pattern].
(GBr 2,6.8ii) Then the <s>Pragāthas</s> work properly.
(GBr 2,6.8jj) The exceeding [pattern] is the form of the heavenly world.
(GBr 2,6.8kk) Or, regarding the exceeding [pattern]: the self is the <s>Bṛhatī</s> [meter].
(GBr 2,6.8ll) The vital breaths are the <s>Satobṛhatī</s>.
(GBr 2,6.8mm) He recited the <s>Bṛhatī</s>.
(GBr 2,6.8nn) That is the self.
(GBr 2,6.8oo) Then the <s>Satobṛhatī</s>.
(GBr 2,6.8pp) Those are the vital breaths.
(GBr 2,6.8qq) Then the <s>Bṛhatī</s>.
(GBr 2,6.8rr) Then the <s>Satobṛhatī</s>.
(GBr 2,6.8ss) He thereby goes surrounding the self with vital breaths.
(GBr 2,6.8tt) Or, regarding the exceeding [pattern]: the self is the <s>Bṛhatī</s>.
(GBr 2,6.8uu) Offspring are the <s>Satobṛhatī</s>.
(GBr 2,6.8vv) He recited the <s>Bṛhatī</s>.
(GBr 2,6.8ww) That is the self.
(GBr 2,6.8xx) Then the <s>Satobṛhatī</s>.
(GBr 2,6.8yy) Those are offspring.
(GBr 2,6.8zz) Then the <s>Bṛhatī</s>.
(GBr 2,6.8aaa) Then the <s>Satobṛhatī</s>.
(GBr 2,6.8bbb) He thereby goes surrounding the self with offspring.
(GBr 2,6.8ccc) Or, regarding the exceeding [pattern]: the self is the <s>Bṛhatī</s>.
(GBr 2,6.8ddd) Cattle are the <s>Satobṛhatī</s>.
(GBr 2,6.8eee) He recited the <s>Bṛhatī</s>.
(GBr 2,6.8fff) That is the self.
(GBr 2,6.8ggg) Then the <s>Satobṛhatī</s>.
(GBr 2,6.8hhh) Those are cattle.
(GBr 2,6.8iii) Then the <s>Bṛhatī</s>.
(GBr 2,6.8jjj) Then the <s>Satobṛhatī</s>.
(GBr 2,6.8kkk) He thereby goes surrounding the self with cattle.
(GBr 2,6.8lll) The <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>, having prepared the vital breaths, hands it to the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>.
(GBr 2,6.8mmm) 'Generate this one!'
(GBr 2,6.8nnn) He recites the <s>Sukīrti</s> (good fame) [hymn].
(GBr 2,6.8ooo) The <s>Sukīrti</s> is indeed of divine origin.
(GBr 2,6.8ppp) Thereby he generates the sacrificer in the sacrificial, divine womb.
(GBr 2,6.8qqq) He recites the <s>Vṛṣākapi</s> [hymn].
(GBr 2,6.8rrr) The <s>Vṛṣākapi</s> is indeed the self.
(GBr 2,6.8sss) He thereby prepares his self.
(GBr 2,6.8ttt) He applies the <s>Nyūṅkha</s> (nasal intonation).
(GBr 2,6.8uuu) The <s>Nyūṅkha</s> is indeed food.
(GBr 2,6.8vvv) He thereby bestows food upon him, like a breast to a newborn child.
(GBr 2,6.8www) It is fivefold.
(GBr 2,6.8xxx) For the person (<s>puruṣa</s>) is fivefold, arranged in five parts:
(GBr 2,6.8yyy) Hair, skin, bone, marrow, and brain.
(GBr 2,6.8zzz) Having prepared the sacrificer as extensive as the person, he hands him to the <s>Acchāvāka</s>.
(GBr 2,6.8aaaa) 'Prepare the foundation for this one!'
(GBr 2,6.8bbbb) He recites the <s>Evayāmarut</s> [hymn].
(GBr 2,6.8cccc) The <s>Evayāmarut</s> is indeed the foundation.
(GBr 2,6.8dddd) He thereby finally establishes him in the foundation.

body.translated_text: These are called the <s>Sahacarāṇi</s> (companion recitations): the <s>Nābhānediṣṭha</s>, the <s>Vālakhilya</s>, the <s>Vṛṣākapi</s>, and the <s>Evayāmarut</s>. One may either recite them together or not recite them together. If one were to omit any of these, it would be as if something were omitted from the <s>Yajamāna</s> (sacrificer). If the <s>Nābhānediṣṭha</s> [is omitted], his seed would be omitted. If the <s>Vālakhilyas</s>, his vital breaths would be omitted. If the <s>Vṛṣākapi</s>, his self (<s>Ātman</s>) would be omitted. If the <s>Evayāmarut</s> — the <s>Evayāmarut</s> is a firm foundation — one should make him hear from that very foundation, both divine and human. One may either recite them together or not recite them together. Now, <s>Buḍila Āśvitarāsya</s>, being the <s>Hotṛ</s> in a <s>Viśvajit</s> (all-conquering sacrifice), considered: 'Of these ritual arts in the year-long <s>Viśvajit</s>, two <s>Ukthas</s> (recitations) of the <s>Hotṛ</s> fall into the midday [pressing]. Come, let me have the <s>Evayāmarut</s> recited in this very manner.' He had it recited thus. While it was being recited thus, <s>Gośla</s> came. He said: 'O <s>Hotṛ</s>, why does your <s>Śastra</s> (recitation) float about like a rudderless [boat]?' 'What happened?' '<s>Evayāmarut</s> is being recited to the north.' He said: '<s>Indra</s> is indeed the midday [deity]. Why do you wish to remove <s>Indra</s> from the midday?' 'I do not wish to remove <s>Indra</s> from the midday,' he said. 'But this meter is not suited for the midday — it is <s>Jāgata</s> (in <s>Jagatī</s> meter) or more-than-<s>Jāgata</s>. And it belongs to the <s>Maruts</s>.' 'Do not confuse [the rite] thus!' He [<s>Gośla</s>] said: 'Stop, O <s>Acchāvāka</s>!' Then he exercised authority over the instruction. He said: 'The <s>Acchāvāka</s> recites [hymns] with <s>Indra</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s> as limbs. Now you should insert [the <s>Evayāmarut</s>] after the <s>Hotṛ</s>'s <s>Raudrī Dhāyyā</s> (meditation verse to <s>Rudra</s>) and before the <s>Māruta Sūkta</s> (hymn to the <s>Maruts</s>).' 'So be it.' Even now it is recited in that very manner. Just as on the sixth <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> day the sacrifice is properly arranged and the <s>Yajamāna</s>'s progeny is [assured] — how is it that the <s>Nābhānediṣṭha</s> remains unrecited while one recites the <s>Vālakhilyas</s>? Seed comes first, then the vital breaths. So too [for] the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> (priest). The <s>Nābhānediṣṭha</s> remains unrecited while one recites the <s>Vṛṣākapi</s>. Seed comes first, then the self. How then is the <s>Yajamāna</s>'s progeny [secured]? How are the vital breaths made secure? The <s>Yajamāna</s> is indeed prepared through this entire sacrificial rite. Just as an embryo in the womb — his vital breaths would be [formed] within. If the <s>Vṛṣākapi</s> [is] the self, it would be as [the embryo] that lies being formed. For not everything comes into being all at once at the beginning. One limb after another comes into being as it is formed. If all are performed on the same day, the sacrifice is properly arranged and the <s>Yajamāna</s>'s progeny is [assured]. Then the <s>Hotṛ</s> should recite the <s>Evayāmarut</s>. That is his firm foundation. In that [foundation] he finally establishes him; he establishes him. [9]

children.text: (GBr_2,6.10x) saṃtatais tryahair avyavachinnair yanti ya evaṃvidvāṃsa upayanti || 10 ||

body.translated_text: The sixth day is indeed the field of the gods (<s>Devakṣetra</s>). They who reach the sixth day reach the field of the gods. The gods do not dwell in one another's house; season does not dwell in [another] season's house, they say. The <s>Ṛtvijs</s> (priests) perform the <s>Ṛtuyājas</s> (seasonal offerings) each in their proper place, without handing over [to one another]. When they arrange the seasons, each is the progenitor in its proper place. They say: one should not command with seasonal commands (<s>Ṛtupraiṣas</s>), nor should one utter the <s>Vaṣaṭkāra</s> with seasonal commands. Speech is indeed the seasonal commands. Speech is exhausted on the sixth day. If they were to command with seasonal commands, if they were to utter the <s>Vaṣaṭkāra</s> with seasonal commands, they would encounter speech that is exhausted, pacified, broken, and carrying away. They would fall from the unshaken sacrifice. They would go astray from the sacrifice, from breath, from progeny, from cattle. Therefore one should command with <s>Ṛgma</s> (verse-based commands). The <s>Vaṣaṭkāra</s> should be based on <s>Ṛgma</s> verses. Then they do not encounter speech that is exhausted, pacified, broken, and carrying away. They do not fall from the unshaken sacrifice. They do not go astray from the sacrifice, from breath, from progeny, from cattle. He places the <s>Pārucchepa</s> [hymns] in both pressings before the <s>Prasthitayājyā</s> (offering verses during procession). <s>Rohita</s> (reddish) is indeed the name of this <s>Chandas</s> (meter) that is <s>Pārucchepa</s>. With this, <s>Indra</s> ascended seven heavenly worlds. He who knows thus ascends seven heavenly worlds. They ask: 'Five-footed [verses] are the form of the fifth day, six-footed of the sixth — then why are seven-footed [verses] recited on the sixth day?'

body.translated_text: The gods and <s>Asuras</s> contended in these worlds. The gods drove the <s>Asuras</s> out from these worlds with the sixth day. The <s>Asuras</s>, taking whatever treasures they had in their hands, rushed into the ocean. The gods, pursuing them, seized their hand-held treasures with this very <s>Chandas</s> (meter). That is this <s>Pada</s> (foot), the recurring <s>Pada</s>. That is the hook for drawing [them] back. He who knows thus seizes the wealth of his enemy and drives him out from all these worlds. Heaven is the deity that bears the sixth day. The <s>Stoma</s> (praise-form) is the thirty-three-fold. The <s>Sāman</s> (chant) is the <s>Raivata</s>. The <s>Chandas</s> (meter) is the <s>Atichandas</s> (super-meter). He prospers according to the deity, according to the <s>Stoma</s>, according to the <s>Sāman</s>, according to the <s>Chandas</s> — whoever knows thus. That which has the same concluding [pattern] is the form of the sixth day. If the first day [is the same as] the last day — that is this recurring <s>Pada</s>: that it is the sixth, that it has horses, that it has chariots, that it returns, that it turns back, that it has an inner form, that yonder world is invoked, that it has the <s>Nābhānediṣṭha</s>, that it has the <s>Pārucchepa</s>, that it has the <s>Nārāśaṃsa</s>, that it has two-footed [verses], that it has seven-footed [verses], that it is accomplished, that it has the <s>Raivata</s> [<s>Sāman</s>] — that is the form of the third day. These are the forms of the sixth day. The essence of the meters, anointed by the sixth day, overflowed. <s>Prajāpati</s> drew it up with the <s>Nārāśaṃsī Gāyatrī</s>, the <s>Raibhī Triṣṭubh</s>, the <s>Parikṣityā Jagatī</s>, and the <s>Gāthā Anuṣṭubh</s>. These meters, recited on the sixth day, become unwearied (<s>Ayātayāma</s>).
