body.translated_text:
Now, that the <s>Stotriya</s> and <s>Anurūpa</s> are in two-footed (<s>Dvipadā</s>) meter — '<s>imā nu kaṃ bhuvanā sīṣadhāma</s>' [ṚV 10.157.1] —
for a person (<s>puruṣa</s>) is two-footed.
A person has two supports.
The person is indeed the sacrifice.
Therefore the <s>Stotriya</s> and <s>Anurūpa</s> are in two-footed meter.
Now he recites the <s>Sukīrti</s> (good-fame hymn): '<s>apendra prāco maghavann amitrān</s>' [PS 19.16.8a].
The <s>Sukīrti</s> has its origin in the gods.
He who knows this <s>Sukīrti</s> as having divine origin establishes fame; being famous among beings, he becomes established in the heavenly world.
He becomes established with offspring and cattle — he who knows this.
Now he recites the <s>Vṛṣākapi</s> hymn: '<s>vi hi sotor asṛkṣata</s>' [ṚV 10.86.1].
<s>Āditya</s> (the Sun) is indeed <s>Vṛṣākapi</s>.
Because, trembling, he rains down seed — therefore he is <s>Vṛṣākapi</s> (the bull-ape).
That is the <s>Vṛṣākapi</s>-nature of <s>Vṛṣākapi</s>.
He who knows this shines like <s>Vṛṣākapi</s> in all worlds.
In the third feet of its verses, at beginning and end, he makes <s>nyūṅkha</s> and <s>ninarda</s> sounds.
The <s>nyūṅkha</s> is food.
The <s>ninarda</s> is strength.
He thereby deposits the eating of food in strength for him.
Now he recites the <s>Kuntāpa</s> hymns.
<s>Kuya</s> indeed is a name for what is despised.
Because it heats (<s>tapati</s>) that — therefore they are <s>Kuntāpas</s>.
That is the <s>Kuntāpa</s>-nature of the <s>Kuntāpas</s>.
The despised things are burned away for him — having burned the despised, he becomes established in the heavenly world.
He becomes established with offspring and cattle — he who knows this.
The first fourteen of these are: '<s>idaṃ janā upa śruta</s>' (Hear this, O people).
He recites them in the <s>Pragrāha</s> manner, as with the <s>Vṛṣākapi</s>.
For it has the <s>Vārṣa</s> (rain) form.
It follows the pattern of <s>Vṛṣākapi</s>.
Now he recites the <s>Raibhī</s> verses:
'<s>vacyasva rebha vacyasva</s>' [ṚVKh 5.9.1].
For the gods and seers, singing aloud (<s>rebhantaḥ</s>), went to the heavenly world.
Even so the sacrificers,

body.translated_text: (GBr 2,6.14a) Now he recites the <s>Ādityāś ca Aṅgirasīś ca</s> [hymns]: '<s>Ādityā</s>s, O singer, led the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee) to the <s>Aṅgirases</s>' [ṚVKh 5.20.1, ŚS 20.135.6]. (GBr 2,6.14b) This is called the 'God-leading' (<s>Devanītha</s>). (GBr 2,6.14c) The <s>Ādityas</s> and the <s>Aṅgirases</s> competed in the heavenly world: 'We shall reach heaven first!' — 'No, we [shall reach] first!' (GBr 2,6.14d) The <s>Aṅgirases</s> saw the pressing for the next day (<s>śvaḥsutyā</s>). (GBr 2,6.14e) They said to <s>Agni</s>: 'Go, announce the pressing for tomorrow to the <s>Ādityas</s>.' (GBr 2,6.14f) But the <s>Ādityas</s> saw the pressing for today (<s>adyasutyā</s>). (GBr 2,6.14g) They said to <s>Agni</s>: 'The pressing for today is ours. (GBr 2,6.14h) Be our <s>Hotṛ</s> (invoking priest) — we approach you.' (GBr 2,6.14i) <s>Agni</s>, going [to the <s>Aṅgirases</s>], said: 'The <s>Ādityas</s> see a pressing for today. Whom did you name as your <s>Hotṛ</s>? They are calling for us — we [belong to] them.' (GBr 2,6.14j) The <s>Aṅgirases</s> became angry: 'Do not go! We are [your patrons]!' (GBr 2,6.14k) <s>Agni</s> replied: 'No! The blameless ones are calling me. (GBr 2,6.14l) For it is an offence not to go to the call of a blameless one. (GBr 2,6.14m) Therefore, even if [the invitation is] from too far or too small [a patron], one should go to the call of the sacrificer. (GBr 2,6.14n) For it is an offence not to go to the call of a blameless one.' (GBr 2,6.14o) The <s>Aṅgirases</s> then officiated the sacrifice for the <s>Ādityas</s>. (GBr 2,6.14p) To them [the <s>Ādityas</s> led this earth as the <s>dakṣiṇā</s>. (GBr 2,6.14q) But they did not accept her. (GBr 2,6.14r) She, this [earth], rejected, with heads on both sides, the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> [offerings] pierced by grief, lamenting, wandered about in anger: 'They did not accept me!' (GBr 2,6.14s) From her burst forth those chasms (<s>pradaras</s>) which are found [on earth]. (GBr 2,6.14t) Therefore one should not reject a <s>dakṣiṇā</s> that is offered back, nor should one destroy it. (GBr 2,6.14u) Lest one should destroy the <s>dakṣiṇā</s>. (GBr 2,6.14v) Therefore, if there be a rival of the same birth, one should give it to him. (GBr 2,6.14w) The <s>dakṣiṇā</s> does not then turn away. (GBr 2,6.14x) He establishes grief at the end in the hateful rival — [that is] the one who shines yonder [the sun]. (GBr 2,6.14y) He then recites: '<s>Ādityas</s>, O singer, led the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> to the <s>Aṅgirases</s> — that, O singer, they returned' [ṚVKh 5.20.1abc, ŚS 20.135.6abc]. (GBr 2,6.14z) For they did not return this earth. (GBr 2,6.14aa) 'That, O singer, they returned' — for they returned that [sun] yonder. (GBr 2,6.14bb) 'That, O singer, they accepted from us' [ṚVKh 5.20.2a, ŚS 20.135.7a]. (GBr 2,6.14cc) For they did not accept this earth. (GBr 2,6.14dd) 'That, O singer, they accepted from us' — having seized [it], they seized the sun. (GBr 2,6.14ee) 'The days [are] not alike, not discerning' [ṚVKh 5.20.2c, ŚS 20.135.7c] — for the discerner of days is the one who shines yonder. (GBr 2,6.14ff) He then recites: 'The sacrifices [are] not alike, not leading the way' [ṚVKh 5.20.2d, ŚS 20.135.7d]. (GBr 2,6.14gg) The <s>dakṣiṇā</s> is indeed the leader of the sacrifice. (GBr 2,6.14hh) Just as we should rightly [do]: what has fallen and exceeds — he indeed is the lord, the lifter. (GBr 2,6.14ii) 'And the white swift-flying one, and the youngest with [swift] feet, and he carries forth the swift measure' [ṚVKh 5.20.3, ŚS 20.135.8]. (GBr 2,6.14jj) He indeed is the white one, he is the swift-flying one, he indeed is the youngest with feet. (GBr 2,6.14kk) 'And he carries forth the swift measure' [ṚVKh 5.20.3c, ŚS 20.135.8c]. (GBr 2,6.14ll) '<s>Ādityas</s>, <s>Rudras</s>, <s>Vasus</s> — spread this! Accept this gift, O <s>Aṅgiras</s>! This gift is vast, expansive; this gift is great and broad. May the gods bestow it — may it be divine for you; may you accept it day after day!' [ṚVKh 5.20.4-5, ŚS 20.135.9-10] — Thus when he recites the <s>Ādityāś ca Aṅgirasīś ca</s>, it is for the attainment of heaven. (GBr 2,6.14mm) He recites them day after day, just like the <s>Nivid</s> insertions. (GBr 2,6.14nn) Then he recites the <s>Bhūtecchadas</s> (creature-covering [hymns]): 'You, O <s>Indra</s>, release the shelter' [ṚVKh 5.21.1, ŚS 20.135.11]. (GBr 2,6.14oo) These worlds are indeed the <s>Bhūtecchadas</s>. (GBr 2,6.14pp) The gods indeed poured out food against the <s>Asuras</s>, wishing to strike them down with beings, desiring to cross over. (GBr 2,6.14qq) These gods covered them from all beings. (GBr 2,6.14rr) Because these gods covered them from all beings, therefore [they are called] <s>Bhūtecchadas</s> (creature-coverers). (GBr 2,6.14ss) That is the creature-covering nature of the creature-coverers.

children.text: (GBr_2,6.15x) kāmārto vai retaḥ siñcati [ed. kāmārtau, corr. Patyal]
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,6.15x) One impelled by desire indeed pours forth seed.

children.text: (GBr_2,6.15y) retasaḥ siktāt prajāḥ prajāyante prajānāṃ prajananāya
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,6.15y) From the seed that is poured forth, creatures are born — for the procreation of creatures.

children.text: (GBr_2,6.15z) prajāvān prajanayiṣṇur bhavati prajātyai prajāyate prajayā paśubhir ya evaṃ veda || 15 ||
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,6.15z) He becomes possessed of offspring and desirous of procreating; he is born for procreation, with offspring and cattle — he who knows thus. [15]

body.translated_text: (GBr 2,6.15a) Then he recites the <s>Āhanasyā</s> [hymns]: 'Of this narrow-piercing one' [ṚVKh 5.22.1, ŚS 20.136.1]. (GBr 2,6.15b) From <s>Āhanasyā</s> indeed all this has been born. (GBr 2,6.15c) From <s>Āhanasyā</s> indeed [all] this is reproduced. (GBr 2,6.15d) [This is] for the attainment and procreation of all this. (GBr 2,6.15e) He should recite six of them. (GBr 2,6.15f) Six indeed are the seasons. (GBr 2,6.15g) The seasons are the ancestors. (GBr 2,6.15h) The ancestors are <s>Prajāpati</s>. (GBr 2,6.15i) <s>Prajāpati</s> is [the lord of] <s>Āhanasyā</s>. (GBr 2,6.15j) He should recite ten — this is the teaching of <s>Śāmbhavya</s>. (GBr 2,6.15k) The <s>Virāj</s> [meter] has ten syllables. (GBr 2,6.15l) The sacrifice belongs to the <s>Virāj</s>. (GBr 2,6.15m) Embryos live by it. (GBr 2,6.15n) <s>Śrī</s> (prosperity) is the <s>Virāj</s>. (GBr 2,6.15o) Glory and food [come from it]. (GBr 2,6.15p) He thereby establishes <s>Śrī</s>, the <s>Virāj</s>, in glory and food. (GBr 2,6.15q) As [these correspondences] become established, all this is established along with them. (GBr 2,6.15r) He becomes established with offspring and cattle — he who knows thus. (GBr 2,6.15s) He should recite three — this is [the teaching of] <s>Vātsya</s>. (GBr 2,6.15t) Indeed, the seed when poured out becomes threefold: the egg, the membrane, and the afterbirth. (GBr 2,6.15u) The origin is threefold: the mother, the father, and that which is born — that is the third. (GBr 2,6.15v) It would be inauspicious if one were to recite a fourth. (GBr 2,6.15w) Some say he should recite all sixteen.

children.text: (GBr_2,6.16qq) upāpto yad aindrābārhaspatyā tṛtīyasavane tad yad etaṃ tṛcam aindrābārhaspatyaṃ sūktaṃ śaṃsaty aindrābārhaspatyā paridhānīyā viśo adevīr abhyācarantīr iti_
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,6.16qq) It is connected that the <s>Aindrā-Bārhaspatya</s> [belongs] to the third pressing. When he recites this <s>Aindrā-Bārhaspatya</s> triplet as the hymn, the <s>Aindrā-Bārhaspatya</s> enclosing verse [is]: 'The godless peoples who come against [us].'

children.text: (GBr_2,6.16rr) aparajanā ha vai viśo devīr na hy asyāparajanaṃ bhayaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,6.16rr) The peoples who are without later-born [descendants] are the divine [ones]; for there is no fear from one who has no later-born [descendants].

children.text: (GBr_2,6.16ss) śāntāḥ prajāḥ kḷptāḥ sahante yatraivaṃvidaṃ śaṃsati yatraivaṃvidaṃ śaṃsatīti brāhmaṇam || 16 ||
children.translated_text: (GBr 2,6.16ss) The creatures become peaceful, ordered, and enduring — wherever one who knows thus recites, wherever one who knows thus recites — thus is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [teaching]. [16]

body.translated_text: (GBr 2,6.16a) Then he recites the <s>Dādhikrī</s> [verse]: 'I have praised <s>Dadhikrāvan</s>' [ṚV 4.39.6, ṚVKh 5.22.13, ŚS 20.137.3]. (GBr 2,6.16b) After that he recites the subsequent <s>Pāvamānī</s> [verses]: 'The pressed [<s>Soma</s> juices], sweetest' [ṚV 9.101.4, ŚS 20.137.4] — <s>Dadhikrī</s> is indeed food. (GBr 2,6.16c) The <s>Pāvamānīs</s> are purification. (GBr 2,6.16d) But some, having recited the <s>Pāvamānīs</s> first, then recite the <s>Dādhikrī</s> afterward, saying 'This speech is food-consuming; [<s>Soma</s>] which purifies.' (GBr 2,6.16e) One should not do thus; for speech perishes when hungry. (GBr 2,6.16f) He should recite the <s>Dādhikrī</s> first and then the subsequent <s>Pāvamānīs</s>. (GBr 2,6.16g) When he recites the <s>Dādhikrī</s> — this speech spoke a speech in the <s>Āhanasyā</s>. (GBr 2,6.16h) He thereby purifies speech with the divine strainer. (GBr 2,6.16i) It is in the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> meter. (GBr 2,6.16j) Speech indeed is the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>. (GBr 2,6.16k) He thereby purifies speech with its own meter. (GBr 2,6.16l) He recites it in half-verses. (GBr 2,6.16m) [This is] for firm establishment. (GBr 2,6.16n) Then he recites the <s>Pāvamānīs</s>. (GBr 2,6.16o) The <s>Pāvamānīs</s> are indeed purification. (GBr 2,6.16p) This speech spoke a speech in the <s>Āhanasyā</s>. (GBr 2,6.16q) He thereby purifies speech with the <s>Pāvamānīs</s>. (GBr 2,6.16r) They are all in the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> meter. (GBr 2,6.16s) Speech indeed is the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>. (GBr 2,6.16t) He thereby purifies speech with its own meter. (GBr 2,6.16u) He recites them in half-verses. (GBr 2,6.16v) [This is] for firm establishment. (GBr 2,6.16w) 'The drop (<s>Drapsa</s>) stood upon the soma-stalk-bearing [cow]' [ṚV 8.96.13, ŚS 20.137.7] — he recites this triplet (<s>tṛca</s>), the <s>Aindrā-Bārhaspatya</s> hymn. (GBr 2,6.16x) This, however, has been set free [from its original context]. (GBr 2,6.16y) When he recites this <s>Aindrā-Bārhaspatya</s> triplet as the final <s>Aindrā-Jāgata</s> triplet, some say 'This is the maintenance (<s>dhāraṇa</s>) of the pressing.' (GBr 2,6.16z) One should not do thus. (GBr 2,6.16aa) This speech has the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> as its foundation among these priestly offices — that is the <s>Aindrā-Bārhaspatya</s> at the third pressing. (GBr 2,6.16bb) When he recites this <s>Aindrā-Bārhaspatya</s> triplet as the final <s>Aindrā-Jāgata</s> triplet, he thereby gratifies him in his own foundation, with his own deities. (GBr 2,6.16cc) One may optionally enclose it [with a frame verse]. (GBr 2,6.16dd) Or optionally with the last [verse] of the triplet. (GBr 2,6.16ee) They say: 'Should one combine the recitations on the sixth day, or should one not combine them?' (GBr 2,6.16ff) 'How does he combine them on other days?' (GBr 2,6.16gg) 'How does he not combine them here?' (GBr 2,6.16hh) But some say one should never combine them. (GBr 2,6.16ii) For the heavenly world is the sixth day. (GBr 2,6.16jj) The heavenly world is indeed not to be united. (GBr 2,6.16kk) 'Nobody rests in the heavenly world [completely].' (GBr 2,6.16ll) Therefore he does not combine them. (GBr 2,6.16mm) That he does not combine them — that is the form of the heavenly world. (GBr 2,6.16nn) If indeed he does combine them — [the hymns of] <s>Nābhānediṣṭha</s>, the <s>Vālakhilyas</s>, <s>Vṛṣākapi</s>, and <s>Evayāmarut</s> — these are the <s>Uktha</s> hymns here; therefore he does not combine them. (GBr 2,6.16oo) The <s>Vṛṣākapi</s> [hymn] is of <s>Indra</s>. (GBr 2,6.16pp) It contains all meters; it is the wild speech (<s>aitaśapralāpa</s>) [of <s>Indra</s>].

body.text: (GBr_2,6.16col) ity atharvavede gopathabrāhmaṇottarabhāge ṣaṣṭhaḥ prapāṭhakaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (GBr 2,6 colophon) Thus ends the sixth <s>Prapāṭhaka</s> (chapter) of the Latter Part of the <s>Gopatha Brāhmaṇa</s> of the <s>Atharvaveda</s>.

body.text: (GBr_col) ity atharvavedabrāhmaṇapūrvottaraṃ samāptam ||
body.translated_text: (GBr colophon) Thus is completed the Prior and Latter [Parts] of the <s>Atharvaveda Brāhmaṇa</s> [i.e., the <s>Gopatha Brāhmaṇa</s>].
